A population of cells derived from a single cell is called a clone, and a clone is genetically identical. In general, plants retain "totipotency", the ability to differentiate into all the cells that make up an individual, even in the somatic cells of the adult, so in many cases clones can be produced from various somatic cells through the regeneration of individuals by tissue culture.

On the other hand, in higher animals such as mammals, only very limited cells, such as eggs and fertilised eggs, have "totipotency", so the production of clones is extremely difficult. The procedure by which Dolly, the world's first cloned sheep, announced in 1997, was produced was as follows.

Step 1: Mammary gland cells of a sheep of strain 1 are collected and cultured under special conditions.

Step 2: The nucleus is removed from an unfertilised egg of a sheep of strain 2.

Step 3: The cells prepared in Step 1 and Step 2 are fused, and cells in which cleavage has started normally are placed in the uterus of a sheep of strain 3 to make it pregnant.

After many failures, Dolly was born. Choose from A–I the correct description of the genetic composition of Dolly. (3 points)

A. Completely genetically identical to the strain 1 sheep

B. Completely genetically identical to the strain 2 sheep

C. Completely genetically identical to the strain 3 sheep

D. Genetically almost identical to the strain 1 sheep, but with mitochondrial genes of the strain 2 sheep mixed in

E. Genetically almost identical to the strain 1 sheep, but with mitochondrial genes of the strain 3 sheep mixed in

F. Genetically almost identical to the strain 2 sheep, but with mitochondrial genes of the strain 1 sheep mixed in

G. Genetically almost identical to the strain 2 sheep, but with mitochondrial genes of the strain 3 sheep mixed in

H. Genetically almost identical to the strain 3 sheep, but with mitochondrial genes of the strain 1 sheep mixed in

I. Genetically almost identical to the strain 3 sheep, but with mitochondrial genes of the strain 2 sheep mixed in

During the development of the mammalian cerebral cortex, neural stem cells are present deep in the brain, and by their cell divisions they produce both neural stem cells themselves and neurons. To analyse the cell cycle of the neural stem cells, mouse embryos were used as a model and thymidine labelled with a radioactive isotope was administered to the mother mouse. The labelled thymidine passes through the placenta and is taken up by the neural stem cells of the embryo that are in the process of DNA synthesis. Because the labelled thymidine is constantly being metabolised, it was administered continuously. Taking the time at which the labelled thymidine was first administered as 0, if the proportion of cells that had incorporated labelled thymidine into their nuclear DNA among all the neural stem cells changed with time as in the figure below, what can be said about the cell cycle of the neural stem cells? Choose from A–I.

Assume, however, that the length of the cell cycle is the same in all the neural stem cells. Also, because the neurons produced by cell division immediately migrate and leave the observed site, the change in the size of the whole cell population at the observed site during the observation period can be ignored. In addition, cells that have incorporated even a small amount of labelled thymidine are counted as cells that have incorporated it. (3 points)

Using the PCR (polymerase chain reaction) method, species can be identified from their DNA to some extent. One of its applications is the identification of "aonori" (青のり, green laver). There are situations in which seaweeds of the genus Enteromorpha (アオノリ属) must be distinguished from those of the genus Ulva (アオサ属), which are used as their substitute. However, because the products are mainly in powdered form, it is difficult to distinguish the two by microscopic observation. If, therefore, a part of the base sequence specific to the genus Enteromorpha is amplified by PCR and checked by electrophoresis, they can easily be distinguished.

A certain "aonori" was tested by the following procedure, and the result below was obtained. In order to conclude that "this sample is not of the genus Enteromorpha", what is necessary in addition to this test? Choose the combination of correct ones from A–J. (3 points)

[Procedure and result]

(1) DNA is extracted from the sample.

(2) Primers corresponding to the base sequence specific to the genus Enteromorpha were added, and that part of the base sequence was amplified by PCR.

(3) This was checked by electrophoresis, but no band corresponding to that base sequence was seen.

[What is necessary in addition]

① Treat DNA known to be from the genus Enteromorpha in the same way and confirm that a band appears.

② Treat DNA known to be from the genus Enteromorpha in the same way and confirm that no band appears.

③ Treat DNA known to be from the genus Ulva in the same way and confirm that a band appears.

④ Treat DNA known to be from the genus Ulva in the same way and confirm that no band appears.

⑤ Treat DNA known to be from neither the genus Enteromorpha nor the genus Ulva in the same way and confirm that a band appears.

⑥ Treat DNA known to be from neither the genus Enteromorpha nor the genus Ulva in the same way and confirm that no band appears.

Rubisco (ルビスコ) is a carboxylase that works in carbon fixation in photosynthesis, and it catalyses the reaction (Reaction 1) in which two molecules of phosphoglycerate are synthesised from ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate and $\mathrm{CO_2}$. On the other hand, however, Rubisco also has oxygenase activity and also catalyses the reaction in which ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate combines with $\mathrm{O_2}$ (Reaction 2).

Reaction 1: ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate + $\mathrm{CO_2}$ + $\mathrm{H_2O}$ → 2 × phosphoglycerate

Reaction 2: ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate + $\mathrm{O_2}$ → phosphoglycerate + phosphoglycolate

Which reaction takes priority is determined by conditions such as the $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ concentrations at the reaction site and the temperature. Of these, the effect of temperature is largely due to the property of Rubisco that "when the temperature rises, its affinity for $\mathrm{CO_2}$ falls markedly, but its affinity for $\mathrm{O_2}$ changes little".

Now let us consider another world, in which only the properties of plant Rubisco differ from those in the real world. In this hypothetical world, Rubisco is assumed to be such that "its affinity for $\mathrm{CO_2}$, like its affinity for $\mathrm{O_2}$, is not affected by temperature". In such a world, how would the distributions of C4 plants, which carry out C4 photosynthesis, and of CAM plants, which carry out crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM), compare with the real world? Considering how the environments in which C4 plants and CAM plants have an advantage over C3 plants, which carry out standard photosynthesis, change with the properties of Rubisco, infer the distributions of C4 plants and CAM plants in the hypothetical world and choose the most appropriate statement from A–I. (4 points)

A. The distributions of both C4 plants and CAM plants expand.

B. The distribution of C4 plants expands, but the distribution of CAM plants changes little.

C. The distribution of C4 plants expands, but the distribution of CAM plants shrinks.

D. The distribution of C4 plants changes little, but the distribution of CAM plants expands.

E. The distributions of both C4 plants and CAM plants change little.

F. The distribution of C4 plants changes little, but the distribution of CAM plants shrinks.

G. The distribution of C4 plants shrinks, but the distribution of CAM plants expands.

H. The distribution of C4 plants shrinks, but the distribution of CAM plants changes little.

I. The distributions of both C4 plants and CAM plants shrink.

Plants show a phenomenon called phototropism, in which they grow towards the direction of light, and it has long been known that the light causing phototropism is blue light. That an organism responds to light of a particular colour means nothing other than that it has a photoreceptor substance that selectively absorbs only light of that colour and causes a physiological phenomenon. About 15 years ago it became clear that what absorbs blue light and causes phototropism is a photoreceptor protein called phototropin. In plants, besides the photoreceptor substances working in photosynthesis, cryptochrome also exists as a blue-light-absorbing photoreceptor substance other than phototropin, so whether cryptochrome is also involved in regulating the direction of plant growth was examined using Arabidopsis (シロイヌナズナ), one of the higher plants.

Fifty Arabidopsis seeds were grown for 4 days in darkness (Figures 1–3, upper row) or under irradiation with blue light from above (Figures 1–3, lower row); the growth direction of the hypocotyl of the seedlings (the organ corresponding to the stem of the seedling) was measured, and the results were shown as histograms. Because the growth direction of the hypocotyl was measured as in Figure 4, 0 degrees represents growth vertically upwards, and −90 degrees and +90 degrees represent growth in horizontal directions. In addition to wild-type individuals (Figure 1), phototropin-deficient mutants (Figure 2) and cryptochrome-deficient mutants (Figure 3) were also examined.

Judging from the experimental results, choose the most appropriate combination of statements from A–I. (4 points)

In the senescence of leaves, which are photosynthetic organs, the equilibrium between the synthesis and degradation of chloroplast proteins, which is normally kept in balance, tilts towards degradation, so chlorophyll decreases and yellowing occurs. Leaves detached from the plant senesce rapidly when kept in the dark, but if cytokinin is given to the leaves at that time, senescence is suppressed. Also, in soybean, leaf senescence progresses as the seeds mature in autumn, but if the young pods (fruits) that grow after pollination are picked off one after another, leaf senescence is delayed. This leaf senescence is thought to be suppressed by cytokinin synthesised in the roots. Choose from A–H the combination of statements considered appropriate concerning experiments on senescence using soybean. Note that the liquid flowing in the xylem vessels is called xylem sap. Not a few climbing plants develop tendrils. Many tendrils are regarded as modified leaves, but there are also tendrils thought to be modified stems. To find out whether the tendrils of a certain climbing plant are a kind of leaf or a kind of stem, it was decided to observe their cells and tissues. In this observation, what information about the tendrils would be especially useful? Choose from A–E. (3 points)

A. Presence or absence of chloroplasts in the internal tissues

B. Presence or absence of stomata on the surface

C. Presence or absence of hairs on the surface

D. Branching pattern of the internal vascular bundles

E. Arrangement of xylem and phloem in cross-section

Planarians, which are flatworms (Platyhelminthes), have a high regenerative ability. The following is known about the regeneration of planarians.

(1) In the body of a normal planarian there is a group of cells that actively carry out DNA synthesis. These cells are called S cells.

(2) When an individual was irradiated with X-rays, which destroy cells with high proliferative ability, its S cells decreased.

(3) When the regeneration of the X-irradiated individuals was observed, they hardly regenerated.

From these findings, the hypothesis "S cells are, at least, stem cells necessary for regeneration" was put forward. Choose from A–F the most appropriate experiment needed to test this hypothesis further. (3 points)

A. Transplant part of the tissue of an X-irradiated individual into a normal individual and examine whether it has regenerative ability.

B. Transplant part of the tissue of a normal individual into an X-irradiated individual and examine whether its regenerative ability recovers.

C. Transplant part of the tissue of an X-irradiated individual into an X-irradiated individual and examine whether its regenerative ability recovers.

D. Transplant S cells of a normal individual into an X-irradiated individual and examine whether its regenerative ability recovers.

E. Transplant S cells of a normal individual into a normal individual and examine whether its regenerative ability changes.

F. Rear an X-irradiated individual for a long period and then examine whether its regenerative ability recovers.

The animal body is equipped with mechanisms that maintain the constancy of the internal environment (homeostasis) against changes in the external environment, and it has the ability to remain active without being greatly affected by environmental changes. The American physiologist Cannon (Cannon, W. B.) removed the sympathetic trunks of the right side of the thorax and abdomen of cats in order to examine the functions of the sympathetic nervous system in maintaining homeostasis. When these cats were placed in various environments and their responses were observed, the following results were obtained.

(1) When the sympathectomised cats were exposed to cold, the hair of the left half from the spine stood on end, but the hair of the right half did not.

(2) When the body temperature of the cats in the cold was recorded, results such as those in Figure a were obtained. The solid lines show the rectal temperature of the control group and the broken lines the rectal temperature of the sympathectomised group. The zigzags below each record show the intensity of the cats' shivering response.

(3) Control cats (3 cats) and sympathectomised cats (2 cats) were each given a stimulus of the same degree to provoke anger. Figure b shows the change in blood glucose level at this time and the record of the blood glucose level before the stimulus.

(4) Unless given special stimuli, the sympathectomised cats lived for more than 3 years in a healthy state in the stable environment of the laboratory without developing any notable impairment.

The black and yellow stripe pattern of the zebrafish is formed by the distribution of black pigment cells and yellow pigment cells. These pigment cells differentiate from common pigment stem cells, but which pigment cell they become is determined by influences from their surroundings. To examine the influence of existing pigment cells, the following experiments were therefore carried out using a method in which individual pigment cells are killed by burning and removed with microscopic laser irradiation. The experiments are shown schematically in the figure below.

Experiment 1: All the yellow pigment cells were removed in one area of a yellow stripe. Two weeks later, a few yellow pigment cells had appeared.

Experiment 2: All the yellow pigment cells were removed in one area of a yellow stripe. In addition, all the black pigment cells around it were removed. Two weeks later, a few yellow pigment cells and many black pigment cells had appeared in the part from which the yellow pigment cells had been removed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-1-14-fig1.png

However, among algae, the chloroplasts of brown algae, chlorarachniophytes and others have four membranes. These four-membrane chloroplasts are thought to have arisen by secondary symbiosis as in the figure below (③–⑤ in the figure below).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-1-30-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): シアノバクテリア様光合成生物 = cyanobacterium-like photosynthetic organism; 核a = nucleus a; 核b = nucleus b; 二重膜葉緑体 = double-membrane chloroplast; 四重膜葉緑体 = four-membrane chloroplast.

① A cyanobacterium-like photosynthetic organism is taken up by organism a.

② A double-membrane chloroplast is formed in organism a.

③ Organism a, which has come to have a double-membrane chloroplast, is taken up by organism b.

④ In organism b, the nucleus of organism a (nucleus a) and other parts degenerate.

⑤ A four-membrane chloroplast is formed in organism b.

In addition, the chloroplasts of land plants, green algae and chlorarachniophytes contain chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b, whereas the chloroplasts of red algae and brown algae contain chlorophyll a and chlorophyll c.

From the above, choose from A–F the correct diagram in which the primary and secondary symbioses are drawn on a phylogenetic tree. In the diagrams, ○ shows the organism that enters and the white arrow (⇨) shows into the cell of which organism it entered. (4 points)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-1-30-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 褐藻 = brown algae; クロララクニオン藻 = chlorarachniophytes; 紅藻 = red algae; 緑藻 = green algae; 陸上植物 = land plants; シアノバクテリア = cyanobacteria.

problems.title: Experiment 1 (seedlings), Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam (plants): question booklet

During the experiments always wear laboratory gloves, and take care that the experimental solutions do not come into contact with your eyes, mouth, skin, etc.

Manual for using the light microscope (see Figure 1)

I. How to use the light microscope
1. Adjust the height of the chair so that you can observe with your back straight.
2. Set the brightness-adjustment knob to "1".
3. Switch the main switch ON. Turn the brightness-adjustment knob to obtain a suitable brightness.
4. Turn the coarse-adjustment knob to lower the stage all the way down.
5. Turn the revolver to set the objective lens to 4× (the lowest magnification).
6. Place the preparation on the stage and fix it with the specimen clip (クレンメル). (This time a sample preparation has been set in advance.)
7. Using the vertical-feed and horizontal-feed knobs of the specimen clip, move the sample preparation so that the part on which letters are written comes to the position of the illuminating light seen from the lens at the top of the condenser.
8. Raise the stage all the way up. Take care that the preparation and the objective lens do not collide.
9. Looking through the eyepieces, turn the coarse-adjustment knob to lower the stage to the position where the image is in focus.
10. Turn the fine-adjustment knob to fine-tune the focus. Using the vertical-feed and horizontal-feed knobs of the specimen clip, try reading the letters on the sample preparation.
11. Rotate the aperture-diaphragm ring of the condenser to adjust the contrast and the depth of focus.
12. To observe at higher magnification, turn the revolver to set the objective lens to 10× or 40×.
Note) If a lens gets dirty during use, tell a TA. The TAs are the staff who support you in your experiments.

II. Eye-width and dioptre adjustment
Adjust each of these following the explanation below. When you look through the microscope wearing glasses, fold back the rubber of the eyeshades to make them shorter.

Eye-width adjustment: move the eyepieces left and right and observe with them matched to the width of your eyes. The correct position is the one in which the round left and right fields of view become a single image.
Dioptre adjustment: set the dioptre-adjustment rings to the 0 position. First, with your right eye, bring the specimen into focus by moving the stage up and down. Next, leaving the stage as it is, look with your left eye and turn the dioptre-adjustment ring of the left eyepiece to bring it into focus.

III. How to use the condenser (see Table 1)
If the brightness of the field of view is not uniform, adjust it by moving the condenser up-down knob (on the left side of the condenser). The condenser has a diaphragm; by opening and closing the diaphragm you can give contrast to the specimen and adjust the depth of focus.

Table 1. Relation between the aperture diaphragm of the condenser and brightness, depth of focus and contrast

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|} \hline & \text{Aperture diaphragm (open)} & \text{Aperture diaphragm (closed)} \\ \hline \text{Brightness} & \text{high} & \text{low} \\ \hline \text{Depth of focus} & \text{shallow} & \text{deep} \\ \hline \text{Contrast} & \text{weak} & \text{strong} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-1-fig1.png

Figure 1. Names of the parts of the light microscope (upright microscope)

Figure labels (Japanese → English): アイシェード = eyeshade; 鏡筒固定つまみ = tube-locking knob; 視度調整環 = dioptre-adjustment ring; レボルバー = revolver; クレンメル = specimen clip; コンデンサ開口絞り環 = condenser aperture-diaphragm ring; フィルター = filter; 粗動ハンドル = coarse-adjustment knob; 微動ハンドル = fine-adjustment knob; クレンメル縦送りハンドル = specimen-clip vertical-feed knob; クレンメル横送りハンドル = specimen-clip horizontal-feed knob; メインスイッチ = main switch; Ｉ：電源ON状態 = I: power ON; Ｏ：電源OFF状態 = O: power OFF; 明るさ調整つまみ = brightness-adjustment knob.

Manual for using the stereomicroscope (see Figure 2)

1. Do not place samples directly on the stage.
2. Adjust the height of the chair so that you can observe with your back straight.
3. Adjust the eye width and the dioptre of the eyepieces. Dioptre-adjustment rings are fitted to both eyepieces, so set both to the 0 position. Next, with your right eye, bring the specimen into focus by moving the stage up and down. Leaving the stage as it is, look with your left eye and turn the dioptre-adjustment ring of the left eyepiece to bring it into focus. When you look through the microscope wearing glasses, fold back the rubber of the eyeshades to make them shorter.
4. When observing or making sections, use incident illumination (left adjustment knob) and transmitted illumination (not used in today's experiment) as suits the observation. Adjust the angle of the incident illumination so that the sample is sufficiently lit.
5. To observe at a different magnification, adjust it by turning the zoom knob.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-1-fig2.png

Figure 2. Names of the parts of the stereomicroscope

Figure labels (Japanese → English): アイシェード = eyeshade; 視度調整環 = dioptre-adjustment ring; 落射LED照明装置 角度調整可能です = incident LED illuminator, angle adjustable; ズームハンドル = zoom knob; 焦準ハンドル = focusing knob; 落射照明 明るさ調整つまみ = incident illumination brightness-adjustment knob; 透過照明 明るさ調整つまみ 本日の実験では使いません = transmitted illumination brightness-adjustment knob, not used in today's experiment; ステージ = stage; メインスイッチ = main switch; Ｉ：電源ON状態 = I: power ON; Ｏ：電源OFF状態 = O: power OFF.

[Materials required for the experiments]
These experiments use the materials, apparatus, instruments and reagents shown below.

Materials
1. Tube vials containing seedlings – 2 (tube vials A and B)
2. Flowers – 3 kinds (Easter lily (テッポウユリ), snapdragon (キンギョソウ), Japanese dock (ギシギシ))

Apparatus, instruments, reagents
3. Light microscope (biological microscope) – 1
4. Stereomicroscope – 1
5. Sample preparation – 1
6. Slide glasses – 10
7. Cover glasses – 20 (in a plastic Petri dish)
8. Petri dish (large) – 1
9. Plastic Petri dishes – 2
10. Dissecting scissors – 1
11. Mounted needle – 1
12. Scalpel – 1
13. Tweezers – 2
14. Dropper – 1
15. Pointed disposable chopstick – 1
16. Filter papers – 10
17. Counter – 1
18. Laboratory tissues – 1 box (Kimwipes)
19. Paper towels – 1 bundle
20. Laboratory gloves (size M) – 2 pairs
21. Red pencil – 1
22. Marker pen – 1
23. Nail varnish – 1
24. Calculator – 1
25. Aceto-orcein – 1 bottle

Experiment 1. Observation of cell division using seedlings

[Introduction]
Angiosperms separate from the parent plant with seeds, or fruits containing seeds, as dispersal units, and when they reach a site suitable for growth they germinate and become new individuals. In this process the plant individual maintains its form and grows in an orderly way by strictly controlling where cell division takes place and how often. In this problem you will observe seedlings (young sprouts) of Crepis (クレピス; a plant of the family Asteraceae) and the cell divisions taking place in their tissues.
Tube vials A and B contain Crepis seedlings stained by the Feulgen method. Because in Feulgen staining only the parts that contain DNA are stained, it can stain the nuclei and chromosomes alone clearly. In addition, the intensity of the staining is proportional to the amount of DNA present. Seedlings A were left for 4 days in the light at 21 °C after sowing and then immediately fixed in Carnoy's solution. Seedlings B were prepared under the same conditions and then, before fixation, treated with reagent C for 3 hours and fixed in the same way.

[Question 1] Choose one seedling from specimen A and observe the whole of it carefully under the stereomicroscope. In the answer box, draw schematically the outline of the whole seedling with a black pencil, and fill in with the red pencil the parts that are strongly coloured by the Feulgen staining.

Observation of the seedlings
1. Transfer the seedlings in tube vial A, together with the liquid, to a plastic Petri dish. Write "A" on the lid of the Petri dish with the marker pen.
2. Choose a specimen that is easy to observe, move it to the centre with the tweezers and observe it under the stereomicroscope. Use the tweezers and the mounted needle as necessary.
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験（植物）問題冊子

実験中はかならず実験用手袋を着用し，実験液が目，口，皮膚などに触れないよう注意すること。

生物顕微鏡使用マニュアル（図1を参照）

I．生物顕微鏡の使い方
1．背筋を伸ばして観察できるようにイスの高さを調整する。
2．明るさ調整つまみを「1」にする。
3．メインスイッチの電源をONにする。明るさ調整つまみを回して適度な明るさにする。
4．粗動ハンドルを回してステージを一番下まで下げる。
5．レボルバーを回して対物レンズを4倍（最低倍率）にする。
6．ステージにプレパラートをのせてクレンメル（標本押さえ）で固定する。（今回はサンプルプレパラートがあらかじめセットしてある。）
7．コンデンサ上部のレンズから見えている照明光の位置に，サンプルプレパラートの文字が書いてある部位がくるように，クレンメル縦送りハンドルと横送りハンドルを使って移動させる。
8．ステージを一番上まで上げる。プレパラートと対物レンズがぶつからないように注意すること。
9．接眼レンズをのぞいてピントが合う位置まで粗動ハンドルを回してステージを下げる。
10．微動ハンドルを回してピントを微調整する。クレンメル縦送りハンドルと横送りハンドルを使用してサンプルプレパラートの文字を読んでみる。
11．コンデンサの開口絞り環を回転させてコントラストや焦点深度を調整する。
12．倍率を上げて観察する場合には，レボルバーを回して対物レンズを10倍，40倍にする。
注）使用中レンズがよごれた場合にはTAまで申し出ること。TAは皆さんの実験のサポートを行うスタッフです。

II．眼幅，視度調整
下記の説明に従ってそれぞれについて調整すること。また，眼鏡をかけて検鏡するときは，アイシェードのゴムを折り返して短くする。

眼幅調整：接眼レンズを左右に動かして自分の眼の幅にあった状態で観察する。左右の丸い視野像が一個になった位置が正常な位置になる。
視度調整：視度調整環を0の位置に合わせる。まず，右目で観察する標本にステージを上下させてピントを合わせる。次に，ステージをそのままの状態にして，左目でのぞき，左側の接眼レンズの視度調整環を回してピントを合わせる。

III．コンデンサの使い方（表1を参照）
視野の明るさが一様でない場合，コンデンサ上下動ハンドル（コンデンサの左側）を動かして調整する。コンデンサには絞りがついており，絞りを開閉することにより標本にコントラストをつけたり，焦点深度を調整することができる。

表1．コンデンサの開口絞りと明るさ，焦点深度，コントラストの関係

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|} \hline & \text{開口絞り（開）} & \text{開口絞り（閉）} \\ \hline \text{明るさ} & \text{大} & \text{小} \\ \hline \text{焦点深度} & \text{浅} & \text{深} \\ \hline \text{コントラスト} & \text{弱} & \text{強} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-1-fig1.png

図1．生物顕微鏡（正立顕微鏡）各部名称

実体顕微鏡使用マニュアル（図2を参照）

1．ステージに直接試料をのせないこと。
2．背筋を伸ばして観察できるようにイスの高さを調整すること。
3．接眼レンズの眼幅，視度調整をすること。視度調整環は接眼レンズの双方についているので双方とも0の位置に合わせる。次に，右目で観察する標本にステージを上下させてピントを合わせる。ステージをそのままの状態にして，左目でのぞき，左側の接眼レンズの視度調整環を回してピントを合わせる。眼鏡をかけて検鏡するときは，アイシェードのゴムを折り返して短くすること。
4．観察や切片作製のときは，落射照明（左側の調整つまみ）と透過照明（本日の実験には使用しません）を観察に応じて使い分けること。落射照明は角度を調整して，試料に光が十分当たるようにすること。
5．倍率を変えて観察する場合には，ズームハンドルを回して調節する。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-1-fig2.png

図2．実体顕微鏡各部名称

【実験に必要なもの】
この実験では，下に示した材料，装置，器具，試薬を用います。

材料
1．実生入り管ビン　2本（管ビンAおよびB）
2．花　3種類（テッポウユリ，キンギョソウ，ギシギシ）

装置，器具，試薬
3．生物顕微鏡　1台
4．実体顕微鏡　1台
5．サンプルプレパラート　1枚
6．スライドガラス　10枚
7．カバーガラス　20枚（プラスチックシャーレ中）
8．シャーレ（大）　1個
9．プラスチックシャーレ　2個
10．解剖バサミ　1個
11．柄付針　1本
12．メス　1本
13．ピンセット　2本
14．スポイト　1本
15．先のとがった割りばし　1本
16．ろ紙　10枚
17．カウンター　1台
18．実験用ティッシュ　1箱（キムワイプ）
19．ペーパータオル　1束
20．実験用手袋（Mサイズ）　2組
21．赤鉛筆　1本
22．マジックペン　1本
23．マニキュア　1本
24．電卓　1台
25．酢酸オルセイン　1本

実験1．実生をつかった細胞分裂の観察

【はじめに】
被子植物は種子あるいは種子を含む果実を散布体として親植物から分離して，生育適地にたどり着くと発芽して新たな個体となります。この過程で植物個体は細胞分裂が起こる場所やその頻度を厳密に制御することで，個体の形態の維持と秩序だった成長をしています。この問題ではクレピス（キク科植物）の実生（芽生え）とその組織でおきている細胞分裂を観察します。
管ビンA，Bにはフォイルゲン染色されたクレピスの実生が入っています。フォイルゲン染色法はDNAが含まれる部分だけが染色されるので，核や染色体だけを明瞭に染色することができます。また，その染色の濃さは含まれるDNA量に比例します。Aの実生は，播種後，21℃明所に4日間静置して，直ちにカルノア液で固定したものです。Bの実生は，同様の条件で調製した後，固定の前に3時間，試薬Cで処理し，同様に固定したものです。

【問1】Aの標本から実生を1つ選び，実体顕微鏡で全体を注意深く観察せよ。解答欄に実生全体の輪郭を黒鉛筆で模式的に描き，フォイルゲン染色によって強く発色している部分を赤鉛筆でぬりつぶせ。

実生の観察
1．管ビンＡ内の実生を液ごとプラスチックシャーレに移します。マジックペンでシャーレのふたに「A」と記入します。
2．観察しやすい標本を選び，ピンセットで中央に移動し，実体顕微鏡で観察します。必要に応じてピンセットや柄付針を使用すること。

problems.title: Experiment 1 (seedlings), Question 2
problems.problem:
Experiment 1. Observation of cell division using seedlings (continued)

[Question 2] For seedling A and seedling B, make preparations of the cells of regions 1, 2 and 3 shown in Figure 3, and answer (1)–(5) below. Make and observe the preparations following the explanation in "Supplement: how to make chromosome preparations" on page 11.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-2-fig1.png

Figure 3. Regions of the seedlings for observing cell division. A was fixed immediately 4 days after germination. B was fixed after treatment with reagent C for 3 hours, 4 days after germination. Regions 1 and 3: about 1 mm each of the root apical meristem; region 2: about 1 mm of the central part of the seedling.

(1) Write the names of the phases of cell division in Figure 4.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-2-fig2.png

Figure 4. Micrographs of the phases (a–e) of the cell division cycle. Root apical meristem cells of kikutanigiku (キクタニギク) stained with aceto-orcein.

(2) Of regions 1, 2 and 3 of Figure 3 in the Crepis specimens, in which region is the chromosome number easiest to count? Write the number of the region in the answer box. Also count the chromosome number of Crepis and write it in the answer box.
(3) For regions 1 and 3 shown in Figure 3, observe the preparations, write the number of cells in each phase of cell division observed in each field of view on the observation record sheet attached at the end of the answer sheets, and total the observation results. Also write on the answer sheet the number of cells observed, the frequency of each phase and the estimated time required for each phase of cell division. In Crepis the duration of one cell cycle is 10.4 hours. Next, arrange the frequencies of the phases and write the frequency (%) of the mitotic phase in the answer box. For making chromosome preparations and observing the cells, refer to "Supplement: how to make chromosome preparations" on page 11 and "Method of observing chromosome preparations" on page 9. For identifying the phases, refer to the example of kikutanigiku in Figure 4.
(4) From the comparison of regions 1 and 3 observed in (3), state the difference between the two, and describe in about 200 characters what happened to cell division as a result of the treatment with reagent C.
(5) What kind of chemical do you think was used as reagent C? Give the name of one reagent.

Method of observing chromosome preparations
1. Hold the slide you have made up against the light and check how the cells have spread. A properly made chromosome preparation looks like Figures 5 and 6. If the cells have not spread as in the figures, make the preparation again.
2. Place the preparation on the stage of the light microscope, look over the whole of it with the 10× objective lens, and decide roughly on the area to observe. For example, in Figure 7 the area in the rectangular frame is the area to observe.
3. Under the 40× objective lens, count the number of cells in each phase of cell division. To count efficiently, after deciding on the first observation point, first count the total number of cells in the field of view with the counter and write it in the field-1 column of the item "Total number of cells in one field of view" on the observation record sheet. Next, count the number of cells in each of the phases (b–e of Figure 4) seen in this field of view. The number of cells in phase a of Figure 4 is calculated as the "Total number of cells in one field of view" minus the sum of the numbers of cells in phases b–e.
4. When the count for one field of view is finished, shift the stage horizontally in a straight line, as shown in Figure 8, so as not to overlap the field just seen, and move to the next field of view. Repeat this and count the cells.
5. As a guide, the number of cells to observe is a total of 600 or more. If you think the number of cells observed is not enough, shift vertically so that the fields of view do not overlap and make additional counts.
Note) Counting is easy when about 100–200 cells are seen in one field of view; if there are more than this, counting the cells becomes difficult.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-2-fig3.png

Figure 5 (left). Field of view under the 40× objective lens. Figure 6 (right). An example of an enlarged image of a preparation that has been made.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-2-fig4.png

Figure 7. Spread of the cells on a slide that has been made, and the area to observe

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 散らした細胞の観察可能領域 = area of spread cells that can be observed; 観察しようとする領域 = area to be observed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-2-fig5.png

Figure 8. Method of counting the cells. Each ○ shows one field of view; move in a fixed direction so that the fields of view do not overlap, and count.

Figure labels (Japanese → English): ○は1観察視野 = ○ is one field of view.

Supplement: how to make chromosome preparations

How to make the chromosome preparations is shown repeatedly on the displays in the exam room, so refer to them if you are not sure of an operation.

1. The seedlings are stained by the Feulgen method. This time, already stained seedlings are provided in the two tube vials A and B. Tube vial A has already been transferred to a Petri dish. Transfer tube vial B to a Petri dish in the same way and write "B" on the lid of the Petri dish with the marker.
2. Place a new filter paper on the bench. On it, place a slide glass wiped well with a Kimwipe.
3. Write the symbol of the tube vial (A or B) at the upper left of the slide glass with the marker.
4. Place one stained seedling on the slide glass. Using the scalpel, cut off only the meristem coloured reddish purple. As a guide, cut off about 1 mm. Take care, because if you take too much the cells overlap one another and are hard to observe. Remove the parts other than the meristem. If excess liquid remains, absorb it with filter paper.
5. Drop one drop of aceto-orcein on the cut meristem and put on a cover glass. With more than one drop it becomes difficult to spread the cells, and with too little the cells spread poorly.
6. Place a filter paper on one corner of the cover glass and, while lightly holding that corner down through the filter paper with your index finger, lightly tap the cut meristem several times through the cover glass with the tip of the pointed disposable chopstick. Take care at this time that the cover glass does not slip. Spread the cells so that the meristem becomes a single layer, but not so much that the cells are broken.
7. Sandwich the whole preparation in a filter paper folded in two, lightly stroke around the cover glass through the filter paper and absorb the excess aceto-orcein. After that, press the top of the specimen hard and vertically with the tip of your thumb to squash it.
8. Seal around the cover glass with nail varnish. If you apply too much nail varnish it touches the objective lens and soils it, so use a suitable amount.
9. Observe the preparation with the light microscope.
problems.problem_orig:
実験1．実生をつかった細胞分裂の観察（続き）

【問2】Aの実生とBの実生について，図3に示す1，2，3の領域の細胞のプレパラートを作製し，以下の(1)～(5)に答えよ。なおプレパラートは，11ページの補足：染色体標本の作り方の説明に従って作製し，観察すること。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-2-fig1.png

図3．実生と細胞分裂の観察部位。Aは発芽4日後，直ちに固定したもの。Bは発芽4日後，試薬Cで3時間処理した後に固定したもの。領域1と領域3：根の頂端分裂組織の各1 mm程度，領域2：実生中央部の1 mm程度。

(1) 図4の細胞分裂の各時期の名称を記入せよ。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-3-2-fig2.png

図4．細胞分裂周期の各時期（a–e）の顕微鏡写真。キクタニギクの根の頂端分裂組織細胞を酢酸オルセインで染色したもの。

(2) クレピス標本の図3の領域1，2，3の中で染色体数が最も数えやすい領域はどれか。解答欄に領域の番号を記せ。また，クレピスの染色体数を数えて解答欄に記入せよ。
(3) 図3に示す領域1と領域3について，プレパラートを観察し，視野ごとに観察された各細胞分裂時期の細胞数を，解答用紙の最後につけてある観察記録用紙に記入し，観察結果を集計せよ。また，解答用紙に観察細胞数と各時期の頻度および細胞分裂の各時期に要する推定時間を記入せよ。クレピスでは1細胞周期の時間が10.4時間である。次に，各時期の頻度を整理し，分裂期の頻度（％）を解答欄に記入せよ。染色体標本の作り方と細胞の観察は，11ページの補足：染色体標本の作り方と9ページの染色体標本の観察方法を参考にせよ。時期の判定は図4のキクタニギクの例を参考にすること。
(4) (3)で観察した領域1と領域3の比較から，両者の違いを記し，試薬Cの処理により細胞分裂に何が起こったかを200字程度で述べよ。
(5) 試薬Cはどのような薬品を使ったと考えられるか。試薬の名称を一つ挙げよ。

染色体標本の観察方法
1．作製したスライドを明るい方向に透かしてみて，細胞の広がり具合を確かめます。適切に作製された染色体標本は図5と図6のように見えます。細胞の広がり具合が図のようになっていない場合はプレパラートを作り直すこと。
2．生物顕微鏡のステージにプレパラートをおき，10倍の対物レンズでひととおり全体を見わたして，観察領域の見当をつけます。例えば，図7では四角枠領域が観察領域となります。
3．40倍の対物レンズ下で，細胞分裂の各時期の細胞数を計測します。手際よく計測するためには最初の観察ポイントを決めた後，まず視野内の細胞数の総数をカウンターで計測し，観察記録用紙の「1視野細胞総数」の項目の視野1の欄に記入します。次にこの視野内で見られる細胞のそれぞれの時期（図4のb～e）について細胞数を数えます。図4のaの時期の細胞数は「1視野細胞総数」からb～eの時期の細胞数の総和を差し引いた値として計算します。
4．1観察視野について計測が終わると，今見た視野と重ならないように，図8に示すように横方向に1直線にステージをずらし，次の観察視野まで移動します。これを繰り返して，細胞の計測を行います。
5．観察する細胞の数の目安は，細胞の総数が600以上です。観察細胞数が足りないと考えられる場合，視野が重ならないように縦方向にずらして追加計測を行うこと。
注）1観察視野に100～200細胞が見えるくらいがカウントしやすく，それよりも多い場合は細胞数を数えることが困難になります。

図5．40倍対物レンズ下の視野　図6．作製された標本の拡大像の一例

図7．作製したスライドの細胞の広がり具合と観察領域

図8．細胞数の計測方法。○は1観察視野を示しており，視野が重ならないように一定方向に移動し計測を行う。

補足：染色体標本の作り方

染色体標本の作り方は試験室内のディスプレイに繰り返し映し出されていますので，操作がわからないときは参考にしてください。

1．実生をフォイルゲン染色します。今回，すでに染色された実生が，2本の管ビンAおよびBに用意されています。管ビンAはすでにシャーレに移されています。同様に管ビンBもシャーレに移し，マジックでシャーレのふたに「B」と記入します。
2．実験台の上に新しいろ紙を置きます。その上に，キムワイプでよく拭いたスライドガラスを置きます。
3．スライドガラスの左上に，管ビンの記号（AまたはB）をマジックで記入する。
4．染色した実生をスライドガラス上に1本置きます。メスを用いて，赤紫色に発色した分裂組織だけを切り取ります。切り取る目安としては1 mm程度になります。多くとりすぎると細胞同士が重なって観察しにくくなるので注意すること。分裂組織以外の部位は取り除くこと。余分な液が残っている場合は，ろ紙で吸い取ること。
5．切り取った分裂組織に酢酸オルセインを1滴滴下し，カバーガラスをかけます。1滴より多くなると細胞を散らすのが難しくなり，少なすぎると細胞が散りにくくなります。
6．カバーガラスのひと隅にろ紙をのせ，そのひと隅をろ紙の上から人差し指で，軽く押さえたまま，先のとがった割りばしの先で切り出した分裂組織をカバーガラスの上から数回繰り返し軽くたたきます。このとき，カバーガラスがずれないように注意すること。また，分裂組織が1層になり，かつ細胞が壊れない程度に細胞を散らすこと。
7．二つ折りにしたろ紙でプレパラート全体を挟み，カバーガラスの周辺をろ紙の上から軽くなぞり，余分の酢酸オルセインを吸い取ります。その後で標本上部を親指の先で垂直に強く押しつぶします。
8．カバーガラスの周囲をマニキュアで封じます。マニキュアをつけすぎると対物レンズに触れて，レンズを汚すので，適当な量にすること。
9．プレパラートを生物顕微鏡で観察します。

problems.title: Experiment 2 (flowers), Question 4
problems.problem:
Experiment 2. The structure of angiosperm flowers

[Introduction]
Land plants have evolved complex reproductive organs so that gametes meet one another efficiently and fertilisation takes place reliably. In angiosperms, a flower is made up of four kinds of elements gathered in concentric circles: from the outside inwards, sepals, petals, stamens and pistils. When petals and sepals cannot be distinguished by shape or colour, the two together are called the perianth. However, not all flowers have this kind of structure; in particular, petals and tepals evolved to attract pollinators such as insects, and are vestigial in wind-pollinated flowers. All these elements are considered to be homologous to leaves (modified leaves, floral leaves). The evidence given for this is the existence of mutants in which petals have changed into leaves, of double flowers in which stamens have changed into petals, and so on.
In this problem you will observe the flowers of Easter lily (テッポウユリ), snapdragon (キンギョソウ) and Japanese dock (ギシギシ), which differ greatly in appearance, and consider the factors that bring about the differences in flower structure.

[Question 4] From the statements below, choose from ア–キ the correct description of the flower structure of (1) Easter lily, (2) snapdragon and (3) Japanese dock, and answer with the symbols.

ア. The structure that looks like 6 sepals consists of 3 outer tepals and 3 inner tepals. There are bisexual flowers with both stamens and pistils and female flowers with only pistils.
イ. There are no sepals; the structure that looks like 6 petals can be distinguished into 3 outer tepals and 3 inner tepals.
ウ. There is one pistil in the centre, surrounded by stamens, and on the outside two scales enclose them.
エ. It has a calyx divided into 4 sepals, a corolla divided into 4 petals, 6 stamens and one pistil whose interior is divided into 3 locules.
オ. It has a calyx divided into 5 sepals, a corolla divided into 5 petals, 4 stamens and one pistil whose interior is divided into 2 locules.
カ. The petals are reduced and remain as small lodicules near the base of the ovary; it has 3–6 stamens and one pistil.
キ. There are no sepals; the structure that looks like 8 petals can be distinguished into 4 outer tepals and 4 inner tepals. There are bisexual flowers with both stamens and pistils and male flowers with only stamens.
problems.problem_orig:
実験2．被子植物の花のつくり

【はじめに】
陸上植物は，配偶子同士が効率よく出会い，確実に受精をするために複雑な生殖器官を進化させました。被子植物では，外側から順に，がく，花弁（花びら），雄ずい（雄しべ），雌ずい（雌しべ）の4つの要素が同心円状に集まって花が構成されています。また，形や色で花弁とがくが区別できない場合，両者を合わせて花被とよびます。ただし，すべての花がこのような構造を持つわけではなく，とくに花弁や花被片は昆虫などの花粉媒介者を誘うために進化したものであり，風媒花では痕跡的です。これらの要素はいずれも葉に相同なもの（葉が変化したもの，花葉）と考えられています。この根拠として花びらが葉に変化した突然変異体や，雄ずいが花びらに変化した八重咲きの花などの存在があげられます。
この問題では，みかけの大きく異なる，テッポウユリ，キンギョソウ，ギシギシの花を観察し，花の構造の違いをもたらしている要因について考えます。

【問4】以下の文章から，（1）テッポウユリ，（2）キンギョソウ，（3）ギシギシの花の構造の説明としてア～キの中から正しいものを選び，記号で答えよ。

ア．6枚のがく片のようにみえる構造は，外花被片3枚，内花被片3枚からなる。雄ずいと雌ずいの両方をもつ両性花と雌ずいしかない雌花がある。
イ．がく片がなく，6枚の花弁のようにみえる構造は，外花被片3枚，内花被片3枚に区別できる。
ウ．中心に1本の雌ずいがあり，その周囲を雄ずいが囲み，その外側を2枚の鱗片が包んでいる。
エ．4枚に分かれたがく片，4枚に分かれた花弁，6本の雄ずい，内部が3室に分かれた1本の雌ずいをもつ。
オ．5枚に分かれたがく片，5枚に分かれた花弁，4本の雄ずい，内部が2室に分かれた1本の雌ずいをもつ。
カ．花弁は退化して小さな鱗皮として子房の基部付近に残り，3–6本の雄ずい，1本の雌ずいをもつ。
キ．がく片がなく，8枚の花弁のようにみえる構造は，外花被片4枚，内花被片4枚に区別できる。雄ずいと雌ずいの両方をもつ両性花と雄ずいしかない雄花がある。

problems.title: Experiment 2 (flowers), Question 7
problems.problem:
Experiment 2. The structure of angiosperm flowers (continued)

[Question 7] In experiments using thale cress (シロイヌナズナ), mutants have been obtained in which the arrangement and composition of the floral leaves (sepal – petal – stamen – pistil) are changed. Many of these mutants can be divided broadly into 3 groups by the features of the composition of their floral leaves.

Group 1: consisting only of stamens and pistils
Group 2: consisting only of sepals and pistils
Group 3: consisting only of sepals and petals

Of the statements ア–ウ below, which consider the morphological features of these mutants and the cause of the 3 groups, choose the most appropriate one and answer with its symbol.

ア. The mutants tend to arise by two adjacent kinds of floral leaves changing at the same time. From this it is thought that these mutations arose through loss of function of genes expressed across two adjacent kinds of floral leaves.
イ. The mutants tend to arise by the 4 kinds of floral leaves changing independently. From this it is thought that these mutations arose through separate loss of function of the genes involved in forming each organ.
ウ. The mutants tend to arise by 3 kinds of floral leaves changing at the same time. From this it is thought that the 4 kinds of floral leaves are formed corresponding to 3 regions formed by combinations of the expression of 3 kinds of genes.
problems.problem_orig:
実験2．被子植物の花のつくり（続き）

【問7】シロイヌナズナを用いた実験で，花葉（がく－花弁－雄ずい－雌ずい）の配置や構成が変化した突然変異体が得られています。これらの変異体の多くは，花葉の構成の特徴から大きく3つのグループに分けることができます。

グループ1：雄ずい，雌ずい　のみからなる
グループ2：がく，雌ずい　のみからなる
グループ3：がく，花弁　のみからなる

これらの変異体の形態的特徴と，3つのグループが生じる原因について考察した以下の文章のア～ウのうち，最も適切なものを選び記号で答えよ。

ア．変異体は，隣り合った2種類の花葉が同時に変化して生じる傾向がある。このことから隣り合う2種類の花葉にまたがって発現する遺伝子が機能を失うことによって，これらの変異が生じたと考えられる。
イ．変異体は，4種類の花葉が独立に変化して生じる傾向がある。このことから，それぞれの器官の形成に関与する遺伝子が別個に機能を失うことによって，これらの変異が生じたと考えられる。
ウ．変異体は，3種類の花葉が同時に変化して生じる傾向がある。このことから，4種類の花葉は3種類の遺伝子の発現の組み合わせで形成される3つの領域に対応して形成されていると考えられる。

problems.title: Experiment 2 (flowers), Question 8
problems.problem:
Experiment 2. The structure of angiosperm flowers (continued)

[Question 8] From studies of mutants such as those shown in [Question 7] above, a model that explains well the morphogenesis of angiosperm flowers has been proposed, called the ABC model. The ABC model explains that combinations of the expression of 3 genes (transcription factors) control the development of each organ of the flower. Choose from ア–ウ below the appropriate statement explaining the morphogenesis of the thale cress (シロイヌナズナ) flower using the ABC model, and answer with its symbol.

ア. In the region where only gene A is expressed "sepals" differentiate, in the region where genes A and B are expressed "petals", in the region where genes B and C are expressed "stamens", and in the region where only gene C is expressed "pistils".
イ. In the region where none of genes A, B and C is expressed "sepals" differentiate, in the region where gene A is expressed "petals", in the region where gene B is expressed "stamens", and in the region where only gene C is expressed "pistils".
ウ. In the region where only gene A is expressed "sepals" differentiate, in the region where genes A and B are expressed "petals", in the region where genes B and C are expressed "stamens", and in the region where genes A and C are expressed "pistils".
problems.problem_orig:
実験2．被子植物の花のつくり（続き）

【問8】上記の【問7】で示したような突然変異体の研究から，被子植物の花の形態形成をうまく説明できるモデルが提案されており，ABCモデルとよばれています。ABCモデルでは，3つの遺伝子（転写因子）の発現の組み合わせが，花の各器官の発生を制御していると説明しています。ABCモデルを用いてシロイヌナズナの花の形態形成を説明した文章として適切なものを以下のア～ウの中から選び記号で答えよ。

ア．遺伝子Aのみが発現する領域は「がく」，遺伝子AとBが発現する領域は「花弁」，遺伝子BとCが発現する領域は「雄ずい」，遺伝子Cのみが発現する領域は「雌ずい」が分化する。
イ．遺伝子A，B，Cがいずれも発現しない領域では「がく」，遺伝子Aが発現する領域では「花弁」，遺伝子Bが発現する領域では「雄ずい」，遺伝子Cのみが発現する領域では「雌ずい」が分化する。
ウ．遺伝子Aのみが発現する領域は「がく」，遺伝子AとBが発現する領域は「花弁」，遺伝子BとCが発現する領域は「雄ずい」，遺伝子AとCが発現する領域は「雌ずい」が分化する。

【問9】突然変異体の研究から考えられたABCモデルは，進化の過程で生じた多様な花の形も説明することができると考えられています。（1）テッポウユリ，（2）キンギョソウ，（3）ギシギシの花の形態についてA，B，Cの3つの遺伝子の発現様式を用いて説明した場合，花葉と遺伝子発現のパターンの関係を模式的に示した図として適切なものを図9のア～コの中から選び記号で答えよ。両性花，雌花，雄花がある種では両性花の遺伝子発現のパターンを選びなさい。なお，図中の記号と花葉の名称は，3つの異なる遺伝子の発現とその遺伝子が発現している部位を示します。例えば，図9のアでは穎で遺伝子Aのみ，鱗皮で遺伝子AとBの両方，雄ずいで遺伝子BとCの両方，雌ずいで遺伝子Cのみが発現していることを示します。

problems.title: Experiment 1 (crucian carp), Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam (animals): question booklet

At the beginning of the question booklet there is an explanation of how to use the stereomicroscope. Its content is the same as in the plant exam.

During the experiments always wear laboratory gloves, and take care that the experimental solutions do not come into contact with your eyes, mouth, skin, etc.

This exam is divided into Experiment 1 and Experiment 2. Experiment 1 ends 1 hour after the start of the exam, and the materials, reagents and apparatus are then exchanged.

Manual for using the stereomicroscope

1. Do not place the sample directly on the stage.
2. Adjust the height of the chair so that you can observe with your back straight.
3. Adjust the eye width and the dioptre of the eyepieces. Dioptre-adjustment rings are fitted on both eyepieces, so set both to the 0 position. Next, looking with your right eye, move the stage up and down to focus on the specimen to be observed. Leaving the stage as it is, look with your left eye and turn the dioptre-adjustment ring of the left eyepiece to focus. When you observe wearing glasses, fold back the rubber of the eye shades to shorten them.
4. When observing, use the incident illumination (left adjustment knob) and the transmitted illumination (right adjustment knob) as suits the observation. Adjust the angle of the incident illumination so that the sample is well lit.
5. To observe at a different magnification, turn the zoom handle to adjust it.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-1-fig1.png

Names of the parts of the stereomicroscope

Figure labels (Japanese → English): アイシェード = eye shade; 視度調整環 = dioptre-adjustment ring; ズームハンドル = zoom handle; 焦準ハンドル = focusing handle; 落射照明明るさ調整つまみ = incident-illumination brightness knob; 透過照明明るさ調整つまみ = transmitted-illumination brightness knob; 落射LED照明装置 角度調整可能です = incident LED illuminator, angle adjustable; ステージ = stage; メインスイッチ = main switch; I：電源ON状態 = I: power ON; O：電源OFF状態 = O: power OFF.

Experiment 1. Dissection and molecular phylogeny of the crucian carp

[Materials needed for the experiment]
In this experiment the materials, instruments and apparatus shown below are used.

1. Crucian carp (フナ) — 1
2. Stereomicroscope — 1
3. Dissecting instruments — 1 set: scissors, scalpel, mounted needle, fine-tipped forceps, round-tipped forceps (1 each)
4. Calculator — 1
5. Counter — 1
6. Vernier calipers (see the photograph on the next page) — 1
7. Laboratory gloves — 2 pairs
8. 90 mm Petri dish (containing ethanol) — 1
9. Laboratory tissues (Kimwipes) — 1 box
10. Paper towels — 1 bundle
*15 ml tubes — 24
*Stopwatch — 1
*Marker pen — 1
*Coloured drawing paper — 1 sheet
(Note) Items marked * are used in Experiment 2.

[Introduction]
The feeding organs and digestive organs of animals have shapes suited to their feeding habits (the kinds of things they eat, etc.). In this experiment you will dissect a crucian carp and consider what kind of feeding habits it has. Also, the goldfish is an artificial breed produced from the crucian carp, but there has so far been much debate about from what kind of crucian carp the goldfish was produced. In this experiment you will read the results of a recent phylogenetic analysis using molecular (DNA) information and consider the origin of the goldfish.

[Question 1] For the crucian carp provided, measure the body length by the procedure shown in Figure 1 and write the measured value in the table on the answer sheet (write it in millimetres to one decimal place).

Figure 1. Measuring the body length
The body length is measured with the vernier calipers, as in the figures below, from the tip of the mouth to the centre of the crease that forms slightly in front of the caudal fin when the caudal fin is bent to left and right (the posterior end of the hypural) (figure below, left; note that this is not the position where the scales end and the caudal fin begins). If the caudal fin cannot be bent, measure taking the point between the third and second scales counted from the caudal fin (figure below, right) as the posterior end of the hypural.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-1-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 動かない場合は、ここで測定 = if it does not move, measure here.
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験（動物）問題冊子

問題冊子の最初に，実体顕微鏡の使い方の説明があります。内容は植物の試験と同じです。

実験中はかならず実験用手袋を着用し，実験液が眼，口，皮膚などに触れないよう注意すること。

この試験は実験1と実験2に分かれています。実験1は試験開始後1時間で終了し，材料と試薬，器具類を入れ替えます。

実体顕微鏡使用マニュアル

1．ステージに直接試料をのせないこと。
2．背筋を伸ばして観察できるようにイスの高さを調節すること。
3．接眼レンズの眼幅，視度調整をすること。視度調整環は接眼レンズの双方についているので双方とも0の位置に合わせる。次に，右目で観察する標本にステージを上下させてピントを合わせる。ステージをそのままの状態にして，左目でのぞき，左側の接眼レンズの視度調整環を回してピントを合わせる。眼鏡をかけて検鏡するときは，アイシェードのゴムを折り返して短くすること。
4．観察のときは，落射照明（左側の調整つまみ）と透過照明（右側の調整つまみ）を観察に応じて使い分けること。落射照明は角度を調整して，試料に光が十分当たるようにすること。
5．倍率を変えて観察する場合には，ズームハンドルを回して調節する。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-1-fig1.png

実体顕微鏡各部名称

実験1．フナの解剖と分子系統

【実験に必要なもの】
この実験では，下に示した材料，器具，装置を用います。

1．フナ　1匹
2．実体顕微鏡　1台
3．解剖道具　1式：ハサミ，メス，柄付針，先細ピンセット，先丸ピンセット（各1本）
4．電卓　1台
5．カウンター　1台
6．ノギス（次ページの写真参照）　1本
7．実験用手袋　2組
8．90 mm シャーレ（エタノールが入っている）　1枚
9．実験用ティッシュ（キムワイプ）　1箱
10．ペーパータオル　1束
*15 ml チューブ　24本
*ストップウォッチ　1台
*マジックペン　1本
*色画用紙　1枚
(注) *は実験2で使用します。

【はじめに】
動物の摂食器官や消化器官は，食性（食べているものの種類など）に適した形をもっています。本実験ではフナを解剖し，どのような食性を持っているかを考察します。また，金魚はフナから作り出された人工品種ですが，金魚がどのようなフナから作り出されたのかという点には，これまでに多くの議論がありました。この実験では，最近行われた分子（DNA）情報を使った系統解析の結果を読み取り，金魚の起源について考察します。

【問1】与えられたフナについて，図1に示した手順で体長を測定し，測定値を解答用紙の表に記入せよ（ミリメートルの単位で小数点第一位まで記入）。

図1．体長の測定
体長は，下図のように，口の先から尾鰭のやや前方の尾鰭を左右に曲げた時にできる皺の中心（下尾骨後端）までをノギスを使って測定します（下図左，鱗が途切れて尾鰭になる位置ではないことに注意）。尾鰭が折り曲げられない場合は、尾鰭から数えて3つめと2つめの鱗の間（下図右）を下尾骨後端として測定して下さい。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-1-fig2.png

problems.title: Experiment 1 (crucian carp), Question 2
problems.problem:
Experiment 1. Dissection and molecular phylogeny of the crucian carp (continued)

[Question 2] Dissect the crucian carp following the procedure shown in Figures 2 and 3. Then answer (1)–(2) below. Do not damage or throw away the dissected crucian carp; leave it laid out on the tray. After measuring, keep the intestine and the gill rakers immersed in the ethanol in the 90 mm Petri dish.

(1) Measure the length of the intestine. Also find the ratio of the length of the intestine to the body length (relative gut length = intestine length ÷ body length). Write each value in the answer box.
(2) Take out the first gill arch, count the number of folds (gill rakers) on the front part of the gill arch, and write the number in the answer box. Use the stereomicroscope if necessary. In that case, place the gill rakers on the lid of the Petri dish and observe them.

Figure 2. Dissection procedure and measurement of the intestine

1. Longitudinal incision of the abdomen: insert the scissors at the anus as in figure ① below, and cut open in the direction shown by the arrow in figure ② below, up to below the pectoral fin. The crucian carp provided has already been cut open a little from the anus.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): ①肛門に鋏の先端を入れ(切れ目を入れてある), ②矢印の方向に，胸鰭の下まで切開する。 = ① insert the tip of the scissors into the anus (a cut has been made), ② cut open in the direction of the arrow up to below the pectoral fin.

2. Incision of the lateral body wall of the abdomen: using the scissors, cut the body wall open from the anus in the direction of arrow ③.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig2.png

3. Removal of the abdominal body wall: cut the body wall with the scissors from the base of the pectoral fin in the direction of arrow ④. Then lift the body wall and cut it away without damaging the internal organs (use the scalpel if necessary).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig3.png

4. Removal of the gonad: if the gonad is developed, remove it to expose the intestine.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig4.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 切除した体壁 = body wall that has been cut away; 生殖巣（卵巣） = gonad (ovary); 生殖巣を取り除き腸を露出させる = remove the gonad and expose the intestine.

5. Measurement of the intestine length: the crucian carp and the common carp are called "stomachless fish" and do not have an organ that can clearly be called a stomach. Therefore, the whole digestive tract from the oesophagus to the anus is regarded as the intestine, and its length is measured. The intestine is covered by the mesentery, so remove it, stretch out the intestine as in the figures and measure it. If it breaks along the way, measure the length of each piece of the digestive tract and add them up.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig5.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig6.png

The intestinal tube is folded, so remove the mesentery with the forceps or the mounted needle and stretch out the intestine. Measure from the base of the oesophagus. Measure the total length of the intestine.

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 腸間膜を取り除き，折り畳まれている腸管を延ばす。 = remove the mesentery and stretch out the folded intestinal tube; 食道まで延ばす。 = stretch it out as far as the oesophagus.

Figure 3. Removing the gill arch and observing the gill rakers
The gill arches are arranged on the left and right. The photographs below show the mouth cavity and gill arches of the Japanese sea bass (スズキ), a piscivorous marine fish. Remove only one of the gill arches that are foremost seen from the mouth and outermost seen from the side (the first gill arch). As in the photograph below (centre), you may also take out all the gill arches of one side and then cut off only the first gill arch. If you damage it while taking it out, remove the gill arch of the other side. Count the number of gill rakers of the first gill arch you have removed. Use the stereomicroscope if necessary. In that case, turn the lid of the Petri dish upside down, place the gill arch on it and observe it.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig7.png

Left: mouth cavity and first gill arches of the Japanese sea bass. Centre: gill arches (left side); the arrows are the gill rakers of the first gill arch. Right: the first gill arch; count the number of gill rakers in this state (in this case 24).

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 第1鰓弓 = first gill arch; 鰓弓（左） = gill arches (left); 第1鰓弓の鰓耙(24本) = gill rakers of the first gill arch (24); 第1鰓弓（左） = first gill arch (left).

Procedure for taking out the gill arch

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig8.png

① Cut open the operculum in the direction of the arrow. ② Cut open from the mouth in the direction of the arrow, up to the base of the gills.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig9.png

③ Cut the lower end of the gill arch. ④ Insert the scissors in the direction of the arrow and expose the upper part of the gill arch. ⑤ Cut the upper end of the gill arch. ⑥ Count the number of gill rakers of the first gill arch.
problems.problem_orig:
実験1．フナの解剖と分子系統（続き）

【問2】フナを図2，図3に示す手順に沿って解剖しなさい。その上で，以下の(1)～(2)に答えなさい。なお，解剖したフナは壊したり捨てたりせず，バット上に並べておくこと。計測後の腸と鰓耙は，90 mm シャーレの中のエタノールに浸けておくこと。

(1) 腸の長さを測定せよ。また，腸の長さと体長の比（腸長比＝腸長÷体長）を求めよ。それぞれの値を解答欄に記入せよ。
(2) 第1鰓弓を取り出し，鰓弓の前部にある襞（鰓耙）の本数を数え，本数を解答欄に記入せよ。必要に応じて，実体顕微鏡を用いなさい。この場合，鰓耙をシャーレの蓋の上にのせて観察せよ。

図2．解剖の手順と腸の測定

1．腹部の縦断切開：下図①のように肛門からハサミを入れ，下図②の矢印で示した方向に胸鰭の下まで切開します。なお配布したフナは，あらかじめ肛門から少し切開してあります。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig1.png

2．腹部体側壁の切開：ハサミを使って，肛門から矢印③の方向に体壁を切開します。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig2.png

3．腹部体壁の除去：胸鰭の付根から矢印④の方向に体壁を鋏で切開します。その後，体壁を持ち上げ，内臓を壊さないように体壁を切除します（必要があればメスを使います）。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig3.png

4．生殖巣の除去：生殖巣が発達している場合は，それを取り除いて腸を露出させます。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig4.png

5．腸長の測定：フナやコイは「無胃類」といわれ，明確に胃と呼べる器官を持っていません。このため，食道から肛門までの全ての消化管を腸とみなし，その長さを測定します。なお，腸は腸間膜に覆われているので，これを除き，図のように腸を引きのばして測定します。途中で切れた場合は各消化管断片の長さを測定し，足し合わせます。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig5.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig6.png

腸管は折り畳まれているので，ピンセットや柄付針で腸間膜を取り除き，腸を延ばす。食道の付根から測定する。腸の全長を測定する。

図3．鰓弓の摘出と鰓耙の観察
鰓弓は左右に並んでいます。下の写真は，魚食性の海水魚であるスズキの口腔と鰓弓です。口から見て一番前方，側面から見て一番外側の鰓弓（第1鰓弓）を片方だけ摘出します。下写真（中央）のように，片側の鰓弓全てを取出してから，第1鰓弓だけを切除しても構いません。取り出す途中で壊してしまった際は，もう一方の鰓弓を摘出します。摘出した第1鰓弓の鰓耙数をかぞえます。必要に応じて実体顕微鏡を用いて下さい。この場合，シャーレのフタを裏返して鰓弓をのせて観察して下さい。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig7.png

スズキの口腔と第1鰓弓。鰓弓（左側）。矢印は第1鰓弓の鰓耙。第1鰓弓。この状態で鰓耙数を数える（この場合24本）。

鰓弓取り出しの手順

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig8.png

①鰓蓋を矢印の方向に切開する。②口から矢印の方向に向かって，鰓の根元まで切開する。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-2-fig9.png

③鰓弓の下部末端を切断する ④矢印の向きにハサミを入れ,鰓弓上部を露出させる ⑤鰓弓の上部末端を切断する。 ⑥第1鰓弓の鰓耙数を測定する。

problems.title: Experiment 1 (crucian carp), Question 3
problems.problem:
Experiment 1. Dissection and molecular phylogeny of the crucian carp (continued)

[Question 3] The shape of the gill rakers (their length and density) and the length of the intestine are thought to be related to the feeding habits of a fish. Here, suppose that the numbers of gill rakers and the relative gut lengths of the Japanese sea bass (スズキ), the goldfish and the Japanese white crucian carp (ゲンゴロウブナ) lie in the ranges of the table below.

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|} \hline & \text{Number of gill rakers} & \text{Relative gut length} \\ \hline \text{Japanese sea bass} & 24 \sim 30 & 1.0 \sim 2.0 \\ \hline \text{Goldfish} & 30 \sim 56 & 2.0 \sim 4.3 \\ \hline \text{Japanese white crucian carp} & 56 \sim 128 & 3.4 \sim 7.2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

From a comparison of the numbers of gill rakers and the relative gut lengths, consider what kind of feeding habits each of the three kinds of fish in the table has. In particular, for the gill rakers, refer to the function inferred from their position and structure. Also, estimate the feeding habits of the crucian carp you observed on the basis of your measured values.
(Write about 300 characters inside the frame on the answer sheet. If the answer is accurate, fewer characters are acceptable.)
problems.problem_orig:
実験1．フナの解剖と分子系統（続き）

【問3】鰓耙の形状（長さや密度）と腸の長さは，魚の食性と関係があると考えられています。ここで，スズキと金魚，ゲンゴロウブナの鰓耙数と腸長比が，以下の表の範囲であるとします。

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|} \hline & \text{鰓耙数（本）} & \text{腸長比} \\ \hline \text{スズキ} & 24 \sim 30 & 1.0 \sim 2.0 \\ \hline \text{金魚} & 30 \sim 56 & 2.0 \sim 4.3 \\ \hline \text{ゲンゴロウブナ} & 56 \sim 128 & 3.4 \sim 7.2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

鰓耙数と腸長比の比較から，表の3種類の魚がそれぞれどのような食性を持っているか考察せよ。とくに，鰓耙については，位置と構造から推察される機能に言及せよ。また，あなたが観察したフナの食性を計測値にもとづいて推定せよ。
（解答用紙の枠内に300字程度で記述して下さい。的確な解答であれば，文字数は少なくてもよい）。

problems.title: Experiment 1 (crucian carp), Question 4
problems.problem:
Experiment 1. Dissection and molecular phylogeny of the crucian carp (continued)

[Question 4] Recently, in order to clarify the origin of the goldfish, a phylogenetic analysis based on the base sequences of mitochondrial DNA was carried out (Komiyama et al., 2009, Gene 430: 5-11). The phylogenetic tree obtained in this analysis is shown in Figure 4 below. The text enclosed in a box on the next page explains the results. Referring to the figure and the explanation, answer (1)–(3) below.
If you do not know how to read a phylogenetic tree, read "Supplement: how to read a molecular phylogenetic tree — an example from the chordates" (pages 10–11), which comes after this question, before answering [Question 4]. If you know how to read a phylogenetic tree, you do not need to read the supplement.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-4-fig1.png

Figure 4. Phylogenetic relationships of the crucian carps based on the base sequences of the control region of mitochondrial DNA

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 0.01（置換／塩基座位） = 0.01 (substitutions/site); Komiyama et al. (2009) の図2を問題用に改変した。枝の末端は、コイ・フナ・金魚の各個体を示す。 = Figure 2 of Komiyama et al. (2009), modified for this question. The tips of the branches show individual common carp, crucian carp and goldfish.

In this study, three kinds of Japanese crucian carp shown as I–VI in the figure (golden crucian carp (キンブナ), silver crucian carp (ギンブナ) and Japanese white crucian carp (ゲンゴロウブナ)), one kind of Chinese crucian carp (gibel carp (ギベリオブナ)), the goldfish and the common carp (コイ) were used as material. Of these, the common carp is the outgroup (a control group for deciding the root of the phylogenetic tree) and is shown as the group that branched off earliest on the tree. The tree was constructed from 740 base sites of the control region (D-loop region) of mitochondrial DNA. The tree showed the results a)–e) below.
a) The Japanese crucian carps were not a monophyletic group but were divided into two main lineages. One of them was closely related to the group containing the Chinese gibel carp.
b) Among the crucian carps used as material, the first to branch off was the Japanese white crucian carp from Japan.
c) The Japanese crucian carps other than the Japanese white crucian carp are lineages of the golden crucian carp and the silver crucian carp, and these formed a monophyletic group.
d) The red crucian carp (ヒブナ) is often said to be the origin of the goldfish. However, the red crucian carp used here was not closely related to the goldfish but was instead included in the group of the golden crucian carp.
e) The goldfish has various breeds whose external morphology differs greatly (Shubunkin, Demekin, Ranchu, etc.). These breeds are also included in this analysis, but the changes in the base sequence of mitochondrial DNA between the breeds and in the goldfish as a whole were very slight compared with the crucian carps and the common carp, which change little morphologically.

(1) The red crucian carp in the explanation is located at one of ☆1–☆6 in the phylogenetic tree. Which position is the most appropriate? Write it in the answer box.
(2) To which of the groups gibel carp, golden crucian carp, silver crucian carp, goldfish, Japanese white crucian carp and common carp does each of I–VI in the phylogenetic tree correspond? Write them in the answer boxes.
(3) From the results of this molecular phylogenetic analysis, from which crucian carp appearing in the explanation is the goldfish most likely to have been produced? Write it in the answer box.

Supplement: how to read a molecular phylogenetic tree — an example from the chordates

By comparing the base-sequence data (DNA sequences) of homologous genes or non-coding regions between organisms, the phylogenetic relationships between the organisms can be estimated. The estimated phylogenetic relationships are shown in a diagram called a phylogenetic tree. Suppose that Figure 5 on the next page is the phylogenetic tree obtained when the phylogenetic relationships of the chordates are estimated from base sequences. This figure can be read as follows.

1. The order of the branchings of the tree shows the order in which the lineage of each animal separated from the other lineages. In this tree, among the vertebrates, the lineage leading to the zebrafish, a fish, separates first, and then the lineage of the lungfish branches off.

2. In this tree, of the bird, crocodile and turtle, the bird and the crocodile separate from the same node of the tree (node 7). The turtle separates from the node one step further out (node 6). A node of the tree shows the common ancestor of the animals located on the branches beyond it. That is, animals whose nodes are closer derive from a common ancestor that existed more recently and are shown to be phylogenetically more closely related. Therefore, in this figure the crocodile and the bird are more closely related than the crocodile and the turtle, both reptiles. A taxon in which all the organisms included derive from one ancestor, such as the tetrapods, the amniotes and the mammals, is called a monophyletic group. On the other hand, a taxon such as the reptiles, in which all the organisms belonging to it come to derive from one ancestor only when one lineage is excluded, is called a paraphyletic group (if the lineage of the birds is excluded, the reptiles are a monophyletic group).

3. The length of the horizontal branches of this tree reflects differences in base sequence. In this figure, the length of a horizontal branch is taken to be the number of base substitutions observed between the animals divided by the number of base sites used as data (1000 sites) (equal to the probability that a base substitution occurs per base site). The figure shows that, in the gene used as data, 50 base substitutions ($0.05\times1000$) occurred in the human lineage after it separated from the mouse, and 40 base substitutions ($0.04\times1000$) occurred in the mouse lineage after it separated from the human, so that 90 base substitutions are observed between the human and the mouse. In this figure the length of the vertical branches has no particular meaning.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2011-4-4-fig2.png

Figure 5. Molecular phylogenetic tree of the chordates

Figure labels (Japanese → English): ショウジョウバエ = fruit fly; ナメクジウオ = lancelet; ホヤ（カタユウレイボヤ） = sea squirt (vase tunicate); ゼブラフィッシュ = zebrafish; ハイギョ = lungfish; カエル = frog; トリ = bird; ワニ = crocodile; カメ = turtle; ヘビ = snake; トカゲ = lizard; ヒト = human; ネズミ = mouse; 魚類と四足動物の(最後の)共通祖先 = (last) common ancestor of fishes and tetrapods; 両生類と有羊膜類の共通祖先 = common ancestor of amphibians and amniotes; 爬虫類と鳥類の共通祖先 = common ancestor of reptiles and birds; 有羊膜類の共通祖先 = common ancestor of the amniotes; ヒトとネズミの共通祖先 = common ancestor of human and mouse; 魚類 = fishes; 両生類 = amphibians; 鳥類 = birds; 爬虫類 = reptiles; 哺乳類 = mammals; 有羊膜類 = amniotes; 四足動物 = tetrapods; 脊椎動物 = vertebrates; 頭索動物 = cephalochordates; 尾索動物 = urochordates; 脊索動物 = chordates; 無脊椎動物 = invertebrates; 塩基置換数/データの塩基座位数 = number of base substitutions / number of base sites in the data.

One hour after the start of the exam, Experiment 1 ends and the dissected crucian carp is collected (keep the intestine and the gill rakers immersed in the ethanol in the Petri dish). After that, the materials and reagents for Experiment 2 are handed out.
