problems.title: Part 3 (nervous system), Question 3
problems.problem:
Part 3: Observation of the silkworm nervous system

Question 3
In insects, the concentration of nervous function in the brain has not progressed as far as in us, and functions are distributed among the ganglia; partly for this reason, insects can stay alive even if the body is tied with a thread to block the exchange of body fluid. By carrying out ligation experiments using this property, it became clear that the moulting and metamorphosis of insects are under endocrine control by hormones. It is now known that ecdysteroid, synthesised and secreted by the prothoracic glands in the thorax, causes moulting, and that JH, synthesised and secreted by the corpora allata, has the role of determining the nature of the moult.
The silkworm, whose final larval instar is the 5th instar, normally starts making a cocoon at the end of the 5th instar, pupates and then emerges as an adult. During the larval period ecdysteroid is secreted in large amounts especially from just before a moult up to the moult, but the secretion of JH may stop once in the middle of the 5th instar, and this causes pupation (see the next page).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-3-8-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): ホルモン濃度 = hormone concentration; 脱皮 = moult; 蛹化 = pupation; 羽化 = emergence (eclosion); エクジステロイド = ecdysteroid; 3齢 = 3rd instar; 4齢 = 4th instar; 5齢 = 5th instar; （吐糸） = (spinning); 蛹 = pupa; 成虫 = adult; 前胸腺 = prothoracic gland; アラタ体 = corpora allata.

We therefore treated the corpora allata, or ligated silkworm larvae with thread to stop the circulation of the body fluid, as in 1–5 below. For the change expected as a result, choose the most suitable one, for 1 and 2 from イ–ニ and for 3, 4 and 5 from ホ–チ, and also answer briefly the reason why it turns out so.

1. Remove the corpora allata from a larva just after it has become a 4th instar (A).
2. Transplant the corpora allata of a 4th-instar larva into a larva just after it has become a 5th instar (B).
3. Ligate a larva just after it has become a 4th instar (A) between the head and the thorax (a).
4. Ligate a larva before spinning (C) between the head and the thorax (a).
5. Ligate a larva before spinning (C) behind the thorax (b).

イ. It becomes a 4th-instar larva.
ロ. It becomes a 5th-instar larva.
ハ. It becomes a 6th-instar larva.
ニ. It becomes a pupa.
ホ. Both the part in front of and the part behind the ligature remain larval.
ヘ. Only the part in front of the ligature becomes a pupa.
ト. Only the part behind the ligature becomes a pupa.
チ. Both the part in front of and the part behind the ligature become pupae.
problems.problem_orig:
第３部　カイコ神経系の観察

問３
昆虫では神経機能の脳への集中化が我々ほど進んでおらず各神経節に機能が分散されていることもあり、糸で体を縛って体液の交流を遮断しても生きていくことができます。この特性をもちいて結紮実験を行うことにより、昆虫の脱皮・変態現象がホルモンによる内分泌支配であることが明らかになりました。現在では、胸部にある前胸腺で合成され分泌されるエクジステロイドが脱皮を引き起こし、アラタ体で合成され分泌されるＪＨが脱皮の性質を決定する役割をもっていることがわかっています。
５齢幼虫が終齢であるカイコは、通常５齢幼虫の終わりに繭を作り始め蛹化しその後羽化します。幼虫期においてエクジステロイドは特に脱皮直前から脱皮時に多く分泌されていますが、ＪＨは５齢の中期で分泌が一度止まることがあり、これが蛹化を引き起こします（次ページ参照）。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-3-8-fig1.png

そこで以下の１-５のようにアラタ体を処置、またはカイコ幼虫を糸で結紮し体液の循環を止めてみました。その結果予想される変化について最も適切なものを、１、２はイ～ニから，３、４、５はホ～チから選択し、さらにそのようになる理由を簡単に答えなさい。

１．４齢になった直後の幼虫（A）からアラタ体を摘出・除去する。
２．５齢になった直後の幼虫（B）に４齢幼虫のアラタ体を移植する。
３．４齢になった直後の幼虫（A）の頭部と胸部の間（a）を結紮する。
４．吐糸前の幼虫（C）の頭部と胸部の間（a）を結紮する。
５．吐糸前の幼虫（C）の胸部の後ろ（b）を結紮する。

イ．４齢幼虫になる。
ロ．５齢幼虫になる。
ハ．６齢幼虫になる。
ニ．蛹になる。
ホ．結紮の前・後部とも幼虫のままになる。
へ．結紮の前部のみ蛹になる。
ト．結紮の後部のみ蛹になる。
チ．結紮の前・後部とも蛹になる。

problems.title: Experiment 1 (extraction and gelation of pectin), Question 1
problems.problem:
Plant physiology and biochemistry (time limit 120 minutes)

Introduction

As the ripening of a fruit proceeds, softening occurs in the pericarp because components that make up the cell wall, such as pectin, are broken down. Pectin binds to other cell-wall components such as cellulose and acts, so to speak, like a "cement" that joins plant cells together; it is abundant in the fruits of tomatoes and citrus. Pectin has a main chain of galacturonic acid, an acidic sugar, and has one carboxyl group per galacturonic acid. It is known that calcium ions entering between the carboxyl groups of neighbouring pectin main chains form cross-links between pectins, which then form a gel (Figure 1).
Besides binding to calcium, the molecular weight of pectin also has a large influence on its properties. High-molecular-weight pectin made of very long chains of galacturonic acid does not dissolve well in water, but low-molecular-weight pectin dissolves readily in water. Therefore, it is water-soluble pectin that is subject to control by the formation of calcium cross-links. However, if the reduction in molecular weight goes too far, cross-links can no longer be formed, and the ability to form a gel is lost. Looking at actual fruits, in unripe fruits pectin is in a very long form, so as it is, it does not dissolve in water and cannot gather to form a gel. In overripe fruits, on the other hand, the pectin itself has been broken down into pieces, so it too cannot form a gel.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-4-1-fig1.png

Figure 1. Cross-linked structure of pectin and calcium ions

Figure labels (Japanese → English): ガラクツロン酸残基 = galacturonic acid residue; ペクチン主鎖（ポリガラクツロン酸） = pectin main chain (polygalacturonic acid).

Samples and apparatus

Samples
Dried cell walls A and B (1 tube each, white label)
Tomato (green, red: 1 piece each, 10 g)

Apparatus
Micropipettes (P1000, P200, P20: 1 each)
Pipette tips (white, yellow: 1 box each)
Float (1), cap locks (2)
Cut-off pipette tips (1 bag of 2), cuvettes (6)
1.5 ml microtubes (1 plastic beaker full)
Mortars (2, containing quartz sand), pestles (2)
Wash bottle (1, containing distilled water), single-edged razor blade (1)
Plastic tray (1), 15 ml tubes (3)
Ice box (1, containing ice), centrifuge (1)
Stopwatch (1)
Plastic beaker (1, for scooping ice)

Reagents
0.25% ammonium oxalate (two 1.5 ml tubes, yellow label)
8.8% NaCl (one 15 ml tube)
100% ethanol (two 1.5 ml tubes, green label)
0.1 M NaOH solution (three 1.5 ml tubes, blue label)
Milk (calcium-fortified) (one 1.5 ml tube)
0.01% BTB (bromothymol blue) solution (one 1.5 ml tube)
BTB solution colour standards (blue, yellow: 1 each)
0.5% pectin solution (degree of methylation 85%) (one 20 ml container, red label)

The Kimwipes and Kimtowels on the desk may also be used freely.

Use the two plastic beakers for waste: one is for solids such as tips and razor blades, the other for liquids.

Notes

The problem has two parts, Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, so read through the experiments and all the questions before you start working. You do not need to answer the questions in order; carry out Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 at the same time. In particular, Experiment 2 has a question asking about devices for carrying out the experiment well, so work out your plan during waiting times in the experimental procedure.

Experiment 1. Extraction and gelation of pectin

In newly synthesised pectin, the carboxyl groups of the galacturonic acid residues are methylated. These methylated carboxyl groups are demethylated by the activity of pectin methylesterase (Figure 2), which makes them bind more easily to the calcium ions present in the cell wall. When calcium ions enter between pectins that carry demethylated carboxyl groups, calcium-mediated cross-links between the pectins are formed. These cross-links become very strong when both pectins have seven or more consecutive demethylated galacturonic acids. On the other hand, between pectins in which methyl groups partly remain, the binding is weak and loose, so it can be said that the construction of the cell wall is regulated by the degree of methylation. Gelation by cross-link formation is also observed when pectin and calcium are reacted in a test tube. In Experiment 1, you will extract pectin from tomato cell walls, react it with calcium, and consider the properties of the pectin from the state of the gel formed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-4-1-fig2.png

Figure 2. The reaction of pectin methylesterase

Figure labels (Japanese → English): メチル化ペクチン（100%） = methylated pectin (100%); ペクチンメチルエステラーゼ = pectin methylesterase; 脱メチル化ペクチン = demethylated pectin.

● Extraction of pectin
1. To 10 mg of each of the dried cell walls handed out (tomato A and tomato B), add 1 ml of 0.25% ammonium oxalate and heat in a water bath for 20 min. The TA will do the water-bath heating, so when you are ready, fit a cap lock to each tube, insert the tubes in the float and then raise your hand to let the TA know. Start Experiment 2 as well during the water-bath heating.
2. After cooling to about room temperature in ice, centrifuge using the centrifuge (12,000 rpm, 10 min, room temperature). Using a micropipette, collect the supernatant (pectin fraction). Take care at this point not to draw up anything other than the supernatant (precipitate or floating matter).
3. Using the collected pectin fraction and 100% ethanol, prepare in a 1.5 ml microtube a solution with a final ethanol concentration of 80%, and keep it in ice for 5 min.
4. Centrifuge at 12,000 rpm, 10 min, room temperature.
5. Discard the supernatant completely and check the remaining precipitate (transparent) for each sample. Dissolve the precipitate completely in 400 µl of distilled water to obtain pectin A and B. Do not take distilled water directly from the wash bottle: first put a suitable amount of distilled water into a 1.5 ml microtube, and take portions from it with the micropipette.

● Gelation of pectin
1. Take 100 µl (room temperature) of each of pectin A and B, extracted from tomato A and tomato B respectively. After adding 200 µl of milk, stir well and leave in ice for 5 min.
2. Centrifuge at 12,000 rpm, 5 min, room temperature, and remove everything except the precipitate with a pipette. Check the precipitate for each sample.

Experiment 1. Questions

Question 1
Are the cell walls of tomato A and tomato B that were handed out from the green tomato or the red tomato? Answer with green or red.
Also explain the grounds for your answer, including the observations made during the pectin extraction and the results of the pectin–calcium gel formation experiment.
problems.problem_orig:
植物生理生化学（制限時間１２０分）

はじめに

果実の成熟が進行するのに伴って、果皮ではペクチンなど細胞壁を構成する成分が分解されることにより軟化が生じています。ペクチンは、セルロースなど他の細胞壁成分と結合して植物細胞をつなぎ合わせる、いわば「セメント」のような働きをしており、トマトや柑橘類の果実に多く含まれています。ペクチンは、酸性糖であるガラクツロン酸を主鎖とし、ガラクツロン酸1個あたり1つのカルボキシル基を有しています。隣りあったペクチン主鎖のカルボキシル基の間に、カルシウムイオンが入り込むことでペクチン間の架橋が形成され、ゲル化することが知られています（図１）。
またペクチンの性質には、カルシウムとの結合以外にも、その分子量が大きな影響を与えます。非常に長いガラクツロン酸の鎖で構成された高分子量のペクチンは、あまり水に溶けませんが、低分子量のペクチンは水に溶けやすい性質を持っています。そのため、カルシウム架橋の形成による制御を受けるのは、水溶性のペクチンということになります。しかし、低分子化が進みすぎても架橋の形成ができなくなるため、ゲル化する能力を失ってしまいます。実際の果実を見ると、未熟な果実ではペクチンが非常に長い形態をとっているため、そのままでは水に溶けず、集まってゲルを作ることができません。一方、熟しすぎた果実では、ペクチン自体がバラバラに分解されており、こちらもゲル化することができません。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-4-1-fig1.png

図１　ペクチンとカルシウムイオンの架橋構造

サンプルと器具類

サンプル
乾燥細胞壁AおよびB（各1本、ラベル白）
トマト（緑、赤：各1片、10 g）

器具
マイクロピペット（P1000、P200、P20：各1本）
ピペットチップ（白、黄：各1箱）
フロート（1枚）、キャップロック（2個）
先切ピペットチップ（2本入り1袋）、キュベット（6個）
1.5 ml マイクロチューブ（プラスチックビーカー1杯）
乳鉢（2個、石英砂入り）、乳棒（2本）
洗瓶（1個、蒸留水入り）、片刃カミソリ（1枚）
プラスチック製バット（1個）、15 ml チューブ（3本）
アイスボックス（1個、氷入り）、遠心分離機（1台）
ストップウオッチ（1個）
プラスチックビーカー（1個、氷すくい用）

試薬
0.25% シュウ酸アンモニウム（1.5 ml チューブ2本、ラベル黄）
8.8% NaCl（15 ml チューブ1本）
100% エタノール（1.5 ml チューブ2本、ラベル緑）
0.1 M NaOH 溶液（1.5 ml チューブ3本、ラベル青）
牛乳（カルシウム添加）（1.5 ml チューブ1本）
0.01% BTB（ブロモチモールブルー）溶液（1.5 ml チューブ1本）
BTB 溶液色見本（青、黄：各1個）
0.5% ペクチン溶液（メチル化度85%）（20 ml 容器1個、ラベル赤）

また、机の上においてあるキムワイプ、キムタオルは自由に使えます。

２つのプラスチックビーカーは廃棄物用に使ってください。１つはチップやカミソリなどの固体用、もうひとつは液体用です。

諸注意

問題は実験１、実験２の２部構成になっていますので実験内容と設問全体に眼を通してから作業に取りかかってください。すべての問題を順番に解く必要はなく、実験１と実験２を同時に進めてください。特に、実験２には実験をうまく行うための工夫を問う問題があるので、実験操作の待ち時間などにプランを練ってください。

実験１．ペクチンの抽出とゲル化

合成されたばかりのペクチンでは、ガラクツロン酸残基のカルボキシル基はメチル化されています。このメチル化カルボキシル基はペクチンメチルエステラーゼの活性（図２）により脱メチル化されることにより、細胞壁に存在しているカルシウムイオンと結合しやすくなります。脱メチル化されたカルボキシル基を持ったペクチン同士の間にカルシウムイオンが入り込むことで、カルシウムを介したペクチン間の架橋が形成されます。この架橋は、双方のペクチンに連続した7つ以上の脱メチル化ガラクツロン酸が存在している場合、非常に強固なものとなります。一方、部分的にメチル基が残っているペクチンの間では、弱くゆるやかな結合となることから、メチル化の度合いで細胞壁構築の調節が行われている、と言うことができます。架橋形成によるゲル化は、試験管の中でペクチンとカルシウムを反応させた場合でも観察されます。実験１ではトマトの細胞壁からペクチンを抽出し、カルシウムと反応させることで生成されるゲルの状態からペクチンの性質について考察します。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-4-1-fig2.png

図２　ペクチンメチルエステラーゼの反応

●ペクチンの抽出
１．配布された乾燥細胞壁 10 mg（トマトAおよびトマトB）に、1 mlの 0.25% シュウ酸アンモニウムを加え、湯煎を 20 min行う。湯煎はTAが行うので、準備ができたらそれぞれのチューブにキャップロックを取り付け、フロートに差し込んでから挙手により知らせること。湯煎の間に実験２も開始しなさい。
２．氷中で室温程度に冷ました後、遠心機を用いて遠心分離を行う（12,000 rpm、10 min、室温）。マイクロピペットを用いて上清（ペクチン画分）を回収する。この際に上清以外（沈殿物や浮遊物）を吸い込まないように注意すること。
３．回収したペクチン画分と100% エタノールを用いて、1.5 mlマイクロチューブ内でエタノールの最終濃度が80%となる溶液を準備し、氷中に 5 min保持する。
４．12,000 rpm、10 min、室温で遠心分離する。
５．上清を完全に捨て、それぞれのサンプルについて残った沈殿物（透明）を確認する。沈殿物を 400 µlの蒸留水に完全に溶かし、ペクチンAおよびBを得る。蒸留水は洗瓶から直接取らず、一度適当な量の蒸留水を1.5 mlマイクロチューブに入れたものを用意し、そこからマイクロピペットで分取すること。

●ペクチンのゲル化
１．トマトA、トマトBそれぞれから抽出したペクチンAおよびBについて、100 µl（室温）ずつを分取する。200 µl の牛乳を加えた後、よく撹拌し、氷中に 5 min 置く。
２．12,000 rpm、5 min、室温で遠心分離し、沈殿物以外をピペットで取り除く。それぞれのサンプルについて沈殿を確認する。

実験１．問題

問１
配布されたトマトAとトマトBの細胞壁は、緑のトマト、赤いトマトのどちらであるか。緑、赤で答えよ。
また、そのように考えた根拠を、ペクチン抽出過程での観察結果や、ペクチン-カルシウムゲル形成実験の結果を含めて説明せよ。

problems.title: Experiment 2 (pectin methylesterase activity), Question 3
problems.problem:
Experiment 2. Measurement of pectin methylesterase activity

About 50% of the cell wall of tomato fruit is made of pectin, and as the ripening/softening of the fruit proceeds, the molecular weight of the pectin becomes lower. In addition, as the fruit ripens, pectin methylesterase acts and promotes the demethylation of pectin (Figure 2), so that calcium-mediated cross-links between pectins are formed. On the other hand, it is known that pectin-degrading enzymes, which break pectin down and lower its molecular weight, preferentially hydrolyse demethylated pectin. Therefore, for pectin to be reduced in molecular weight, pectin methylesterase and pectin-degrading enzymes must work together. In this way pectin, through the change in water solubility caused by the reduction in molecular weight and through the regulation of gelation by calcium, is involved in the process by which the properties of the cell wall change, that is, in the regulation of fruit firmness. In Experiment 2, you will consider the relation between fruit ripening and the enzyme reaction by measuring the activity of pectin methylesterase.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-4-1-fig2.png

Figure 2. The reaction of pectin methylesterase

Figure labels (Japanese → English): メチル化ペクチン（100%） = methylated pectin (100%); ペクチンメチルエステラーゼ = pectin methylesterase; 脱メチル化ペクチン = demethylated pectin.

● Extraction of pectin methylesterase
1. Add 5 ml of 8.8% NaCl to 10 g of tomato and grind it in the mortar (containing quartz sand). Do the grinding while cooling: move (some of) the ice into the plastic tray and bury the lower part of the mortar in the ice. If you cannot grind it well, it is a good idea to put the tomato back on the plastic wrap film, chop it there with the razor blade and return it to the mortar. Work quickly so that the temperature does not rise. Two kinds of tomato are used: an unripe green tomato and a ripe red tomato.
2. Using a cut-off pipette tip, collect 2 ml of the supernatant from the mortar, 1.0 ml into each of two 1.5 ml tubes, and centrifuge at 12,000 rpm, 1 min, room temperature.
3. Collect the supernatant in a 1.5 ml microtube, and finally prepare one 1.5 ml microtube each, red and green, containing 1 ml of solution (enzyme solution). Keep the prepared enzyme solutions and the remaining supernatant on ice.

● Measurement of pectin methylesterase activity
1. Mix 4.0 ml of the 0.5%※ pectin provided (degree of methylation 85%), 0.3 ml of 0.01% BTB (bromothymol blue) solution and 1.5 ml of distilled water in a 15 ml tube. Do not take distilled water directly from the wash bottle: first put a suitable amount of distilled water into a 1.5 ml microtube, and take portions from it with the micropipette. Add 0.1 M NaOH solution 20 µl at a time, mixing well, until the solution has the same colour as the blue colour standard. Prepare three such solutions in total.

※ Concentration expressed as solute (g)/solution (ml) × 100. For example, 1% salt water is an aqueous solution of 100 ml containing 1 g of salt.

2. Divide the prepared solution (one tube) equally between two cuvettes, and use them as the test cuvettes for the enzyme solutions extracted from the red and the green tomato respectively. With the preparation above, three sets (six cuvettes) of enzyme activity measurements are possible.
3. After adding 0.1 ml of enzyme solution to a cuvette, start the reaction by stirring the solution well with the tip of the pipette, and measure the number of seconds (sec) needed for the solution to change from blue to yellow (the state in which all the methyl groups in the pectin have been hydrolysed: see Figure 2). The maximum is 300 sec; if the solution remains blue after 300 sec, it is taken as no activity. In this exam, the unit of pectin methylesterase activity is defined as follows: when the reaction is carried out with the volumes prepared in 1.–3. above, the activity that completely hydrolyses the methyl groups of 1 mg of pectin (degree of methylation 85%) in 1 sec is 1 unit.

Experiment 2. Questions

Question 3
1) For the pectin methylesterase activity, write the formula for finding $y$ (unit) when the time needed for the solution to change from blue to yellow is $x$ (sec).
2) Give the pectin methylesterase activities of the red and green tomatoes in units.
Also explain the devices you used, within the conditions and methods of this experiment, to determine the enzyme activity as accurately as possible. You may change the experimental method, on condition that you use only the apparatus provided.
problems.problem_orig:
実験２．ペクチンメチルエステラーゼ活性の測定

トマト果実の細胞壁は約50%がペクチンで構成されており、果実の成熟／軟化過程が進むにつれて、ペクチンが低分子化していきます。また、果実成熟に伴って、ペクチンメチルエステラーゼが働き、ペクチンの脱メチル化が促されることで（図２）、カルシウムを介したペクチン間の架橋が形成されます。一方、ペクチンを分解して低分子化するペクチン分解酵素は、脱メチル化ペクチンを優先的に加水分解することが知られています。そのため、ペクチンが低分子化されるためには、ペクチンメチルエステラーゼとペクチン分解酵素が協調して働く必要があります。このようにペクチンは、低分子化による水溶性の変化と、カルシウムによるゲル化の調節によって、細胞壁の性質が変化していく過程、すなわち果実の硬さの調節に関わっています。実験２ではペクチンメチルエステラーゼの活性を測定することで、果実成熟と酵素反応の関連性について考察します。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-4-1-fig2.png

図２　ペクチンメチルエステラーゼの反応

●ペクチンメチルエステラーゼの抽出
１．トマト 10 gに5 mlの 8.8% NaClを加え、乳鉢（石英砂入り）ですりつぶす。すりつぶす作業は、プラスチック製のバットに氷（一部）を移し、乳鉢の下部を氷に埋めて冷やしながら行う。うまくすりつぶせない場合は、ラップフィルム上に戻し、その上でカミソリを用いてトマトを刻んでから乳鉢に戻すとよい。温度が上がらないように素早く行うこと。トマトは、未成熟な緑のトマトと成熟した赤いトマトの2種類を用いる。
２．先切ピペットチップを用いて乳鉢より上澄み 2 mlを 2本の 1.5 mlチューブに 1.0 mlずつ集め、12,000 rpm、1 min、室温で遠心分離する。
３．上清を 1.5 ml マイクロチューブに集め、最終的に 1 ml の溶液（酵素液）が入った1.5 ml マイクロチューブを赤、緑各1本用意する。調製した酵素液と余った上清は氷上に保存する。

●ペクチンメチルエステラーゼ活性の測定
１．用意された0.5%※ ペクチン（メチル化度 85%）4.0 mlと、0.3 mlの0.01% BTB（ブロモチモールブルー）液、1.5 mlの蒸留水を15 mlチューブで混合する。蒸留水は洗瓶から直接取らず、一度適当な量の蒸留水を1.5 mlマイクロチューブに入れたものを用意し、そこからマイクロピペットで分取すること。溶液が色見本の青色と同じ色になるまで0.1 M NaOH溶液を20 µlずつよく混ぜながら加える。同様の溶液を計3本準備する。

※ 溶質(g)/溶液(ml)×100で表されている濃度。たとえば1% 食塩水は、1 gの食塩を含む100 mlの水溶液のことである。

２．作成した溶液（1本分）を2個のキュベットに二等分し、それぞれを赤、緑のトマトから抽出した酵素液の試験用キュベットとする。以上の準備により3セット（キュベット6個）の酵素活性測定が可能となる。
３．0.1 mlの酵素液をキュベットに加えた後、ピペットの先端で溶液をよくかき混ぜて反応をスタートし、溶液が青色から黄色になる（ペクチン中の全てのメチル基が加水分解された状態：図２参照）までに要する秒数（sec）を測定する。最大で 300 secとし、300 sec経過しても青色のままの場合は活性なしとする。今回の試験では、ペクチンメチルエステラーゼの活性の単位について、上記１．〜３．で準備した液量で反応を行った際に、1 mgのペクチン（メチル化度 85%）のメチル基を 1 sec間に完全に加水分解する活性を 1 unitと定義する。

実験２．問題

問３
１）ペクチンメチルエステラーゼ活性について、溶液が青色から黄色に変わるのに要した時間を $x$ (sec)としたとき、$y$ (unit)を求めるための式を記せ。
２）赤と緑のトマトのペクチンメチルエステラーゼ活性を、unitで答えよ。
また、本実験条件および方法の中で、酵素活性をできるだけ正確に求めるために行った工夫について説明せよ。実験の方法は、与えられた器具のみを用いることを条件に変更してもよい。

problems.title: Problem 1 (restriction-enzyme analysis of DNA), Question 1
problems.problem:
Marine biology (time limit 120 minutes)

Introduction
DNA is the molecular entity of genes, and the means of analysing this DNA have become important things that support the foundations of present-day biological technology. Among the methods of analysing DNA, partial cutting of DNA with restriction enzymes and separation by electrophoresis are important techniques for amplifying a single DNA. In this experiment, the aim is to deepen your understanding of DNA experiments by actually cutting DNA with a restriction enzyme and carrying out electrophoresis.
Also, the base sequences of DNA and the amino acid sequences of proteins give us various kinds of information. For example, it is known that even between homologous genes possessed by different organisms, the base sequences and amino acid sequences differ little by little between organisms, and basically it is thought that the more distant the relationship between organisms, the greater the difference between the sequences. In other words, the size of the difference between sequences shows whether the organisms are evolutionarily close or distant. By comparing the sequence data of genes between organisms in this way, it is possible to infer the phylogenetic relationships between organisms; such an analysis is called molecular phylogenetic analysis. The phylogenetic relationships inferred by molecular phylogenetic analysis are shown in a diagram called a molecular phylogenetic tree. Furthermore, by mapping onto the molecular phylogenetic tree obtained the presence or absence, similarities and differences of the various features (morphology, mode of development, ecology, etc.) that each organism has, it also becomes possible to infer when in evolution those features were acquired. In this experiment, you will observe developmental stages of several species of animals and, by considering them together with a phylogenetic tree, consider the diversity and evolution of the modes of development of animals.

Samples and apparatus
1.5 ml tube rack
  10× buffer (B) — 1 tube
  Distilled water (W) — 1 tube
  Loading dye (D) — 1 tube
  Size marker (M) — 1 tube
  Plasmid DNA (あ) — 1 tube
  Plasmid DNA (い) — 1 tube
  Plasmid DNA (う) — 1 tube
  Empty 1.5 ml tubes — 6
Ice box
  Restriction enzyme SalI (S) — 1 tube
Micropipettes (P2, P20, P200) — 1 each
Tips (white, for P2) — 1 box
Tips (yellow, for P20, P200) — 1 box
Tube rack (small) — 1
Electrophoresis apparatus — 1 box
Agarose gel (it is in the electrophoresis apparatus) — 1
Timer — 1
Round Petri dish — 1
Centrifuge — 1
Container for used tips (plastic cup) — 1
Upright microscope — 1
4-well dish containing the samples (X, Y, Z-1, Z-2) — 1
Cavity slides — 5
Cover glasses — 1 box

The Kimwipes and Kimtowels on the desk may be used freely.

Problem 1: Analysis of DNA using a restriction enzyme

To study the evolution of a gene, DNA of a certain gene was isolated from 6 species of animals by the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) method, and each was cloned using a plasmid vector. After cloning, the base sequences of the isolated DNAs were determined, and a map of the cleavage sites of restriction enzymes was also made.

Of the 6 kinds of DNA isolated, the cleavage sites of the restriction enzyme SalI in the plasmid DNAs containing 3 kinds (called A, B, C) are as in Figure 1 below. The solutions containing these plasmid DNAs are in the tubes "あ, い, う". Using a restriction enzyme, we want to infer with SalI which of the DNA fragments "A, B, C" each of the plasmids "あ, い, う" contains.

Figure 1

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-5-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): プラスミドベクター領域 = plasmid vector region; 1000 塩基対 = 1000 base pairs.

(Note) The figure is shown in a linearised state, but the plasmid DNA actually handed out is circular.

Question 1
The absorbance of the 3 kinds of plasmid DNA solution was measured. However, because absorbance cannot be measured accurately when the concentration of the substance in the solution is high, a diluted solution was made by dissolving 2 µl of the DNA solution handed out in 998 µl of distilled water, and the absorbance of that diluted solution was measured. The results are 0.032, 0.044 and 0.021, in the order "あ, い, う". On the basis of these values, calculate the volume of the DNA solutions "あ, い, う" (as handed out) needed to obtain 0.8 µg of DNA. Write the units in your answer as well. Also, give the values to 3 significant figures. Here, the relation between the absorbance A of DNA for light of wavelength 260 nm and the concentration c of DNA (unit µg/µl) is expressed by the following formula.

$$A = 20c$$

Memo: Absorbance: when light passes through a homogeneous solution, light of particular wavelengths that depend on the dissolved substance is absorbed. Because the degree of this absorption is proportional to the concentration of the substance, the concentration of the substance can be known by measuring the absorbance.

On units: µ (micro) means 1/1000 of m (milli), and n (nano) means 1/1000 of micro.
problems.problem_orig:
海洋生物学（制限時間１２０分）

はじめに
DNAは遺伝子の分子的実体であり、このDNAの解析手段は現在の生物学のテクノロジーの根幹を支える重要なものになっています。DNAの解析方法のうち、制限酵素を用いたDNAの部分切断や電気泳動による分離は、単一のDNAを増幅するための重要な手法となっています。本実験では、実際に制限酵素を用いてDNAを切断し、電気泳動を行うことで、DNA実験に対する理解を深めることをねらいとしています。
また、DNAの塩基配列やタンパク質のアミノ酸配列は様々な情報を我々に与えます。例えば、それぞれの生物が持つ相同な遺伝子間でも、生物間で塩基配列やアミノ酸配列が少しずつ異なることが知られており、基本的には、類縁関係が遠い生物間ほど配列の差が大きくなると考えられています。つまり、配列の差の大小はその生物が進化的に近いか遠いかを表しています。このように生物間で遺伝子の配列データを比較することで、生物間の系統関係を推定することが可能であり、このような解析を分子系統解析と呼びます。そして、分子系統解析により推定された系統関係は分子系統樹と呼ばれる図で表されます。さらに得られた分子系統樹に、それぞれの生物のもっている様々な特徴（形態、発生様式、生態など）の有無や類似点、相違点を当てはめることで、それらの特徴が進化上いつ獲得されたかを推定することも可能になります。本実験では、複数種の動物の発生段階を観察し、系統樹と合わせて考えることで、動物の発生様式の多様性や進化について考察します。

サンプルと器具
1.5mlチューブ立て
  10 x 緩衝液　(B)　１本

問１
３種類のプラスミドDNA溶液の吸光度を測定した。但し吸光度は溶液中の物質の濃度が高いと正確に測れないため、配布したDNA溶液の2 µlを998 µlの蒸留水に溶かした希釈溶液を作製し、その希釈溶液の吸光度を測定した。その結果は「あ、い、う」の順で0.032, 0.044, 0.021である。その値を元に、DNAを0.8 µg得るために必要な（配布した）「あ、い、う」のDNA溶液の量を計算しなさい。解答には単位も記載してください。また、有効数字３桁で示しなさい。但し、DNAの波長260nmの光に対する吸光度AとDNAの濃度c（単位はµg/µl）の関係は以下の計算式で表される。

$$A = 20c$$

メモ：吸光度とは、光が均一な溶液を通過するとき、溶けている物質に依存する特定の波長の光が吸収される。その吸光の度合いは物質の濃度に比例するため、吸光度を測定することにより物質の濃度を知ることができる。

単位について：µ（マイクロ）はm（ミリ）の1/1000、n（ナノ）はマイクロの1/1000を表します。

problems.title: Problem 1 (restriction-enzyme analysis of DNA), Question 2
problems.problem:
Problem 1: Analysis of DNA using a restriction enzyme

To study the evolution of a gene, DNA of a certain gene was isolated from 6 species of animals by the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) method, and each was cloned using a plasmid vector. After cloning, the base sequences of the isolated DNAs were determined, and a map of the cleavage sites of restriction enzymes was also made.

Of the 6 kinds of DNA isolated, the cleavage sites of the restriction enzyme SalI in the plasmid DNAs containing 3 kinds (called A, B, C) are as in Figure 1 below. The solutions containing these plasmid DNAs are in the tubes "あ, い, う". Using a restriction enzyme, we want to infer with SalI which of the DNA fragments "A, B, C" each of the plasmids "あ, い, う" contains.

Question 2
We want to make reaction solutions for treating the plasmid DNAs with the restriction enzyme under the following conditions. Prepare the solutions using the micropipettes. The reaction conditions are set as follows.

・For each DNA, 0.8 µg is to be reacted.
・Adjust the final concentration of the buffer (a solution for adjusting to the optimum salt concentration for the enzyme reaction) to 1×. Here, taking 1× as the buffer concentration optimum for the reaction, the buffer handed out is a concentrated solution at the multiple of that concentration that is shown. For example, a buffer labelled 30× is at 30 times the buffer concentration optimum for the reaction.
・Add 1.0 µl of the restriction enzyme SalI solution to one reaction solution.
・Add distilled water to make the total volume of solution 20 µl.
・Add SalI last.
・When all the solutions have been added, mix gently once and then centrifuge to make the liquid uniform.

When preparation is finished, put the tubes containing the reaction solutions in the tube rack (small) and hand it to an assistant. The assistant will put the tubes into an incubator at 37 °C. Time 30 minutes from the time you handed the tubes to the assistant. You may work on other problems during that free time.

After 30 minutes have passed, tell an assistant and receive your samples. Then run them by electrophoresis.

(Caution) Wear gloves when working on the electrophoresis. Some of the nucleic acid staining reagents used in electrophoresis are suspected of being carcinogenic. In this experiment a reagent called "GelRed", which is said not to be carcinogenic, is used, but it is best to be careful. Do not touch the gel or the liquid in the electrophoresis tank with your hands.

The agarose gel used for electrophoresis is handed out ready-made. GelRed has been added to that gel beforehand as the nucleic acid staining reagent. Add 4 µl of loading dye to each sample, mix lightly and then add half the volume to one well (hole). The remaining half is a spare. Also, add 5 µl of the size marker (DNA of known lengths) solution, for estimating the size of DNA, to one of the wells. There are 8 wells; add "あ, い, う, size marker" from one end. That is, only 4 wells are used. When everything has been put into the wells, switch on the electrophoresis tank and run the electrophoresis for 20 minutes.

If you fail in adding a sample, run the spare sample in a remaining well.

After the electrophoresis has finished, switch off, place the gel in the round Petri dish, put on the lid and hand it quickly to an assistant. Do not peel off the number on the lid.

An assistant will take a photograph of the gel; receive the photograph, stick it in the appropriate place on the answer sheet, and show briefly which sample (あ, い, う, size marker) was run in which lane. Because taking the photograph takes time, move on to the following problems.

Memo: On nucleic acid staining reagents
Reagents for staining nucleic acids are indispensable to molecular-biology experiments, and there are many kinds. Ethidium bromide is well known as such a reagent. Also, a staining reagent called GelRed is used in the gel handed out this time. Many of these reagents have the property of entering and binding in the gaps between base pairs of nucleic acids, especially DNA (this is called intercalation), and the property of absorbing light of particular wavelengths and emitting fluorescence. As a result, these reagents become concentrated in regions containing large amounts of nucleic acid, and when light of a particular wavelength is shone on them, the fluorescence specific to the reagent is emitted more strongly than in the surroundings, so the presence of nucleic acid can be known. Also, because of the property of entering between the base pairs of DNA, these substances may change the structure of DNA, and some have been reported to be carcinogenic.
problems.problem_orig:
問題１　制限酵素を使ったDNAの解析

遺伝子の進化について調べるため、６種の動物からある遺伝子に関するDNAをポリメラーゼチェインリアクション(PCR)法にて単離し、プラスミドベクターを用いてそれぞれをクローニングした。クローニングの後、単離したDNAの塩基配列を決定し、また制限酵素の切断部位についてマップを作成した。

単離された６種類のDNAの内、３種類（A, B, Cとする）が含まれたプラスミドDNAにおける制限酵素SalIの切断サイトは以下の図１の通りである。また、それらのプラスミドDNAが含まれている溶液は「あ、い、う」のチューブに入っている。制限酵素を用いて、「あ、い、う」のそれぞれのプラスミドが「A, B, C」のどのDNA断片を含むものかどうかをSalIを用いて推測したい。

問２
プラスミドDNAを制限酵素処理するための反応液を以下の条件で作製したい。その溶液をマイクロピペットを使って準備しなさい。但し、反応条件は以下のように設定します。

・それぞれのDNAについて、0.8 µgを反応させる。
・緩衝液（酵素反応の至適塩濃度に合わせるための溶液）の最終濃度を1 xに合わせなさい。但し、1 xを反応に最適な緩衝液濃度とすると、配布されている緩衝液はその濃度の倍数が示された濃度の高い溶液となっている。例えば30 xと表示してある緩衝液については、反応に最適な緩衝液濃度の30倍の濃度である。
・制限酵素SalI溶液は1.0 µlを１つの反応液に加える。
・蒸留水を加えて、合計の溶液量を20 µlとする。
・SalIは最後に加える。
・全ての溶液を加えたら一度そっと混合してから遠心にかけ、液を均一にする。

準備が終了したら反応液が入ったチューブをチューブ立て（小）に挿し、アシスタントに渡してください。アシスタントがチューブを37度の恒温器へと入れます。アシスタントにチューブを渡した時間から30分を測ってください。その空き時間は他の問題に取り組んで構いません。

30分経過後、アシスタントに告げて自分のサンプルを受け取ってください。その後、電気泳動にかけなさい。

（注意）電気泳動は手袋をして作業してください。電気泳動の際に用いる核酸染色試薬には発がん性が示唆されているものもあります。本実験では，発ガン性のないとされている「ゲルレッド」という試薬を使用していますが、気を付けるに越したことはありません。ゲルや泳動槽内の液体には手を触れないこと。

泳動に利用するアガロースゲルは作成済みのものを配布しています。そのゲルには核酸染色試薬としてゲルレッドがあらかじめ加えてあります。１つのサンプルについてローディングダイを4 µl加え、軽く混ぜた後にウェル（穴）の１つへと半分量を加えなさい。残りの半分は予備です。また、DNAのサイズを推定するためのサイズマーカー（既知の長さのDNA）溶液5 µlをウェルの一つに加えなさい。ウェルは８個ありますが、端から「あ、い、う、サイズマーカー」を加えることとします。つまり４つのウェルのみを使用します。全てをウェルに入れ終わったら、泳動槽のスイッチを入れ、20分泳動しなさい。

もしサンプルを加えるのに失敗したら、予備のサンプルを余っているウェルに流しなさい。

泳動終了後はスイッチを切り、丸形シャーレにゲルを置き、蓋をして速やかにアシスタントに渡してください。蓋についている番号ははがさないでください。

アシスタントがゲルの写真を撮影するので、その写真を受け取り解答用紙の該当部分に貼り付け、どのレーンにどのサンプル（あ、い、う、サイズマーカー）を泳動したのかを簡単に示しなさい。写真撮影には時間がかかるため、続いての問題に移りなさい。

メモ：核酸の染色試薬について
核酸を染色するための試薬は分子生物学的実験に必要不可欠であり、数多くの種類があります。このような試薬として臭化エチジウムが有名です。また、今回配布したゲルにはゲルレッドという染色試薬が使われています。これらの試薬の多くには核酸、特にDNAの塩基対と塩基対の間の隙間に入り込み結合する（これをインターカレーションといいます）性質と、特定の波長の光を吸収して蛍光を発する性質があります。結果として、核酸が大量に含まれる領域にはそれらの試薬が濃縮されることになり、特定の波長の光を当てることにより試薬に特異的な蛍光が周囲よりも強く発せられるため、核酸の存在を知ることができます。また、DNAの塩基対間に入り込むという性質から、これらの物質はDNA構造を変化させる可能性があり、発ガン性を持つものが報告されています。

problems.problem:
Problem 1: Analysis of DNA using a restriction enzyme

Question 3
Of the 6 kinds of DNA isolated, the remaining 3 kinds (called D, E, F) were also inserted into the plasmid vector in the same way. For the insertion, each DNA was cut with PstI and inserted into the PstI site of the plasmid vector by a ligation reaction (Figure 2 A–B).
Next, when we checked with restriction enzymes whether the insertion had gone well, a strange phenomenon occurred for D. The D fragment is 1000 base pairs and is known to have one EcoRI cleavage site at about 700 base pairs. The length of the plasmid vector is 3000 base pairs, and the PstI recognition site is flanked by the cleavage sites of two kinds of restriction enzyme, EcoRI and XhoI. That is, the conceptual diagram of the expected restriction map of the vector is as in Figure 2 B.
Now, when the vector into which the D fragment had been inserted was treated with the two restriction enzymes EcoRI and XhoI at the same time and analysed by electrophoresis in an agarose gel, unlike the expectation, there was one more band (Figure 3). On investigation, the size of that band was about 1000 base pairs. State what structure the plasmid DNA obtained is inferred to have. You may use a diagram in your answer.

Figure 2

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-5-3-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): PstI の認識配列 = PstI recognition sequence; PstI による切断 = cleavage by PstI; ライゲーション反応 = ligation reaction; PstI により切断された DNA 末端同士はライゲーション反応によりつなげることができる。 = DNA ends cut by PstI can be joined to each other by a ligation reaction.; B DNA の制限酵素地図 = B Restriction map of the DNA; プラスミドベクター = plasmid vector; D 断片 = fragment D; PstI でプラスミドベクターと D 断片を切断し、ライゲーション反応によりつなげる = the plasmid vector and fragment D are cut with PstI and joined by a ligation reaction; プラスミドベクター領域 = plasmid vector region.

Figure 3

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-5-3-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 泳動方向 = direction of migration; 塩基対 = base pairs.

Lane 1 is the band pattern actually obtained in the above experiment; lane 2 is the DNA cleavage pattern obtained when the experiment was redone after the above experiment, and when it was redone, a band pattern of the expected sizes (one band each of 3000, 700 and 300 base pairs) was obtained. Lane 3 is the size marker. The numbers on the right are the sizes of each band estimated on the basis of the size marker. The band pattern of lane 1 differs from the expectation: one extra band of 1000 base pairs is obtained.

問３
単離された６種類のDNAの内、残りの３種類（D, E, Fとする）についても同様にプラスミドベクターに組み込んだ。組み込みはそれぞれのDNAをPstIで切断し、プラスミドベクターのPstIサイトへと連結反応により挿入させた（図２A－B）。
続いて組み込みがうまくいったかどうか、制限酵素を用いて確認したところ、Dについて不思議な現象が生じた。Dの断片は1000塩基対であり、おおよそ700塩基対のところにEcoRIの切断サイトを１カ所有することが分かっている。プラスミドベクターの長さは3000塩基対であり、PstIの認識サイトはEcoRIとXhoIの２種類の制限酵素の切断サイトで挟まれている。すなわち、予想されるベクターの制限酵素マップの概念図は図２Bの通りである。

problems.title: Problem 2 (phylogenetic tree and development), Question 1
problems.problem:
Problem 2: Phylogenetic tree and development

When molecular phylogenetic analysis was carried out using the base sequences of the genes A–F cloned in the above experiment, a phylogenetic tree of the following shape was obtained. Also, when the base sequences were queried against a database, it became clear that D is a flounder (ヒラメ), E is a crab (カニ) and F is a jellyfish (クラゲ).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-5-5-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): クラゲ = jellyfish; カニ = crab; ヒラメ = flounder.

In the process of isolating DNA from the 6 kinds of organisms, the 3 kinds of organisms A, B and C were in their breeding season, and eggs and sperm could be isolated. Some of them were allowed to develop and the larval forms were observed. The dishes X, Y and Z-1 contain fixed larvae of one of A, B and C each. The dish Z-2 contains another developmental stage of the same species of animal as the larvae in dish Z-1.

Prepare slides of the samples in the dishes X, Y, Z-1 and Z-2 as described below, carry out microscope observation, and answer the following questions.

Slide preparation method
While checking with the naked eye the samples that have sunk to the bottom of the dish, draw them up with a micropipette, and put the sample out together with the liquid into the hollow part of a cavity slide. Always use a cover glass when observing.

Question 1
Give the name of each of the larvae X, Y and Z-1.
problems.problem_orig:
問題２　系統樹と発生

上記の実験でクローニングしたA〜Fの遺伝子の塩基配列を用いて分子系統解析を行ったところ、以下のような形の系統樹が得られた。また、塩基配列をデータベースに照会したところ、Dはヒラメ、Eはカニ、Fはクラゲであることが判明した。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-5-5-fig1.png

６種類の生物からDNAを単離する過程で、A、B、Cの３種類の生物は生殖シーズンであり、卵と精子が単離できた。その一部を発生させ、幼生形態を観察した。X、Y、Z−１のシャーレ内にはA、B、Cのいずれかの固定した幼生が入っている。Z−２のシャーレ内にはZ−１のシャーレ内の幼生と同種の動物の別の発生段階が入っている。

X、Y、Z−１、Z−２のシャーレに入っているサンプルのプレパラートを以下の要領で作製し、顕微鏡観察を行い、以下の問いに答えよ。

プレパラート作製法
シャーレの底に沈んでいるサンプルを肉眼で確認しながらマイクロピペットで吸い取り、ホールスライドグラスのへこんでいる部分に液ごとサンプルを出す。観察の際には必ずカバーガラスを用いること。

problems.title: Moulds and yeasts, Question 1 (spore sketches)
problems.problem:
Plant morphology (time limit 120 minutes)

Introduction
Fungi (true fungi) are a group of micro-organisms that multiply by spores, and they include organisms such as mushrooms, moulds and yeasts. Both the large mushrooms visible to the naked eye and the moulds that grow on food and the like have basically the same body, consisting of a structure called "hyphae", in which cells are joined in threads. The hyphae spread over whatever serves as their source of nutrients (food, culture media, etc.), secrete enzymes, decompose the surrounding material, absorb the nutrients they need and grow by adding cells at their tips (tip growth). Eventually they form spores at the ends of the hyphae and reproduce; those in which many spores are formed in a colony by asexual reproduction are generally called "moulds". Those in which many hyphae gather and develop to a large size in order to make spores are "mushrooms". "Yeasts" have only a spore-like unicellular body, do not form hyphae and multiply in the unicellular state; this is considered the simplest body plan of the fungi.
Species and genera of moulds and yeasts are classified by the shape of their spores and by the features of how the spores are formed. Therefore, to examine their species or genus, it is necessary to isolate and culture only one species on a medium (pure culture), to observe it carefully, and to read off information on the shape of the spores and on the process by which the spores are formed.
In this experiment you will make preparations from colonies of fungi pure-cultured beforehand on agar media containing nutrients, observe their features with a biological microscope and identify the genera of the moulds and yeasts.
In many moulds the spores are formed from cells of a particular shape (spore-forming cells), but in some cases the spore-forming cells have no special shape and the spores are formed directly from ordinary hyphae. When spores are made continuously, as if sent out one after another from a spore-forming cell, the spores remain joined like a chain and form chains; but if the surface of the spores is sticky (viscous), the spores form clumps and, further, the colony may also become sticky. Spores are not necessarily unicellular; they may be multicellular. Multicellular spores are divided by septa (partitions between cells) and may consist of two cells or of more cells. Also, spores and hyphae are not necessarily colourless and transparent; some are coloured brown. Note that, since the somatic cells of yeasts have the same function as spores, in this problem the somatic cells of yeasts are regarded as spores.

Samples and apparatus
First, take out the 2 pairs of tweezers and the marker pen that have been handed out.

Next, check the equipment. Check that you have the following: slide glasses, cover glasses, a needle with a handle, a dropper bottle containing mounting fluid, 6 Petri dishes inoculated with moulds, 2 plastic beakers, Kimwipes, a wash bottle, Kimtowels.

The Kimwipes and Kimtowels on the desk may be used freely.

Use the 2 plastic beakers for things to be discarded, such as preparations you have finished observing: one is for solids such as slide glasses, the other for liquids.

When observing, take care with the following.

First, the microscopes have been set to fixed positions of eye width, stage height, dioptre (focus) and condenser diaphragm. These positions may not be suitable for actual observation, so adjust them yourself to suit your observation. In particular, adjusting the dioptre of the left and right eyepieces and the condenser diaphragm (which changes the contrast) gives an image that is easier to observe.

Second, spores stick to the needle with a handle and to the tweezers. If spores of two or more kinds of mould are mixed in the preparation you are about to observe, you cannot observe correctly. When you have finished observing one Petri dish, before observing the next Petri dish, always wipe them carefully with a Kimwipe moistened with water from the wash bottle.

The problem consists of 4 questions, from Question 1 to Question 4. Look through the whole problem before you start work.

Observing the Petri dishes and making preparations

1. First, observe the colour and the surface of the colonies with the naked eye. Because the hyphae and cells grow radially from the inoculation point in the centre of the Petri dish (where the fungus was inoculated) towards the periphery, the colonies become concentric.

2. Next, turn the Petri dish upside down, place it on the microscope stage and observe the hyphae with transmitted light from the underside of the colony. Bring a low-power (4× or 10×) objective lens as close as possible to the bottom of the Petri dish and, while lowering the stage, find the position where it comes into focus. In the hyphae that have grown into the agar medium, septa can be seen. In some cases spores (conidia) are formed here and there from the hyphae that have grown down into the agar medium.

3. Many fungi form spores on the surface of the colony. Place the Petri dish with its lid removed on the microscope stage and observe the surface of the colony in the same way as in 1. Take care at this time that the objective lens does not touch the colony. In the centre of the colony you can see the mature state in which spores are being made, and at the periphery a younger state, so find a place suitable for observation. You can see stalks rising from the hyphae that have grown over the medium and spores being formed.

4. To observe spore formation in more detail, you need to make a preparation. With the needle with a handle, cut out a small piece of the spores and part of the mycelium observed in 3. above together with the agar medium, and place it on a slide glass. Put one drop of mounting fluid (10% ethanol solution) on it. Then, taking care that no air bubbles get in, carefully lay a cover glass over the sample and squash it lightly.

5. Place the preparation on the stage, first observe it with the low-power (4×) objective lens, and when you have found a part where spores are being formed, move it to the centre of the field of view. Turn the revolver and observe with higher-power (10×, 20×, 40×) objective lenses (in this observation the 100× oil-immersion lens is not used). Observe whether the spores and hyphae are coloured, how many cells there are, where the spores are formed from and how they are connected to the hyphae.

Problem: Observation of moulds and yeasts and identification of their genera

Petri dishes A–F are agar media containing nutrients, each inoculated with a fungus of a different genus and cultured at room temperature. First, observe each colony well with the naked eye; then open the lid of the Petri dish, place it on the microscope stage and, using a low-power (4× or 10×) objective lens, observe well how the spores are formed. Take care that the objective lens does not touch the colony. Next, make preparations and, after observing the features of each fungus, answer the following questions.

Question 1
Observe the morphology of the spores of each fungus and make sketches following the example. In the sketches it is important to show the features of the organism clearly. You do not need to draw the cell contents. As in the example, try to show the presence or absence of septa (partitions between cells), the presence or absence of colouring, etc. with lines and dots (in the example, dots are drawn in the parts coloured brown). Also, if the spore morphology varies (differences in size, number of cells, etc.), show several examples.

Example) Spores of the genus Ulocladium (ウロクラディウム属)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2012-7-1-fig1.png
problems.problem_orig:
植物形態学（制限時間１２０分）

はじめに
菌類（真菌類）は胞子により増える微生物の仲間で、きのこ・カビ・酵母などの生物を含んでいます。肉眼で見える大型のきのこも、食べ物などに生えるカビも、その体は基本的に同様で、細胞が糸状に連なった「菌糸」という構造からなっています。菌糸は栄養源となるもの（食べ物や培地など）の上に張りめぐらされ、酵素を分泌して、周囲のものを分解し、必要な栄養を吸収して、先端に細胞を継ぎ足すようにして成長（先端成長）していきます。やがて、菌糸の末端に胞子を作り、繁殖しますが、無性生殖によりコロニー（集落）にたくさんの胞子が形成されているものを、一般に「カビ」といいます。菌糸がたくさん集まって胞子を作るために大型に発達したものが「きのこ」です。また、「酵母」は、胞子状の単細胞の体しか持たず、菌糸を作らずに、単細胞の状態で増殖しますが、これはもっとも単純な菌類の体制と考えられます。
カビや酵母の種や属は、胞子の形や、胞子がどのように作られるかという特徴により分類されます。したがって、その種や属を調べるには、一種のみを培地上に分離して培養（純粋培養）し、これを丹念に観察して、胞子の形や、胞子が作られる過程についての情報を読み取る必要があります。
この実験では、あらかじめ栄養の入った寒天培地上で、純粋培養した菌類のコロニーからプレパラートを作成して、生物顕微鏡でその特徴を観察し、カビや酵母の属を同定します。
多くのカビでは、胞子は特定の形をした細胞（胞子形成細胞）から形成されますが、胞子形成細胞が特別な形をなさず、通常の菌糸から直接、胞子が形成される場合もあります。胞子形成細胞から胞子が次々と送り出されるように連続して作られると、胞子は鎖のようにつながった状態を保ち、連鎖しますが、胞子の表面に粘り気（粘性）があると、胞子は塊をなし、さらに、コロニーに粘性を生じることもあります。胞子は単細胞であるとは限らず、多細胞の場合もあります。多細胞の胞子は、隔壁（細胞の仕切り）により仕切られており、二細胞のことも、あるいは、それ以上の細胞からなることもあります。また、胞子や菌糸は無色で透明とは限らず、褐色に着色するものもあります。なお、酵母は、体細胞が胞子と同様の機能をもつことから、本問題では、酵母の体細胞は胞子とみなします。

サンプルと器具
まず、配布されたピンセット２本とマジックペンを取り出してください。

次に、機材を確認します。手元に次のものがあるか、確認してください。スライドグラス、カバーグラス、柄付き針、マウント液をいれたスポイト瓶、カビを植えたシャーレ６枚。プラスチックビーカー２個、キムワイプ、洗瓶、キムタオル。

机の上においてあるキムワイプ、キムタオルは自由に使えます。

２つのプラスチックビーカーは観察を終えたプレパラートなど廃棄する物を入れるのに使ってください。１つはスライドガラスなどの固体用、もうひとつは液体用です。

観察にあたっては、次のことに注意して下さい。

第一に、顕微鏡は、目の幅、ステージの高さ、視度（ピント）、コンデンサーの絞りを一定の位置に合わせてあります。この位置では、実際の観察には不適切な場合がありますので、各自で観察に合うように調整して使用してください。特に、左右の接眼レンズの視度、コンデンサーの絞り（コントラストが変化する）を調節すると、より観察しやすい像が得られます。

第二に、柄付き針やピンセットには、胞子が付着します。観察しようとするプレパラートに、二種以上のカビの胞子が混在すると正しい観察ができません。一つのシャーレの観察が終わり、次のシャーレを観察する前に、かならず、洗瓶の水で湿らせたキムワイプで丁寧に拭き取るようにしてください。

問題は問１から問４までの４問からなっています。全体に眼を通してから作業に取りかかってください。

シャーレの観察とプレパラートの作成方法

１．まず、肉眼でコロニーの色や表面の様子を観察します。菌糸や細胞は、シャーレ中央の接種点（菌を植え付けたところ）から周辺に向けて放射状に成長していくため、同心円状になります。

２．次にシャーレを逆さまにして顕微鏡のステージに乗せ、コロニーの裏側から透過光により、菌糸の様子を観察します。低倍率（４倍か１０倍）の対物レンズを、シャーレの底面ぎりぎりまで近づけ、ステージを下げながら、ピントの合うところを探します。寒天培地の内部に伸長した菌糸には隔壁が入っている様子が観察されます。寒天培地の中に潜った菌糸のところどころから胞子（分生子）が形成されている場合もあります。

３．多くの菌はコロニーの表面に胞子を形成します。ふたをはずしたシャーレを顕微鏡のステージに乗せ、１．と同様にしてコロニー表面の様子を観察しましょう。このとき、対物レンズがコロニーに接触しないように注意してください。コロニーの中央部では成熟して胞子が作られている様子が、周辺部ではより若い状態がみられますので、観察に適した箇所を探して下さい。培地上に伸びた菌糸から柄が立ち上がって胞子が形成されている様子が観察できます。

４．より詳しく胞子形成の様子を観察するにはプレパラートを作成する必要があります。上記３．で観察された胞子と菌糸体の一部を寒天培地ごと、わずかに柄付針で切り出し、スライドグラスの上にのせます。その上に、マウント液（10%エタノール溶液）を一滴たらします。そして、気泡が入らないよう注意しながら丁寧にカバーグラスを試料の上にかぶせ、軽く押しつぶします。

５．プレパラートをステージに乗せ、まず、低倍率（４倍）の対物レンズで観察し、胞子が形成されている部分が見つかったら視野の中心に移動します。レボルバーを回して、より高倍率（１０倍、２０倍、４０倍）の対物レンズで観察しましょう（今回の観察では、１００倍の油浸レンズは使用しません）。胞子や菌糸に色がついているかどうか、細胞数はいくつか、胞子はどこから形成され、どのように菌糸とつながっているか、観察してください。

問題　カビ・酵母の観察と属の同定

A〜Fのシャーレは栄養の入った寒天培地に、それぞれ別の属の菌を接種し、室温で培養したものです。まず、肉眼でそれぞれのコロニーをよく観察し、次いでシャーレのふたを開けて、顕微鏡のステージの上にのせ、低倍率（４倍か１０倍）の対物レンズを用いて、胞子がどのように作られているか、よく観察してください。対物レンズがコロニーに接触しないように注意しましょう。次に、プレパラートを作成して、それぞれの菌の特徴を観察したうえで、以下の問いに答えなさい。

【問１】

Animal centrosomes act as microtubule-organising centres and also function as regulators of cell-cycle progression. In addition, a mechanism operates so that centrosome duplication occurs only once per cell cycle. To confirm this mechanism, cell-fusion experiments were carried out using human fibroblasts.

The figure shows schematically the experiments carried out and their results. The grey-filled parts represent nuclei, and the black dots represent centrosomes. The cell-cycle stage of each nucleus in the figure is the result of determining at which stage of DNA replication it is. When G1 cells were fused with each other, no significant difference was seen from the case in which no fusion was carried out.

① Components in the cytoplasm of S phase cause a G1-phase nucleus to advance to S phase and also bring about centrosome duplication.

② The cytoplasm of G2 phase contains an inhibitory substance that suppresses centrosome duplication of a G1-phase nucleus.

③ Components in the cytoplasm of S phase promote the duplication of the two centrosomes of a G2-phase nucleus.

Consider an experiment in which a gene for the enzyme β-galactosidase and a gene for resistance to the antibiotic ampicillin are introduced into Escherichia coli. A substance called X-gal is a substrate of β-galactosidase and turns blue when it is hydrolysed by β-galactosidase. E. coli normally has the β-galactosidase gene, so when E. coli is cultured on an agar plate medium containing X-gal, its colonies become blue.

Now, a transformation experiment is carried out using an ampicillin-sensitive strain of E. coli that lacks the β-galactosidase gene. As the genes to be introduced, a plasmid containing the β-galactosidase gene and the ampicillin-resistance gene is used. When the E. coli into which the plasmid has been introduced are spread on a medium containing X-gal and ampicillin, only the E. coli that have been transformed should be obtained, as a small number of blue colonies. By choosing these blue colonies and culturing them, it is possible to select and culture only the E. coli that have taken up the plasmid.

At this time, the following experiments were carried out as controls (control experiments).

Control I: The β-galactosidase-gene-deficient strain is given the transformation treatment using this plasmid. The E. coli obtained are cultured on a medium that contains ampicillin but does not contain X-gal.

Control II: The β-galactosidase-gene-deficient strain is given the transformation treatment using this plasmid. The E. coli obtained are cultured on a medium that does not contain ampicillin but contains X-gal.

Control III: The β-galactosidase-gene-deficient strain is given the transformation treatment without using this plasmid. The E. coli obtained are cultured on a medium containing ampicillin and X-gal.

What result is expected in each case? Choose the correct combination from A–J. Note that when E. coli is cultured on an ordinary agar plate medium, it forms white colonies. (5 points)

Expected results

① A small number of colonies arise. All the colonies that arise are blue.

② A small number of colonies arise. All the colonies that arise are white.

③ A large number of colonies arise. A very small fraction of them are blue, and the great majority of the rest are white.

④ No colonies arise.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c}  & \text{A} & \text{B} & \text{C} & \text{D} & \text{E} & \text{F} & \text{G} & \text{H} & \text{I} & \text{J} \\ \hline \text{Control I} & \text{①} & \text{①} & \text{①} & \text{①} & \text{①} & \text{②} & \text{②} & \text{②} & \text{②} & \text{②} \\ \text{Control II} & \text{①} & \text{①} & \text{②} & \text{②} & \text{③} & \text{①} & \text{②} & \text{②} & \text{③} & \text{③} \\ \text{Control III} & \text{③} & \text{④} & \text{③} & \text{④} & \text{④} & \text{③} & \text{③} & \text{④} & \text{③} & \text{④} \end{array}$$

At the posterior end of the Drosophila embryo there is cytoplasm called the pole plasm, and only the cells that take it up become pole cells. The pole cells migrate through the embryo and are incorporated into the gonads; eventually, after going through the process of gametogenesis in the gonads of the adult, they differentiate into eggs or sperm.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-1-4-fig1.png

In Drosophila, by artificially synthesising a double-stranded RNA with a sequence complementary to any chosen gene and injecting it into the embryo, the mRNA of that gene can be degraded. From experiments in which double-stranded RNA was injected into embryos, the following observations were obtained in late embryogenesis.

[Observations]

• Injection of double-stranded RNA against gene $P$: pole cells were present inside the gonads.
• Injection of double-stranded RNA against gene $Q$: pole cells were present outside the gonads.
• Injection of double-stranded RNA against gene $R$: there were no pole cells anywhere in the embryo.

In addition, in all the experiments on genes $P$, $Q$ and $R$, no gametes were formed. From these results, what kind of genes are genes $P$, $Q$ and $R$ thought to be? Choose the most appropriate combination from A–F. (5 points)

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c|c|c|c}  & \text{A} & \text{B} & \text{C} & \text{D} & \text{E} & \text{F} \\ \hline \text{Apoptosis-suppressing gene (a gene that functions so that pole cells do not undergo apoptosis)} & P & P & Q & Q & R & R \\ \text{Gametogenesis gene (a gene necessary for pole cells to differentiate into eggs or sperm)} & Q & R & P & R & P & Q \\ \text{Migration-related gene (a gene necessary for pole cells to migrate to the gonads)} & R & Q & R & P & Q & P \end{array}$$

Sea urchins of species X become blastulae 20 hours after fertilisation and begin gastrulation 5 hours after that. Sea urchins of species Y, on the other hand, become blastulae 7 hours after fertilisation and begin gastrulation 3 hours after that. It is also known that, in both sea urchins, by immersing them once in seawater of low osmotic pressure and then returning them to normal seawater (hypotonic seawater treatment), even unfertilised eggs develop with the same time course as fertilised eggs. Experiments were carried out using these two species of sea urchin, and the following experimental results 1–6 were obtained.

1. When the nucleus was removed from unfertilised eggs of species X and hypotonic seawater treatment was carried out, they became blastulae 20 hours after the treatment, and development stopped there.

2. When the nucleus was removed from unfertilised eggs of species Y and hypotonic seawater treatment was carried out, they became blastulae 7 hours after the treatment, and development stopped there.

3. When unfertilised eggs of species X were fertilised with sperm of species Y, they became blastulae 20 hours after fertilisation and began gastrulation 5 hours after that.

4. When unfertilised eggs of species Y were fertilised with sperm of species X, they became blastulae 7 hours after fertilisation and began gastrulation 3 hours after that.

5. When the nucleus of a fertilised egg of species Y was transplanted into an enucleated unfertilised egg of species X and hypotonic seawater treatment was carried out, it became a blastula 20 hours after fertilisation and began gastrulation 3 hours after that.

6. When the nucleus of a fertilised egg of species X was transplanted into an enucleated unfertilised egg of species Y and hypotonic seawater treatment was carried out, it became a blastula 7 hours after fertilisation and began gastrulation 5 hours after that.

Now, if an unfertilised egg of species X is fertilised with sperm of species Y, the nucleus of this fertilised egg is transplanted into an enucleated unfertilised egg of species Y, and hypotonic seawater treatment is carried out, how is development expected to proceed? Choose from A–I. (5 points)

A. It becomes a blastula 7 hours after the treatment, and development stops there.

B. It becomes a blastula 7 hours after the treatment and begins gastrulation 3 hours after that.

C. It becomes a blastula 7 hours after the treatment and begins gastrulation 5 hours after that.

D. It becomes a blastula 13.5 hours after the treatment, and development stops there.

E. It becomes a blastula 13.5 hours after the treatment and begins gastrulation 3 hours after that.

F. It becomes a blastula 13.5 hours after the treatment and begins gastrulation 5 hours after that.

G. It becomes a blastula 20 hours after the treatment, and development stops there.

H. It becomes a blastula 20 hours after the treatment and begins gastrulation 3 hours after that.

I. It becomes a blastula 20 hours after the treatment and begins gastrulation 5 hours after that.

In the exoskeleton of the red swamp crayfish (アメリカザリガニ) there are red chromatophores and white chromatophores, and slight changes in the shade of the body colour are seen as a result of the aggregation and dispersion of the pigment granules contained in them. Such movement of pigment granules is called chromatophore movement. In red chromatophores, it is known that chromatophore movement is caused by red pigment-concentrating hormone contained in the eyestalks. In addition, corazonin, a hormone discovered in insects, also affects chromatophore movement in the red swamp crayfish.

Part of the exoskeleton of red swamp crayfish that had been kept in a light place and light-adapted was excised, these hormones were administered, and the changes in each type of chromatophore were examined as a chromatophore dispersion index (a value taking the dispersed state as 5 and the aggregated state as 1); the results are Figure 1 and Figure 2. Figure 1 shows the change with time in the chromatophore dispersion index after corazonin was administered. Figure 2 shows the chromatophore dispersion index when red pigment-concentrating hormone and corazonin were administered at different concentrations.

Salamander larvae (at the stage at which the forelimbs and hindlimbs have come out) were anaesthetised and subjected to surgery to remove the pituitary gland, and its effects were examined. The experiment was carried out with 20 individuals divided into the following three groups.

Group (1): individuals that were anaesthetised and had the pituitary surgically removed (10 individuals)

Adult toads (ヒキガエル) are completely terrestrial animals; they do not normally enter ponds or rivers, and they live mainly at night, crawling about on the ground and eating small animals, chiefly insects. Towards the end of autumn they burrow deep into the soil or under fallen leaves and settle down for the winter, but in spring, one evening, they suddenly appear above ground, and both males and females begin to move towards the pond in which they were born, for breeding. To find out how toads find the pond in which they breed, several hypotheses were set up and an experiment was carried out.

[Hypotheses]

① They gather, attracted by the calls of the males heard from the pond. (The first males reach the pond by chance.)

② Because the toads begin their activity after sunset, they find the direction of the pond using the direction of the set sun as a cue.

③ They visually remember the route from the breeding pond.

④ They can sense the Earth's magnetic field lines (geomagnetism) and find the direction of the pond on that basis.

⑤ They remember the smell of the ground along their route.

⑥ They gather, attracted by some chemical substance in the pond water.

[Experiment] Many toads heading from east to west towards the breeding pond were captured, put in equal numbers into two boxes, and covered with black cloth so that they could not see outside. When the subsequent behaviour of the toads was examined, most individuals of the control group again began to move towards the pond, but the experimental group did not try to move in a fixed direction, and each individual moved in a different direction.

The arrangement of leaves follows a regular pattern that is fixed for each plant. For example, in many plants that bear one leaf at each node, the angle made by successive leaves (with the stem as the centre) is constant at about 135–140°, and therefore the leaves form a neat spiral. Species that have been carried by humans to regions where they do not originally occur and have spread there are called alien species. At present, many alien plant species have been reported, and some of them flourish vigorously in the areas they have invaded and have become a problem. In such alien plant species, abnormal flourishing is sometimes seen only in the invaded area and not in the native area. As an explanation of such a phenomenon, there is the idea that in the native area there are herbivores (natural enemies) that suppress the population growth of the plant, but they are absent from the area invaded by the alien species, so that an outbreak occurred. In that case, there is a prediction that, because the plant is released from its natural enemies in the invaded area, it stops defending itself against natural enemies; this is called the enemy release hypothesis. Furthermore, there is a prediction that the advantage arises that the energy saved by stopping defence can be invested in growth, and the alien species becomes stronger in competition with other plants. This is called the increased competitive ability hypothesis.

A researcher chose an alien plant species for which there was no large environmental difference between the native area and the invaded area other than the presence or absence of herbivores (natural enemies), and carried out a cultivation experiment using native-area lines and invaded-area lines. The cultivation experiment was carried out under a condition with natural enemies (natural enemies present) and a condition without them (natural enemies absent), and the amount of feeding damage, the amount of growth and the fitness were examined (figure below). In this plant species it was known that fitness is represented by the number of seeds, so the number of seeds produced during the cultivation period was taken as the fitness. The researcher concluded that differences in the properties predicted by the enemy release hypothesis and the increased competitive ability hypothesis have arisen between the native-area and invaded-area lines, and that these are very likely to have brought about adaptive differentiation.

The above conclusion consists of three elements: "there are differences predicted by the enemy release hypothesis", "there are differences predicted by the increased competitive ability hypothesis" and "these differences are adaptive differentiation". The experiments are carried out in the order Experiment 1, 2, 3.

[Materials required for the experiments]
Experiments 1, 2 and 3 use the materials, apparatus and reagents shown below.

  The tweezers are also used in Experiment 3.

• Black pencils – 2 (in the drawer)

Experiment 2

  Tap water (for washing the slide glass)
• Transparent plastic box (submission box) – 1
  The submission box is also used in Experiment 3
• Light microscope (biological microscope) – 1
  The light microscope is also used in Experiment 3

Experiment 3
• Zebrafish Danio rerio (white mutant individuals) – 2
• Slide glasses (unmarked) – 2

  2-phenoxyethanol 0.06%
• Fish net – 1
• Dropper (with the tip cut off) – 1
• Modelling clay (in the submission box) – 1

How to use the light microscope
1) Adjust the amount of light to a suitable brightness.
2) Turn the coarse-adjustment knob to lower the stage all the way down.
3) Turn the revolver to set the objective lens to 4× (the lowest magnification).
4) Set the specimen and move the part you want to observe into the illuminating light.
5) Raise the stage all the way up.
6) While looking through the eyepieces, lower the stage with the coarse-adjustment knob to the position where the image is in focus.
7) Turn the fine-adjustment knob to fine-tune the focus.
8) Use the condenser diaphragm to adjust the contrast and the depth of focus.
※ Eye width and eyesight differ between individuals, so correct for your own differences.
※ The 100× objective lens is not used in this experiment.
※ If a lens gets dirty during use, tell an exam assistant.

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 接眼レンズ = eyepiece; レボルバー = revolver; 対物レンズ = objective lens; 標本押さえ = specimen clip; 粗動ハンドル = coarse-adjustment knob; 微動ハンドル = fine-adjustment knob; 光源スイッチ = light switch; 標本押さえレバー = specimen-clip lever; 標本移動ハンドル = specimen-moving knob; ステージ = stage; コンデンサー = condenser; コンデンサー絞り = condenser diaphragm; 光量調節つまみ = light-intensity knob; 接眼レンズ部の拡大 = enlarged view of the eyepieces; 視度調整環 = dioptre-adjustment ring; メガネをかけている場合は接眼レンズのゴムカバーをこのように折り返す = if you wear glasses, fold back the rubber eyecups of the eyepieces like this.

Experiment 1 Dissection and morphological observation of the mantis shrimp

[Introduction]
Mantis shrimp (シャコ) is the collective name for the species belonging to the phylum Arthropoda, subphylum Crustacea, order Stomatopoda. About 450 species of Stomatopoda are known worldwide so far. Mantis shrimps are used as food, and the Japanese are said to be the people who eat the most mantis shrimp in the world. Thus mantis shrimps are a taxonomic group important as a fishery resource. In Japan, the Seto Inland Sea is one of the main areas where they are caught.
Mantis shrimps can easily be distinguished from other taxonomic groups of the subphylum Crustacea by having raptorial appendages, large sickle-shaped appendages. The destructive power of the raptorial appendages is great, and they can even smash the shell of a Manila clam (アサリ). In external appearance mantis shrimps resemble shrimps (order Decapoda), but the degree of fusion of the body segments and the form and function of the appendages differ greatly from those of shrimps.
Carry out this experiment following the procedure below and answer Questions 1 to 4.

Step 1 Mantis shrimps have sharp spines and may cause injury, so wear laboratory gloves and handle them carefully. Transfer the mantis shrimp to the dissecting tray and check that it has no missing appendages or other damage. If the specimen is damaged it will be replaced, so tell an assistant.

Step 2 Observe the external morphology, paying attention to the structure of the body segments, and answer the following question.

[Question 1] Place the mantis shrimp on the dissecting tray with its head end upward and, with a black pencil on Kent paper, sketch it as seen from the dorsal side, with the head upward, so that the structure of the body segments can be understood. Next, colour the head of the sketch red, the thorax blue and the abdomen yellow with the coloured pencils. Where a boundary between head, thorax and abdomen does not appear externally because of the fusion of segments, show the boundary with a dotted line (black pencil). There is no need to draw the appendages.

実験１　シャコの解剖と形態観察

【はじめに】
シャコは節足動物門・甲殻亜門・口脚目に属する種の総称である。口脚目はこれまでに世界で約450種が知られている。シャコは食用として利用され，世界で最もシャコを食べているのは日本人であると言われている。このようにシャコは水産資源として重要な分類群である。日本国内では，瀬戸内海が主要な産地の一つとなっている。
シャコは大きな鎌状の付属肢である捕脚をもつことで，他の甲殻亜門の分類群と容易に区別できる。捕脚の破壊力は大きく，アサリの殻をたたき割ることもできる。シャコは外見的にはエビ類（十脚目）に似ているが，体節の癒合の程度や付属肢の形態および機能などがエビとは大きく異なる。
この実験は以下の手順に従って行い，問1から問4の設問に答えること。

手順1　シャコはとげが鋭く怪我をする恐れがあるため，実験用手袋を着用して注意深く扱うこと。シャコを解剖バットに移し，付属肢などに欠損がないか確認しなさい。標本が破損している場合は交換するので申し出ること。

手順2　体節構造に注意して外部形態を観察し，次の問に答えなさい。

【問1】シャコの頭部が上になるように解剖バットの上に置き，体節構造が分かるように，頭部が上になる向きで背面から見たところを黒鉛筆でケント紙にスケッチしなさい。次にスケッチの頭部を赤色，胸部を青色，腹部を黄色の色鉛筆で塗り分けなさい。頭部・胸部・腹部の境界が節の癒合により外見にあらわれない場合は，境界を点線（黒鉛筆）で示しなさい。なお，付属肢を描く必要はない。

problems.title: Experiment 2 (sheep blood cells), Question 5
problems.problem:
Experiment 2 Observation of sheep blood cells

[Introduction]
The blood of fishes and mammals contains a variety of blood cells. Most of them are red blood cells, which are used for transporting oxygen. The other main blood cells are the white blood cells, which include neutrophils, lymphocytes and others; these are involved in the defence of the body.
In this experiment, a blood smear is made from sheep blood and stained, and the red and white blood cells are observed while being distinguished from each other. Carry out the experiment following the procedure below and answer Questions 5 and 6 on page 14. Pages 8 to 13 describe the procedure, so start the experimental work only after you have fully understood the procedure.
※ Carry out the following operations wearing laboratory gloves and safety glasses.
※ You may make up to 3 smears.

Step 1 In the way practised in the preliminary session, make a blood smear using the sheep blood in the 1.5 mL tube. The details of the procedure for making the preparation are as follows.
1) Arrange the slide glasses, cover glasses and other apparatus needed in positions where they are easy to use.
• The side of the slide glass with one end painted white is the front; place it so that this end is on the right.
• A ○ mark is drawn near the centre of the back of the slide glass.
• Operations 2)–5) below must be carried out quickly, so start them only after you have fully understood the procedure and practised the operations.
• There are 3 slide glasses and 3 square cover glasses each, and you may use all of them.
2) After stirring the blood in the tube gently, put a toothpick (rear end) into the tube and take up some blood on it.
3) Touch the toothpick with the blood to the front of the slide glass, placed on a paper towel, near its centre (where the ○ mark is drawn on the back), and put the blood on the slide glass.
• Repeat this operation if necessary to adjust the amount of blood deposited.
4) Holding a square cover glass as in Figure 1, touch it to the slide a little to the left of the deposited blood as in Figure 2, and, keeping it like this, shift it slightly to the right so that it touches the blood (Figure 3, ① ②). The blood then spreads along the line where the cover glass meets the slide glass; next, slide the cover glass quickly and smoothly as far as the left end of the slide glass (Figure 3, ③ ④).
• You may devise your own way of holding the cover glass.
5) Hold the slide glass firmly in your hand and shake it, blowing air on it, so that the blood dries well.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig1.png

Figure 1. How to hold the square cover glass. Figure 2. Touch the cover glass to the slide a little to the left of the blood, then shift it to the right.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig2.png

Figure 3. How to move the cover glass (side view). Caution: after smearing, do not put the cover glass on the slide glass.

Step 2 Fix and stain the preparation as follows.
1) Dip the slide glass with the blood smear into the fixative and move it slowly up and down 10 times.
2) Touch the edge of the slide glass to a Kimwipe to soak up the excess fixative.
3) Then carry out operations 1) and 2) above with staining solutions A and B, in that order.
4) In the plastic cup containing the washing water, wash the preparation for about 10 seconds, slowly stirring the water with the slide glass.
5) Wipe off the water on the back of the slide glass with a Kimwipe. Take care not to mix up the front and back of the slide glass.
6) Hold the slide glass firmly in your hand and shake it to dry it well. Except for the part where the blood was smeared, you may soak up the water with a Kimwipe.
7) It can be seen with the naked eye that the blood cells are stained pale purple. Ideally the smear is uniform over the whole area, but even with an uneven smear parts of it can be used, and there is often no problem for observation.

Step 3 Observe the stained and dried preparation under the microscope and find a place where the blood cells are spread as uniformly as possible (see Figure 4).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig3.png

A suitable smear; example unsuitable for observation 1 (many blood cells overlapping); example unsuitable for observation 2 (density of blood cells too low)

Figure 4. State of the blood smear.

Step 4 Take the slide glass off the microscope and, with a new toothpick, put a small drop of mounting medium on the place found in Step 3 (roughly is fine).
• Take up a small amount by dipping the rear end of the toothpick in the mounting medium.
• Take care that the toothpick does not touch the slide glass directly.

Step 5 Following the cautions below, put a round cover glass for mounting (with grid) on the place where the mounting medium was dropped and leave it for about 5 minutes so that it settles.
• Have the white-painted end of the slide glass on the right.
• Take care with the orientation of the round cover glass (see Figure 5).
• You may use the tweezers when holding the round cover glass.
• Do not wipe off mounting medium that has squeezed out.
• A round cover glass once used for mounting cannot be reused, so do not peel it off the slide glass.
• If the mounting fails, you may use another preparation that you have made and the second round cover glass, but only one of them may be used for your answers.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig4.png

Figure 5. Orientation of the round cover glass (with grid). Place the round cover glass on the slide glass so that the ◎ mark shown by the thick arrow is on the left and the small characters shown by the thin arrow are at the top.

Step 6 Observe the mounted preparation under the microscope. Following the cautions below, check the stained blood cells and the grid on the slide glass with the 4× or 10× objective lens (Figure 6).
• Set the slide glass on the microscope with the white-painted end on the right.
• When the blood cells are in focus, the grid and symbols are blurred (Figure 6, left), but changing the focus slightly makes them clearly visible (Figure 6, right).
• It is best to focus on the blood cells when observing and, when finding a position, to focus on the grid and symbols without changing the field of view.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig5.png

Figure 6. How the grid of the round cover glass and the blood cells look.

• In the symbols on the round cover glass, the left one is a letter and the right one a number. Take care with the following, which are easily confused.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig6.png

The letter G and the number 6; the letter I and the number 1; the letter O and the number 0 (the first character is always a letter)

Figure 7. Examples of easily confused symbols.

• To observe individual blood cells, use the 40× objective lens. Adjust the light source and the condenser diaphragm of the microscope so that observation is easiest.
※ The 100× objective lens is not used in this experiment.

<Description of the blood cells>
Red blood cells: the blood cells observed in the largest numbers are the red blood cells. They are stained reddish purple (the small blood cells seen in large numbers in Figure 8). The red blood cells of mammals are characterised by lacking a nucleus.
White blood cells: there are various types; of these, the following are stained as in Figure 8.
Eosinophils: the cytoplasm is stained deep pink or reddish purple. The nucleus is stained dark blue or bluish purple and has several constrictions. The diameter is at least twice that of a red blood cell.
Neutrophils: the cytoplasm is stained very pale bluish purple or reddish purple. The nucleus is stained dark blue or bluish purple; its shape is complex and it may look like a knotted string. The diameter is at least twice that of a red blood cell.
Lymphocytes: the cell is spherical or slightly distorted spherical, and the nucleus takes up most of it. The nucleus is stained dark blue or bluish purple. Slightly smaller than the other white blood cells.
Monocytes: the cytoplasm is stained a slightly deeper bluish purple than in neutrophils. The nucleus is large, stained dark blue or bluish purple, and has constrictions. The diameter is at least twice that of a red blood cell.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig7.png

Figure 8. Micrographs of white blood cells. In each picture the large cell is a white blood cell and the other, small cells are red blood cells.

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 好酸球 = eosinophil; 好中球 = neutrophil; リンパ球 = lymphocyte; 単球 = monocyte.

[Question 5] Identify 3 of the 4 types of white blood cell given as examples on the previous page (you may choose any types), choose one blood cell of each, and write its position on the smear on the answer sheet as described below. Do not include the area outside the grid pattern of the cover glass in your observations.

<How to answer>
