• If you could not find 3 types of white blood cell, write "not found" in the "type of white blood cell" box of the answer sheet.

Example answer for the position of a white blood cell

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig8.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 白血球の位置をマークする = mark the position of the white blood cell; 格子の番号を記入する = write the number of the grid square.
problems.problem_orig:
実験２　ヒツジの血球観察

【はじめに】
魚類や哺乳類の血液中には，さまざまな血球細胞が含まれている。そのほとんどは酸素の運搬に使われる赤血球である。その他の主な血球として，好中球やリンパ球などを含む白血球があり，これらは生体防御に関わっている。
この実験では，ヒツジの血液を用いて血液塗抹標本を作製し，血球染色を施して赤血球と白血球とを区別しつつ観察する。以下の手順に従って実験を行い，14ページにある問5と問6の設問に答えること。8ページから13ページまでは手順を記述しているので，十分に手順を理解してから実験操作を始めること。
※　以下の操作は，実験用手袋と保護メガネを着用して行うこと。
※　塗抹標本は3枚まで作製してよい。

手順1　予備体験で行った要領で，1.5 mL容チューブに入ったヒツジの血液を用いて血液塗抹標本を作製する。標本作製手順の詳細は以下のとおりである。
1) スライドガラスやカバーガラス等，必要な器具類を使いやすい位置に配置する。
・スライドガラスは，一方が白く塗ってある側が表で，これが右側になるようにおく。
・スライドガラス裏側の中心付近に○印が描いてある。
・以下の操作2)～5)は，手際よく進める必要があるので，十分に手順を理解し，操作を練習した上で始めること。
・スライドガラスと角型カバーガラスはそれぞれ3枚ずつあるので，それらをすべて使って良い。
2) チューブ内の血液を軽くかくはんした後，つまようじ（後端側）をチューブ内に入れ，血液をつける。
3) 血液のついたつまようじを，ペーパータオルの上にのせたスライドガラスの表側中央付近（裏側に○印が描いてある）に接触させ，血液をスライドガラス上につける。
・必要に応じてこの操作を繰り返し，血液の滴下量を調整する。
4) 角型カバーガラスを図1のように持って，滴下した血液の少し左側に図2のようにつけ，このまま右側にわずかにずらして血液に接触させる（図3，①②）。すると，血液はカバーガラスとスライドガラスの境界部に広がるので，次にカバーガラスをスライドガラスの左端まで素早くなめらかにすべらせる（図3，③④）。
・カバーガラスの持ち方は各自工夫して良い。
5) スライドガラスをしっかりと手で持って振り，風を当てて血液をよく乾燥させる。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig1.png

図1. 角型カバーガラスの持ち方　図2. カバーガラスは血液の少し左側につけてから右にずらす

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig2.png

図3. カバーガラスの動かし方（側面図）　注意：塗抹後、カバーガラスはスライドガラスにかけない

手順2　以下の要領で，標本を固定・染色する。
1) 血液を塗布したスライドガラスを固定液につけ，ゆっくりと10回上下する。
2) スライドガラスの端をキムワイプにつけ，余分な固定液を吸い取る。
3) 次いで，上記1)，2)の操作を染色液A，Bの順に行う。
4) 洗浄水の入ったプラスチックコップ中で，スライドガラスで水をゆっくりとかき回すようにして，約10秒間標本を洗う。
5) スライドガラスの裏側についた水をキムワイプで拭き取る。スライドガラスの表裏を間違えないように注意する。
6) スライドガラスをしっかりと手で持って振り，よく乾燥させる。血液を塗抹した部分以外は，キムワイプで水を吸い取ってもよい。
7) 血球が薄紫色に染まっているのが肉眼で観察される。全体に均一に塗布されているのが理想だが，塗布ムラがあっても部分的に使用可能であり，観察には支障がないことが多い。

手順3　染色・乾燥した標本を顕微鏡で観察し，できるだけ血球が均一に塗布されている場所を探す（図4参照）。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig3.png

適当な塗布状態　観察に適さない例1（血球が多数重なりあっている）　観察に適さない例2（血球密度が低すぎる）

図4. 血液の塗布状態

手順4　スライドガラスを顕微鏡から取り出し，手順3で特定した場所（大体で良い）に，新しいつまようじを使って封入剤を少量たらす。
・つまようじの後端を封入剤につけて少量をとる。
・つまようじが直接スライドガラスに触れないように注意する。

手順5　次の注意に従って，封入剤をたらした場所に封入用の丸型カバーガラス（格子入り）を載せ，約5分間放置してなじませる。
・スライドガラスの白く塗ってある側を右にする。
・丸型カバーガラスの向きに注意すること（図5を参照）。
・丸型カバーガラスを保持する際は，ピンセットを使っても良い。
・はみ出した封入剤は拭き取らない。
・一度封入に使用した丸型カバーガラスは再利用できないので，スライドガラスからはがさないこと。
・封入に失敗した場合，別に作製した標本と2枚目の丸型カバーガラスを使用しても良いが，解答に用いるのはどちらか一方のみとする。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig4.png

図5. 丸型カバーガラス（格子入り）の向き　カバーガラス（丸型）は，太矢印で示した◎印が左に，細矢印で示した小さな文字が上になるようにしてスライドガラスに載せる。

手順6　封入した標本を顕微鏡で観察する。次の注意に従って，4倍もしくは10倍の対物レンズを用いて，染色された血球とスライドガラスの格子を確認する（図6）。
・スライドガラスの白く塗ってある方を右側にして顕微鏡にセットする。
・血球にピントが合った状態だと格子や記号がぼやける（図6左）が，少しピントを変えるとはっきり見える（図6右）。
・観察時は血球にピントを合わせ，位置を調べるときには視野を変えずに格子と記号にピントを合わせるとよい。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig5.png

図6. 丸型カバーガラスの格子と血球の見え方

・丸型カバーガラス上の記号は，左がアルファベット，右が数字である。なお，次のものは間違いやすいので気をつけること。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig6.png

アルファベットのGと数字の6　アルファベットのIと数字の1　アルファベットのOと数字の0（最初の文字は必ずアルファベット）

図7. 間違いやすい記号例

・個々の血球を観察するには，40倍の対物レンズを用いる。顕微鏡の光源とコンデンサー絞りを最も観察しやすいように調整する。
※この実験では100倍の対物レンズは使用しない。

＜血球の説明＞
赤血球：最も多数観察される血球が赤血球である。赤紫色に染色される（図8に多数認められる小型の血球）。哺乳類の赤血球は核を欠くことが特徴である。
白血球：様々なタイプがあり，そのうち以下のものは図8のように染色される。
好酸球：細胞質は濃いピンク色あるいは赤紫色に染色される。核は濃い青色もしくは青紫色に染まり，複数にくびれる。直径は赤血球の2倍以上。
好中球：細胞質は非常に薄い青紫色あるいは赤紫色に染色される。核は濃い青色もしくは青紫色に染まり，形状は複雑で，コブのあるひも状に見えることもある。直径は赤血球の2倍以上。
リンパ球：細胞は球形もしくはややゆがんだ球形で，大部分を核が占める。核は濃い青色もしくは青紫色に染まる。他の白血球よりもやや小さい。
単球：細胞質は好中球よりもやや濃い青紫色に染色される。核は大きく，濃い青色もしくは青紫色に染まり，くびれがある。直径は赤血球の2倍以上。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-5-fig7.png

図8. 白血球の顕微鏡像　各図中の大きい細胞が白血球，それ以外の小さい細胞が赤血球である。

【問5】前ページで例にあげた4種類の白血球のうち3種類（どの種類を選んでもよい）を同定し，それぞれについて1つの血球細胞を選び，塗抹標本上の位置を以下の要領で解答用紙に記入しなさい。なお，カバーガラスの格子模様の外側は観察対象にしないこと。

＜解答の方法＞
・解答として選んだ白血球の種類を記せ。
・その白血球が位置する格子の番号とその格子内のおおまかな位置を下の例にしたがって解答用紙に記入せよ。
・白血球が3種類見つからなかった場合には、解答用紙の「白血球の種類」欄に“見つからなかった”と記すこと。

白血球位置の解答例

problems.title: Experiment 3 (zebrafish tail fin), Question 7
problems.problem:
Experiment 3 Observation of blood cells in the blood vessels of the zebrafish tail fin

[Introduction]
The tail fin of small fishes such as the medaka and the zebrafish is a very thin organ, but many blood vessels run through it. The blood contains many red blood cells, which can easily be seen with a microscope. For these reasons, the tail fin of small fishes is suitable material for observing the blood flow of a living animal.
In this experiment, the red blood cells flowing in the blood vessels of the tail fin of a zebrafish (white mutant individual) are observed, their shape is grasped in three dimensions, and how the morphological features of red blood cells affect their function is considered. The zebrafish is a fish species that has been used in various kinds of research in recent years because it is easy to rear and breed. The wild type shows a distinct pattern of longitudinal stripes, but various mutants have also been produced, and the white mutant used in this experiment is one of them.
Carry out this experiment following the procedure below and answer Questions 7 and 8. Start the experimental work only after you have fully understood the procedure.
※ You may use both zebrafish in the experiment.

Step 1 Using the fish net, put one zebrafish into the plastic cup containing the anaesthetic solution and wait until the fish turns on its side because of the anaesthesia (about 2–5 minutes).

Step 2 Prepare the slide glass on which the fish will be placed. Put the slide glass on a paper towel and lay a Kimwipe cut to about one eighth of a sheet on the slide glass.

Step 3 Suck the fish that has turned on its side into the dropper head first and transfer it, together with the water, onto the Kimwipe on the slide glass. Then wrap the fish's body in the Kimwipe so that only the tail fin can be seen (Figure 9).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-7-fig1.png

Figure 9. Procedure for making the preparation for observing blood flow in the tail fin.

Step 4 Wipe off the water drops on the back of the slide glass and set it on the stage of the light microscope.
• After about 5 minutes or more in this state, the blood flow gradually becomes weaker. Once the blood flow has stopped completely, observation becomes difficult, so carry out the following observations and answers quickly.

Step 5 Observe the tail fin using the 4× objective lens. Many blood vessels and particles flowing in them are seen. These particles are red blood cells.

Step 6 Choose a suitable blood vessel and observe it in more detail using the 10× objective lens.
• Take care that the objective lens does not touch the fish's body or the Kimwipe.
If water or dirt gets on the objective lens and observation becomes difficult, tell an exam assistant and have the lens cleaned.

[Question 7] Using the modelling clay, shape and reproduce in three dimensions the external form of the red blood cells you observed.
• Use all the clay to make one red blood cell.
• Put the shaped clay in the submission box and hand it in at the end of the exam.
• When you have finished observing, quickly return the fish to the aquarium.
problems.problem_orig:
実験3　ゼブラフィッシュ尾ビレ血管内の血球観察

【はじめに】
メダカやゼブラフィッシュなどの小型魚類の尾ビレはとても薄い器官であるが，その中には多くの血管が走行している。血液中には多数の赤血球が含まれており，顕微鏡を用いて容易に確認できる。これらの理由から，小型魚類の尾ビレは生きた動物の血流を観察する材料として適している。
この実験では，ゼブラフィッシュ（白色変異個体）の尾ビレにある血管中を流れる赤血球を観察し，そのかたちを立体的にとらえるとともに，赤血球の形態的特徴がその機能にどのように影響しているかを考察する。ゼブラフィッシュは，飼育・繁殖の容易さなどから，近年様々な研究に用いられている魚種である。野生型は明瞭な縦じま模様を呈するが，様々な変異体も作出されており，本実験で用いる白色変異個体もそのひとつである。
この実験は以下の手順に従って行い，問7と問8の設問に答えること。十分に手順を理解してから実験操作を始めること。
※　ゼブラフィッシュは2尾とも実験に用いてよい。

手順1　魚すくいネットを用いて，ゼブラフィッシュ1尾を麻酔液の入ったプラスチックコップに入れ，魚が麻酔によって横転するまで待つ（約2～5分間）。

手順2　魚を載せるスライドガラスを準備する。スライドガラスをペーパータオル上に置き，8分の1枚程度に切ったキムワイプをスライドガラスの上に載せておく。

手順3　横転した魚をスポイトに頭から吸い込み，スライドガラスに載せたキムワイプの上に水ごと魚を出して移す。次いで，尾ビレだけが見えるように魚体をキムワイプで包んで置く（図9）。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-3-7-fig1.png

図9. 尾ビレの血流観察標本の作製手順

手順4　スライドガラス裏側の水滴を拭き取り，生物顕微鏡のステージに設置する。
・この状態で約5分以上経過すると，徐々に血流が弱くなってくる。血流が完全に止まると観察が難しくなるので，手早く以下の観察，解答を行うこと。

手順5　4倍の対物レンズを使用して尾ビレを観察する。多数の血管とその中を流れる粒子が観察される。この粒子が赤血球である。

手順6　適当な血管を選び，10倍の対物レンズを用いてより詳しく観察する。
・対物レンズが魚体やキムワイプにつかないように注意すること。
もし対物レンズに水や汚れが付着し，観察しづらくなったら，試験補助者に申し出てレンズを掃除してもらうこと。

【問7】観察した赤血球の外形を，粘土を用いて立体的に成形し再現しなさい。
・すべての粘土を使って1個の赤血球をつくること。
・成形の終わった粘土は提出箱に入れて，試験終了時に提出すること。
・観察が終わった魚は速やかに水槽に戻すこと。

problems.title: Experiment 1 (BAP activity), Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam (biochemistry): question booklet

[Materials required for the experiments]
This experiment uses the apparatus and reagents shown below.

Common to Experiment 1 and Experiment 2
• Micropipette 20 – 1
• Micropipette 200 – 1
• Micropipette 1000 – 1
• Oil-based marker pen – 1
• Stopwatch – 1
• Calculator – 1
• Ruler – 1
• Sellotape – 1
• Plastic container for collecting used tips – 1
• Safety glasses – 1
• Laboratory gloves – 1
• 1.5 mL tubes (pack of 30) – 1 bag
• 15 mL tube – 1
• Filter tips for micropipette 20 – 1 box
• Filter tips for micropipette 200 – 1 box
• Filter tips for micropipette 1000 – 1 box
• 96-well microplate – 1
• Test BAP solution (unknown concentration) (1.5 mL tube) – 1

Experiment 1
• 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0) (15 mL tube) – 1
• Activity-assay solution (15 mL tube) – 1
• Enzyme-reaction stop solution (15 mL tube) – 1
• 10 mM p-nitrophenol aqueous solution (1.5 mL tube) – 1

Experiment 2
• Protein standard solution (100 µg/mL) (1.5 mL tube) – 1
• Protein colour reagent (15 mL tube) – 1
• Desalted water (15 mL tube) – 1

[Introduction]
Proteins make up more than 50% of the dry weight of most cells and play important roles in the activities of life. Among them, the most important type of protein is the enzyme. Enzymes act as catalysts that regulate the metabolism of organisms and selectively increase the rates of the chemical reactions that take place in cells. By investigating the properties of various enzymes, the mechanisms of life can be clarified.

Alkaline phosphatase is an enzyme present widely, from bacteria to higher animals; it hydrolyses phosphate esters to produce an alcohol (or a phenol) and inorganic phosphate (Equation 1). The compound broken down in this case is called the substrate. In (Equation 1), the phosphate ester ($\mathrm{R{-}O{-}PO_3H_2}$) is the substrate of alkaline phosphatase.

$$\mathrm{R{-}O{-}PO_3H_2 + H_2O \rightarrow R{-}OH + H_3PO_4} \qquad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

In this practical exam, the biochemical properties of an alkaline phosphatase of bacterial origin (Bacterial Alkaline Phosphatase; hereafter abbreviated BAP) are investigated. Each competitor is given 1 mL of a BAP solution of unknown concentration as the sample (hereafter called the "test BAP solution"). Using it, carry out Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 and answer Questions 1 to 9. Experiment 3 is a hypothetical experiment, so read the outline of the experiment carefully and then answer Question 10.
If you can judge that an experiment is not going well, or if you have not obtained good data, you may redo the experiment from the beginning.

Experiment 1 Measurement of the enzyme activity of the test BAP solution

[Outline of the experiment]
Following the [Experimental procedure] on pages 6–8, measure the enzyme activity of the test BAP solution and calculate the amount of enzyme activity contained in 1 mL of the test BAP solution. Before starting the experimental procedure, read the [Principle of the BAP activity assay] below carefully and understand it.

[Principle of the BAP activity assay]
When p-nitrophenyl phosphate (hereafter abbreviated PNPP) is used as the substrate, p-nitrophenol is produced by enzymatic hydrolysis (Equation 2). p-Nitrophenol is yellow in alkaline solution, and when its absorption spectrum is measured it is known to absorb visible light of wavelength 405 nm strongly. The substrate PNPP, on the other hand, is colourless and transparent and does not absorb light of 405 nm. Using this, the change over time in the amount of p-nitrophenol produced by the enzyme reaction can be followed by measuring the absorbance (the strength of absorption) at 405 nm.
In general, the BAP activity assay uses PNPP as the substrate, and the enzyme reaction is carried out at 25 °C in 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0). Under these reaction conditions, the amount of enzyme activity that produces 1 µmol ($10^{-6}$ mol) of p-nitrophenol in 1 minute is defined as 1 U (unit). The actual activity measurement and the calculation of the amount of enzyme activity are done as follows. First, the enzyme reaction is started with PNPP as the substrate; after a fixed time the reaction is stopped and the absorbance at 405 nm is measured. Since the absorbance is proportional to the molar concentration of p-nitrophenol, the molar concentration of the p-nitrophenol contained in the reaction solution, that is, of the p-nitrophenol produced by the enzyme reaction, can be found. From the molar concentration and the volume of the reaction solution, the number of moles of p-nitrophenol in the reaction solution is obtained, and by further dividing by the reaction time, the number of moles of p-nitrophenol produced by the enzyme reaction in 1 minute can be calculated. Finally, the amount of enzyme activity (unit: U) is determined following the definition above.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-4-1-fig1.png

(Equation 2)

Figure labels (Japanese → English): p-ニトロフェノール = p-nitrophenol; リン酸 = phosphoric acid.

[Experimental procedure]
In Experiment 1 a solution containing sodium hydroxide (NaOH), a strongly alkaline poisonous substance, is handled, so always wear laboratory gloves and safety glasses during all experimental operations.

1) Following ①–⑤ below, carry out the enzyme reaction with two samples: the test BAP solution and a blank (a control experiment without BAP).
① The following reagents are used for the enzyme reaction.
• 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0)
• Test BAP solution: 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0) containing BAP (unknown concentration)
• Activity-assay solution: 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0) containing 2 mM PNPP
• Enzyme-reaction stop solution: 10 M NaOH aqueous solution [poisonous substance]
② Write "BAP" and "blank", respectively, on two 1.5 mL tubes. Add 490 µL of activity-assay solution to each tube. To this add 10 µL of the test BAP solution or of 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0), quickly close the lid of the tube, turn it upside down 3 or 4 times to mix the liquid (mixing by inversion) and start the reaction (for the composition see Table 1).
[Note] The BAP and blank reactions need not be started at the same time. You may start one after the other has finished, or start them a few seconds apart.

Table 1 Composition of the reaction solutions

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|} \hline \text{Tube} & \text{BAP} & \text{Blank} \\ \hline \text{Activity-assay solution} & 490 & 490 \\ \hline \text{Test BAP solution} & 10 & 0 \\ \hline \text{1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.0)} & 0 & 10 \\ \hline \end{array} \qquad (\text{unit: } \mu\text{L})$$

③ Leave to stand at room temperature (25 °C) for 3 minutes (enzyme reaction).
④ Add 500 µL of enzyme-reaction stop solution and mix quickly by inversion (stopping the reaction).
⑤ Leave the reaction solutions of ④ to stand at room temperature until the next operation 2) is finished.

2) To calculate the amount of enzyme activity, it is necessary to know the number of moles of p-nitrophenol produced by the enzyme reaction. In this experiment, the absorbances of p-nitrophenol standard solutions of known concentration are measured to make a molar concentration–absorbance standard line, and using it the molar concentration of p-nitrophenol in the enzyme-reaction solution is found and the number of moles is calculated. For this purpose, following ①–⑤ below, prepare standard solutions of six molar concentrations: 0, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50 and 100 µM. Note that 1 µM = 1 µmol/L.
① The following reagents are used to prepare the standard solutions.
• 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0)
• Enzyme-reaction stop solution [poisonous substance]
• 10 mM p-nitrophenol aqueous solution
② In a 15 mL tube, prepare 10 mL of a solution of 1 M Tris-HCl buffer (pH 8.0) and enzyme-reaction stop solution mixed 1:1 (by volume) (hereafter called the "dilution solution").
③ Write 0, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50 and 100, respectively, on six 1.5 mL tubes (the numbers mean the molar concentration of p-nitrophenol). Add 990 µL of dilution solution to the "100" tube, add 10 µL of 10 mM p-nitrophenol aqueous solution to it and mix by inversion. This is the 100 µM standard solution.
④ Prepare a dilution series of p-nitrophenol solutions as follows. Add 500 µL of dilution solution to each of the 1.5 mL tubes "50", "25", "12.5" and "6.25". Take 500 µL of the 100 µM standard solution prepared in ③ above, transfer it to the "50" tube and mix well by inversion. This is the 50 µM standard solution. Next, transfer 500 µL of the 50 µM standard solution to the "25" tube and mix; this is the 25 µM standard solution. Repeat the same operation to prepare the 12.5 and 6.25 µM standard solutions as well.
⑤ Add only 500 µL of dilution solution to the "0" 1.5 mL tube; this is the 0 µM standard solution.

3) Following Table 2 on the next page, transfer 200 µL each of the reaction solutions prepared in operation 1) and of the p-nitrophenol standard solutions prepared in operation 2) to the 96-well microplate (2 wells per solution). After writing your name-tag number in the upper right corner of the microplate, raise your hand and tell an exam assistant that it is ready for measurement. The exam assistant will measure the absorbance (405 nm) with a plate reader, so receive the paper on which the measurement results are printed.

Table 2 Arrangement of the solutions (part of the 96-well microplate)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|l} \hline \text{BAP} & \text{BAP} & \text{Blank} & \text{Blank} & \diagup & \diagup & \text{Operation 1) [reaction solutions]} \\ \hline 0~\mu\text{M} & 6.25~\mu\text{M} & 12.5~\mu\text{M} & 25~\mu\text{M} & 50~\mu\text{M} & 100~\mu\text{M} & \text{Operation 2) [standard solutions]} \\ \hline 0~\mu\text{M} & 6.25~\mu\text{M} & 12.5~\mu\text{M} & 25~\mu\text{M} & 50~\mu\text{M} & 100~\mu\text{M} & \\ \hline \end{array}$$

[Note] Under the measurement conditions of the plate reader used in Experiment 1, measured values higher than the true absorbance are given. Therefore, even a sample that should have no absorbance gives a measured value slightly higher than 0. To know the exact absorbance of each solution, a zero-point correction must be made by subtracting the excess. Here, taking the true absorbance of the 0 µM p-nitrophenol standard solution to be 0, the value obtained by subtracting the measured absorbance of the 0 µM p-nitrophenol standard solution from the measured absorbance of each solution is called the "zero-point-corrected absorbance". In the following questions, always use the zero-point-corrected absorbances.

[Question 1] Using the results of the absorbance measurement of the p-nitrophenol standard solutions, draw the molar concentration–absorbance (zero-point-corrected values) standard line on the graph paper of the answer sheet. Also express the standard line as the equation of a linear function. Draw it considering what values should be taken on the horizontal and vertical axes, and how the axes should be named. Absorbance is a dimensionless value, so no unit needs to be attached. Stick the printed paper with the absorbance measurement results used in this question onto the answer sheet (page 1) and submit it (use Sellotape).

実験試験（生化学）問題冊子

【実験に必要なもの】
この実験では，下に示した器具および試薬を使う。

実験1と実験2共通
□マイクロピペット20　1本
□マイクロピペット200　1本
□マイクロピペット1000　1本
□油性ペン　1本
□ストップウォッチ　1個
□電卓　1個
□定規　1個
□セロテープ　1個
□廃チップ回収用プラスチック容器　1個
□保護メガネ　1個
□実験用手袋　1個
□1.5 mL容チューブ（30本入り）　1袋
□15 mL容チューブ　1本
□マイクロピペット20用フィルター付チップ　1箱
□マイクロピペット200用フィルター付チップ　1箱
□マイクロピペット1000用フィルター付チップ　1箱
□96穴マイクロプレート　1個
□供試BAP溶液（濃度未知）（1.5 mL容チューブ）　1本

実験1
□1 M Tris-HCl緩衝液（pH 8.0）（15 mL容チューブ）　1本
□活性測定用溶液（15 mL容チューブ）　1本
□酵素反応停止液（15 mL容チューブ）　1本
□10 mM p-ニトロフェノール水溶液（1.5 mL容チューブ）　1本

実験2
□タンパク質標準液（100 µg/mL）（1.5 mL容チューブ）　1本
□タンパク質発色試薬（15 mL容チューブ）　1本
□脱塩水（15 mL容チューブ）　1本

【はじめに】
タンパク質は，大部分の細胞で乾燥重量の50%以上を占めていて，生命活動で重要な役割を担っている。その中で，もっとも重要なタイプのタンパク質が酵素である。酵素には，触媒として生物の代謝を調節し，細胞内で起こる化学反応の速度を選択的に高める役割がある。様々な酵素の性質を調べることで，生命の仕組みを明らかにすることができる。

アルカリ性フォスファターゼは，細菌から高等動物まで幅広く存在する酵素であり，リン酸エステルを加水分解して，アルコール（またはフェノール）と無機リン酸を生成させる（式1）。このとき分解される化合物を基質と呼ぶ。（式1）では，リン酸エステル（$\mathrm{R{-}O{-}PO_3H_2}$）がアルカリ性フォスファターゼの基質である。

$$\mathrm{R{-}O{-}PO_3H_2 + H_2O \rightarrow R{-}OH + H_3PO_4} \qquad \text{（式1）}$$

本実験試験では，細菌由来のアルカリ性フォスファターゼ（Bacterial Alkaline Phosphatase; 以下BAPと略す）の生化学的性質を調べる。各選手には濃度未知のBAP溶液1 mLが試料として与えられる（以下「供試BAP溶液」と呼ぶ）。それを用いて実験1と実験2を実施し，問1～問9に答えなさい。また，実験3は仮想実験であるので，実験の概要をよく読んでから問10に答えなさい。
なお，実験がうまくいってないと判断できる場合，あるいは良いデータが得られなかった場合は，実験を最初からやり直しても良い。

実験1　供試BAP溶液の酵素活性の測定

【実験の概要】
6～8ページの【実験操作】に従って，供試BAP溶液の酵素活性を測定し，供試BAP溶液1 mL中に含まれる酵素活性量を算出する。実験操作に入る前に，下記の【BAPの活性測定法の原理】をよく読んで理解しておくこと。

【BAPの活性測定法の原理】
基質としてリン酸p-ニトロフェニル（p-nitrophenyl phosphate; 以下PNPPと略す）を用いると，酵素的加水分解によってp-ニトロフェノールが生成する（式2）。p-ニトロフェノールはアルカリ性溶液中では黄色に呈色し，吸収スペクトルを測定すると405 nmの波長の可視光をよく吸収することが分かっている。一方，基質のPNPPは無色透明で，405 nmの光を吸収しない。このことを利用すれば，酵素反応によって生成するp-ニトロフェノール量の経時変化を，405 nmでの吸光度（吸収の強さ）を測定することによって追跡できる。
一般にBAPの活性測定は，PNPPを基質として用い，1 M Tris-HCl緩衝液（pH 8.0）中25℃で酵素反応をおこなう。この反応条件下で，1分間に1 µmol（$10^{-6}$ mol）のp-ニトロフェノールを生成させる酵素活性量を1 U（ユニット）と定義する。実際の活性測定および酵素活性量の算出は次のようにしておこなう。まず，PNPPを基質として酵素反応を開始し，一定時間後に反応を停止させて405 nmでの吸光度を測定する。吸光度とp-ニトロフェノールのモル濃度が比例関係にあることから，反応液に含まれるp-ニトロフェノール，すなわち酵素反応によって生成したp-ニトロフェノールのモル濃度を知ることができる。モル濃度と反応液の容積から反応液中のp-ニトロフェノールのモル数が求められ，さらに反応時間で割ることによって1分間の酵素反応によって生成したp-ニトロフェノールのモル数を算出できる。最後に，上記の定義に従って酵素活性量（単位; U）を決定する。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-4-1-fig1.png

（式2）

【実験操作】
実験1では強アルカリ性の劇物である水酸化ナトリウム（NaOH）を含む溶液を扱うため，全ての実験操作で実験用手袋と保護メガネを必ず着用すること。

1) 以下の①～⑤に従って，供試BAP溶液およびブランク（BAPを含まない対照実験）の2つの試料について酵素反応をおこなう。
①　酵素反応には以下の試薬類を使用する。
・1 M Tris-HCl緩衝液（pH 8.0）
・供試BAP溶液：BAP（濃度未知）を含む1 M Tris-HCl緩衝液（pH 8.0）
・活性測定用溶液：2 mM PNPPを含む1 M Tris-HCl緩衝液（pH 8.0）
・酵素反応停止液：10 M NaOH水溶液［劇物］
②　2本の1.5 mL容チューブに，それぞれBAP，ブランクと書く。各チューブに活性測定用溶液を490 µL加える。これに供試BAP溶液または1 M Tris-HCl緩衝液（pH 8.0）を10 µL加え，素早くチューブのフタを閉めて3，4回逆さまにして液を混ぜ（転倒混和），反応を開始する（組成については表1を参照）。
［注意］BAPとブランクの反応は同時に開始する必要はない。一方が終わってからもう一方を開始してもよいし，何秒かずらして開始してもよい。

表1　反応液の組成

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|} \hline \text{チューブ} & \text{BAP} & \text{ブランク} \\ \hline \text{活性測定用溶液} & 490 & 490 \\ \hline \text{供試BAP溶液} & 10 & 0 \\ \hline \text{1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.0)} & 0 & 10 \\ \hline \end{array} \qquad (\text{単位：} \mu\text{L})$$

③　室温（25℃）で3分間静置する（酵素反応）。
④　酵素反応停止液を500 µL加え，素早く転倒混和する（反応停止）。
⑤　次の操作2）が終わるまで，④の反応液は室温で静置しておく。

2）酵素の活性量の算出において，酵素反応によって生成したp-ニトロフェノールのモル数を知る必要がある。本実験では，濃度既知のp-ニトロフェノール標準液の吸光度を測定して，モル濃度－吸光度の標準直線を作成し，それを利用して酵素反応液中のp-ニトロフェノールのモル濃度を求め，モル数を算出する。そのために，以下の①～⑤に従って，0，6.25，12.5，25，50，100 µMの6種類のモル濃度の標準液を調製する。なお，1 µM = 1 µmol/Lである。
①　標準液の調製には以下の試薬類を使用する。
・1 M Tris-HCl緩衝液（pH 8.0）
・酵素反応停止液［劇物］
・10 mM p-ニトロフェノール水溶液
②　1 M Tris-HCl緩衝液（pH 8.0）と酵素反応停止液を1:1（容積比）で混合した溶液（以下「希釈用溶液」と呼ぶ）を15 mL容チューブに10 mL調製する。
③　6本の1.5 mL容チューブに，それぞれ0，6.25，12.5，25，50，100と書く（数字はp-ニトロフェノールのモル濃度を意味する）。「100」のチューブに990 µLの希釈用溶液を加え，これに10 mM p-ニトロフェノール水溶液を10 µL加え，転倒混和する。これを100 µM標準液とする。
④　以下の要領で，p-ニトロフェノールの希釈系列の溶液を調製する。「50」「25」「12.5」「6.25」の1.5 mL容チューブそれぞれに500 µLの希釈用溶液を加える。上記③で調製した100 µM標準液を500 µL取り，「50」のチューブに移し，よく転倒混和する。これを50 µM標準液とする。次に，50 µM標準液500 µLを「25」のチューブに移して混和し，これを25 µM標準液とする。同様の操作を繰り返し，12.5，6.25 µM標準液も調製する。
⑤「0」の1.5 mL容チューブには，希釈用溶液のみを500 µL加え，これを0 µM標準液とする。

3）次ページの表2に従って，操作1）で調製した反応液および操作2）で調製したp-ニトロフェノール標準液を各200 µLずつ96穴マイクロプレートへ移す（1つの溶液につき2穴ずつ）。マイクロプレートの右上の角に自分の名札番号を書いた後，挙手して試験補助者に測定の用意ができたことを知らせる。試験補助者がプレートリーダーで吸光度（405 nm）を測定するので，その測定結果がプリントされた紙を受け取る。

表2　溶液の配置（96穴マイクロプレートの一部）

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|l} \hline \text{BAP} & \text{BAP} & \text{ブランク} & \text{ブランク} & \diagup & \diagup & \text{操作1)【反応液】} \\ \hline 0~\mu\text{M} & 6.25~\mu\text{M} & 12.5~\mu\text{M} & 25~\mu\text{M} & 50~\mu\text{M} & 100~\mu\text{M} & \text{操作2)【標準液】} \\ \hline 0~\mu\text{M} & 6.25~\mu\text{M} & 12.5~\mu\text{M} & 25~\mu\text{M} & 50~\mu\text{M} & 100~\mu\text{M} & \\ \hline \end{array}$$

［注意］実験1で用いるプレートリーダーの測定条件では，真の吸光度よりも高い測定値を与えてしまう。そのため，吸光度を持たないはずの試料であっても，0よりもわずかに高い測定値になる。各溶液の正確な吸光度を知るためには，高くなった分を差し引いてゼロ点補正をおこなう必要がある。ここでは，0 µM p-ニトロフェノール標準液の真の吸光度が0になると考えて，各溶液の吸光度の測定値から0 µM p-ニトロフェノール標準液の吸光度の測定値を引いた値を「ゼロ点補正した吸光度」とする。以下の問では，全てゼロ点補正した吸光度を用いて考えること。

【問1】　p-ニトロフェノール標準液の吸光度測定の結果を用いて，モル濃度－吸光度（ゼロ点補正した値）の標準直線を解答用紙のグラフ用紙に描きなさい。また，標準直線を一次関数の数式で表しなさい。横軸，縦軸にはそれぞれ何の数値をとったらよいか，また軸の名称はどのように付けるかを考えて描くこと。吸光度は無次元の値であるので，単位をつける必要はない。なお，本問で使用した吸光度測定結果のプリント紙は，解答用紙（1ページ）に貼付して提出しなさい（セロテープを使用）。

problems.title: Experiment 2 (protein and specific activity), Question 5
problems.problem:
Experiment 2 Protein determination of the test BAP solution and calculation of the specific activity

[Outline of the experiment]
Following the [Experimental procedure] on pages 9 and 10, measure the protein concentration of the test BAP solution and calculate the specific activity of BAP from the measured values obtained. Before starting the experimental procedure, read [Specific activity of enzymes] and [Principle of the colorimetric determination of proteins – the Bradford method –] carefully and understand them.

[Specific activity of enzymes]
To understand correctly the properties of an enzyme as a protein or as a catalyst, the enzyme must be purified. As an index of the degree of this purification, the "specific activity" is often used. The specific activity is the enzyme activity per 1 mg of protein in the sample containing the enzyme; to find it, the enzyme activity in the sample (already calculated in Experiment 1) and the amount of protein must be measured.

[Principle of the colorimetric determination of proteins – the Bradford method –]
When the dye Coomassie Brilliant Blue G250 binds to the side chains of basic amino acids and aromatic amino acids in proteins, its peak of visible-light absorption shifts from 465 nm to 595 nm, and its colour changes from brown to blue. Since the protein concentration and the absorbance at 595 nm are then proportional, the protein concentration in a solution can be determined by making a standard line with protein standard solutions of known concentration. The method of protein determination that uses this is called the Bradford method. In this practical exam, a bovine serum albumin solution is used as the protein standard solution.

[Experimental procedure]
1) To make the standard line, prepare a dilution series of the protein standard solution. On five 1.5 mL tubes write the concentrations of the protein solutions to be prepared, 0, 6.25, 12.5, 25 and 50, and put 0.5 mL of desalted water into each. Next, transfer 0.5 mL of the 100 µg/mL standard solution to the "50" tube and mix by inversion. This is the 50 µg/mL standard solution. In the same way, transfer 0.5 mL of the 50 µg/mL standard solution to the "25" tube; this is the 25 µg/mL standard solution. Repeat the same operation to prepare the 12.5 and 6.25 µg/mL standard solutions as well (the "0" tube contains only desalted water).

2) Write 0, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50, 100 and BAP on seven 1.5 mL tubes. Transfer 50 µL of each standard solution prepared in 1) (0–100 µg/mL) to the tube with the corresponding label. Into the "BAP" tube transfer 50 µL of the test BAP solution. Then add 0.5 mL of protein colour reagent to all these tubes. After mixing by inversion, leave them to stand at room temperature for 3 minutes.

3) As in Table 3, transfer 200 µL of each reaction solution of 2) to the 96-well microplate (2 wells per reaction solution) and promptly tell an exam assistant by raising your hand. The exam assistant will measure the absorbance (595 nm) with a plate reader, so receive the paper on which the measurement results are printed.

Table 3 Arrangement of the reaction solutions (part of the 96-well microplate)

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline 0 & 6.25 & 12.5 & 25 & 50 & 100 & \text{BAP} \\ \hline 0 & 6.25 & 12.5 & 25 & 50 & 100 & \text{BAP} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

[Question 5] On the basis of the measurement results of the standard solutions, draw the standard line on the graph paper of the answer sheet. Further, express the standard line as the equation of a linear function. Consider what values should be taken on the horizontal and vertical axes, and how the axes should be named, and write them on the answer sheet. Stick the printed paper with the absorbance measurement results used in this question onto the answer sheet (page 3) and submit it (use Sellotape).
problems.problem_orig:
実験2　供試BAP溶液のタンパク質の定量と比活性の算出

【実験の概要】
9, 10ページの【実験操作】に従って，供試BAP溶液のタンパク質濃度を測定し，得られた測定値からBAPの比活性を算出する。実験操作に入る前に，【酵素の比活性】，【タンパク質の比色定量の原理－ブラッドフォード法－】をよく読んで理解すること。

【酵素の比活性】
酵素のタンパク質あるいは触媒としての性質を正しく理解するためには，その酵素の精製が必要である。この精製の度合いの指標として，「比活性」がしばしば用いられる。比活性とは，酵素が含まれる試料中のタンパク質1 mg当たりの酵素活性であり，これを求めるためには，試料中の酵素活性（実験1で算出済み）とタンパク質量を測定する必要がある。

【タンパク質の比色定量の原理－ブラッドフォード法－】
クマシーブリリアントブルーG250という色素は，タンパク質中の塩基性アミノ酸や芳香族アミノ酸の側鎖と結合した時，可視光の吸収のピークが465 nmから595 nmへシフトし，茶色から青色へ呈色する。このとき，タンパク質濃度と595 nmの吸光度は比例関係にあるため，既知濃度のタンパク質標準液を用いて標準直線を作成することにより，溶液中のタンパク質濃度を決定することができる。これを利用したタンパク質定量法は，ブラッドフォード法と呼ばれる。また，本実験試験ではタンパク質標準液として，ウシ血清アルブミン溶液を使用する。

【実験操作】
1）標準直線を作成するため，タンパク質標準液の希釈系列の溶液を調製する。5本の1.5 mL容チューブに，これから調製するタンパク質溶液の濃度0，6.25，12.5，25，50を書き，それぞれに0.5 mLの脱塩水を移す。次に，100 µg/mL標準液の0.5 mLを「50」のチューブに移し，転倒混和する。これを50 µg/mL標準液とする。同様に，50 µg/mL標準液の0.5 mLを「25」のチューブに移し，これを25 µg/mL標準液とする。同様の操作を繰り返し，12.5，6.25 µg/mL標準液も調製する（「0」のチューブには，脱塩水のみが入っている）。

2）7本の1.5 mL容チューブに，0，6.25，12.5，25，50，100，およびBAPと書く。1）で調製した各標準液（0～100 µg/mL）の50 µLを，対応するラベルのチューブに移す。「BAP」のチューブには，50 µLの供試BAP溶液を移す。続いて，これらすべてのチューブに，0.5 mLのタンパク質発色試薬を加える。転倒混和した後，3分間，室温で静置する。

3）表3のように，2）の反応液の各200 µLを96穴マイクロプレートへ移し（1つの反応液につき，2穴ずつ），挙手によって速やかに試験補助者に知らせる。試験補助者がプレートリーダーで吸光度（595 nm）を測定するので，その測定結果がプリントされた紙を受け取る。

表3　反応液の配置（96穴マイクロプレートの一部）

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline 0 & 6.25 & 12.5 & 25 & 50 & 100 & \text{BAP} \\ \hline 0 & 6.25 & 12.5 & 25 & 50 & 100 & \text{BAP} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

【問5】標準液の測定結果を元に，解答用紙のグラフ用紙に標準直線を描きなさい。さらにその標準直線を一次関数の数式で表しなさい。横軸，縦軸にはそれぞれ何の数値をとったらよいか，また軸の名称はどのように付けるかを考えて解答用紙に記入しなさい。なお，本問で使用した吸光度測定結果のプリント紙は，解答用紙（3ページ）に貼付して提出しなさい（セロテープを使用）。

problems.title: Experiment 3 (carboxypeptidase Y, hypothetical), Question 10
problems.problem:
Experiment 3 (hypothetical) Inferring the primary structure of BAP with carboxypeptidase Y

[Outline of the experiment]
Carboxypeptidase Y (Carboxypeptidase Y; hereafter abbreviated CPY) is an enzyme that catalyses the hydrolysis of proteins. CPY cleaves off the amino acids at the carboxy terminus of a protein one at a time. The cleaved amino acid is released from the main body of the protein. In the protein remaining after the original carboxy-terminal amino acid has been released, a new carboxy terminus arises. The new carboxy-terminal amino acid is the amino acid just before the original carboxy terminus. The amino acid that has thus newly become the carboxy terminus is in turn acted on by CPY and is released from the main body of the protein later than the first amino acid. By following the change over time in the kinds and amounts of the amino acids released by the action of CPY, the order of the amino acids near the carboxy terminus of a protein can be found.

[Question 10] Figure 2 shows the change over time in the kinds and amounts of the amino acids released after the start of the digestion of $1 \times 10^{-9}$ mol of BAP with CPY. From the experimental results of Figure 2, the order of 4 amino acids, including the original carboxy-terminal amino acid of BAP, can be inferred. Give the inferred order with the original carboxy-terminal amino acid on the far right.

problems.problem_orig:
実験3（仮想）カルボキシペプチダーゼYによるBAPの一次構造の推定

【実験の概要】
カルボキシペプチダーゼY（Carboxypeptidase Y; 以下CPYと略す）は，タンパク質の加水分解を触媒する酵素である。CPYはタンパク質中のカルボキシ末端のアミノ酸を一つずつ切断する。切断されたアミノ酸はタンパク質本体から遊離する。タンパク質から本来のカルボキシ末端のアミノ酸が遊離した残りのタンパク質には，新たなカルボキシ末端が生じる。新たなカルボキシ末端のアミノ酸は，本来のカルボキシ末端のひとつ前のアミノ酸ということになる。こうして新たにカルボキシ末端となったアミノ酸は，さらにCPYの作用を受けて最初のアミノ酸に遅れてタンパク質本体から遊離する。CPYの働きによって遊離したアミノ酸の種類と量の時間変化を追うことで，タンパク質のカルボキシ末端付近のアミノ酸の配列順序を知ることができる。

【問10】　図2は，$1 \times 10^{-9}$ molのBAPをCPYで分解し始めてから遊離するアミノ酸の種類と量の経時変化を示している。図2の実験結果から，BAPの本来のカルボキシ末端のアミノ酸を含めて4個のアミノ酸の配列順序を推定できる。推定した配列順序を本来のカルボキシ末端のアミノ酸が一番右側になるようにして答えなさい。

Experiment 1 Observation of rice

[Introduction]
The grass family (Poaceae) is a large taxonomic group of about 10,000 species; besides providing the major cereals such as rice, wheat and maize, its members are used in many ways, for example as livestock fodder, as lawn grass and as a raw material for sugar (sugar cane). In grasses, as in other monocots, the structure of the flower is trimerous (the stamens and perianth parts are multiples of 3), but in the course of their diversification various parts of the flower have become reduced and vestigial, or have been lost.
Figure 2 below shows the basic structure of the grass flower. In grasses, several florets gather to form a spikelet. On the outermost side of the spikelet is the first glume, and inside it is the second glume. Enclosed by the first and second glumes there are several florets. A floret consists, in order from the outside, of the lemma, the palea, the lodicules, the stamens and the pistil.
In this experiment you will observe the rice flower in detail and consider the morphological evolution of the flowers of the grass family.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-5-1-fig2.png

Figure 2. Whole views of the spikelet and floret of wild oat (カラスムギ), and dissection of the floret

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 第1苞穎 = first glume; 第2苞穎 = second glume; 小穂 = spikelet; 小花 = floret; 外花穎 = lemma; 内花穎 = palea; 芒 = awn; 葯 = anther; 柱頭 = stigma; 鱗皮 = lodicule.

[Question 1] Figure 2 above shows the flower of wild oat, but in this experiment you will observe the flower of rice. Following Figure 2, draw on the answer sheet ① a whole view of the spikelet, ② a whole view of the floret and ③ a dissection of the floret of rice. Also, referring to the [Introduction] text above and to Figure 2, write the names of the parts. problems.title: Experiment 2 (plant polysaccharides), Question 5
problems.problem:
Experiment 2 Analysis of plant polysaccharides

[Introduction]
Starch is a polysaccharide made of glucose (grape sugar), the energy source of cells, and it functions as an energy-storage substance. Starch is composed of amylose, which has a linear structure, and amylopectin, which has a branched structure; in rice it is abundant in the endosperm cells. Kinds of rice include glutinous rice (もち米), whose starch consists almost entirely of amylopectin, and non-glutinous rice (うるち米), which contains 20–30% amylose. On the other hand, cellulose, the fibrous component of plant cell walls, is also a polysaccharide made of glucose, but the structure of the glucose and the type of bond differ from those of starch.

[Qualitative analysis of polysaccharides]
Polysaccharides such as starch and cellulose can be hydrolysed by glucanases. Glucanases include, for example, one that cleaves the 1→4 bonds of α-glucose in polysaccharides (glucanase I) and a glucanase that hydrolyses the 1→4 bonds of β-glucose (glucanase II). In this experiment you will deduce from the experimental results what kinds of polysaccharide the samples you have been given contain. After the polysaccharides have been hydrolysed with a glucanase, the reducing sugars obtained (sugars such as glucose and maltose that form an aldehyde group in basic solution) are reacted with the sugar-detection reagent, and the red precipitate formed is checked.
The polysaccharides are also coloured by the iodine–starch reaction. The iodine–starch reaction is a reaction in which a colour appears because iodine is taken up into the helical structure formed by the straight glucose-chain parts of starch; when the helices formed by the straight glucose-chain parts are long, it gives a blue colour, and as the helix length becomes shorter it gives blue-violet, red-violet and red-brown. On the other hand, when the helices are extremely short or absent, it is colourless. From the results of the hydrolysis of the polysaccharides and of the colour reaction, you will consider the properties of starch and cellulose.

Operation 1 Hydrolysis of starch and cellulose

1) You have been given the three kinds of sample powder A, B and C in 15 mL tubes, 2 tubes of each, 6 tubes in all. First, add 10 mL of glucanase I solution to one 15 mL tube containing sample powder A and stir well (the sample powder does not dissolve completely, so shake the tube vigorously to suspend it). Next, add 10 mL of glucanase I solution also to each of the 15 mL tubes containing sample powder B and sample powder C, and stir well. To the remaining 15 mL tube of each of sample powders A, B and C, add 10 mL of glucanase II solution each and stir well. Measure the 10 mL of glucanase solution with a Komagome pipette (use the graduations of the Komagome pipette for measuring) and add it to the sample powder.

2) After adding glucanase solution to all the sample powders and suspending them thoroughly for 15 seconds, leave them to stand at room temperature for 5 minutes.

3) Using micropipette 1000, collect 500 µL of supernatant into a new 1.5 mL tube. Take care at this point not to draw in sediment or floating material as far as possible. To show which tube is which combination of sample powder and glucanase solution, write the sample name clearly on the tube lid with the oil-based marker pen, following the example below. Also write your name-tag number (Figure 5).

(Example) For the combination of sample powder A and glucanase I → A-I

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-5-5-fig1.png

Figure 5. Example of labelling the A-I sample of the competitor with name-tag number B90

4) Add 500 µL of sugar-detection reagent to the 500 µL of supernatant collected in the 1.5 mL tube, and mix the contents well by turning the 1.5 mL tube upside down several times (from here on this operation is called mixing by inversion). Heat the liquid in a water bath for 5 minutes and then centrifuge it (2,000 $g$, room temperature, 10 seconds). The water bath and the centrifugation are carried out by the exam assistants, so fit a cap lock to each 1.5 mL tube, insert the tubes into the float (see Figure 6) and then let them know that you are ready by raising your hand (work on the next Operation 2 while waiting for the water bath and centrifugation).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-5-5-fig2.png

Figure 6. How to use the cap locks and the float

Figure labels (Japanese → English): キャップロック = cap lock; 1.5 mL容チューブ = 1.5 mL tube; フロート = float.

5) After receiving the 1.5 mL tubes that have finished the 5-minute water bath and centrifugation, check each sample visually for a red precipitate.

[Question 5] For each glucanase, state which sample powders were hydrolysed by reaction with glucanase I and with II. Submit each 1.5 mL tube in which sugar detection was carried out by putting it in the small box for submitting the experimental samples.
problems.problem_orig:
実験2　植物性多糖類の分析

【はじめに】
デンプンは細胞のエネルギー源であるグルコース（ブドウ糖）からなる多糖類であり，エネルギー貯蔵物質として機能している。デンプンは直鎖状構造を持つアミロースと分枝構造を持つアミロペクチンから構成されており，米では胚乳細胞内に多く含まれている。米の種類には，デンプンがほぼすべてアミロペクチンで構成されているもち米や20～30%のアミロースを含むうるち米がある。一方，植物細胞壁の繊維成分であるセルロースもグルコースからなる多糖類であるが，グルコースの構造や結合様式がデンプンと異なっている。

【多糖類の定性分析】
デンプンやセルロースなどの多糖類は，グルカナーゼによって加水分解することができる。グルカナーゼには，多糖類中のαグルコースの1→4結合を切断するもの（グルカナーゼI）やβグルコースの1→4結合を加水分解するグルカナーゼ（グルカナーゼII）などがある。この実験では配付された試料にどのような多糖類が含まれているのかを実験結果より推察する。多糖類をグルカナーゼで加水分解した後，得られた還元糖（グルコースやマルトースなどの，塩基性溶液中でアルデヒド基を形成する糖のこと）を糖検出試薬と反応させ，生成する赤色沈殿を確認する。
また多糖類をヨウ素デンプン反応によって呈色させる。ヨウ素デンプン反応とは，デンプン中のグルコース直鎖部分が形成するらせん構造の中にヨウ素が取り込まれることによって呈色を示す反応であり，グルコース直鎖部分が形成するらせん長が長い場合には青色を呈し，らせん長が短くなるにつれて青紫色，赤紫色，赤褐色を呈する。一方，らせん長が極めて短い場合やない場合には無色を呈する。多糖類の加水分解と呈色の反応結果をもとにデンプンとセルロースの性質について考察する。

操作１　デンプンとセルロースの加水分解

１）15 mL容チューブに入った3種類の試料粉末A，B，Cはそれぞれ2本ずつ，計6本，配付されている。まず，試料粉末Aが入った1本の15 mL容チューブにグルカナーゼI溶液を10 mL加え，よく撹拌する（試料粉末は完全には溶解しないので，チューブを激しく振って懸濁させる）。次いで，試料粉末Bと試料粉末Cが入った15 mL容チューブそれぞれにもグルカナーゼI溶液を10 mL加え，よく撹拌する。1本ずつ残った試料粉末A, B, Cの各15 mL容チューブには，グルカナーゼII溶液をそれぞれ10 mLずつ加え，よく撹拌する。なお，グルカナーゼ溶液10 mLはコマゴメピペットを用いて計量し（計量はコマゴメピペットの目盛りを参考にする），試料粉末に加える。

２）全ての試料粉末にグルカナーゼ溶液を加え，15秒間しっかりと懸濁した後，室温で5分間静置する。

３）マイクロピペット1000を用い，上清500 µLを新たな1.5 mL容チューブに回収する。この時，なるべく沈殿物や浮遊物を吸い込まないように注意すること。どのチューブがどの試料粉末とグルカナーゼ溶液の組み合わせなのかを示すために，以下の例にならってチューブのふたに油性ペンで明瞭にサンプル名を記すこと。また，名札番号についても記入すること（図5）。

（例）試料粉末Aとグルカナーゼ I の組み合わせの場合　→　A-I

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-5-5-fig1.png

図5. 名札番号がB90の選手のA-Iサンプルの表記例

４）1.5 mL容チューブに回収した上清500 µLに糖検出試薬500 µLを加え，1.5 mL容チューブを数回逆さまに反転させることで内容物をよく混合する（以降，この操作を転倒混和と呼ぶ）。その液を5分間，湯煎した後、遠心分離（2,000 $g$，室温，10秒間）を行う。湯煎と遠心分離は試験補助者が行うため，それぞれの1.5 mL容チューブにキャップロックを取り付け，フロートに差し込んだ後（図6を参照），準備ができたことを挙手により知らせること（湯煎と遠心分離の待ち時間中に次の操作2に取り組むこと）。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2013-5-5-fig2.png

図6. キャップロックとフロートの使用方法

５）5分間の湯煎と遠心分離が終わった1.5 mL容チューブを受け取った後，各サンプルについて赤色沈殿を目視にて確認する。

【問5】グルカナーゼIやIIと反応させてどの試料粉末が加水分解されたかを，グルカナーゼごとにそれぞれ答えなさい。また糖検出を行った各1.5 mL容チューブは実験サンプル提出用小箱に入れて提出すること。

ヨウ素デンプン反応とは，デンプン中のグルコース直鎖部分が形成するらせん構造の中にヨウ素が取り込まれることによって呈色を示す反応であり，グルコース直鎖部分が形成するらせん長が長い場合には青色を呈し，らせん長が短くなるにつれて青紫色，赤紫色，赤褐色を呈する。一方，らせん長が極めて短い場合やない場合には無色を呈する。

【問8】グルコースを主体としたエネルギー貯蔵物質は，動物細胞にもグリコーゲンとして存在する。グリコーゲンの構造はデンプンよりもさらにグルコース鎖の分枝構造が多いと考えられている。このグリコーゲンを使ってヨウ素デンプン反応を行ったときにはどのような呈色を示すのか，その理由とともに答えなさい。

Escherichia coli sometimes swims in a straight line and sometimes changes direction at random. When E. coli swimming under a microscope was observed, in liquid medium it traced the track in Figure 1. When a solution of galactose, which E. coli can use, was supplied from the upper direction in the figure so that it seeped out of the mouth of a thin glass tube, it traced the track in Figure 2. The average speed of E. coli while moving in a straight line was almost constant.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-1-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): ガラクトースの拡散方向 = direction of diffusion of galactose; 出発点 = starting point; 図1 = Figure 1; 図2 = Figure 2.

Which of statements ①–⑤ are considered correct from these results? Choose the most appropriate combination from A–J. (4 points)

① In the movement of E. coli, an "all-or-none law" operates, depending only on whether galactose is "present" or "absent".

② In the movement of E. coli, a sense that responds to changes in the concentration of galactose operates.

③ In E. coli, it cannot be said that there is a relationship between the presence or absence of galactose and the direction of movement by the flagella.

④ In E. coli, the frequency of changes of direction is lower when it is heading towards a higher galactose concentration than when it is heading towards a lower galactose concentration.

⑤ In E. coli, the frequency of changes of direction is lower when it is heading towards a lower galactose concentration than when it is heading towards a higher galactose concentration.

A. ①②

B. ①③

C. ①④

D. ①⑤

E. ②③

F. ②④

G. ②⑤

H. ③④

I. ③⑤

J. ④⑤

γ (gamma)-globulin is a protein that works as an antibody, binding specifically to molecules that act as antigens. The structure of this molecule was elucidated through the accumulation of experimental results such as the following.

① Rabbit γ-globulin was treated with the protease papain. When the digestion products were examined, it had been split into two kinds of peptide fragment, present in a ratio (ratio of numbers of molecules) of 2 : 1. Call the more abundant component X and the less abundant component Y. X and Y had almost the same molecular weight.

② X inhibited the action of the undigested γ-globulin (binding to the antigen). Also, X only bound to the antigen and could not make it insoluble. On the other hand, Y did not inhibit the action of γ-globulin.

③ As in ①, when γ-globulin was cleaved with the protease pepsin, the digestion products separated into one component of high molecular weight and several small peptide fragments. Call the high-molecular-weight component Z. Z, like X, inhibited the action of the undigested γ-globulin (reaction with the antigen). Also, Z was about twice the size of X and Y and could make the antigen insoluble.

④ When γ-globulin was treated with a suitable reducing agent (which cleaves disulfide bonds (S–S bonds) between peptides), two kinds of peptide with different molecular weights were obtained, present in a ratio of 1 : 1. Call these two kinds V and W.

⑤ X and Y obtained by digesting rabbit γ-globulin were each injected into sheep, giving antibodies against X and antibodies against Y. The antibodies against X bound to both V and W, and the antibodies against Y bound only to V.

Choose from A–H the most appropriate schematic diagram showing the positions of V and W in the γ-globulin molecule, and Z, as deduced from experimental results ①–⑤. The lines joining the □ or ■ in the diagrams represent S–S bonds. (5 points)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-1-2-fig1.png

When a DNA molecule is replicated in both directions from one replication start site (origin of replication), in what directions do the DNA strands being replicated elongate? Choose the most appropriate schematic diagram from A–I. (4 points)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-1-3-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 複製開始点 = replication start site.

At the end of the 19th century, Buchner showed that when sucrose (cane sugar) was added to an extract obtained by grinding yeast and filtering it, fermentation took place and alcohol was produced. Harden, who was taking Buchner's research further, noticed that fermentation stopped before the sucrose had been used up. Moreover, he discovered that when boiled yeast extract was added to the fermentation liquid in which this reaction had stopped and sucrose remained, fermentation started again. He also confirmed that the boiled yeast extract itself had no fermenting ability. Choose from A–E the most appropriate inference that can be drawn from this experiment. (3 points)

A. A protease originally present in the yeast breaks down the enzymes needed for fermentation.

B. An enzyme other than the enzymes involved in fermentation breaks down the sugar.

C. Fermentation requires a heat-resistant substance other than enzymes, and this substance is consumed as fermentation proceeds.

D. Fermentation occurs less readily when oxygen is present.

E. The carbon dioxide produced by fermentation inhibits the fermentation reaction.

Loci $d$ and $p$ are on the same chromosome, and $d$ is located farther from the centromere than $p$. Consider the process by which a diploid offspring is born by parthenogenesis from an individual in which alleles $d_1$ and $p_1$, and $d_2$ and $p_2$, are linked (genotype $d_1 p_1 / d_2 p_2$). Assuming that one crossover occurred between $d$ and $p$ in the first meiotic division, in which of cases ①–③ could offspring with the genotypes below be born? Choose the correct combination from A–F. (5 points)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-1-5-fig1.png

Schematic diagram of the bivalent chromosome formed at metaphase of the first meiotic division

Figure labels (Japanese → English): セントロメア = centromere.

① The case in which the two nuclei formed in the first meiotic division fuse and the second meiotic division then takes place

② The case in which, in the second meiotic division, the two nuclei derived from one of the two nuclei formed in the first meiotic division fuse

③ The case in which one nucleus doubles after the end of the second meiotic division

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{Genotype of the offspring} & d_1 p_2 / d_1 p_2 & d_1 p_1 / d_1 p_2 & d_1 p_1 / d_2 p_1 \\ \hline \text{A} & \text{①} & \text{②} & \text{③} \\ \text{B} & \text{①} & \text{③} & \text{②} \\ \text{C} & \text{②} & \text{①} & \text{③} \\ \text{D} & \text{②} & \text{③} & \text{①} \\ \text{E} & \text{③} & \text{①} & \text{②} \\ \text{F} & \text{③} & \text{②} & \text{①} \end{array}$$

Because plant cells are joined to one another by cell walls, when each cell is to be examined in detail it can be effective to digest the polysaccharides of the cell wall with enzymes and isolate the cells as protoplasts. A certain biology club tried to make protoplasts from the guard cells of broad bean (ソラマメ) in order to study guard cells. First, they peeled the epidermis from a broad bean leaf, but it did not peel off cleanly and a little mesophyll tissue remained attached. When this was treated with enzymes that digest cell-wall polysaccharides, many spherical protoplasts were obtained, but they appeared to include a mixture of protoplasts of different origins. To distinguish them, the features and properties of each protoplast serve as clues.

Taking ① as protoplasts derived from mesophyll cells, ② as protoplasts derived from guard cells and ③ as protoplasts derived from epidermal cells other than guard cells, to which of protoplasts ①–③ do the following features or properties ア–ウ apply? Choose the most appropriate combination from A–L. (5 points)

ア. Chloroplasts are well developed.

イ. When irradiated with blue light, the diameter increases.

ウ. When immersed in a hypertonic solution, the diameter decreases.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}  & \text{ア} & \text{イ} & \text{ウ} \\ \hline \text{A} & \text{① only} & \text{② only} & \text{① and ③} \\ \text{B} & \text{① only} & \text{② only} & \text{all of ①②③} \\ \text{C} & \text{① only} & \text{② and ③} & \text{① and ③} \\ \text{D} & \text{① only} & \text{② and ③} & \text{all of ①②③} \\ \text{E} & \text{① and ②} & \text{② only} & \text{① and ③} \\ \text{F} & \text{① and ②} & \text{② only} & \text{all of ①②③} \\ \text{G} & \text{① and ②} & \text{② and ③} & \text{① and ③} \\ \text{H} & \text{① and ②} & \text{② and ③} & \text{all of ①②③} \\ \text{I} & \text{① and ③} & \text{② only} & \text{① and ③} \\ \text{J} & \text{① and ③} & \text{② only} & \text{all of ①②③} \\ \text{K} & \text{① and ③} & \text{② and ③} & \text{① and ③} \\ \text{L} & \text{① and ③} & \text{② and ③} & \text{all of ①②③} \end{array}$$

Two lines, a and b, of Arabidopsis thaliana (シロイヌナズナ) differ greatly in root growth. To find the cause, marks were made by scattering graphite powder on the root surface, and the relationship between their positions (distance from the root tip) and their displacement velocity (the velocity at which they move away from the root tip) was examined and summarised in a graph (Figure 1). Also, the epidermal cells were counted from the root tip, and the relationship between the distance from the tip and the cumulative number of epidermal cells (the number of epidermal cells contained between the tip and any given position) was examined and summarised in a graph (Figure 2).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-1-8-fig1.png

Figure 1. Relationship between the velocity at which the marks of graphite powder attached to the root surface move away from the root tip (displacement velocity) and their position (distance from the root tip). The results of line a are shown by the solid curve and the results of line b by the dotted curve.

Figure 2. Relationship between the number of epidermal cells counted from the root tip (cumulative number of epidermal cells) and the distance from the root tip. The results of line a are shown by the solid curve and the results of line b by the dotted curve.

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 変位速度 = displacement velocity; 累積表皮細胞数 = cumulative number of epidermal cells; 根端からの距離 = distance from the root tip.

Which of statements ①–⑥ can be concluded from these results about the roots of a and b? Choose the most appropriate combination from A–I. (5 points)

① Comparing epidermal cells that have stopped elongating, those of a are longer than those of b.

② Comparing epidermal cells that have stopped elongating, those of b are longer than those of a.

③ Epidermal cells that have stopped elongating are the same length in a and b.

④ Comparing the rate of division of the epidermal cells, that of a is higher than that of b.

⑤ Comparing the rate of division of the epidermal cells, that of b is higher than that of a.

⑥ The rate of division of the epidermal cells is the same in a and b.

A. ①④

B. ①⑤

C. ①⑥

D. ②④

E. ②⑤

F. ②⑥

G. ③④

H. ③⑤

I. ③⑥

Skeletal muscle is a tissue made of bundles of giant cells called muscle fibres, and the muscle fibres contain bundles of myofibrils. A myofibril is a repetition of a unit structure called the sarcomere (Figure 1) and is the basic structure that brings about muscle contraction. The length of a typical skeletal-muscle sarcomere is about 2.5 µm. As shown in Figure 1, the actin filaments extending from the Z membrane (sometimes also called the Z line, Z band or Z disc) are about 1.0 µm long, and the myosin filaments are about 1.6 µm long. Because the myosin filaments interact with the actin filaments and act so as to pull the actin filaments in, the distance between the Z membranes becomes shorter as a result, and the whole muscle also contracts.

The tension per sarcomere is greater the more myosin heads interact with the actin filaments. However, the myosin heads that can interact with actin are present only on about 0.6 µm on each side of the myosin filament; the central approximately 0.4 µm has no myosin heads and therefore cannot react with actin. It is also known that when the sarcomere is stretched to about 4.0 µm so that the actin filaments and myosin filaments are separated, the interaction between the myosin heads and the actin filaments disappears, but because the two sides are connected by a weakly elastic protein, the original structure is restored when the pulling force is removed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-1-9-fig1.png

Figure 1: Schematic diagram of a sarcomere

Figure labels (Japanese → English): アクチンフィラメント = actin filament; ミオシンフィラメント = myosin filament; Z膜 = Z membrane; ミオシンの頭部がある部分 = region with myosin heads.

From the following statements about the tension generated by a sarcomere, choose the one that is $\underline{\text{not correct}}$ from A–F. (4 points)

A. When the sarcomere length is 3.6 µm or more, there is almost no tension.

B. At sarcomere lengths of 2.4–3.6 µm, the tension increases as the length becomes shorter.

C. At sarcomere lengths of 2.0–3.6 µm, the tension increases as the length becomes shorter.

D. When the sarcomere length is 2.0–2.4 µm, the magnitude of the tension is constant.

E. When the sarcomere length becomes 2.0 µm or less, the actin filaments from the two sides collide and the tension decreases.

F. At sarcomere lengths of 1.6 µm or less, the myosin filaments become a large resistance between the Z membranes and the tension decreases sharply.

In all cells of the mouse, an enzyme called isocitrate dehydrogenase is expressed. The gene for this enzyme, $M$, is located on an autosome. Two molecules of the polypeptide chain produced from this gene by transcription and translation bind to each other (this is called a dimer) to form the active enzyme.

Mice of strain W and strain Z differ slightly in the $M$ gene. Call the allele of $M$ carried by strain W $M_a$, and the allele carried by strain Z $M_b$. Also, call the polypeptide chain derived from $M_a$ the a chain and the polypeptide chain derived from $M_b$ the b chain. When the dimers of this enzyme were purified from the livers of strain W and strain Z mice and separated by a method called electrophoresis, two different dimers, a chain/a chain (a/a) and b chain/b chain (b/b), were detected respectively, as in Figure 1. Next, when the purified dimers a/a and b/b were once dissociated into single polypeptide chains (called monomers) and then mixed, allowed to form dimers again and separated by electrophoresis, three kinds, a/a, a/b and b/b, were detected, as in Figure 2. However, when the two were mixed while still dimers, only the two kinds a/a and b/b were detected.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-1-10-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 系統W = strain W; 系統Z = strain Z; 電気泳動 = electrophoresis; 単量体にした後混ぜた場合 = mixed after conversion to monomers; 二量体のまま混ぜた場合 = mixed while still dimers; 白毛 = white coat; 黒毛 = black coat; 8細胞期の胚 = 8-cell-stage embryo; 卵膜を除去 = egg membrane removed; 割球を混ぜる = blastomeres mixed; 胚盤胞まで培養 = cultured to the blastocyst; 仮親の子宮へ移植 = transferred to the uterus of a foster mother; 産まれたキメラマウス = chimeric mouse born; 図1 = Figure 1; 図2 = Figure 2; 図3 = Figure 3.

Now, using early embryos of mice of the white-coated strain W and the black-coated strain Z, a chimeric mouse in which cells of strain W and strain Z were mixed in roughly equal numbers was produced as in Figure 3. Skeletal muscle is formed by cell fusion. If isocitrate dehydrogenase dimers are purified from the skeletal muscle of this chimeric mouse and separated by electrophoresis, what kinds of dimer will be detected? Choose the most appropriate from A–I. (5 points)

A. a/a only

B. a/b only

C. b/b only

D. either a/a or a/b

E. either b/b or a/b

F. one of a/a, a/b or b/b

G. both a/a and b/b

H. all of a/a, a/b and b/b

I. either a/a and a/b, or b/b and a/b

The compound eyes of insects arise from a group of cells called a primordium (compound-eye primordium) inside the body of the larva. In a certain insect species, the compound-eye colour of the wild type is red, and this red is due to vermilion and brown pigments coexisting in the cells of the compound eye. Let $Q$ be the wild-type allele involved in the synthesis of the vermilion pigment, $q$ the recessive allele that has lost its function, $T$ the wild-type allele involved in the synthesis of the brown pigment and $t$ the recessive allele that has lost its function. Then with genotype $Qqtt$ or $QQtt$ the compound eyes are vermilion, with genotype $qqTt$ or $qqTT$ the compound eyes are brown, and with genotype $qqtt$ the compound eyes are white.

Furthermore, it is known that this insect has another gene involved in compound-eye colour. The function of that gene is to take up the vermilion or brown pigments, or the substances from which they are made, into the cells of the compound-eye primordium from outside. When its function is lost, the resulting compound eyes are white. Compound-eye primordia can be transplanted, and a compound eye arises from a transplanted compound-eye primordium. Using this, three transplantation experiments were carried out and the following results were obtained.

Experiment 1: A compound-eye primordium taken from a wild-type larva was transplanted into a larva of genotype $qqtt$, and the colour of the compound eye arising from the transplanted primordium was examined: it was white.

Experiment 2: A compound-eye primordium taken from a wild-type larva was transplanted into a larva that produces white compound eyes, and the colour of the compound eye arising from the transplanted primordium was examined: it was red.

Experiment 3: A compound-eye primordium taken from a larva of genotype $qqtt$ was transplanted into a wild-type larva, and the colour of the compound eye arising from the transplanted primordium was examined: it was red.

Further transplantation experiments were carried out with the combinations shown in the following table. The right-hand column of the table shows the compound-eye colour expected as the result of each experiment. Judging from the results of Experiments 1–3, which of A–G is considered correct? (5 points)

$$\begin{array}{c|l|l|c}  & \text{Combination used in the transplantation experiment} &  & \text{Result} \\  & \text{Larva from which the compound-eye primordium is taken} & \text{Larva into which the compound-eye primordium is transplanted} & \text{Colour of the compound eye arising from the transplanted primordium} \\ \hline \text{A} & qqTt & Qqtt & \text{red} \\ \text{B} & qqTt & \text{wild type} & \text{brown} \\ \text{C} & Qqtt & qqTt\quad \text{compound eyes become white} & \text{white} \\ \text{D} & qqTt & Qqtt\quad \text{compound eyes become white} & \text{vermilion} \\ \text{E} & qqTT\quad \text{compound eyes become white} & QQtt & \text{red} \\ \text{F} & QQtt\quad \text{compound eyes become white} & \text{wild type} & \text{vermilion} \\ \text{G} & qqTT\quad \text{compound eyes become white} & qqTt & \text{brown} \end{array}$$

Moulting and metamorphosis of insects are regulated by corpus allatum hormone, secreted from the corpora allata in the head, and prothoracic gland hormone, secreted from the prothoracic glands in the thorax. The figure is a graph of the developmental stages of the silkworm moth (カイコガ) and the changes in the amounts of the hormones, with a schematic diagram of a larva.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-1-12-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): ホルモン量（相対値）= amount of hormone (relative value); アラタ体ホルモン = corpus allatum hormone; 前胸腺ホルモン = prothoracic gland hormone; 4齢へ脱皮 = moult to the 4th instar; 5齢へ脱皮 = moult to the 5th instar; 蛹へ脱皮 = moult to the pupa; 頭部 = head; 胸部 = thorax; 腹部 = abdomen.

• When corpus allatum hormone and prothoracic gland hormone act at the same time, the larva moults while remaining a larva and becomes the next instar.
• When only prothoracic gland hormone acts, the larva metamorphoses (pupates).
• In the larval period, the 4th instar lasts about 6 days and the 5th instar about 10 days.

Insects that moult harden their soft integument from immediately after moulting, and enzyme X is known to play a major role in this process. There is a report that enzyme X, when activated, polymerises with other substances, resulting in hardening of the integument. A certain biology club wanted to investigate enzyme X and planned the following experiments.

$$\begin{array}{c|l|l|l|l}  & \text{Planned experiment} & \text{Result: morphology} & \text{Result: inactive enzyme X} & \text{Result: activated enzyme X} \\ \hline \text{Experiment 1} & \text{Ligation※ between the head and thorax on day 2 of the 4th instar} & \text{the part posterior to the ligature pupated} & \text{detected in the integument anterior to the ligature} & \text{detected in the integument posterior to the ligature} \\ \text{Experiment 2} & \text{On day 2 of the 5th instar, ditto} & \text{ditto} & \text{ditto} & \text{ditto} \\ \text{Experiment 3} & \text{Ligation between the thorax and abdomen on day 2 of the 5th instar} & \text{the part anterior to the ligature pupated} & \text{detected in the integument posterior to the ligature} & \text{detected in the integument anterior to the ligature} \\ \text{Experiment 4} & \text{Corpora allata of day 3 of the 4th instar transplanted into the abdomen on day 2 of the 5th instar} & \text{moulted into a 6th-instar larva without becoming a pupa} & \text{not detected} & \text{detected in the whole integument} \\ \text{Experiment 5} & \text{Individuals on day 1 of the 4th instar and day 1 of the 5th instar each ground up and an extract prepared} & \text{—} & \text{not present} & \text{not present} \\ \text{Experiment 6} & \text{Individuals on day 5 of the 4th instar and day 9 of the 5th instar each ground up and an extract prepared} & \text{—} & \text{present} & \text{present} \end{array}$$

※ Ligation (結紮): tying part of the body tightly with thread so that the body fluid of the larva cannot move.

If the results above were obtained from the experiments, choose from A–F the statement about enzyme X that agrees with the experimental results. (5 points)

A. It is synthesised in the corpora allata and sent to the integument of the whole body before moulting.

B. It is synthesised in the integument of the whole body before moulting.

C. It begins to be synthesised from the 5th larval instar.

D. It is not activated when corpus allatum hormone is present.

E. It is activated autonomously, unrelated to corpus allatum hormone and prothoracic gland hormone.

F. It does not act at moults from larva to larva.

The bodies of many multicellular organisms are built on three axes: anterior–posterior, dorsal–ventral and left–right. In the fruit fly (ショウジョウバエ), the directions of the anterior–posterior axis and the dorsal–ventral axis are determined in early embryogenesis by concentration gradients of factors distributed unevenly within the embryo. Specifically, the direction of the anterior–posterior axis is determined by the action of factor α, which forms a concentration gradient from the anterior to the posterior of the embryo, and factor β, which forms a concentration gradient from the posterior to the anterior. On the other hand, the direction of the dorsal–ventral axis is determined by factor γ, which forms a concentration gradient from the ventral to the dorsal side. However, the mechanism that determines the direction of the third axis, the left–right axis, is not clear. A researcher therefore put forward the following two hypotheses.

Hypothesis 1: A factor separate from those that determine the directions of the anterior–posterior and dorsal–ventral axes exists, and its concentration gradient determines the direction of the left–right axis.

Hypothesis 2: The direction of the left–right axis is determined depending on the directions of the anterior–posterior and dorsal–ventral axes.

To test these hypotheses, the effect on the direction of the left–right axis of completely reversing only the direction of the anterior–posterior axis was examined. First, to reverse the direction of the anterior–posterior axis completely, factor α and factor β were artificially exchanged (reversed embryo). In this case the position of the micropyle in the eggshell does not change, so the original anterior–posterior direction and the anterior–posterior direction of the reversed embryo can be judged independently. Next, these reversed embryos were used to judge which hypothesis is correct. The direction of the left–right axis was judged from the way the gut, which is formed by the late stage of embryogenesis, curves.

problems.title: Part 1, Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam 1: Zoology (time limit 90 minutes)

Introduction
The fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster) is a model organism often used as research material in genetics and other fields. In crossing experiments, unmated females and males are collected, and crossing is begun by transferring females and males with the appropriate combination of genotypes into the same medium. Here we consider what differences there are between female and male fruit flies, and what could be devised to make it possible to distinguish the sexes at an early stage of development.

Samples and apparatus
Take the two tweezers already handed out from your belongings. Apart from these, the experiment uses 1 stereomicroscope, 1 light microscope, 5 slide glasses, 1 box of cover glasses, 1 empty Petri dish, 1 dropper and 5 microtubes. The slide glasses are in a plastic beaker and the microtubes are in a tube rack. Check that all of these are present.

The contents of the microtubes are: phosphate buffer, 1 tube (marked P on top); samples containing adult fruit flies, 3 tubes (marked ① to ③ on top); empty, 1 tube (marked A on top). Microtube A is for submitting as an answer. Use the empty Petri dish as necessary for taking the fruit flies out of and putting them back into the microtubes.

Part 1

Observe the wild-type females and males (sample ①) under the stereomicroscope.

Question 1. On the dorsal side of the thorax there are several relatively conspicuous bristles. In what arrangement do the bristles grow on the scutellum (the inverted-triangular or semicircular structure seen at the part marked ☆ in the figure below)? 実験試験1　動物学（制限時間90分）

はじめに
キイロショウジョウバエ（Drosophila melanogaster）は、遺伝などの研究材料としてよく使われるモデル生物です。交配実験では未交尾の雌雄を集めておき、適切な遺伝子型の組合せをもった雌雄を同じ培地に移し入れることによって交配が開始されます。ここでは、ショウジョウバエの雌雄にはどのような違いがあるのか、またどのような工夫をすれば発生の早い段階で雌雄の区別が可能になるかを考えます。

サンプルと器具
配布済みのピンセット2本を各自の持ち物から出しなさい。それ以外に実験で使用するのは、実体顕微鏡1台、光学顕微鏡1台、スライドガラス5枚、カバーガラス1箱、空のシャーレ1枚、スポイト1個、マイクロチューブ5本です。スライドガラスはプラスチックビーカーの中に、マイクロチューブはチューブラックにあります。これらがそろっていることを確認しなさい。

なお、マイクロチューブの中身は、リン酸緩衝液が1本（上面にPの表記）、ショウジョウバエの成虫が入ったサンプルが3本（上面に①～③の表記）、空が1本（上面にAの表記）です。マイクロチューブAは解答として提出するためのものです。空のシャーレは必要に応じてマイクロチューブ内のショウジョウバエを出し入れするのに使ってください。

第１部

野生型の雌雄（サンプル①）を実体顕微鏡下で観察しなさい。

問題1．胸部背面には比較的目立つ剛毛が複数存在する。中胸小楯板（下図の☆印部分に見られる逆三角形あるいは半円形の構造）には剛毛がどのような状態で生えているか。剛毛基部の位置と剛毛の数、向きが分かるようにスケッチしなさい。

problems.title: Part 2, Question 3
problems.problem:
Part 2

Dissect the abdomens of the wild-type females and males (sample ①) using the tweezers. As in the preliminary session, drop phosphate buffer onto a slide glass and dissect under the stereomicroscope. Then remove the parts not needed for observation, cover with a cover glass and observe with the light microscope. The slide glasses used for dissection and observation can be used any number of times by wiping off the sample and buffer.

The pair of yellow, spiral organs that are conspicuous when a male is dissected are the testes (in some cases the colour may be pale). The base of each testis (the side at the centre of the spiral) connects to the seminal vesicle (the swollen yellow part), and the sperm that have acquired motility are stored here. There is also a pair of translucent sacs, the accessory glands; at mating, proteins secreted by the accessory glands are passed into the female's body in addition to the sperm.

Question 3. Sketch the testis, seminal vesicle and accessory gland so that it can be seen how they are connected, and write in their names.

第２部

野生型の雌雄（サンプル①）の腹部を、ピンセットを用いて解剖しなさい。予備体験と同様に、スライドガラス上にリン酸緩衝液を滴下し、実体顕微鏡下で解剖すること。その後、観察に不要な部分は取り除き、カバーガラスを被せ、光学顕微鏡で観察しなさい。解剖や観察に使用したスライドガラスは、サンプルおよび緩衝液を拭き取ることによって、何度でも使用できる。

雄を解剖したときに目立つ、黄色い1対の渦巻き状の器官は精巣である（場合によっては色が薄いことがある）。精巣の基部（渦巻きの中心側）は貯精嚢（ふくらみのある黄色い部分）につながり、運動性を獲得した精子はここに蓄えられる。また、1対の半透明の袋である付属腺があり、交尾のときには精子以外にも付属腺から分泌されたタンパク質が雌の体内に受け渡される。

問題3．精巣・貯精嚢・付属腺がどのようにつながっているか分かるように、スケッチし、これらの名称を記入しなさい。

第２部

野生型の雌雄（サンプル①）の腹部を、ピンセットを用いて解剖しなさい。予備体験と同様に、スライドガラス上にリン酸緩衝液を滴下し、実体顕微鏡下で解剖すること。その後、観察に不要な部分は取り除き、カバーガラスを被せ、光学顕微鏡で観察しなさい。解剖や観察に使用したスライドガラスは、サンプルおよび緩衝液を拭き取ることによって、何度でも使用できる。

雌を解剖したときに目立つ、1対の房状の白いかたまりは卵巣である。卵巣は十数本の卵巣小管からなるが、その中で卵母細胞が形成され、徐々に大きくなる。

問題4．卵巣中にある最も発達した卵の1つをスケッチしなさい。また、その方向が分かるように、スケッチ上でより若い卵母細胞が存在する側に☆印を記入しなさい。

problems.title: Part 2, Question 5
problems.problem:
Part 2

Dissect the abdomens of the wild-type females and males (sample ①) using the tweezers. As in the preliminary session, drop phosphate buffer onto a slide glass and dissect under the stereomicroscope. Then remove the parts not needed for observation, cover with a cover glass and observe with the light microscope. The slide glasses used for dissection and observation can be used any number of times by wiping off the sample and buffer.

The oviducts (lateral oviducts) coming from the left and right ovaries join further back to form the common oviduct. Attached to the common oviduct are a transparent, slender tubular seminal receptacle and two (rarely three) brown spermathecae. In a mated female, sperm are stored in the seminal receptacle and the spermathecae, and fertilisation takes place when an unfertilised egg that has come down the common oviduct passes near their openings.

Question 5. Sketch one of the brown spermathecae.

問題5．茶色い受精嚢の1個をスケッチしなさい。

problems.title: Part 3, Question 6
problems.problem:
Part 3

How can the sexes of the fruit fly be separated at developmental stages before the adult? In third-instar (final-instar) larvae the sexes can be distinguished, because the testes are larger than the ovaries. However, this would probably require skill, and it may become necessary to distinguish the sexes at an even earlier stage of development. We will therefore use the recessive mutant white ($w$) of a gene on the X chromosome. Wild-type ($+$) adults have red compound eyes, but the mutant $w$ has white compound eyes. Sample ② is females and males of the $w$ strain.

Besides the compound eyes, there are other traits that differ between the $+$ and $w$ strains. For example, the ocelli on the top of the head are pigmented in the $+$ strain but white in the $w$ strain.

Question 6. Sketch the ocelli of the fruit fly. Also, so that their arrangement can be seen, mark with ☆ on the sketch the part corresponding to the front of the head.

第３部

ショウジョウバエが成虫になる前の発生段階で雌雄を分けるには、どのようにすればよいのだろうか。三齢（終齢）幼虫では精巣の方が卵巣よりも大きいので、雌雄を判別することができる。しかし、これには熟練を要するであろうし、発生のもっと早い段階で雌雄の区別が必要になることがあるかもしれない。そこで、X染色体上にある劣性の遺伝子変異体white（$w$）を利用することにする。野生型（$+$）の成虫は複眼が赤いが、変異体$w$は複眼が白い。サンプル②は$w$系統の雌雄である。

problems.title: Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam 2: Evolutionary ecology (time limit 90 minutes)

Introduction
Arabidopsis kamchatica (ミヤマハタザオ), of the family Brassicaceae, is distributed mainly in Alaska, Siberia, the Kamchatka Peninsula, Hokkaido and Honshu. In the Chubu region it occurs in bright places such as along rivers, along forest roads and on rocky ground, over an extremely wide altitudinal range of 30–3000 m. Its habitats are at most a few square kilometres in size and form distinct populations, and the populations are geographically discontinuous from one another. It is a plant whose centre of distribution lies in the north, and its density is higher at higher altitudes, but every population has the same life history of germination, growth, flowering and fruiting (Figure 1), and the populations are maintained by reproduction by seed. Surveys in the field over several years showed that the high-altitude populations have the life history of a typical perennial herb, with many individuals that live for several years or more and reproduce many times. In contrast, the low-altitude populations had high individual mortality in summer and showed a life history close to that of an annual herb, in which most individuals die within one year and can reproduce only once in their lifetime. Thus there are various differences between the populations, but they are the same species and can interbreed with one another.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-4-1-fig1.png

Figure 1 Life history of Arabidopsis kamchatica. Every population passes through these stages over a period of several months to several years.

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 種子 = seed; 発芽 = germination; 栄養成長 = vegetative growth; ロゼット = rosette; 葉 = leaf; 根 = root; 開花 = flowering; つぼみ = bud; 花 = flower; 花茎 = flowering stem; 結実 = fruiting; 果実（中に種子が10～30粒入っている） = fruit (containing 10–30 seeds).

Samples and apparatus
Check that the biological material, Arabidopsis kamchatica, is lined up as follows: 6 individuals from the Magosajima population (孫佐島, Shizuoka Prefecture, altitude about 500 m) in a green tray on the left, and 6 individuals from the Murodo population (室堂, Toyama Prefecture, altitude about 2400 m) in a black tray on the right. From the experiment set handed out, take out the ruler, the magnifying glass and the scissors and put them on the desk (do not take out the tweezers). You are, however, free to use or not to use the apparatus put on the desk. The Kimwipes, Kim Towels, plastic beakers (2) and wash bottle (containing water) on the desk may be used freely.

Problems
Read the following text, observe the plants handed out carefully, and answer Questions 1–4.

Seeds were collected from the Magosajima population near Magosajima, Shizuoka Prefecture (altitude about 500 m), and from the Murodo population near Murodo, Toyama Prefecture (altitude about 2400 m), and were sown and grown in the same laboratory. These cultivated individuals set fruit automatically by self-pollination, so seeds were collected from them. The plants handed out were obtained by sowing and growing these seeds in the same laboratory. Sowing and cultivation were carried out with 20 hours of day (light, 20 °C) and 4 hours of night (dark, 18 °C). All the seeds were sown on the same day, and about 70 days have passed. For each population, the proportion of seeds that had germinated at 28 days after sowing and the time taken to germinate were as shown in Figure 2 and Figure 3, respectively. Of these, only the plants that germinated have been handed out.

Figure 2 Proportion of individuals that had germinated at 28 days after sowing, in two populations of Arabidopsis kamchatica.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-4-1-fig3.png

Figure 3 Time taken to germinate, at 28 days after sowing, in two populations of Arabidopsis kamchatica. The points show the mean values, and the lines show the range from the minimum to the maximum value.

実験試験2　進化生態学（制限時間90分）

はじめに
アブラナ科のミヤマハタザオ（Arabidopsis kamchatica）はおもにアラスカ、シベリア、カムチャッカ半島、北海道、本州に分布します。中部地方では30～3000 mという極めて広い標高帯の川沿い、林道沿い、岩場などの明るい場所に出現します。生息場所は大きくても数平方kmで明瞭な集団を構成し、集団と集団の間は地理的に不連続です。北方に分布中心がある植物であり、高標高ほど生育密度が高いのですが、どの集団も発芽・成長・開花・結実という同じ生活史をもち（図1）、種子繁殖によって集団が維持されています。野外で数年にわたる調査を行った結果、高標高の集団は、数年以上生きて何度も繁殖する個体が多い典型的な多年草の生活史を示しました。一方で、低標高の集団は夏の個体死亡率が高く、大多数の個体が1年以内に死亡し生涯に1回しか繁殖できないという、一年草に近い生活史を示しました。このように集団間にさまざまな違いがありますが、お互いに交配可能な同種です。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-4-1-fig1.png

図１　ミヤマハタザオの生活史。どの集団も数ヶ月から数年かけてこれらの段階を経る。

サンプルと器具
生物材料としてミヤマハタザオが、静岡県孫佐島（まごさじま、標高約500 m）集団由来の6個体が緑のトレーに入って左側に、富山県室堂（むろどう、標高約2400 m）集団由来の6個体が黒のトレーに入って右側に並んでいることを確認しなさい。配布してある実験セットのなかから、物差し・ルーペ・はさみを机の上に出しなさい（ピンセットは出してはいけません）。ただし、机の上に出した器具は、使用するのも使用しないのも自由です。机上のキムワイプ、キムタオル、プラスチックビーカー（2つ）、洗びん（水入り）は自由に使えます。

問題
以下の文を読み、配布された植物を良く観察し、問題1～4に答えなさい。

静岡県孫佐島付近（標高約500 m）にある孫佐島集団と、富山県の室堂付近（標高約2400 m）にある室堂集団で種子を採集し、それを同じ実験室で播種・栽培した。これらの栽培個体は自家受粉によって自動的に結実したので、それらから種子を採集した。これらの種子を同じ実験室で播種・栽培して得られた植物を配布する。播種・栽培は、昼20時間（明条件、20℃）・夜4時間（暗条件、18℃）で行った。全ての種子を同じ日に播種し、約70日が経過している。それぞれの集団の播種後28日時点での発芽した種子の割合と発芽にかかった時間は、それぞれ図2、図3のようだった。このうち、発芽した植物だけを配布してある。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-4-1-fig2.png

図２　ミヤマハタザオ２集団の、播種後28日時点の発芽した個体の割合。
