problems.title: Experiment 1, Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam 3: Physiology (time limit 90 minutes)

Introduction
The activity of eukaryotic cells requires oxygen. However, because the body of a multicellular animal such as a human is formed of a very large number of cells, oxygen does not reach the deep parts of the body unless it is carried by the blood. Mammals in particular sometimes exercise vigorously, so they need a large amount of oxygen. For this reason, special oxygen-carrying cells, the red blood cells, work in the blood to supply oxygen to every corner of the body.

The inside of a red blood cell is filled with a protein called haemoglobin. A haemoglobin molecule is formed of four polypeptide chains (two α chains and two β chains) and contains four molecules called haem (figure on the right). Haem contains iron, and oxygen is carried by binding to this iron.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-5-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): α₁鎖, α₂鎖, β₁鎖, β₂鎖 = α₁ chain, α₂ chain, β₁ chain, β₂ chain; ヘム = haem; ▲ヒトのヘモグロビン = ▲ human haemoglobin; ▲ヘモグロビンの立体構造 = ▲ three-dimensional structure of haemoglobin; 出典：「スクエア最新図説生物 neo」吉里勝利他監修 第一学習社（2013） = Source: "Square Saishin Zusetsu Seibutsu neo", supervised by Katsutoshi Yoshizato et al., Daiichi Gakushusha (2013).

So how much haemoglobin is contained in a red blood cell?

In this task you will use preserved sheep blood (below called preserved blood) and carry out two experiments. In the first experiment you will use a haemocytometer to measure the concentration of red blood cells in the preserved blood. In the second experiment you will first make a haemoglobin solution by physically breaking the cell membranes by exposing the preserved blood to a hypotonic solution. Next you will measure the absorbance of this solution and calculate the haemoglobin concentration from that value. The final goal of this task is to find "the number of haemoglobin molecules contained in one red blood cell" from the values obtained in the two experiments.

Samples, apparatus and reagents
Sample
□ 10 mL of preserved sheep blood diluted to 1/20 with physiological saline (15 mL centrifuge tube with cap),
Apparatus
□ Haemocytometer  □ Counter  □ Upright microscope
□ Centrifuge  □ 5 spectrophotometer cells (your exam number is written on the rack)
□ Micropipettes (P1000, P200)
□ White pipette tips (for P1000), 1 box  □ Yellow pipette tips (for P200), 1 box
□ 20 microtubes  □ 5 15 mL centrifuge tubes with caps
□ Plastic beakers (2; for discarded tips and for waste liquid)
Reagents
□ Pure water, 50 mL (50 mL centrifuge tube with cap; white label)
□ Physiological saline, 50 mL (50 mL centrifuge tube with cap; light blue)
□ Diluted physiological saline, 1.2 mL each (microtubes)
 • Physiological saline diluted to 1/4 with pure water (red label)
 • Physiological saline diluted to 1/2 with pure water (yellow label)
 • Physiological saline diluted to 3/4 with pure water (blue label)

Precautions
• The preserved blood is not toxic or infectious, but do not touch your eyes or mouth with hands that have preserved blood on them.
• Use the pipette tips and other apparatus so that liquids do not mix unintentionally.
• Use the oil-based pen for labelling. However, do not use it on the transparent faces of the spectrophotometer cells.

Experiment 1: Concentration of red blood cells in the blood
In animals, a large number of red blood cells is needed to carry oxygen to the many tissues of the body. You will calculate the concentration of red blood cells contained in the preserved blood and find the number of red blood cells contained in the blood of one individual animal (in this experiment, a sheep).

Experiment
1. To bring the 1/20-diluted preserved blood to a concentration suitable for counting, dilute it 100-fold. First, using the P1000 micropipette, put 900 µL of physiological saline into each of 2 microtubes. Next, close the cap of the 1/20-diluted preserved blood tightly, invert it up and down about 5–6 times to stir it, and mix well. Next, using the P200 micropipette, put 100 µL of the 1/20-diluted preserved blood into one of the microtubes containing physiological saline, and mix well until uniform by gently drawing it in and out repeatedly with the micropipette (pipetting). Take 100 µL of this suspension, put it into the other microtube containing physiological saline, and mix well by pipetting.
2. With the P200 micropipette, draw up 20 µL of the preserved blood diluted 100-fold from the original concentration, and let it flow gently into one of the sample inlets of the haemocytometer (Figure 1).
3. Set the haemocytometer on the upright microscope.
4. After focusing on the scale (the vertical and horizontal lines) of the haemocytometer with the 4× objective, change to the 10× objective, focus again and observe the cells. Choose 2 of the 4 counting areas (ア to エ) enclosed by red lines in Figure 2, and count the number of red blood cells contained in each area using the counter. However, red blood cells that overlap the outermost frame are not to be counted.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-5-1-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 計数エリア（グリッド部位） = counting area (grid region); サンプル注入口 = sample inlet; 図1 = Figure 1.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-5-1-fig3.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 深さ 0.1mm = depth 0.1 mm; 図2 = Figure 2.

Question 1. Write down the numbers of red blood cells in the 2 areas you counted and find their mean. Also, from the mean, calculate the number of red blood cells contained in 1 mL of the original preserved blood before the 1/20 dilution. Take a counting area as 1 mm wide and 0.1 mm deep (Figure 2), and $1\ \text{mL} = 10^{3}\ \text{mm}^{3}$. Be sure to write out the calculation, and give the answer to 2 significant figures, with the unit, in the form $\bigcirc.\bigcirc \times 10^{\bigcirc}$ cells/mL.
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験３　生理学（制限時間90分）

はじめに
真核細胞の活動には酸素が必要です。しかしながら、ヒトなどの多細胞動物では非常に多くの細胞から個体が形成されているため、血液によって酸素を運ばなければ、生体の深部にまで酸素が行き渡りません。特に、哺乳類などは時に激しい運動をするので、多量の酸素が必要です。そのため、血液では体内の隅々にまで酸素を供給するための特別な酸素運搬細胞、赤血球が働いています。

赤血球の内部はヘモグロビンと呼ばれるタンパク質で満たされています。ヘモグロビン分子は、４つのポリペプチド鎖（α鎖２つ、β鎖２つ）から形成されており、ヘムと呼ばれる分子を４つ含んでいます（右図）。ヘムは鉄を含んでおり、この鉄と酸素が結合することで、酸素を運搬しています。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-5-1-fig1.png

では、いったいどれくらいのヘモグロビンが赤血球に含まれているのでしょう？

この課題では、ヒツジ保存血（以下、保存血と呼ぶ）を使い、2 つの実験をします。1つめの実験では、血球計算盤を使い、保存血の赤血球濃度を計測します。2 つめの実験では、まず保存血を低張液にさらすことにより細胞膜を物理的に破壊し、ヘモグロビン溶液を作製します。次に、この溶液の吸光度を測定し、その値を元にヘモグロビン濃度を計算します。2 つの実験によって得られた値から、「赤血球 1 個に含まれるヘモグロビン分子の数」を求めるのが、この課題の最終目標です。

サンプルと器具類
サンプル
□生理食塩水で 1/20 に希釈したヒツジ保存血 10 mL（ふた付き 15 mL 遠沈管）、
器具
□血球計算盤　□カウンタ　□正立顕微鏡
□遠心機　□分光光度計用セル 5 つ（ラックに受験番号が記載されています）
□マイクロピペット（P1000、P200）
□ピペットチップ白（P1000 用）１箱　□ピペットチップ黄（P200 用）1 箱
□マイクロチューブ 20 本　□ふた付き 15 mL 遠沈管 5 本
□プラスチックビーカー（2 つ；チップ捨て用、廃液捨て用）
試薬
□純水 50 mL（ふた付き 50 mL 遠沈管；白ラベル）
□生理食塩水 50 mL（ふた付き 50 mL 遠沈管；水色）
□希釈生理食塩水　各 1.2 mL（マイクロチューブ）
　・純水で 1/4 に希釈した生理食塩水（赤ラベル）
　・純水で 1/2 に希釈した生理食塩水（黄ラベル）
　・純水で 3/4 に希釈した生理食塩水（青ラベル）

注意事項
・保存血に毒性や感染性はありませが、保存血が付いた手で目や口を触らないでください。
・ピペットチップ等の器具については、意図せず液体が混合しないよう使用してください。
・油性ペンはラベリングに使用してください。ただし、分光光度計用セルの透明な面には使用しないでください。

実験１　血液中の赤血球の濃度
動物では、体内の多くの組織に酸素を運ぶために多量の赤血球が必要とされます。保存血に含まれる赤血球の濃度を算出し、動物（本実験ではヒツジ）１個体の血液中に含まれる赤血球の数を調べます。

実験
1．1/20 希釈保存血を計数に適した濃度にするため、100 倍に希釈する。まず、2 本のマイクロチューブに P1000 マイクロピペットを使ってそれぞれ 900 μL の生理食塩水を入れなさい。次に 1/20 希釈保存血のふたをしっかりと閉め、上下に 5～6 回ほど転倒、撹拌し、よく混合しなさい。次に、P200 マイクロピペットを使って 1/20 希釈保存血 100 μL をどちらかひとつの生理食塩水の入ったマイクロチューブに入れ、マイクロピペットで軽く出し入れを繰り返し（ピペッティング）、均一になるようによく混合しなさい。この懸濁液から 100 μL 回収し、もう一方の生理食塩水の入ったマイクロチューブに入れ、ピペッティングでよく混合しなさい。
２．P200 マイクロピペットで元の濃度の 100 倍に希釈した保存血を 20 μL 吸い取り、血球計算盤のサンプル注入口（図 1）のどちらか一方に静かに流し込みなさい。
３．血球計算盤を正立顕微鏡にセットしなさい。
４．4 倍の対物レンズで血球計算盤のメモリ（縦横の線）にピントを合わせた後、10 倍の対物レンズに変更し、再びピントを合わせて細胞を観察しなさい。図 2 の赤い線で囲まれた 4 カ所の計数エリア（ア～エ）の中から 2 カ所を選択し、各エリア内に含まれる赤血球の数を、カウンタを用いてそれぞれ計数しなさい。ただし、一番外側の枠と重なっている赤血球についてはカウントしないこととする。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-5-1-fig2.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-5-1-fig3.png

問題 1．計数した 2 カ所のエリアの赤血球数を記し、平均値を求めなさい。また、平均値から 1/20 希釈する前のもともとの保存血 1 mL に含まれる赤血球の数を算出しなさい。ただし、計数エリアは幅 1 mm、深さ 0.1 mm（図 2）、$1\ \text{mL}=10^{3}\ \text{mm}^{3}$ である。計算過程を必ず記述し、有効数字 2 桁、単位を$\bigcirc.\bigcirc \times 10^{\bigcirc}$ 細胞個／mL というかたちで答えなさい。

problems.title: Experiment 1, Question 2
problems.problem:
Experiment 1: Concentration of red blood cells in the blood
In animals, a large number of red blood cells is needed to carry oxygen to the many tissues of the body. You will calculate the concentration of red blood cells contained in the preserved blood and find the number of red blood cells contained in the blood of one individual animal (in this experiment, a sheep).

Question 2. Assuming that 6% of the body mass of a sheep is blood, calculate the total number of red blood cells contained in one sheep of 80 kg. Take the specific gravity of blood as 1.0 g/mL, and give the answer to 2 significant figures.
problems.problem_orig:
実験１　血液中の赤血球の濃度
動物では、体内の多くの組織に酸素を運ぶために多量の赤血球が必要とされます。保存血に含まれる赤血球の濃度を算出し、動物（本実験ではヒツジ）１個体の血液中に含まれる赤血球の数を調べます。

問題 2．ヒツジの体重の 6 %が血液成分と仮定し、80 kg のヒツジ 1 頭に含まれる全赤血球細胞の数を計算しなさい。ただし、血液の比重を 1.0 g/mL とし、有効数字 2 桁で答えなさい。

problems.title: Experiment 2, Question 3
problems.problem:
Experiment 2: Concentration of haemoglobin in the blood
Red blood cells burst easily when the osmotic pressure of the external solution is lowered, and their internal substances flow out. This phenomenon is called haemolysis. In the next experiment, the haemoglobin present inside the cells is made to flow out by haemolysis, and its concentration is measured optically. Together with the result of Experiment 1, you will find "the number of haemoglobin molecules contained in one red blood cell", the final goal of this experiment.

Experiment
1. First, close the cap of the 1/20-diluted preserved blood tightly, invert it up and down about 5–6 times to stir it, and mix well. Next, put 1.0 mL of the 1/20-diluted preserved blood into each of 5 microtubes and centrifuge them at 5,000 rpm for 2 minutes. At this time, take care that the arrangement of the tubes is balanced.
2. After the treatment, check that the red blood cells have sedimented in each microtube, carefully draw off the unneeded supernatant with the P1000 micropipette and discard it into the waste container.
3. Into each of the 5 microtubes in which the red blood cells have sedimented, put 1.0 mL each of physiological saline, physiological saline diluted to 1/4 with pure water, physiological saline diluted to 1/2 with pure water, physiological saline diluted to 3/4 with pure water and pure water (5 in total) with the P1000 micropipette, and stir well by pipetting.
4. Leave them to stand for 3 minutes and centrifuge them under the same conditions as before (after the treatment, sketch the state of the blood in the microtubes: Question 3).
5. With the P1000 micropipette, transfer 0.8 mL of the supernatant of each microtube to each of the 5 15 mL centrifuge tubes, and then dilute 5-fold with pure water.
6. After stirring the diluted supernatants well by pipetting, write 生理 (physiological), 3/4, 1/2, 1/4 and 純水 (pure water) on the upper part of the cells with the felt-tip pen, put 2 mL of each into its spectrophotometer cell and line them up in the cell stand.
7. Raise your hand and hand the samples, together with the cell stand, to a member of staff (the staff will measure the absorbance* of each sample at 555 nm with the spectrophotometer.)
*Absorbance refers to the degree to which a substance absorbs light.

(Reference) The absorbance $A$ in relation to the concentration of a substance is defined by Equation ① below.
$A = -\log_{10}\mathrm{T} = -\log_{10}(I/I_{0})$ ・・・ Equation ①
(where T is the transmittance of the light, and $I_{0}$ and $I$ are the intensities of the incident light and the transmitted light)

$A = \varepsilon\,\mathrm{CL}$ ・・・ Equation ②

The ε shown by haemoglobin at a wavelength of 555 nm is 13.0.
Note: mol / L is called the molar concentration and is a unit that expresses the number of molecules in a solution.
 1 mol / L means that 1 L of solution contains $6.0 \times 10^{23}$ molecules.

Question 3. Sketch the state of each sample in the microtubes after the centrifugation treatment marked with ＊. Also, from these experimental results, write down the characteristics of the dissolution of the blood and what can be learned about red blood cells from those characteristics.

　1 mol / L は 1 L の溶液に $6.0 \times 10^{23}$ 個の分子が含まれていることを表している。

Experiment 2: Concentration of haemoglobin in the blood
Red blood cells burst easily when the osmotic pressure of the external solution is lowered, and their internal substances flow out. This phenomenon is called haemolysis. In the next experiment, the haemoglobin present inside the cells is made to flow out by haemolysis, and its concentration is measured optically. Together with the result of Experiment 1, you will find "the number of haemoglobin molecules contained in one red blood cell", the final goal of this experiment.

Experiment
3. Into each of the 5 microtubes in which the red blood cells have sedimented, put 1.0 mL each of physiological saline, physiological saline diluted to 1/4 with pure water, physiological saline diluted to 1/2 with pure water, physiological saline diluted to 3/4 with pure water and pure water (5 in total) with the P1000 micropipette, and stir well by pipetting.
4. Leave them to stand for 3 minutes and centrifuge them under the same conditions as before (after the treatment, sketch the state of the blood in the microtubes: Question 3).
5. With the P1000 micropipette, transfer 0.8 mL of the supernatant of each microtube to each of the 5 15 mL centrifuge tubes, and then dilute 5-fold with pure water.
6. After stirring the diluted supernatants well by pipetting, write 生理 (physiological), 3/4, 1/2, 1/4 and 純水 (pure water) on the upper part of the cells with the felt-tip pen, put 2 mL of each into its spectrophotometer cell and line them up in the cell stand.
7. Raise your hand and hand the samples, together with the cell stand, to a member of staff (the staff will measure the absorbance* of each sample at 555 nm with the spectrophotometer.)
*Absorbance refers to the degree to which a substance absorbs light.

Question 4. Draw a graph with the absorbance obtained on the vertical axis and the concentration of the stepwise-diluted physiological saline on the horizontal axis. Also, choose from among the 5 steps of diluted physiological saline whose absorbance was measured the highest concentration of physiological saline at complete dissolution (the state in which the red blood cells are completely haemolysed), and write down its absorbance.

problems.title: Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam 4: Plant molecular biology (time limit 90 minutes)

Introduction
Blue roses, blue carnations
— Creating new flowers by gene transfer —

Just as the word “Blue rose” carries the meaning of “impossible” or “something that does not exist”, the creation of blue roses and blue carnations had until now been considered impossible. However, with the development of genetic recombination technology in recent years, their development has succeeded: the blue rose (Applause, 喝采) has been given the flower language “dreams come true”, and the blue carnation (Moondust) “eternal happiness”. The colour of a flower is broadly determined by what kind of pigments accumulate in the petals; the red petals of roses and carnations contain much of a pigment called cyanidin, and the orange petals much of a pigment called pelargonidin (see the figure below). However, roses and carnations do not have the gene encoding flavonoid 3′,5′-hydroxylase, called the blue gene, and for this reason the petals of these plants could not biosynthesise delphinidin, a blue pigment. Suntory Flowers therefore succeeded in creating varieties with blue petals by introducing the cDNA (note) of the blue gene possessed by pansy and petunia into carnations and roses using genetic recombination technology. These plants are genetically modified plants, but with national approval the blue carnation went on sale in Heisei 13 and 14 [2001 and 2002], and the blue rose in Heisei 21 [2009].
Note) cDNA is DNA synthesised by reverse transcriptase using RNA as a template.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2014-7-1-fig1.png

Flavonoid (anthocyanin) synthesis pathway

Figure labels (Japanese → English): バラの花色色素合成の経路 = pathway of the synthesis of rose flower-colour pigments; 赤色遺伝子 = red gene; 青色遺伝子（フラボノイド3',5'水酸化酵素） = blue gene (flavonoid 3′,5′-hydroxylase); シアニジン = cyanidin; ペラルゴニジン = pelargonidin; デルフィニジン = delphinidin; バラがもともと持っている色素 = pigments that roses originally have; 青色色素 = blue pigment; サントリーフラワーズHPより = from the Suntory Flowers website.

Samples and apparatus

Check them, putting a tick ✔ in each □. If anything is missing, let us know by raising your hand.

Samples and reagents
□ DNA solutions ①–⑤ (1 tube each)
□ DNA marker (blue label: 1 tube)
□ Buffer (10× concentration) (yellow label: 1 tube)
□ Xylene cyanol solution (green label: 1 tube)
□ Distilled water (white label: 1 tube)
□ Restriction enzyme solution (HindIII) (red label, on ice: 1 tube)

Apparatus
□ Micropipettes (P200 and P20: 1 each)
□ Pipette tips (yellow: 1 box)
□ 1.5 mL microtubes (3)
□ Ice box (with ice: 1)
□ Stopwatch (1)
□ Electrophoresis apparatus and agarose gel (1 set)
□ Floater (1)
□ Mini centrifuge (1)
□ Ruler (take it out of your own experiment set and put it on the desk)
□ Gloves (take them out of your own experiment set and put them on the desk)
□ Marker pen (take it out of your own experiment set and put it on the desk)

In addition, the Kimwipes and Kim Towels placed on the desk may be used freely.

Use the 2 plastic beakers for waste: one is for solids such as tips, the other for liquids.

Experiment. Restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis of DNA
In this experiment you will examine whether the blue gene contained in 4 kinds of Moondust is derived from pansy or from petunia.

Since ordinary carnations do not have the blue gene, a carnation that has the blue gene can be said to be a genetically modified carnation. Therefore, for these 4 kinds of Moondust, part of the base sequence of the blue gene was amplified using the PCR method, which is used in genetic diagnosis and elsewhere (hereafter called the PCR amplification product). When these were electrophoresed as a preliminary experiment, the band appeared at the same position for the PCR amplification products of both blue genes, the one derived from pansy and the one derived from petunia. In other words, it was not possible to tell them apart by the molecular size of the PCR amplification product. Then, on looking at the base sequences of the PCR amplification products, it was found that only the blue gene derived from pansy has, within the PCR amplification product, a sequence that is recognised and cut by a restriction enzyme (HindIII). In this experiment you will actually carry out restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis on the DNA amplified by PCR, and discuss the results on the basis of the bands that appear.

Carry out the experiment below, answering as instructed.

Restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis
1. The DNA solutions handed out, of 5 kinds (DNA solutions ①–④ are from the flowers of Moondust kinds ①–④ above, respectively, and DNA solution ⑤ is from the leaves of one of Moondust kinds ①–④), each contain 8 µL of a solution containing a PCR amplification product. Add 12 µL of the solution prepared by the procedure below (restriction enzyme mix) to each DNA solution, and carry out the restriction enzyme treatment in a total volume of 20 µL. Also answer Question 1 on the reaction mixture for the restriction enzyme treatment.
• Use an empty 1.5 mL microtube to prepare the restriction enzyme mix. Work out for yourself the volume you think is needed for the reactions of the 5 DNA solutions, and prepare it.
• As for the restriction enzyme, prepare the restriction enzyme mix so that 2 µL of the restriction enzyme solution (HindIII) handed out goes into each reaction mixture in which the enzyme reaction is carried out. Add this solution to the restriction enzyme mix last.
• Calculate and prepare the buffer so that it is at the optimal concentration when the enzyme reaction is carried out. The buffer handed out this time is at 10 times the optimal concentration.
• Adjust the concentrations of the buffer and the restriction enzyme contained in the restriction enzyme mix with distilled water.
• After adding each solution, mix well to make the restriction enzyme mix uniform. Also, after adding the restriction enzyme mix to each DNA solution, mix well to make it uniform.
When you have finished the preparation up to this point, signal by raising your hand, insert the 5 tubes into the floater and hand them to an assistant. The assistant will put the tubes into a 37 °C water bath and carry out the restriction enzyme treatment for 20 minutes. While waiting you may work on other questions (Questions 2–4). The assistant will return the samples after the treatment is finished.

実験試験４　植物分子生物学（制限時間90分）

はじめに
青いバラ、青いカーネーション
～遺伝子導入による新しい花の作出～

“Blue rose”という言葉には「不可能」や「存在しないもの」という意味があるように、青いバラや青いカーネーションの作出はこれまで不可能とされてきました。しかしながら近年の遺伝子組換え技術の発達によりそれらの開発に成功し、青いバラ（アプローズ、喝采）の花言葉には「夢 かなう」が、青いカーネーション（ムーンダスト）には「永遠の幸福」が与えられています。花の色は花弁にどのようなな色素が蓄積するかによっておおむね決まっており、バラやカーネーションの赤色花弁にはシアニジン、オレンジ色花弁にはペラルゴニジンという色素が多く含まれています（下図参照）。しかしながら、バラやカーネーションは青色遺伝子と呼ばれるフラボノイド 3’, 5’ 水酸化酵素をコードする遺伝子をもっておらず、そのため、これらの花弁では青色色素であるデルフィニジンを生合成することができなかったのです。そこでサントリーフラワーズはパンジーやペチュニアがもっている青色遺伝子のcDNA注)を、遺伝子組換え技術を用いてカーネーションやバラに導入することで、青色の花弁をもつ品種の作出に成功しました。これらの植物は遺伝子組換え植物ですが、国の許可を得て、青いカーネーションは平成13、14年に、青いバラは平成21年に販売が開始されています。
注）cDNAとはRNAを鋳型にして逆転写酵素により合成したDNA

□ ものさし（自分の実験セットから机の上に出してください）

problems.title: Question 2
problems.problem:
Experiment. Restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis of DNA
In this experiment you will examine whether the blue gene contained in 4 kinds of Moondust is derived from pansy or from petunia.

Since ordinary carnations do not have the blue gene, a carnation that has the blue gene can be said to be a genetically modified carnation. Therefore, for these 4 kinds of Moondust, part of the base sequence of the blue gene was amplified using the PCR method, which is used in genetic diagnosis and elsewhere (hereafter called the PCR amplification product). When these were electrophoresed as a preliminary experiment, the band appeared at the same position for the PCR amplification products of both blue genes, the one derived from pansy and the one derived from petunia. In other words, it was not possible to tell them apart by the molecular size of the PCR amplification product. Then, on looking at the base sequences of the PCR amplification products, it was found that only the blue gene derived from pansy has, within the PCR amplification product, a sequence that is recognised and cut by a restriction enzyme (HindIII). In this experiment you will actually carry out restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis on the DNA amplified by PCR, and discuss the results on the basis of the bands that appear.

Question 2. Looking at the photographs of the carnations provided, can you infer from their colour and shape whether the blue gene of carnation kinds ①–④ is derived from pansy or from petunia? Also explain the reason why you think so.

problems.title: Question 4
problems.problem: Question 4. When a genetically modified organism is brought onto the general market, it is necessary to comply with the “Act on Securing Biological Diversity through Regulation of the Use etc. of Genetically Modified Organisms etc. (Cartagena Act)”. In other words, genetically modified organisms etc. must be kept from affecting wild animals, plants etc. Describe what measures are thought to have been taken in the blue carnations used in this experiment so that they do not affect wild animals, plants etc.
problems.problem_orig: 問題4．遺伝子組換え生物を一般市場に持ち込む場合、「遺伝子組換え生物等の使用等の規制による生物の多様性の確保に関する法律（カルタヘナ法）」を遵守する必要がある。つまり、遺伝子組換え生物等が野生の動植物等へ影響を与えないようにしなければならない。本実験で用いている青いカーネーションでは、野生の動植物等へ影響を与えないようにするためにどのような工夫がなされていると考えられるか述べなさい。

problems.title: Question 5
problems.problem:
Experiment. Restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis of DNA
In this experiment you will examine whether the blue gene contained in 4 kinds of Moondust is derived from pansy or from petunia.

Since ordinary carnations do not have the blue gene, a carnation that has the blue gene can be said to be a genetically modified carnation. Therefore, for these 4 kinds of Moondust, part of the base sequence of the blue gene was amplified using the PCR method, which is used in genetic diagnosis and elsewhere (hereafter called the PCR amplification product). In this experiment you will actually carry out restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis on the DNA amplified by PCR, and discuss the results on the basis of the bands that appear.

Restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis
1. The DNA solutions handed out, of 5 kinds (DNA solutions ①–④ are from the flowers of Moondust kinds ①–④ above, respectively, and DNA solution ⑤ is from the leaves of one of Moondust kinds ①–④), each contain 8 µL of a solution containing a PCR amplification product.

2. Add 2 µL of xylene cyanol solution to the reaction mixture after the restriction enzyme treatment, mix well, and then put 10 µL into a well (hole) of the agarose gel. For the DNA marker, put 5 µL into a well. Load them in this order from the left: marker, restriction-enzyme-treated DNA solution ①, likewise ②, … likewise ⑤. Carry out electrophoresis at 100 V for 20–30 minutes.

• Wear gloves when working on the electrophoresis. If, for example, the gel moves inside the electrophoresis tank, adjust its position wearing gloves, and do not touch the gel or the liquid in the tank with bare hands.
• The agarose gel used for the electrophoresis has been handed out ready-made. Put the solutions prepared as above into the wells. The wells left over are spares. When you have finished putting the 5 reaction mixtures and the DNA marker into the wells, switch on and begin the electrophoresis.
• When you have switched on and started timing the 20–30 minutes with the stopwatch, signal by raising your hand. An assistant will hand you an example photograph of an electrophoresis result taken beforehand (used in Questions 5–9).
• When 20–30 minutes have passed on the stopwatch, switch off. Your electrophoresis result will be photographed by the exam staff and assessed.

Question 5. Using the example photograph of agarose gel electrophoresis handed to you by the assistant, make a graph of the number of base pairs (bp, vertical axis) against the distance from the well to the band (mm, horizontal axis) from the positions of the bands of the DNA marker.

Experiment. Restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis of DNA
In this experiment you will examine whether the blue gene contained in 4 kinds of Moondust is derived from pansy or from petunia.

Since ordinary carnations do not have the blue gene, a carnation that has the blue gene can be said to be a genetically modified carnation. Therefore, for these 4 kinds of Moondust, part of the base sequence of the blue gene was amplified using the PCR method, which is used in genetic diagnosis and elsewhere (hereafter called the PCR amplification product). When these were electrophoresed as a preliminary experiment, the band appeared at the same position for the PCR amplification products of both blue genes, the one derived from pansy and the one derived from petunia. In other words, it was not possible to tell them apart by the molecular size of the PCR amplification product. Then, on looking at the base sequences of the PCR amplification products, it was found that only the blue gene derived from pansy has, within the PCR amplification product, a sequence that is recognised and cut by a restriction enzyme (HindIII). In this experiment you will actually carry out restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis on the DNA amplified by PCR, and discuss the results on the basis of the bands that appear.

Restriction enzyme treatment and electrophoresis
1. The DNA solutions handed out, of 5 kinds (DNA solutions ①–④ are from the flowers of Moondust kinds ①–④ above, respectively, and DNA solution ⑤ is from the leaves of one of Moondust kinds ①–④), each contain 8 µL of a solution containing a PCR amplification product.

2. Add 2 µL of xylene cyanol solution to the reaction mixture after the restriction enzyme treatment, mix well, and then put 10 µL into a well (hole) of the agarose gel. For the DNA marker, put 5 µL into a well. Load them in this order from the left: marker, restriction-enzyme-treated DNA solution ①, likewise ②, … likewise ⑤. Carry out electrophoresis at 100 V for 20–30 minutes.

Question 8. DNA solution ⑤ is the PCR amplification product of DNA extracted from the leaves of one of Moondust kinds ①–④. Which of DNA solutions ①–④ does its band pattern in the electrophoresis after restriction enzyme treatment resemble? If there are several, give them all. Also explain why a PCR amplification product of the blue gene is obtained even when DNA extracted from leaves is used.

実験．DNAの制限酵素処理と電気泳動
本実験では4種類のムーンダストに含まれている青色遺伝子がパンジー由来かペチュニア由来かを調べます。

青色遺伝子は普通のカーネーションにはありませんので、青色遺伝子をもっていれば組換えカーネーションであると言うことができます。そこでこれら4種のムーンダストについて、遺伝子診断等で用いられるPCR法を用いて青色遺伝子の塩基配列の一部を増幅させました（以下PCR増幅産物と呼びます）。予備実験としてそれらの電気泳動を行ったところ、パンジーまたはペチュニアに由来するどちらの青色遺伝子のPCR増幅産物も同じ位置にバンドが現れました。つまり、PCR増幅産物の分子サイズによってこれらの違いを判別することはできませんでした。そこで、PCR増幅産物の塩基配列に着目したところ、パンジー由来の青色遺伝子だけがPCR増幅産物内に制限酵素（HindIII）によって認識・切断される配列をもっていることがわかりました。本実験では実際にPCRによって増幅されたDNAに対して制限酵素処理と電気泳動を行い、現れるバンドをもとに考察を行います。

制限酵素処理および電気泳動
１．配布されたDNA溶液は、5種類（DNA溶液①～④はそれぞれ上記ムーンダストの種類①～④の花由来、DNA溶液⑤はムーンダスト種類①～④のいずれかの葉由来）のPCR増幅産物を含む溶液が8 µLずつ入れられている。

２．制限酵素処理の終了した反応液に2 µLのキシレンシアノール溶液を加え、良く混合した後、アガロースゲルのウェル（穴）に10 µL入れなさい。DNAマーカーについては5 µLをウェルに入れなさい。入れる順番は左からマーカー、制限酵素処理済みのDNA溶液①、同②、･･･同⑤としなさい。100 Vで20～30分間、電気泳動を行いなさい。

問題8．DNA溶液⑤は種類①～④のムーンダストのいずれかの葉から抽出したDNAのPCR増幅産物である。制限酵素処理後の電気泳動におけるバンドパターンはDNA溶液①～④のうちどれと似ていますか。複数ある場合は複数挙げなさい。また、なぜ葉から抽出したDNAを用いても青色遺伝子のPCR増幅産物が得られるのかを説明しなさい。

To examine the number of cultured cells, it was decided to measure the number of cells in the culture medium using the haemocytometer shown in Figure 1. A haemocytometer is a glass plate similar to a glass slide. When water is dropped onto its central part and a cover glass is placed on it, the water fills a recess 0.1 mm deep called the counting chamber. When this is observed under a light microscope, compartments of various sizes can be seen (Figure 2).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-1-1-fig1.png

Figure 1: Haemocytometer

Figure labels (Japanese → English): カバーガラス = cover glass; 血球計算盤 = haemocytometer; 計算室 = counting chamber.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-1-1-fig2.png

Figure 2: View under the light microscope

A cell suspension in which the cultured cells were floating was diluted 10-fold, the counting chamber of this haemocytometer was filled with it using a micropipette, a cover glass was placed on it, and it was observed under a light microscope. Table 1 shows the results of counting the cells in the four compartments ①–④ of the haemocytometer (each compartment is 1 mm × 1 mm).

The ratio of the amount of CO₂ released by an organism through respiration to the amount of O₂ it absorbs (CO₂/O₂) is called the respiratory quotient (RQ). For gases, regardless of the molecular species, equal volumes contain equal numbers of molecules at a given pressure and temperature. Therefore, the RQ can be obtained by measuring the volume ratio of CO₂ to O₂ at a given pressure and temperature.

Suppose that a human eats only glucose (grape sugar, C₆H₁₂O₆) as the metabolic substrate and metabolises it completely. In this case, by passing through glycolysis, the citric acid cycle and the electron transport chain (including oxidative phosphorylation), one molecule of glucose becomes six molecules of carbon dioxide and six molecules of water. Since six molecules of oxygen are consumed in this process, RQ = 1. Because the ratio of O₂ consumed to CO₂ released is expected to differ when the metabolic substrate differs, the diet can be inferred by examining the RQ.

For questions (1)–(3) below, choose the correct combination of answers from A–L. (4 points)

(1) Which process consumes oxygen in the metabolism of glucose?

(ア) glycolysis

(イ) citric acid cycle

(ウ) electron transport chain

(2) Which process produces carbon dioxide in the metabolism of glucose?

(エ) glycolysis

(オ) citric acid cycle

(カ) electron transport chain

(3) The RQs obtained when a sugar, an alcohol and a fatty acid are each used as the metabolic substrate were compared by choosing glucose, ethanol (C₂H₆O) and linoleic acid (C₁₈H₃₂O₂). When the RQs are arranged in decreasing order, which of the following is obtained?

(キ) linoleic acid > glucose > ethanol

(ク) glucose > linoleic acid > ethanol

(ケ) glucose > ethanol > linoleic acid

(コ) linoleic acid > ethanol > glucose

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c}  & \text{A} & \text{B} & \text{C} & \text{D} & \text{E} & \text{F} & \text{G} & \text{H} & \text{I} & \text{J} & \text{K} & \text{L} \\ \hline \text{(1)} & \text{ア} & \text{ア} & \text{ア} & \text{ア} & \text{イ} & \text{イ} & \text{イ} & \text{イ} & \text{ウ} & \text{ウ} & \text{ウ} & \text{ウ} \\ \text{(2)} & \text{エ} & \text{オ} & \text{カ} & \text{カ} & \text{エ} & \text{エ} & \text{オ} & \text{カ} & \text{エ} & \text{オ} & \text{オ} & \text{カ} \\ \text{(3)} & \text{キ} & \text{ク} & \text{ケ} & \text{コ} & \text{キ} & \text{ク} & \text{ケ} & \text{コ} & \text{キ} & \text{ク} & \text{ケ} & \text{コ} \end{array}$$

In Escherichia coli, the genes for the three kinds of enzymes that act in the breakdown of lactose (hereafter called lactose-degrading enzymes) are transcribed when lactose is present in the medium, but are not transcribed when lactose is absent. As the figure shows, regions upstream of the lactose-degrading enzyme genes, called the regulatory gene, the operator and the promoter, are involved in the control of this transcription.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-1-3-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 調節遺伝子 = regulatory gene; プロモーター = promoter; オペレーター = operator; ラクトースの分解にはたらく3種類の酵素の遺伝子 = genes for the three kinds of enzymes that act in the breakdown of lactose.

Mutant strains ア, イ and ウ of E. coli with abnormal lactose metabolism were found. In ア, although there was no abnormality in the genes for the lactose-degrading enzymes, the lactose-degrading enzymes were not synthesised even when it was grown on a lactose medium. On the other hand, in イ and ウ, the lactose-degrading enzymes were synthesised even on a medium without lactose. To examine イ and ウ further, a DNA fragment containing the regulatory gene, promoter and operator regions was extracted from wild-type E. coli and introduced into the mutant strains イ and ウ. As a result, in イ synthesis of the lactose-degrading enzymes on a medium without lactose was no longer seen, but in ウ synthesis of the lactose-degrading enzymes on a medium without lactose continued as before.

From the above experimental results, in which part of the region that controls the lactose-degrading enzymes is the mutation thought to have occurred in each of the mutant strains ア, イ and ウ? Choose the most appropriate combination from A–F. (4 points)

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}  & \text{Mutant strain ア} & \text{Mutant strain イ} & \text{Mutant strain ウ} \\ \hline \text{A} & \text{regulatory gene} & \text{promoter} & \text{operator} \\ \text{B} & \text{regulatory gene} & \text{operator} & \text{promoter} \\ \text{C} & \text{promoter} & \text{regulatory gene} & \text{operator} \\ \text{D} & \text{promoter} & \text{operator} & \text{regulatory gene} \\ \text{E} & \text{operator} & \text{regulatory gene} & \text{promoter} \\ \text{F} & \text{operator} & \text{promoter} & \text{regulatory gene} \end{array}$$

Normally, food poisoning caused by pathogenic bacteria does not develop unless a certain sizeable number of them is ingested. Here, as a fictional story, consider a food-poisoning incident caused by a pathogenic bacterium.

The fictional pathogenic bacterium Vader causes food poisoning when more than 100,000 cells are ingested at one time, but does not cause illness when that number or fewer is ingested. A food-poisoning incident occurred at the restaurant "Star Wars". It had been noticed that the pathogen Vader had contaminated a soup stock, and the stock was to be discarded, but a serious mistake occurred and a few drops of this soup stock got mixed into 1,000 mL of fresh bouillon soup at 12 noon. A later investigation estimated that about 1,000 Vader cells were introduced at that time. When this bouillon soup was served to customers in portions of 100 mL, customers who consumed it up to 8 p.m. did not become ill, but food poisoning occurred among customers who consumed it from 9 p.m. onwards, and "Star Wars" was ordered to suspend business.

Assuming that the Vader cells introduced into the bouillon soup immediately began to divide and multiply, and that the customers drank all of their bouillon soup, what is the generation time of Vader in minutes? Choose the closest time from A–L. The generation time is the time needed for the number of bacteria to double, and Vader is assumed to have continued to divide and multiply at the same rate until the soup was served to the customers. (3 points)

A. 5 min

B. 10 min

C. 15 min

D. 20 min

E. 25 min

F. 30 min

G. 40 min

H. 50 min

I. 60 min

J. 70 min

K. 80 min

L. 90 min

When nondisjunction of a certain chromosome occurs in the first or second division of meiosis, a gamete with one extra chromosome is formed, and when it is fertilised with a normal gamete, a trisomic individual with three homologous chromosomes arises. By knowing the types (alleles) of a gene showing polymorphism in a trisomic individual and in its parents, the origin of the trisomy can be determined.

Now suppose that, at a certain locus close to the kinetochore (centromere) of the autosome that has become trisomic, the genotypes of the parents were heterozygous $a/b$ in the mother and homozygous $c/c$ in the father. When the genotype of the trisomic child was $a/a/c$, $a/b/c$ or $b/c/c$, on which parent's side is the nondisjunction of the chromosome thought to have occurred? And did it occur at the first division or at the second division? Choose the correct combination of answers from A–L. Assume that no recombination occurred between the locus considered here and the kinetochore. (4 points)

① maternal side, first division

② paternal side, first division

③ maternal side, second division

④ paternal side, second division

⑤ maternal side, first or second division

⑥ paternal side, first or second division

The membrane potential of a cell expresses the potential of the inside of the cell membrane taking the outside of the cell membrane as the reference (0 V). The cell membrane has K channels that are always open (leak K channels). Because the concentration of potassium ions (K⁺) in the cytoplasm is kept higher than outside the cell, K⁺ tends to flow out of the cell by diffusion. However, owing to differences between the inside and outside of the cell in the concentrations of ions that cannot pass freely through the cell membrane, and so on, the inside of the cell is negatively charged compared with the outside, so K⁺ tends to flow into the cell. Equilibrium is reached when the outflow and inflow balance. The membrane potential produced in this way is called the resting potential and is given by the following equation, using the K⁺ concentrations in the Nernst equation.

$$V\,(\mathrm{mV}) = 61.5 \log_{10}(C_{\mathrm{Ko}}/C_{\mathrm{Ki}})$$

Here, $C_{\mathrm{Ko}}$ is the extracellular concentration of K⁺ and $C_{\mathrm{Ki}}$ is the intracellular concentration of K⁺. (Note: $\log_{10} 100 = 2$, $\log_{10} 10 = 1$, $\log_{10} 1 = 0$, $\log_{10} 0.1 = -1$, $\log_{10} 0.01 = -2$)

The cell membrane also has many voltage-gated Na channels, which are closed at rest and open temporarily, for a very short time, in response to a voltage stimulus at or above the threshold. When a voltage stimulus at or above the threshold is applied, these voltage-gated Na channels open all at once (excitation). The amount of Na⁺ that moves in this state is very large compared with the amounts of K⁺ and other ions that move through various channels. As a result, a membrane potential that depends strongly on the Na⁺ concentration is produced. This is called the action potential and is observed as a pulse of 1 millisecond or less. Here, the membrane potential during this excitation is also considered to be determined approximately by the Nernst equation.

The following model has been proposed for the diversity of species living on an island far from a continent.

The species diversity of an island is determined by the balance between the immigration rate of species from the continent (number of immigrating species per unit time) and the extinction rate of the species already established (number of species going extinct per unit time). The immigration rate is highest when there are no organisms at all on the island, and it decreases as the number of species living there increases. Each species may go extinct for various reasons, but, owing to effects such as interspecific competition, the extinction rate increases as the number of species increases. Species diversity, that is, the number of species living there, reaches an equilibrium when the immigration rate and the extinction rate become equal. In the figure, the point at which the immigration-rate line and the extinction-rate line cross indicates the equilibrium number of species on that island (Figure 1). The number of species is also strongly affected by the size of the island and by whether its distance from the continent is near or far (Figures 2 and 3).

Hypothesis 1: This plant is cross-pollinated, but the survival rates of individuals of the three genotypes differ. If the survival rate of the homozygous genotypes A₁A₁ and A₂A₂ is taken as 1, the survival rate of the heterozygous genotype A₁A₂ is ( ア ).

Hypothesis 2: In this plant, the survival rates of individuals of the three genotypes are the same. However, it is sometimes self-pollinated and sometimes cross-pollinated, and the ratio of self-pollination to cross-pollination is ( イ ).

To test these hypotheses, the allele frequencies and genotype frequencies at other loci were examined, and all the other loci were found to be in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium. This supports ( ウ ) of the two hypotheses.

③ Almost all affected persons are male.

In diploid Drosophila, sex is determined by the number of X chromosomes, and the presence or absence of the Y chromosome has nothing to do with survival or sex determination. That is, a fly with one X chromosome becomes a male and one with two becomes a female; moreover, Drosophila with zero, or three or more, X chromosomes cannot live. It is known that, in XX/Y females, which have an attached-X chromosome formed by the fusion of two X chromosomes (written $\underline{\mathrm{XX}}$ below) and one Y chromosome, $\underline{\mathrm{XX}}$ and Y always separate at meiosis and $\underline{\mathrm{XX}}$ is inherited as it is, without changing its form. Such an $\underline{\mathrm{XX}}$/Y female was crossed with an X/Y male.

Which of the following statements are appropriate explanations of this cross? Choose the correct combination from A–L. (3 points)

① The sex ratio of the offspring born is male : female = 1 : 2.

② The sex ratio of the offspring born is male : female = 2 : 1.

The three-domain theory, which divides all living organisms into three groups, is generally accepted. The three groups are the archaea (archaebacteria), the bacteria (eubacteria) and the eukaryotes. When the phylogenetic relationships of these three groups are considered, a phylogenetic tree like that in Figure 1 is considered first. This tree does not show the common ancestor of all organisms (corresponding to the root of the tree); it is called an unrooted tree. Placing a root on this tree means considering the order in which the groups branched off from the common ancestor of all organisms, and there are three ways of placing the root, a–c in Figure 2. For example, placing the root at a in Figure 2 gives a rooted tree like that in Figure 3. The black circle in Figure 3 is the common ancestor of all organisms. Here, if it is assumed that the common ancestor had a nucleus, "loss of the nucleus" occurred twice, as in Figure 4. If, however, it is assumed that the common ancestor had no nucleus, "gain of the nucleus" occurred once. In the maximum parsimony method, one of the methods of constructing phylogenetic trees, a tree with fewer changes is considered to be closer to the true tree.

If the root is placed at b and at c in Figure 2 to make two further rooted trees in the same way, and for each the cases in which the ancestral organism has a nucleus and has no nucleus are considered, four trees that differ in the changes in the presence or absence of the nucleus are obtained. Among these four trees, how many can be explained by assuming that a change concerning the nucleus (gain or loss) occurred only once (trees with a minimum number of changes of 1)? problems.title: Experiment 1 (Questions 1-1 to 1-3)
problems.problem:
Practical exam I, mathematical biology (70 minutes). The calculator and ruler in the tote bag that was distributed are used. During the exam, the preliminary-session booklet and the preliminary-session answer sheets may be consulted.

Experiment 1

The generation of circadian rhythms is considered.

Question 1-1

Many genes are involved, interacting in complex ways, in the generation of circadian rhythms. In recent years, however, it has been suggested that, as introduced in the preliminary session, this phenomenon can be understood by considering, roughly, a relationship made up of three genes (Figure 1).

Here, first consider the case in which, for three genes A, B and C, the following relationship holds: when gene A, B or C becomes ON (OFF), it makes gene B, C or A, respectively, OFF (ON). Formulating the ON–OFF of each gene on this basis gives

$$\begin{array}{lll} \text{If A is ON (OFF) at time } t & \text{then} & \text{B is OFF (ON) at time } t+1 \\ \text{If B is ON (OFF) at time } t & \text{then} & \text{C is OFF (ON) at time } t+1 \\ \text{If C is ON (OFF) at time } t & \text{then} & \text{A is OFF (ON) at time } t+1 \end{array}$$

Now, if at time 0 two of the genes A, B and C are ON and the remaining one is OFF, what change over time does the ON–OFF of each gene show after that? As in the preliminary session, calculate up to time 15 using a table like the one below, enter the result in the answer box, and then describe the pattern of the change in about 3 to 4 lines.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-2-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 時刻 = time; 遺伝子 = gene.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-2-1-fig2.png

Figure 1 The three genes A, B and C, and the relationship between the genes whose ON–OFF keeps a rhythm.
Here a T-shaped arrow with a flat tip shows that, when each gene is ON (OFF), it makes the gene at its tip OFF (ON).

Question 1-2

Suppose that four genes A, B, C and D exist as in Figure 2, and that their relationship is formulated as

$$\begin{array}{lll} \text{If A is ON (OFF) at time } t & \text{then} & \text{B is OFF (ON) at time } t+1 \\ \text{If B is ON (OFF) at time } t & \text{then} & \text{C is OFF (ON) at time } t+1 \\ \text{If C is ON (OFF) at time } t & \text{then} & \text{D is OFF (ON) at time } t+1 \\ \text{If D is ON (OFF) at time } t & \text{then} & \text{A is OFF (ON) at time } t+1 \end{array}$$

Here, for each of the cases in which, at time 0, one of the four genes is ON and three are OFF, and in which two are ON and two are OFF, how does the ON–OFF of each gene change over time after that? Calculate using a table as in Question 1-1, enter the result in the answer box, and then describe the pattern of the change in about 3 to 4 lines for each initial condition.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-2-1-fig3.png

Figure 2 The four genes A, B, C and D, and the relationship between the genes whose ON–OFF keeps a rhythm.
Here a T-shaped arrow with a flat tip shows that, when each gene is ON (OFF), it makes the gene at its tip OFF (ON).

Question 1-3

Of the relationship made up of three genes considered in Question 1-1 and the relationship made up of four genes considered in Question 1-2, which is thought to be more suitable as a relationship that generates a biological rhythm? Describe it in about 3 to 4 lines, giving your reasons.
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験Ⅰ　数理生物学（70分）。配布されたトートバック内の電卓，定規を使用する。試験中，予備体験冊子や予備体験解答用紙は参考にしてよい。

実験１

概日リズムの発生について考察する。

問 1-1

概日リズムの生成には多くの遺伝子が複雑に関係し合っている。しかし近年この現象は，予備体験で紹介したように，大まかに 3 つの遺伝子からなる関係を考えることで理解できる事が示唆されている（図１）。

ここではまず，3 つの遺伝子 A，B，C について，遺伝子 A，B，C が ON (OFF) になるとそれぞれ遺伝子 B，C，A を OFF (ON)にする，という関係が成立している場合を考える。これに基づいて各遺伝子の ON-OFF を定式化すると

$$\begin{array}{llll} \text{時刻 } t \text{ で A が ON (OFF)} & \text{ならば} & \text{時刻 } t+1 \text{ で B が} & \text{OFF (ON)} \\ \text{時刻 } t \text{ で B が ON (OFF)} & \text{ならば} & \text{時刻 } t+1 \text{ で C が} & \text{OFF (ON)} \\ \text{時刻 } t \text{ で C が ON (OFF)} & \text{ならば} & \text{時刻 } t+1 \text{ で A が} & \text{OFF (ON)} \end{array}$$

となる。そこで時刻 0 で遺伝子 A，B，C のうち２つが ON，残りが OFF であった場合，その後各遺伝子の ON-OFF はどのような時間的変動を示すのか，予備体験と同様，下図のような表を用いて時刻 15 まで計算し，その結果を解答欄に表記した上，変動の様子を３～４行程度で述べなさい。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-2-1-fig1.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-2-1-fig2.png

図１　3 つの遺伝子 A，B，C と，それらの ON-OFF がリズムを刻む遺伝子間の関係
ここで T 字状の先の平たい矢印は，各遺伝子が ON (OFF) の時にその先の遺伝子を OFF (ON) にする事を示す。

問 1-2

仮に図２のように 4 つの遺伝子 A，B，C，D が存在し，その関係が

$$\begin{array}{llll} \text{時刻 } t \text{ で A が ON (OFF)} & \text{ならば} & \text{時刻 } t+1 \text{ で B が} & \text{OFF (ON)} \\ \text{時刻 } t \text{ で B が ON (OFF)} & \text{ならば} & \text{時刻 } t+1 \text{ で C が} & \text{OFF (ON)} \\ \text{時刻 } t \text{ で C が ON (OFF)} & \text{ならば} & \text{時刻 } t+1 \text{ で D が} & \text{OFF (ON)} \\ \text{時刻 } t \text{ で D が ON (OFF)} & \text{ならば} & \text{時刻 } t+1 \text{ で A が} & \text{OFF (ON)} \end{array}$$

と定式化されているとする。ここで時刻 0 のとき，4 つの遺伝子のうち１つが ON で３つが OFF の場合，及び２つが ON で２つが OFF であった場合それぞれについて，その後の各遺伝子の ON-OFF の時間変動がどのようになるのか，問 1-1 と同様に表を用いて計算し，その結果を解答欄に表記した上で，変動の様子を各初期条件につき３～４行程度で述べなさい。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-2-1-fig3.png

図２　4 つの遺伝子 A，B，C，D と，それらの ON-OFF がリズムを刻む遺伝子間の関係
ここで T 字状の先の平たい矢印は，各遺伝子が ON (OFF) の時にその先の遺伝子を OFF (ON) にする事を示す。

問 1-3

問 1-1 で考察した３遺伝子からなる関係と，問 1-2 で考察した 4 遺伝子からなる関係では，どちらが体内リズムを生成する関係として適していると考えられるか，３～４行程度の理由を付けて述べなさい。

problems.title: Experiment 2 (Questions 2-1 to 2-3)
problems.problem:
Experiment 2

On the rhythm kept by changes in the population size of a biological community, answer the following questions using the model proposed for the year-to-year changes in the population size of the insect introduced in the preliminary session,

$$X_{n+1} = AX_n(1 - X_n).$$

In the calculations of the following questions, use the calculator. Calculate rounding off at the third decimal place.

Question 2-1

Suppose that the population size $X_0$ in year 0 $(n = 0)$ was $X_0 = 0.50$. When $0.00 < A < 2.00$, for $A$ at or below a certain value, after a sufficient number of years has passed, that is, for a sufficiently large $n$, $X_n$ becomes 0. This means that the insect becomes extinct. Therefore, change the value of $A$ from $A = 0.2$ to $1.8$ in steps of 0.2, calculate the population size in each year until the value of $X_n$ no longer changes or becomes periodic, and find the condition on $A$ under which extinction occurs. However, select the calculation results that are the grounds for this, and enter them in the answer box as a table like the one made in the preliminary session.

Question 2-2

Suppose that the population size $X_0$ in year 0 $(n = 0)$ was $X_0 = 0.50$. When $A = 3.20$, $3.50$ and $3.65$, in every case the population size of this insect comes to show periodic year-to-year changes. Therefore, calculate until the periodicity of the change in population size can be sufficiently confirmed, enter the results in the answer box as a table like the one made in the preliminary session, and, on the basis of the results, find the period of the change for each $A$.

Question 2-3

Suppose that the population size $X_0$ in year 0 $(n = 0)$ was $X_0 = 0.40$ or $X_0 = 0.55$. When $A = 3.20$, $3.50$ and $3.65$, calculate in each case the year-to-year change in the population size of the insect after a sufficient number of years has passed, and enter it in the answer box as a table like the one made in the preliminary session. Also, for each of the cases $A = 3.20$, $3.50$ and $3.65$, describe, taking into account the results of Question 2-2 as well, what differences or common features there are, depending on the value of $X_0$, in the period of the year-to-year change and in the values of the population size as it changes.

$$X_{n+1} = AX_n(1 - X_n)$$

を用いて，以下の問いに答えなさい。以下の問題の計算では電卓を使用すること。ただし小数点第３位を四捨五入して計算すること。

問 2-1

0 年目 $(n = 0)$ の個体数 $X_0$ が $X_0 = 0.50$ であったとする。$0.00 < A < 2.00$ のとき，$A$ がある値以下では十分年数が経った後，つまり十分大きな $n$ に対して，$X_n$ が 0 となる。これはこの昆虫が絶滅する事を意味している。そこで $A$ の値を $A = 0.2$ から $1.8$ まで 0.2 刻みに変化させ，各年の個体数を，$X_n$ の値が変わらない，もしくは周期的になるまで計算し，絶滅が起こる $A$ の条件を求めなさい。ただしその根拠となる計算結果を選別し，予備体験で作成したような表として解答欄に表記すること。

問 2-2

0 年目 $(n = 0)$ の個体数 $X_0$ が $X_0 = 0.50$ であったとする。$A = 3.20$，$3.50$，$3.65$ のとき，いずれの場合もこの昆虫の個体数は周期的な年変動を示すようになる。そこで個体数変動の周期性が十分確認できる程度まで計算し，予備体験で作成したような表として解答欄に表記し，その結果に基づいてそれぞれの $A$ について変動の周期を求めなさい。

問 2-3

0 年目 $(n = 0)$ の個体数 $X_0$ が $X_0 = 0.40$ もしくは $X_0 = 0.55$ であったとする。$A = 3.20$，$3.50$，$3.65$ のとき，十分年数が経った後における昆虫の個体数の年変動をそれぞれ計算し，予備体験で作成したような表として解答欄に表記しなさい。また $A = 3.20$，$3.50$，$3.65$ それぞれの場合，その年変動の周期と個体数の変動値に，$X_0$ の値によってどのような違いや共通点があるか，問 2-2 の結果も踏まえ述べなさい。

problems.title: Experiment 1, Question 1-1: distribution of touch-pressure points
problems.problem:
Practical exam II, physiology (45 minutes). Apart from what has already been prepared, nothing may be placed on the laboratory bench except the preliminary-session materials, the pen case that was distributed, writing materials, a watch, a handkerchief, tissues and eye drops.

Introduction

Skin sensations are sensations arising from receptors in the skin, and are classified into touch-pressure sensation, warm sensation, cold sensation and pain sensation (itch). These sensations are used to know the external environment surrounding the organism and to adapt to it. When stimuli such as touch-pressure, cold, warmth and pain are applied to the skin and the thresholds that cause a minimal sensation are examined, there are sites where the threshold is especially low (sensory points). In the preliminary session earlier, you experienced, as examples of these, the measurement of the distribution of touch-pressure points, warm points and cold points.

Exam

Referring to
① the average densities of touch-pressure points and pain points on the index finger, the palm, the inner side of the forearm and the calf, in about 100 people, and
② the distribution of warm points and cold points of 5 people and the effect of applying menthol,
in the data booklet at the end of this booklet, answer Questions 1-1 to 2-3 below.

Experiment 1 Distribution of touch-pressure points (answer with reference to ① of the data booklet)

Question 1-1

①-1 of the data booklet is a graph of the average density of touch-pressure points at different parts of the human body, measured using the same method as in the preliminary experiment. Describe the features of the distribution of touch-pressure points. Also, imagine and state the functional significance of having such a distribution pattern.

皮膚感覚とは皮膚にある受容器から生じる感覚であり，触圧覚，温覚，冷覚，痛覚（痒覚）に分類される。これらの感覚は，生体を取り巻く外的環境を知り，それに適応するために用いられる。皮膚に触圧，冷，温，痛覚などの刺激を与え，最小限の感覚を起こす閾値を調べると，特に閾値が低い部位が存在する（感覚点）。諸君は，先ほどの予備体験において，その例として触圧点，温点，冷点の分布測定を体験した。

problems.title: Experiment 1, Question 1-2: the somatosensory cortex and the homunculus
problems.problem:
Question 1-2

Touch-pressure signals detected by the sensory receptors of the skin are finally conveyed, via nuclei of the medulla oblongata and the thalamus, a relay station for sensory information, to the part of the cerebral cortex (the brain region most highly developed in humans) called the somatosensory cortex, where sensory information is processed (Figure 1). In the somatosensory cortex, the touch-pressure sensations from the various parts of the body are not processed indiscriminately. It is known that the regions involved in processing the touch-pressure information of each part of the body, such as the region that processes the sensation of the hand, the region that processes the sensation of the arm and the region that processes the sensation of the face, each exist separately on the two-dimensional plane of the brain surface. However, the way they are distributed has a characteristic. The extent of each region does not accurately reflect the body surface area; basically, parts where sensation is acute are represented relatively widely. When the body is redrawn on the basis of the extent on the brain surface, a strangely distorted human figure appears (homunculus; Figure 1).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-3-2-fig1.png

Figure 1. The somatosensory cortex of the human cerebral cortex

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 体性感覚野 = somatosensory cortex; 正中線 = midline; 上唇 = upper lip; 舌 = tongue; 下唇 = lower lip.

In the figure on the right above, the part of the homunculus from the forearm to the fingertips is not drawn. Taking into account the touch-pressure density data in ①-1 of the data booklet, imagine and draw the human figure from the forearm to the hand. Also, describe in sentences the reason why you arrived at such a drawing.

皮膚の感覚受容器で感知された触圧覚の信号は，延髄の神経核や感覚情報の中継地である視床を経由して最終的に大脳皮質（人で最も大きく発達している脳領域）の体性感覚野と呼ばれる部分に伝えられて感覚情報処理が行われる（図１）。体性感覚野では，体の各部位からの触圧覚が混然と処理されるのではない。手の感覚を処理する領域，腕の感覚を処理する領域，顔の感覚を処理する領域など，体の各部位の触圧覚情報処理に関わる領域は，脳表面の 2 次元平面上にそれぞれ分かれて存在していることが分かっている。ただ，その分布の仕方には特徴がある。各領域の広さは体表面積を正確に反映はしておらず，基本的に感覚が鋭敏な部分は相対的に広く表現されている。脳表面上での広さを基準に体を描きなおしてみると，奇妙にゆがんだ人体像が現れてくる（ホムンクルス；図１）。

problems.title: Experiment 1, Question 1-5: an artificial skin sensor
problems.problem:
Question 1-5

In recent years, the development of programs and devices for mediating information between humans and machines has been advancing rapidly, such as the development of technology that measures the brain activity or myoelectric potentials of humans and animals to move assistive machines such as prosthetic hands, and the development of artificial retinas aimed at substituting for vision. problems.problem_orig:
問 1-5

近年，ヒトや動物の脳活動や筋電位を計測して義手等の補助機械を動かす技術の開発や，視覚を代用することを目指した人工網膜の開発など，人と機械の間で情報を仲介するためのプログラムや機器の開発が急速に進んでいる。これらの技術開発は，事故等で失われた身体機能を取り戻す一つの手段として，その可能性が検討されている。将来，ヒトの触圧覚の代用が可能な皮膚センサーが開発される場合，その皮膚センサーは実用化の上でどのような機能や特性を必要とするであろうか？その特性を 5 つ以上箇条書きで述べなさい。

Experiment 2 Distribution of warm points and cold points (answer with reference to ② of the data booklet)

Close beneath the skin at the warm points and cold points distributed (scattered) over the skin surface, there are the terminal parts (nerve endings) of nerve cells that sense heat and of nerve cells that sense cold. problems.problem:
Practical exam III: Microbiology (120 minutes)

During the experiments, always wear a white coat. Wear laboratory gloves as necessary, and take care that samples etc. do not come into direct contact with your eyes, mouth, skin, etc.
Start the experiments with Experiment 1, and proceed with your answers following the instructions in the problem text.

Introduction

In the environment and on the surfaces and inside the bodies of animals and plants there exist many "microorganisms" that are difficult to see with the naked eye, and they are involved in diverse phenomena, from the cycling of matter on a global scale to the fermentation of various foods such as yoghurt and bread, and to the maintenance of health and disease. Most of them are unidentified because pure culture is difficult, and it is still impossible to determine how many kinds of microorganisms exist on the Earth; it is no exaggeration to say that their number is countless. While our lives could not be sustained without microorganisms, they also produce substances that are unnecessary or harmful to humans and can cause food poisoning and infectious diseases; for better or worse, they have a deep relationship with humankind.

The classification and species identification of microorganisms are carried out by morphological observation using a microscope, biochemical analysis of the substances that make up the cells, analysis based on differences in the nutrients that can be used for growth in culture, analysis of the genetic information on the chromosomes, and so on. In this experiment, for 5 species of microorganisms that exist in our everyday environment and are known to be harmless to humans, the size of the microorganisms is measured and the species are identified using the PCR (polymerase chain reaction) method, a comparatively new technique with high specificity, and morphological observation with a microscope, a classical technique.

Samples and apparatus

□ Micropipette P20 (1)
□ Pipette tips for the P20 (1 box)
□ Tubes containing cultures of microorganisms (5, each marked with one of the numbers 1 to 5)
□ Tube containing PCR reaction solution (green liquid) (1)
□ Tubes containing primer set solutions (2: PS2 and PS3)
□ Tube containing water (1)
□ PCR 4-strip tube (4 tubes joined together, 1)
□ Calculator
□ Biological microscope (with a micrometer in the eyepiece)
□ Filter paper (2 sheets)
□ Slides (8)
□ Cover slips (8)
□ Plastic bag for discarding tips and tubes
□ Paper cup for discarding glassware

Experiment 1: Classification and identification of microorganisms by PCR

Microorganisms are classified into eukaryotic microorganisms, which have a nucleus, and bacteria (prokaryotic microorganisms), which do not have a nucleus; furthermore, eubacteria are broadly classified into Gram-positive bacteria and Gram-negative bacteria. This classification is a classical method based on the difference in staining when Gram staining is carried out. In general, the cell wall of Gram-positive bacteria has a thicker and stronger peptidoglycan layer than that of Gram-negative bacteria. On the other hand, in Gram-negative bacteria such as Escherichia coli (大腸菌), the peptidoglycan layer is thin. Because the membrane components are destroyed by the alcohol treatment that accompanies the staining procedure, the thickness of the peptidoglycan layer is important for Gram staining, and bacteria with a thick peptidoglycan layer are detected as positive in Gram staining. Gram staining reflects very accurately the classification system based on base sequences that has become possible through the recent development of molecular biology.

In this exam, you analyse the results of PCR for classifying bacteria, and for some of the specimens you actually prepare the PCR reaction mixtures. There are also questions on knowledge related to the principle of the PCR method.

Experimental work

The 5 tubes distributed contain cultures of the following microorganisms:
Tube 1: Schizosaccharomyces pombe (fission yeast, a eukaryotic microorganism)
Tube 1 is not used in this work; it is used in Experiment 2.
Tubes 2–5: each contains one of the following prokaryotic microorganisms (in no particular order).
Ralstonia solanacearum
Micrococcus luteus
Bacillus subtilis (hay bacillus, 枯草菌)
Escherichia coli (大腸菌)

To determine the species of the microorganism cultures of tubes 3, 4 and 5, prepare PCR reaction mixtures within 20 minutes following the procedure below. Competitors who have finished the preparation place the prepared tubes on the desk and get ready for the assistants to collect the samples. Once you are ready for collection, you may move on to the next answers.
(Note) PS2 used in the experiment is a primer set for detecting Gram-negative bacteria, and PS3 is a primer set for detecting E. coli.

1. In the following operations, take care not to touch the openings or lids of the tubes with your fingers. Check that a two-digit number is written on the left side of the PCR 4-strip tube. If there is anything wrong, raise your hand and tell an assistant.
2. Using the micropipette P20, dispense 20 µL of the PCR reaction solution (green) into each of the 3 tubes from the left of the PCR 4-strip tube (the rightmost tube is not used). Change the tip each time, and make sure the solution goes into the bottom of the tube.
3. Using the micropipette P20, add 5 µL of water to each of the 3 tubes containing the PCR reaction solution. Change the tip each time.
4. Add 5 µL of the PS2 primer set solution to each of all 3 PCR reaction mixtures. Change the tip each time.
5. Add 5 µL of the PS3 primer set solution to each of all 3 PCR reaction mixtures. Change the tip each time.
6. Because the cells may have settled, flick the bottom of each microtube gently with the pad of your finger to mix the culture inside well, then add 5 µL of the cell cultures of tube 3, tube 4 and tube 5, in that order from the left of the PCR 4-strip tube, to the PCR reaction mixtures, making the total volume 40 µL.
7. Put the lids on all of the PCR 4-strip tube, including the unused one, place it on the desk and get ready for the assistants to collect it.
(Note) After the assistants have carried out the PCR reaction and electrophoresis on an agarose gel with the collected samples, each competitor's electrophoresis result is marked, and the photograph is returned after the end of the exam.
8. When the tubes are ready for collection, start answering the questions below.
You may answer the work and questions of Experiment 2, which include microscope operation, first.

Answer the following questions on the PCR method and the structure of nucleic acids

Figures 1 and 4 show schematically the results of the analysis by agarose gel electrophoresis of PCR carried out to classify bacteria. In the electrophoresis buffer, nucleic acids are negatively charged, so they move through the gel towards the anode (downwards in the figures). Because of the sieving effect of the agarose gel, nucleic acid fragments with a small molecular weight move faster.
The primer sets used for the PCR are as follows.

PS1: detects Gram-positive bacteria. The size of the reaction product is unknown.
PS2: detects Gram-negative bacteria. The size of the reaction product is 350 bp.
PS3: specifically detects E. coli (Escherichia coli). The size of the reaction product is 580 bp.
PS4: specifically detects Ralstonia solanacearum. The size of the reaction product is 700 bp.
(Note) PS2 and PS3 are the same as those used when the PCR reaction mixtures were prepared in the experimental work.

Question 1-1

This schematic diagram of the electrophoresis result (Figure 1) is the result of the reaction under conditions in which primer set PS1 is present in the reaction mixture. In lane M, a molecular weight marker (100 bp, 200 bp, 300 bp, 400 bp, 500 bp, 600 bp, 700 bp) for measuring molecular weight has been run. The numbers 2 to 5 correspond to the numbers of the tubes containing the microorganisms, and the thick black lines under the numbers show the positions of the wells in which the PCR reaction mixtures were loaded.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-4-1-fig1.png

Figure 1

Find the approximate size of the DNA fragment of the size circled with ○ in Figure 1, and choose the appropriate number from the options below.

1) 100–200 bp
2) 200–400 bp
3) 400–600 bp
4) 600–1000 bp
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験Ⅲ　微生物学（120分）

実験中は，必ず白衣を着用すること。また，実験用手袋は必要に応じて着用し，試料等が眼，口，皮膚などに直接触れないよう注意すること。
実験は，実験１より着手し，問題文の指示に従って解答を進めること。

はじめに

環境中や動植物の表面・体内などには，肉眼では見る事が難しい「微生物」が多数存在し，地球規模での物質循環から，ヨーグルトやパンなど様々な食品の発酵，健康維持や疾病にいたるまで多様な現象に関与している。その大半は純粋培養が難しいために未同定で，地球上に何種類の微生物が存在しているかを確定する事はいまだ不可能であり，その数は無数と言っても過言ではない。微生物がいなければ我々の生活は成り立たない一方で，人類にとって不要・有害な物質を作り出したり，食中毒や感染症の原因になる事もあるなど，善くも悪くも人類とも深い関わりを持っている。

微生物の分類と種の同定は，顕微鏡を用いた形態学的観察，細胞を構成する物質の生化学的な解析，培養時の増殖に利用できる栄養分の違いにもとづく解析，染色体上の遺伝情報の解析などによって行われる。本実験では，身近な環境中に存在し，ヒトには無害である事がわかっている 5 種の微生物について，比較的新しい手法で高い特異性を持つ PCR（ポリメラーゼ連鎖反応）法と，古典的な手法である顕微鏡を使った形態観察を用いて，微生物の大きさの測定や，種の同定を行う。

サンプルと器具

□ マイクロピペット P20（1 本）
□ P20 用ピペットチップ（1 箱）
□ 微生物の培養液が入ったチューブ（１～５のいずれかの番号が表記された５本）
□ PCR 反応用溶液（緑色の液体）が入ったチューブ（1 本）
□ プライマーセット溶液が入ったチューブ（PS2，PS3 の 2 本）
□ 水が入ったチューブ（1 本）
□ PCR 用 4 連チューブ（4 本がつながったもの，1 個）
□ 電卓
□ 生物顕微鏡（接眼レンズにミクロメーターが入っている）
□ ろ紙（2 枚）
□ スライドガラス（8 枚）
□ カバーガラス（8 枚）
□ チップ・チューブの廃棄用ポリ袋
□ ガラス類廃棄用紙コップ

実験１　PCR による微生物の分類と同定

微生物は，核を持つ真核微生物と核を持たない細菌（原核微生物）に分類され，更に真正細菌は大きく分けて，グラム陽性細菌とグラム陰性細菌に分類される。この分類は，グラム染色を行った場合に染色性が異なることに基づいた古典的な方法である。一般的に，グラム陽性菌の細胞壁はグラム陰性菌に比較してペプチドグリカン層が厚く堅固である。一方，大腸菌等のグラム陰性菌ではペプチドグリカン層は薄い。染色操作に伴うアルコール処理によって膜成分は破壊されるので，ペプチドグリカン層の厚さがグラム染色の染色性に重要であり，ペプチドグリカン層が厚い菌はグラム染色で陽性として検出される。グラム染色性は，近年の分子生物学の発展により可能になった塩基配列に基づく分類体系を非常に正確に反映している。

今回の試験では，細菌を分類するための PCR の結果について解析するとともに，一部の検体については実際に PCR 反応液の調製を行う。また PCR 法の原理に関連する知識についての試問を行う。

実験作業

配布した 5 本のチューブには以下の微生物の培養液が入っている
チューブ１：Schizosaccharomyces pombe（分裂酵母，真核微生物）
チューブ１はこの作業では使用せず，実験２で使用する。
チューブ２～５：以下の原核微生物のいずれかが入っている（順不同）。
Ralstonia solanacearum
Micrococcus luteus
Bacillus subtilis（枯草菌）
Escherichia coli（大腸菌）

チューブ３，４，５の微生物培養液について種を判別するために，PCR 用反応液を下記の手順に従って 20 分以内で調製する。調製が完了した受験者は，机の上に調製済みのチューブを置き，補助員が試料を回収できるように準備する。回収できるように準備したら次の解答に移ってよい。
（注）実験に使用する PS2 はグラム陰性菌検出用，PS3 は大腸菌検出用のプライマーセットである。

1. 以下の操作はチューブの開口部や蓋に指を触れないように注意して作業する。PCR 用 4 連チューブの左側に二桁の数字が記入されている事を確認する。不備がある場合は挙手して補助員に知らせる。
2. マイクロピペット P20 を用いて PCR 反応溶液（緑色）を 20 µL ずつ，PCR 用4連チューブの左から３本に分注する（一番右のチューブは使用しない）。チップは一回ごとに交換し，溶液はチューブの底に確実に入れること。
3. PCR 反応溶液を入れた３本のチューブに，マイクロピペット P20 を用いて 5 µL ずつ水を加える。チップは一回ごとに交換する。
4. PS２のプライマーセット溶液を 5 µL ずつ 3 本全ての PCR 反応液に加える。チップは一回ごとに交換する。
5. PS３のプライマーセット溶液を 5 µL ずつ 3 本全ての PCR 反応液に加える。チップは一回ごとに交換する。
6. 細胞が沈殿している場合があるので，マイクロチューブの底を指の腹でやさしくはじいて中の培養液をよく混ぜてから，PCR 用 4 連チューブの左から順に，チューブ３，チューブ４，チューブ５の細胞培養液を 5 µL ずつ PCR 反応液に加え，全量を 40 µL にする。
7. 未使用の一本を含めて，PCR 用 4 連チューブの全てに蓋をしたら，机の上に置き，補助員が回収するのに備える。
（注）回収した試料は，補助員が PCR 反応とアガロースゲルによる電気泳動を行った後，各自の電気泳動の結果を採点し，写真を試験終了後に返却する。
8. チューブの回収の準備ができたら，以下の問題の解答に着手する。
実験２の顕微鏡操作を含む作業と問題から先に解答してもかまわない。

PCR 法と核酸の構造に関する以下の問いに答えなさい

図１と図４は細菌の分類を行うために実施した PCR のアガロースゲル電気泳動による解析結果を模式的に示した図である。電気泳動用の緩衝液中では核酸は負に帯電しているため，ゲル中を陽極側（図の下方向）に移動する。アガロースゲルの篩（ふるい）効果のために，分子量が小さい核酸断片は移動速度が速い。
なお，PCR に利用したプライマーのセットは，下記の通りである。

PS1：グラム陽性菌を検出する。反応産物のサイズは未知である。
PS2：グラム陰性菌を検出する。反応産物のサイズは 350 bp である。
PS3：大腸菌(Escherichia coli)を特異的に検出する。反応産物のサイズは 580 bp である。
PS4：Ralstonia solanacearum を特異的に検出する。反応産物のサイズは 700 bp である。
（注）PS2，PS3 は実験作業で PCR 用反応液を調製した際に使用したものと同一である。

問 1-1

この電気泳動結果の模式図(図 1)は，反応液中にプライマーセット PS1 が存在している条件での反応結果である。M のレーンには分子量を測定するための分子量マーカー(100 bp，200 bp，300 bp，400 bp，500 bp，600 bp，700 bp)が泳動されている。２～５の数字は微生物の入ったチューブの番号に対応しており，番号の下の太い黒線は，PCR 反応液をセットした穴の位置を示している。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-4-1-fig1.png

図 1

図１の○で囲ったサイズの DNA 断片のおおよその大きさを求め下記の選択肢から適切な番号を選びなさい。

1) 100～200 bp
2) 200～400 bp
3) 400～600 bp
4) 600～1000 bp

problems.title: Experiment 1, Question 1-7: making up a primer solution
problems.problem:
Question 1-7

An oligonucleotide DNA with the following sequence was synthesised with an instrument for use as a primer in a PCR reaction.
ATTGACGCTCAGAGACGTTC
(Assume that the 5′ end is not phosphorylated and that it is not a sodium salt.)

1) When the dry weight of the synthesised oligonucleotide DNA is 0.1222 mg, calculate the volume of water to be added to make a 100 µmole/L solution, and give the required volume in µL (rounded off to a whole number). Write not only the answer but also, as appropriate, explanations and calculation formulae, so that the basis of the calculation can be understood.
Use the following formula to calculate the molecular weight (a calculator may be used).

$$\text{Molecular weight of the oligonucleotide DNA} = (\text{number of A} \times 249.09) + (\text{number of G} \times 265.08) + (\text{number of C} \times 225.07) + (\text{number of T} \times 240.08) + \{(63.97) \times (\text{number of bases} - 1)\} + 2.02$$

2) To add 20 pmole ($= 20 \times 10^{-12}$ mole) of the primer to a PCR reaction mixture, how many µL should be measured out from the 100 µmole/L solution made in 1)? Calculate.
problems.problem_orig:
問 1-7

以下の配列のオリゴヌクレオチド DNA を PCR 反応のプライマーとして使用するため，機器を使って合成した。
ATTGACGCTCAGAGACGTTC
(5′端はリン酸化されておらず，ナトリウム塩ではないものとする)

１）合成したオリゴヌクレオチド DNA の乾燥重量が，0.1222 mg の時，100 µmole/L の溶液にするために加える水の量を計算し，必要量を µL（小数点以下を四捨五入）で示しなさい。答えのみではなく，計算の根拠がわかる様に，説明と計算式も，適宜，記入すること。
分子量の計算には次の式を用いる（電卓は使用してもよい）。

$$\text{オリゴヌクレオチドDNAの分子量} = (\text{Aの数} \times 249.09) + (\text{Gの数} \times 265.08) + (\text{Cの数} \times 225.07) + (\text{Tの数} \times 240.08) + \{(63.97) \times (\text{塩基数} - 1)\} + 2.02$$

２）PCR反応液に20 pmole ($= 20 \times 10^{-12}$ mole) 分のプライマーを加えるには，１）で作成した100 µmole/Lの溶液から何µLを測り取ればよいか，計算しなさい。

Experiment 2: Observation of microorganisms with a microscope

Microscope observation procedure

1. Observe the samples in the same way as when you observed microorganisms in the preliminary session.
2. Mix the microorganism culture well, then take up 1 µL with the micropipette and place it on a slide.
(Note) It is difficult to measure out 1 µL accurately with the micropipette P20, but accuracy is not needed for this observation, so measure out 1 µL with the micropipette P20.
3. Cover the cell suspension with a cover slip, then put filter paper on top of it and press lightly with your finger.
4. Set the prepared specimen (slide) on the microscope, first bring it roughly into focus with the 10× objective lens, and finally observe with the 40× objective lens.
5. If the microscope lenses are dirty and this interferes with observation, raise your hand and tell us.

Question 2-4

The haemocytometer (血球計算盤), which is used to count the number of blood cells in blood, the number of cells in a culture and so on, is a special slide engraved with lines in the vertical and horizontal directions that further divide 1 mm equally, and made so that the depth is 0.1 mm when a cover slip is placed on it.

After the haemocytometer was washed, the measurement of the same diluted culture was repeated 3 more times, and the total numbers of cells in the 5 frames were 111, 105 and 117, respectively. problems.problem:
Practical exam IV, botany (120 minutes). Carry out the experiments in the order Experiment 1, Experiment 2. Carry out Experiments 1 and 2 so that you finish the experimental work and the answers for each in about 50 minutes. Apart from what has already been prepared, nothing may be placed on the laboratory bench except the preliminary-session booklet (Practical exams III and IV), the pen case that was distributed (containing a ruler, forceps, pencils, etc.), writing materials, a watch, a handkerchief, tissues and eye drops. During the experiments, always wear a lab coat. Wear the laboratory gloves and the thumb-protecting caps as necessary. Take care that samples etc. do not come into direct contact with your eyes, mouth, skin and so on.

Introduction

Higher plants develop organs such as roots, stems and leaves. Roots, stems and leaves play various roles in the life of a plant. For example, besides supporting the above-ground parts, roots acquire from the soil the water and the various nutrients needed for growth. Roots also use the photosynthetic products supplied from the above-ground parts and develop their structure by carrying out respiration. Stems support the above-ground parts and are also the transport route for the water and nutrients transported between the leaves and the roots. Leaves are the site of photosynthesis using sunlight, and play an important role in allowing the plant to live autotrophically.

Once a plant has germinated and taken root, it cannot move from that place, and it is therefore excellent at adapting to environmental changes. Plants are known to respond to changes in temperature and light intensity, to excess or shortage of nutrients and water, and so on, by regulating their internal metabolic systems and by changing the internal structure of their organs. In this experiment, in order to understand part of such mechanisms of adaptation to the environment that plants have, you will use paddy rice (水稲) to analyse a metabolite in the leaves and to observe the tissue structure of the roots. Paddy rice is a monocotyledon of the genus Oryza in the family Poaceae, and is cultivated as a staple cereal in Japan and in many countries of Asia and Africa. The Poaceae is a large taxonomic group of about 10 000 species and includes many important resource plants: besides major cereals such as wheat (コムギ), barley (オオムギ) and maize (トウモロコシ), also forage grasses, sugar cane (サトウキビ), bamboo (タケ) and others.

Samples and apparatus

At the start of the practical exam, we will read out the items below to check that they are all present. When you have checked an item, put a ✔ in its □. If anything is missing, let us know by raising your hand after the checking is finished.
