Experiment 1 Measuring the amount of a metabolite in paddy rice

Plants, which spread their roots in the ground and cannot move, respond to changes in their surroundings by carrying out the biosynthesis of substances and other processes inside their cells. Among the environmental factors surrounding plants, light is an important one. As shown in Figure 2, it is well known that chloroplasts convert light energy into chemical energy. The chloroplast is a characteristic organelle of plants and contains vitamin C at a high concentration. Because vitamin C plays an important role in maintaining human health, it is used in nutritional functional foods and similar products. A representative function of vitamin C is its reducing ability: it reduces highly reactive oxygen species (active oxygen), such as hydrogen peroxide, produced from oxygen generated in the cell. When active oxygen accumulates in the cell, it becomes harmful to the cell. Humans cannot synthesise vitamin C and must take it in from fruit and vegetables, but plants can synthesise vitamin C from glucose. In this experiment, you will compare the amounts of vitamin C contained in paddy rice seedlings grown under different conditions and consider the role of vitamin C in plants.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-1-fig2.png

Figure 2 Structure of the chloroplast and outline of photosynthesis

Figure labels (Japanese → English): グラナ = grana; チラコイド = thylakoid; 明反応 = light reactions; 暗反応 = dark reactions; カルビン回路 = Calvin cycle; ストロマ = stroma; 内膜 = inner membrane; 外膜 = outer membrane.

Procedure

Checking the end point of the reaction

In this experiment, the amount of vitamin C is measured by using an iodine solution and making use of the fact that the colour of the solution (purple–orange) becomes colourless when iodine becomes hydrogen iodide.

1. Using a dropper, put 300 µL of iodine solution into an empty 1.5 mL microtube.
2. Using the micropipette, add 20 µL of vitamin C solution to the 1.5 mL microtube containing the iodine solution and mix. To mix the solution, close the lid of the tube and mix by lightly flicking the side of the tube with, for example, the back of your index finger. After mixing the solution, check that the colour of the solution has become colourless, and take this colour as the end point of the reaction.

Measuring the amount of vitamin C

In this experiment, you will prepare a cell extract from the leaf blades (Figure 3) of each of the two groups of paddy rice seedlings, A and B, and measure the amount of vitamin C contained in the extract.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-1-fig3.png

Figure 3 Cutting leaves from a paddy rice seedling

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 葉 = leaf; 葉身(8cm以上) = leaf blade (8 cm or more); 葉鞘 = leaf sheath; 切断した葉身 = cut leaf blade; 細かく裁断した葉身 = finely cut leaf blade.

3. Put 300 µL of iodine solution into an empty 1.5 mL microtube using a dropper.
4. First, from one of the groups, A or B, choose 5 well-grown paddy rice seedlings whose leaf blades are 8 cm or longer. Next, for all 5 of the chosen seedlings, cut about 2 cm of leaf from the leaf blade with the scissors, referring to Figure 3. Then cut the leaf blades you have cut out into fine pieces on a sheet of A4 paper.
5. Put the cut leaf pieces into a 5 mL microtube and then add 1.2 mL of extraction solution using a dropper. Next, using a plastic homogeniser pestle, crush the leaf pieces while taking care not to spill the extraction solution, to prepare a cell extract (Figure 4). To crush the leaves, rotate the pestle about 30 times while pressing its tip against the leaf pieces.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-1-fig4.png

Figure 4 Cell extract

6. Using the micropipette, add 20 µL of the cell extract to the tube into which you put the iodine solution in step 3, taking care to suck up as little of the crushed leaf (solid matter) as possible, and mix. Repeat the addition of the cell extract 20 µL at a time, comparing for example with the original colour of the iodine solution, until a change in the colour of the iodine solution can no longer be seen. Record the amount of cell extract added up to the point at which a change in the colour of the iodine solution can no longer be seen. Note that the cell extract is not colourless; take this into account too when deciding the end point of the reaction.
7. Choose 5 paddy rice seedlings from the other group, carry out steps 3 to 6 and measure the amount of vitamin C.

Question 1-1

Give the amount of cell extract added up to the point at which a change in the colour of the iodine solution could no longer be seen, for each of groups A and B. In addition, state which group's paddy rice seedlings are judged to contain the larger amount of vitamin C in their leaf blades, giving your reason.
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験Ⅳ　植物学（120分）。実験は，実験 1，2 の順に行うこと。実験 1，2 はそれぞれ 50 分間程度で実験操作と解答を終えるように行うこと。実験机の上には，すでに準備されているものの他，予備体験冊子(実験試験Ⅲ・Ⅳ)，配付されたペンケース（定規やピンセット，鉛筆等が入ったもの），筆記用具，時計，ハンカチ，ティッシュ，目薬以外のものは置かないこと。実験中は，必ず白衣を着用すること。また，実験用手袋や親指保護用サックについては必要に応じて着用すること。試料等が眼，口，皮膚などに直接触れないよう注意すること。

はじめに

高等植物は根や茎，葉といった器官を発達させる。植物が生きていくうえで，根や茎，葉は様々な役割をになっている。例えば，根は地上部を支える働きのほか，土壌から生育に必要な水分や様々な栄養分を獲得する働きを持つ。また，根は地上部から供給される光合成産物を利用し，呼吸を行うことでその構造を発達させる。茎は地上部を支える働きを持ち，葉と根の間で輸送される水分や栄養分の輸送路にもなっている。葉は太陽光を利用して光合成を行う場であり，植物が独立栄養を営むために重要な役割を果たしている。

植物は発芽した後，ひとたび根ざすとその場所から移動することができないために，環境変化に適応する能力に優れている。温度変化や光強度の変化，養水分の過不足などに応答して，植物は体内の代謝系を調節したり，また器官の内部構造を変化させたりすることが知られている。本実験では，植物が持つそのような環境への適応機構の一部について理解するために，水稲を用い，葉中の代謝物の分析と根の組織構造の観察を行う。水稲はイネ科イネ属の単子葉類であり，日本をはじめアジアやアフリカ諸国において，主食となる穀類として栽培されている。また，イネ科は約１万種からなる大きな分類群で，コムギ，オオムギ，トウモロコシなどの主要な穀物のほか，牧草やサトウキビ，タケなど，重要な資源植物を多く含んでいる。

サンプルと器具

実験試験の最初に以下のものがすべてそろっているかを読みあげて確認します。確認できた場合には，□に✔を入れてください。無いものがあれば，確認作業が終わった後に挙手により知らせてください。

実験１と実験２で使用する植物材料
本実験では明所と暗所でそれぞれ栽培した水稲幼植物体を使用する。

実験１　水稲の代謝物量の測定

地中に根を張って移動することができない植物は，細胞内で物質の生合成などを行って周囲の環境変化に応答している。植物を取り巻く環境要因の中で光は重要なものである。図 2 に示すように葉緑体では光エネルギーを化学エネルギーに変換していることは有名である。葉緑体は特徴的な植物の細胞内小器官であり，高濃度のビタミンCを含んでいる。ビタミンCは人の健康維持に重要な役割を果たしているため，栄養機能食品などに使用されている。ビタミンCの代表的な機能に還元能があり，細胞内で発生した酸素より生じた過酸化水素などの反応性の高い酸素種（活性酸素）を還元する。活性酸素が細胞内で蓄積すると細胞にとって有害となる。人間はビタミンCを合成することができず果物や野菜からビタミンCを摂取する必要があるが，植物ではグルコースからビタミンCを合成することができる。本実験では，栽培条件の異なる水稲幼植物体に含まれるビタミンC量を比較し，植物におけるビタミンCの役割について考察する。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-1-fig2.png

図 2 葉緑体の構造と光合成の概要

操作

反応終点の確認

本実験ではヨウ素溶液を用いて，ヨウ素がヨウ化水素になるときに，溶液の色（紫-オレンジ）が無色になることを利用して，ビタミンC量を測定する。

1. スポイトを用いて，ヨウ素溶液 300 µL を空の 1.5 mL 容マイクロチューブに入れる。
2. マイクロピペットを用いて，ビタミンC溶液 20 µL をヨウ素溶液を入れた 1.5 mL 容マイクロチューブに加えて混合する。溶液を混合する時は，チューブのフタを閉め，チューブの側面を人差し指の裏などで軽くはじいて混合する。溶液を混合した後，溶液の色が無色になっていることを確認し，この色を反応終点とする。

ビタミンC量の測定

本実験では，A とＢの2グループの水稲幼植物体の葉身(図3)から，それぞれ細胞抽出液を調製し，抽出液に含まれるビタミン C 量を測定する。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-1-fig3.png

図 3 水稲幼植物体からの葉の切り出し

3. 空の 1.5 mL 容マイクロチューブに，スポイトを用いてヨウ素溶液 300 µL を入れておく。
4. 最初に，AまたはBのいずれか一方のグループから，葉身が 8 cm 以上のよく育った水稲幼植物体を 5 本選ぶ。次に選んだ水稲幼植物体の 5 本全てについて，図 3 を参考にして，はさみを用いて葉身から 2 cm ほど葉を切り出す。次に，A4用紙の上で切り出した葉身を細かく裁断する。
5. 裁断した葉片を 5 mL 容マイクロチューブに入れた後，スポイトを用いて抽出溶液 1.2 mL を加える。次に，プラスチック製ホモジナイザーペッスルを用い，抽出溶液をこぼさないように気をつけながら，葉片をすりつぶして細胞抽出液を調製する(図 4)。葉をすりつぶすには，葉片にペッスルの先端を押しつけながら，ペッスルを 30 回ほど回転させる。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-1-fig4.png

図 4 細胞抽出液

6. マイクロピペットを用いて，破砕した葉（固形物）をなるべく吸わないように気をつけながら，細胞抽出液 20 µL を，操作3.でヨウ素溶液を入れたチューブに加えて混合する。ヨウ素溶液の元の色と比較したりしながら，ヨウ素溶液の色の変化が確認できなくなるまで細胞抽出液を 20 µL ずつ加える作業を繰り返す。ヨウ素溶液の色の変化が確認できなくなるまでに加えた細胞抽出液の量を記録する。なお細胞抽出液は無色ではないので，この点も考慮して反応終点を決定する。
7. 別のグループから水稲幼植物体を 5 本選んで操作3.から操作6.までの作業を行い，ビタミン C 量を測定する。

問 1-1

ヨウ素溶液の色の変化が確認できなくなるまでに加えた細胞抽出液の量を，A と B のグループについてそれぞれ答えなさい。さらに，どちらのグループの水稲幼植物体の葉身に含まれるビタミン C 量が多いと判断されるかを理由も含めて答えなさい。

problems.title: Experiment 2, Question 2-1: sketch of a rice root cross-section
problems.problem:
Experiment 2 Observation of paddy rice roots

Figure 6 below shows a cross-section of the root of barley (オオムギ), a monocotyledonous plant of the family Poaceae. On the outermost side are the epidermal cells; inside them are the cortical cells, made up of several layers; further inside are the endodermal cells, and inside these is the central cylinder, which contains the vascular system. Such a root structure is seen in common in many seed plants. In this experiment, you will observe the root structure of paddy rice (水稲), a plant of the same family Poaceae as barley. Paddy rice is a plant of the Poaceae cultivated in paddy fields, and can be called a representative example of a plant close to our daily lives. You will prepare freehand sections of paddy rice roots and examine their internal structure by observing the tissue structure of the $\underline{\text{cross-section}}$ under the microscope. You will also compare the differences from the structure of barley roots and consider the function of the characteristic structure that paddy rice roots have.

* Take sufficient care not to cut your fingers with the razor blade when preparing sections. If necessary, protect the thumb of your non-dominant hand (the left thumb if you hold the razor blade in your right hand) by putting on the thumb-protecting cap (or glove) that was distributed.

* For the method of preparing freehand sections of plant tissue and how to operate the microscope, you may refer to the "preliminary-session booklet".

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-5-fig1.png

Figure 6 Photograph (left) of a cross-section of a barley root and its schematic diagram (right)

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 中心柱 = central cylinder; 内皮細胞 = endodermal cells; 表皮細胞 = epidermal cells; 皮層細胞 = cortical cells.

Procedure

Preparing the pith

1. Use a razor blade to prepare the sections. The blade may become blunt with continued use, so replace it whenever necessary.
2. Pour the tap water from the cup into 2 large Petri dishes to about half their depth. Of the 2 Petri dishes, use one for washing the roots after safranin staining and the other for floating the root sections when the roots are cut together with the pith. Use the lids of the Petri dishes as a cutting base when cutting the paddy rice roots with the razor blade in step 5 below.
3. Using a razor blade, cut a piece of pith about 5 cm long and make a slit about 3–4 cm long in the lengthwise direction.

Staining paddy rice roots and preparing freehand sections

4. Put the whole of the 0.5% safranin solution into the small Petri dish.
5. Take out one paddy rice seedling (you may use either A or B paddy rice) and place it on the lid of a Petri dish.
6. As in Figure 7, cut out a piece of root about 5 mm long using the razor blade. When doing so, cut out a part as close to the stem as possible.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-5-fig2.png

Figure 7 Site where the root piece is cut out

Figure labels (Japanese → English): このあたりの根を5 mm = 5 mm of root around here.

7. Using forceps, transfer one small piece of the cut-out root into the 0.5% safranin solution, taking care not to crush it.
8. Stain the root in the 0.5% safranin solution for about 30 seconds.
9. After staining, transfer the root to the large Petri dish filled with water to remove the excess safranin solution.
(If the tap water for washing becomes too red, you may replace it whenever necessary. Discard the waste liquid into the plastic container for collecting waste liquid.)
10. Insert the red-stained root into the pith, taking care not to crush it. At this time, insert it into the pith with the cut surface of the root facing upwards, so that cross-sections of the root can be cut.
11. Prepare freehand sections of the root. Float the root sections that have been cut on the water surface in the Petri dish.
12. After cutting about 4–5 root sections, suck up the sections with a dropper and place them on a glass slide.
13. Put on a cover slip. Absorb and remove excess water by applying a paper towel to the side of the cover slip.
14. Observe the paddy rice root sections under the microscope.

If you cannot find the characteristic structure even when you observe the paddy rice root sections you have prepared, prepare sections again using another paddy rice seedling. Also, following the example of Figure 6, label the names of the parts (epidermis, cortex, endodermis, central cylinder).
problems.problem_orig:
実験２　水稲の根の観察

下の図６は，単子葉類のイネ科植物オオムギの根の横断面図である。最も外側に表皮細胞があり，その内側に数層からなる皮層細胞，さらに内側に内皮細胞があり，それより内側が維管束系を含んだ中心柱である。このような根の構造は多くの種子植物に共通して見られるものである。この実験ではオオムギと同じイネ科植物の水稲の根の構造を観察する。水稲とは水田で栽培されるイネ科植物であり，我々の生活にも身近な植物の代表例といえる。水稲の根の徒手切片を作成し，$\underline{\text{横断面}}$の組織構造について顕微鏡観察を行うことで，その内部構造について調べる。また，オオムギの根の構造との違いについても比較し，水稲の根が持つ特徴的な構造が果たす機能について考察する。

＊切片作成時にカミソリで指を切らないよう，じゅうぶん気を付けること。必要であれば，配付された親指保護用サック（あるいは手袋）を利き手ではないほうの親指（右手でカミソリを持つ場合には左手の親指）に装着して保護すること。

＊なお，植物組織の徒手切片の作成方法や顕微鏡の操作方法については，「予備体験冊子」を参考にしてもよい。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-5-fig1.png

図 6　オオムギの根の横断面の写真（左）とその模式図（右）

操作

ピスの準備

1. 切片の作成にはカミソリを用いる。使用し続けていると切れが悪くなることがあるので，そのつど，交換すること。
2. コップに入った水道水をペトリ皿（大）2 枚に半分程度の深さまで注いでおく。2 枚のペトリ皿のうち，1 枚はサフラニン染色後の根の洗浄に，もう 1 枚は根をピスごと切り出した際に根の切片を浮かべるのに，それぞれ用いる。またペトリ皿のふたは，以下の操作５．において水稲の根をカミソリで切り出すときの下じきとして使用する。
3. カミソリを用いてピスを 5 cm 程度の長さに切りだし，縦方向に 3〜4 cm 程度の切れ込みを入れる。

水稲の根の染色と徒手切片の作成

4. ペトリ皿（小）に 0.5%サフラニン溶液を全量入れる。
5. 水稲の幼植物体（A，B のどちらの水稲を使用しても良い）を一本とりだし，ペトリ皿のふたの上に置く。
6. 図 7 のように 5 mm 程度の長さの根片をカミソリを用いて切り出す。このとき，なるべく茎に近い部分を切り出すこと。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2015-5-5-fig2.png

図 7 根片の切り出し部位

7. 切り出した根の小片１本をつぶさないように，ピンセットを用いて 0.5%サフラニン溶液中に移す。
8. 0.5%サフラニン溶液中で根を約 30 秒間染色する。
9. 染色後，水を注いだペトリ皿（大）に根を移して余分なサフラニン溶液を除去する。
（洗浄用の水道水が赤くなりすぎた場合には，そのつど，交換してもよい。なお，廃液は廃液回収用プラスチック容器に廃棄すること。）
10. 赤く染色された根をつぶさないようにしてピスにはさみこむ。この時，根の横断面を切り出せるように，根の断面を上に向けてピスにはさんでおくこと。
11. 根の徒手切片を作成する。切り出された根の切片はペトリ皿中の水面に浮かべておく。
12. 4〜5 枚ほど根の切片を切り出した後，切片をスポイトで吸い上げ，スライドガラス上にのせる。
13. カバーガラスをかける。余分な水分はカバーガラスの横からペーパータオルを当てて吸水・除去する。
14. 水稲の根の切片を顕微鏡下で観察する。

問 2-1

図６のオオムギの根の構造と比較すると，水稲の根はしばしば特徴的な構造を発達させることが知られている。オオムギの根の構造と異なる点がはっきりと分かるように水稲の根の横断面のスケッチを行いなさい。もし，作成した水稲の根の切片を観察しても特徴的な構造が見つけられない場合には，別の水稲幼植物体を用いて再度，切片を作成すること。また，図６の例にならって各部位の名称（表皮，皮層，内皮，中心柱）を記入しなさい。

Lactose metabolism in Escherichia coli involves a mechanism called the lactose operon. The lactose operon consists of the "repressor gene", the "regulatory region consisting of the promoter and the operator" and the "three genes involved in lactose metabolism".

In the lactose operon, when there is no lactose in the cell, the repressor binds to the operator located upstream of the three genes, and the synthesis of the messenger RNA (mRNA) of the three genes is repressed. When lactose is present in the E. coli cell, the repressor can no longer bind to the operator, and mRNA synthesis begins. Transcription that is induced and occurs by such a mechanism is called "inducible transcription".

On the other hand, in the recessive mutation $i^{-}$ of the repressor gene $i^{+}$, no repressor can be produced, and mRNA comes to be synthesised whether or not lactose, the inducer, is present. Transcription that always takes place regardless of conditions in this way is called "constitutive transcription". In E. coli, a constitutive mutation $o^{C}$, which is dominant over the wild type of the operator ($o^{+}$) and synthesises mRNA even in the absence of lactose, has further been discovered.

In photosynthesis, electrons are passed from H₂O to NADP⁺ through the electron transport chain of the photosystems, producing O₂ and NADPH, and at the same time ATP is synthesised from ADP and inorganic phosphate by the energy of the H⁺ gradient formed between the thylakoid lumen and the stroma. Normally, about 3 molecules of ATP are synthesised in the electron transport that produces 2 molecules of NADPH from 2 molecules of H₂O.

The NADPH and ATP made in this way are used in the Calvin–Benson cycle to fix CO₂ and produce sugar. When sugar is made from 1 molecule of CO₂, 2 molecules of NADPH and 3 molecules of ATP are consumed. Therefore, when exactly 3 molecules of ATP are synthesised in the electron transport that produces 2 molecules of NADPH, that is, when NADPH : ATP = 2 : 3, these are used, with nothing left over or lacking, for the fixation of 1 molecule of CO₂ through to sugar production, so the reaction equation of the whole of photosynthesis, including carbon fixation, can simply be written as

$$\mathrm{CO_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \frac{1}{6}\left(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\right) + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{O_2}$$

In this reaction equation, the compound produced by carbon fixation is converted into glucose and shown as (C₆H₁₂O₆). Also, the H₂O that acts as the electron donor in electron transport is shown on the left-hand side, distinguished from the H₂O entering and leaving in other reactions.

The quantitative ratio of electron transport to ATP synthesis is not fixed but changes with the conditions inside and outside the membrane, and the balance of the overall reaction of photosynthesis then also changes. The figure schematically shows the blood circulatory system of an anuran amphibian (frog). The white circle represents the heart and the hatched ellipses represent capillaries. In this animal, the blood pumped out of the heart is divided into the pulmonary circulation and the systemic circulation, and the pulmonary circulation branches further into the pulmonary artery and the cutaneous artery. Of these, the blood that has gone to the lungs returns to the heart as the pulmonary vein, whereas the blood that has gone to the skin joins the veins of the systemic circulation and returns to the heart. When the animal is under water, the blood flow to the lungs, which become useless, is suppressed, but the blood flow to the skin is maintained, and oxygen can be taken up from the water through the skin.

Practical exam 1: Molecular biology (time limit 90 minutes)

Introduction

In gene cloning using Escherichia coli, the target gene sequence is joined to a relatively small circular DNA called a plasmid. Since the plasmid DNA into which the target gene has been incorporated is replicated inside E. coli cells, the E. coli carrying that plasmid DNA can itself be cultured and the target gene can be purified in large quantities from the cells together with the plasmid DNA. Cloned genes are the starting material for many experiments carried out in modern biology, such as determining the base sequence, artificial modification, and even synthesis of the encoded protein in E. coli. However, knowing how the plasmid DNA and the target gene are joined is important for carrying out later experiments that use the recombinant plasmid as material. In this practical exam you will deepen your understanding of gene cloning through analysis of plasmid DNA.

Samples and apparatus

Check that the following samples and apparatus are all present.

Samples and reagents
Check that the following samples are all present in the plastic tube rack.
• Unlabelled empty 1.5 mL microtubes: 4
• 1.5 mL microtube ① (restriction enzyme SacII, 3 µL) – 1; kept in the ice box containing ice
• 1.5 mL microtube ② (buffer for restriction enzyme SacII (10-fold concentrated), 4 µL) – 1
• 1.5 mL microtube ③ (plasmid DNA solution, 8 µL) – 1
• 1.5 mL microtube ④ (sterile distilled water, 20 µL) – 1
• 1.5 mL microtube ⑤ (blue dye solution for agarose gel electrophoresis, 7 µL) – 1
• 1.5 mL microtube ⑥ (DNA size marker for agarose gel electrophoresis, 7 µL) – 1
The contents of tubes ⑤ and ⑥ are both blue, so take care not to confuse them.

Apparatus
• Micropipette (P-20) – 1
• Pipette tips (for P20, yellow) – 1 box
• Electrophoresis tank – 1 set (with running buffer and agarose gel already set up)
• Stopwatch – 1
• Drawing paper – 3 sheets (white, red and blue, 1 each)

The Kimwipes, Kimtowels and wash bottle (distilled water) on the bench may be used freely. Use the two plastic beakers for waste: one for solids such as pipette tips, the other for liquids.

Items used from those handed out
• Oil-based marker pen – 1
• Laboratory gloves (those whose size was checked at the preliminary trial)

To obtain a certain target gene in large quantities, the following gene cloning was carried out. In the text of the questions below, the target gene that is the object of the experiment is described as "foreign DNA", since it is not originally present in the plasmid.

Step 1. A plasmid that is replicated in E. coli cells was prepared (Figure 1A). This plasmid contains a resistance gene against ampicillin, a type of antibiotic. In a region different from the ampicillin resistance gene there is also a base sequence that the restriction enzyme EcoRI recognises and at which it cuts double-stranded DNA (Figure 1B).
Step 2. The plasmid DNA was cut with the restriction enzyme EcoRI and made linear.
Step 3. Both ends of the foreign DNA (Figure 2) were also cut with EcoRI.
Step 4. The EcoRI-cut plasmid DNA and foreign DNA were mixed and joined using DNA ligase. This reaction is called ligation. By the ligation reaction, the plasmid DNA that had been linear is made circular again.
Step 5. E. coli was transformed by introducing the plasmids after the ligation reaction into E. coli.
Step 6. The transformed E. coli was cultured on agar medium containing ampicillin together with X-gal (a chemical substance that turns blue when broken down by β-galactosidase). In the plasmid used, the EcoRI recognition site into which the foreign DNA was inserted lies inside the β-galactosidase gene. Therefore, if the plasmid DNA becomes circular without the foreign DNA being inserted (self-circularisation), the β-galactosidase gene is restored. On the other hand, in plasmid DNA that has become circular with the foreign DNA inserted, the β-galactosidase gene is disrupted. Thus, in E. coli carrying a self-circularised plasmid, X-gal is broken down by β-galactosidase activity and the colonies become blue. On the other hand, in E. coli carrying a plasmid into which the foreign DNA has been inserted, there is no β-galactosidase activity, so the colonies are white.
Step 7. White E. coli colonies on the agar medium containing X-gal were cultured in large quantities, and the plasmid DNA containing the foreign DNA was recovered.

Question 1.
In distinguishing on agar medium between colonies of E. coli carrying a plasmid into which foreign DNA has been inserted and colonies of E. coli carrying a self-circularised plasmid, we want to develop a method different from the presence or absence of β-galactosidase activity. problems.problem_orig:
実験試験１　分子生物学（制限時間　９０分）

はじめに

大腸菌を用いた遺伝子クローニングでは、プラスミドとよばれる比較的小さな環状DNAに目的の遺伝子配列を連結します。目的遺伝子が組込まれたプラスミドDNAは大腸菌細胞内で複製されるので、そのプラスミドDNAをもつ大腸菌自体を培養し、細胞からプラスミドDNAとともに目的遺伝子を大量に精製することができます。クローニングされた遺伝子は、塩基配列の決定や人工的な改変、さらにはコードするタンパク質の大腸菌内での合成など、現代の生物学でおこなわれる数多くの実験の出発材料となります。ただし、プラスミドDNAと目的遺伝子がどのように連結されているかを把握しておくことは、組換えプラスミドを材料として用いるその後の実験を行う上で重要です。この実験試験ではプラスミドDNAを対象とした解析を通じて、遺伝子クローニングについて理解を深めてもらいます。

サンプルと器具

以下のサンプルと器具がそろっていることを確認しなさい。

サンプルと試薬
プラスチックのチューブ立てに以下のサンプルがそろっていることを確認しなさい。
□ ラベルのされていない空の1.5 mLマイクロチューブ：4本
□ 1.5 mLマイクロチューブ①（制限酵素SacII、3 µL）　1本　氷の入ったアイスボックス中で保存
□ 1.5 mLマイクロチューブ②（制限酵素SacII用の緩衝液（10倍濃縮されたもの）、4 µL）　1本
□ 1.5 mLマイクロチューブ③（プラスミドDNA溶液、8 µL）　1本
□ 1.5 mLマイクロチューブ④（滅菌蒸留水、20 µL）　1本
□ 1.5 mLマイクロチューブ⑤（アガロースゲル電気泳動用の青色の色素液、7 µL）　1本
□ 1.5 mLマイクロチューブ⑥（アガロースゲル電気泳動用DNAサイズマーカー、7 µL）　1本
チューブ⑤と⑥の内容物はともに青色なので、混同しないように注意してください。

器具
□ マイクロピペット（P-20）　1本
□ ピペットチップ（P20用、黄色）　1箱
□ 電気泳動槽　1式（泳動用バッファーとアガロースゲルがセットされている）
□ ストップウォッチ　1個
□ 画用紙　3枚（白、赤、青各1枚）

机の上においてあるキムワイプ、キムタオル、洗ビン（蒸留水）は自由に使えます。２つのプラスチックビーカーは廃棄物用に使ってください。1つはピペットチップなどの固体用、もうひとつは液体用です。

配布物から利用するもの
□ 油性マジックペン　1本
□ 実験用手袋　（予備体験時にサイズを確認したもの）

ある目的遺伝子を大量に入手するため，以下の遺伝子クローニングを行った。以下の問題文では実験の対象となる目的遺伝子を、もともとプラスミドに存在しないことから「外来DNA」と記述する。

ステップ1　大腸菌細胞内で複製されるプラスミドを用意した（図1A）。このプラスミドには、抗生物質の一種であるアンピシリンに対する耐性遺伝子がふくまれる。またアンピシリン耐性遺伝子とは異なる部分には、制限酵素EcoRIが二本鎖DNAを認識し切断する塩基配列がある（図1B）。
ステップ2　プラスミドDNAを制限酵素EcoRIで切断し、直鎖状にした。
ステップ3　外来DNA（図2）の両端もEcoRIで切断した。
ステップ4　EcoRIで切断したプラスミドDNAと外来DNAを混ぜ合わせ、DNAリガーゼをもちいて連結した。この反応をライゲーションと呼ぶ。ライゲーション反応により、直鎖状だったプラスミドDNAは再環状化される。
ステップ5　ライゲーション反応後のプラスミドを大腸菌に導入することにより形質転換した。
ステップ6　形質転換した大腸菌を、アンピシリンとともにX-gal（β-ガラクトシダーゼにより分解されると青色を呈す化学物質）をふくむ寒天培地上で培養した。使用したプラスミドでは、外来DNAを挿入したEcoRI認識部位がβ-ガラクトシダーゼ遺伝子内部に存在する。このため、外来DNAが挿入されずプラスミドDNAが環状化（自己環状化）した場合、β-ガラクトシダーゼ遺伝子は復元される。一方、外来DNAが挿入され環状化したプラスミドDNAでは、β-ガラクトシダーゼ遺伝子は破壊される。従って、自己環状化したプラスミドをもつ大腸菌ではβ-ガラクトシダーゼ活性によりX-galが分解され、コロニーは青色になる。一方、外来DNAが挿入されたプラスミドをもつ大腸菌ではβ-ガラクトシダーゼ活性がないため、コロニーは白色となる。
ステップ7　X-galをふくむ寒天培地上の白い大腸菌コロニーを大量に培養し、外来DNAをふくむプラスミドDNAを回収した。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-1-fig1.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-1-fig2.png

図1．実験に使用したプラスミドDNA
（A）プラスミドDNAの概要　このプラスミドDNAの長さは約3,000塩基対である。図中の黒い四角はアンピシリン耐性遺伝子を、矢印は大まかなEcoRI認識配列の位置を、点線はクローニング部位周辺を示している。
（B）図1A中の点線で囲ったクローニング部位周辺の塩基配列　EcoRIが認識する塩基配列を実線で囲った。なお、図中には後に登場する「SacII認識部位」および「配列ア」と「配列イ」も示してある

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-1-fig3.png

図2．実験に使用した外来DNAの塩基配列
この外来DNAの長さは964塩基対である。このDNAは二本鎖DNAであるが、図中では便宜上片方のDNA鎖のみを示した。図中の下線はEcoRIが認識する配列を示している。なお、図中には後に登場する「配列ウ」と「配列エ」も示してある。

問題１．
外来DNAが挿入されているプラスミドをもつ大腸菌のコロニーと自己環状化したプラスミドをもつ大腸菌コロニーを寒天培地上で判別するにあたり、β-ガラクトシダーゼ活性の有無とは異なる方法を開発したい。この場合、どのような遺伝子の内部に外来DNAの挿入部位を設定すればよいか考え、寒天培地上での判別基準を記せ。ただしプラスミドの別領域にはアンピシリン耐性遺伝子がコードされているとする。

problems.title: Question 2
problems.problem:
Question 2.
The recombinant plasmid DNA in microtube ③ is the foreign DNA shown in Figure 2 incorporated into the plasmid DNA shown in Figure 1A. In this recombinant plasmid DNA, the following two patterns are possible for the orientation of the foreign DNA (Figure 3).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-2-fig1.png

Figure 3. Outline of the recombinant plasmid DNA
Sequences ア and イ are sequences on the plasmid DNA shown in Figure 1B. Sequences ウ and エ are the sequences at the ends of the cloned foreign DNA shown in Figure 2.

Figure labels (Japanese → English): パターン1 = pattern 1; パターン2 = pattern 2; アンピシリン耐性遺伝子 = ampicillin resistance gene; 配列ア = sequence ア; 配列イ = sequence イ; 配列ウ = sequence ウ; 配列エ = sequence エ; 外来DNA = foreign DNA.

In the plasmid DNA there is only one base sequence that the restriction enzyme SacII recognises and at which it cuts double-stranded DNA; it is shown in Figure 1B as the "SacII recognition sequence". The SacII recognition base sequence is also present at only one place in the foreign DNA sequence shown in Figure 2. Following the experimental procedure described below, cut the recombinant plasmid DNA handed out with SacII and subject the DNA fragments to agarose electrophoresis. After electrophoresis, from the lengths of the DNA fragments detected, determine in which pattern of Figure 3 the foreign DNA has been cloned into the plasmid DNA, and state it together with your reasoning.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-1-fig2.png

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-1-fig3.png

[Figure 1B and Figure 2, repeated from the beginning of the exam.]

Experimental procedure
1. Write your examination number with the marker on the lid of an empty microtube. Also write your examination number on the 3 sheets of coloured drawing paper. Write the examination number carefully so that other people can read it.
2. Prepare the restriction enzyme reaction mixture in the microtube on which you wrote your number.
Restriction enzyme SacII ……… 2 µL (microtube ①)
Buffer for SacII (10-fold concentrated) ……… 2 µL (microtube ②)
Plasmid DNA solution ……… 6 µL (microtube ③)
Sterile distilled water ……… 10 µL (microtube ④)
※ The total should be 20 µL. If the reaction mixture has become scattered inside the tube, for example because you dropped the microtube, raise your hand at once and call a TA.
3. Mix the restriction enzyme reaction mixture gently with the tip of the pipette tip.
4. Hold up the white drawing paper and have a TA collect the restriction enzyme reaction mixture (the TA also collects the drawing paper). The TA keeps the collected reaction mixture warm at 37 °C.
5. Taking the time of collection as 0 minutes, time 20 minutes.
6. After 20 minutes, hold up the red drawing paper to a TA and collect your restriction enzyme reaction mixture (the TA collects the drawing paper).
7. Add 5 µL of the blue dye solution for agarose gel electrophoresis in microtube ⑤ to the microtube containing the restriction enzyme reaction mixture, and mix well with the tip of the pipette tip.
8. Put on gloves. Load 20 µL of the restriction enzyme reaction mixture mixed with the dye solution made in the previous step into the third well from the left of the agarose gel set in the electrophoresis tank.
9. Load 5 µL of the DNA size marker in microtube ⑥ into the second well from the left of the agarose gel.
10. After closing the lid of the electrophoresis tank, switch on the power and run the electrophoresis at 100 volts for 25 minutes (you may take off the gloves once electrophoresis has started). Timing the run and stopping the electrophoresis must be done by yourself.
11. When the 25-minute electrophoresis is finished, hold up the blue drawing paper and receive a photograph of the electrophoresis result from a TA (the TA collects the drawing paper). Answer Question 2 on the basis of this electrophoresis result. The agarose gel may be left as it is in the electrophoresis tank. After the exam, the gels will be collected and photographed, and the results will be assessed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-2-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 注意 = Note; 電気泳動結果の写真では、左：DNAサイズマーカー　右：制限酵素反応液 = in the photograph of the electrophoresis result, left: DNA size marker, right: restriction enzyme reaction mixture; DNAサイズマーカー = DNA size marker; 塩基対 = base pairs.

問題２．
マイクロチューブ③中の組み換えプラスミドDNAは，図２で示した外来DNAを図１Aで示したプラスミドDNAに組み込んだものである。この組換えプラスミドDNAでは、外来DNAの向きは以下の２パターン考えられる（図3）。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-2-fig1.png

図3．組換えプラスミドDNAの概要
配列アとイは、図1Bに示したプラスミドDNA上の配列である。配列ウとエは、図2に示したクローニングした外来DNAの末端の配列である。

プラスミドDNA中には制限酵素SacIIが認識し二本鎖DNAを切断する塩基配列が１ヶ所だけあり、図1B中に「SacII認識配列」として示した。また、図2に示した外来DNA配列中にもSacII認識塩基配列は１ヶ所だけ存在する。以下に記述する実験手順に沿って、配布した組換えプラスミドDNAをSacIIで切断し、そのDNA断片をアガロース電気泳動せよ。電気泳動後、検出されたDNA断片の長さから、外来DNAが図3のどちらのパターンでプラスミドDNAにクローニングされているか判定し、その根拠とともに記せ。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-3-1-fig3.png

実験手順
1. 空のマイクロチューブのふたにマーカーで自分の受験番号を記入する。また、3枚の色画用紙にも自分の受験番号を記入する。受験番号は他人が読むことができるように丁寧に書くこと。
2. 自分の番号を書いたマイクロチューブの中に制限酵素反応液を調製する。
制限酵素SacII ……… 2 µL（マイクロチューブ①）
SacII用の緩衝液（10倍濃縮されたもの） ……… 2 µL（マイクロチューブ②）
プラスミドDNA溶液 ……… 6 µL（マイクロチューブ③）
滅菌蒸留水 ……… 10 µL（マイクロチューブ④）
※合計は20 µLとなるはずである。マイクロチューブを落とすなどし、反応液がチューブ内に散らばってしまった場合、すぐに手を挙げてTAを呼ぶこと。
3. 制限酵素反応液をピペットチップの先で軽く混ぜる。
4. 白い画用紙を掲げてTAに制限酵素反応液を回収してもらう（画用紙もTAが回収する）。回収された反応液はTAが37℃で保温する。
5. 回収時を0分として、20分計測する。
6. 20分後、赤い画用紙をTAに掲げて、自分の制限酵素反応液を回収する（画用紙はTAが回収する）。
7. マイクロチューブ⑤に入ったアガロースゲル電気泳動用の青色の色素液5 µLを、制限酵素反応液の入ったマイクロチューブに加え、ピペットチップの先でよく混ぜる。
8. 手袋を着用する。前ステップで作成した色素液を混ぜた制限酵素反応液20 µLを、電気泳動槽にセットされたアガロースゲルの左から3番目の穴に流し込む。
9. アガロースゲルの左から2番目の穴に、マイクロチューブ⑥に入ったDNAサイズマーカー5 µLを流し込む。
10. 電気泳動槽のふたを閉めた後電源を入れ、100ボルトで25分間電気泳動する（電気泳動を開始した時点で手袋を外してよい）。泳動時間の計測と電気泳動の停止は自分で行うこと。
11. 25分間の電気泳動を終えたら、青い画用紙を掲げてTAから電気泳動結果の写真をもらうこと（画用紙はTAが回収する）。この電気泳動結果に基づき、問題2を解答すること。アガロースゲルはそのまま電気泳動槽中に入れたままでよい。試験終了後、ゲルは回収し写真撮影を行い、その結果は評価対象とする。

problems.problem:
Practical exam 2: Developmental biology (time limit 90 minutes)

Introduction

For us Japanese, the sea urchin is a very familiar creature, both as an animal that can easily be touched when playing on the rocky shore and as a food, for example as a sushi topping. On the other hand, in the academic world, sea urchins have long been used by researchers all over the world as model organisms of cell biology and developmental biology. What researchers mainly use as research material are the eggs and embryos, about 100 µm in diameter; observing them under the microscope and describing their shape and the state of their cells in detail for each experiment has led to the discovery of various principles of life. Among marine invertebrates, including sea urchins, there are many that live as plankton in the sea during their developmental period before becoming adults. By actually going to the sea and collecting with a plankton net, you can see countless kinds of plankton, and among them you can see sea urchin embryos at various stages. In this practical exam, through observation with the microscope and sketching, which can be called the basis of biology, a science of "seeing" and also of "showing", you will think about how you should grasp and express the features of the organisms you have seen yourselves.

Samples and apparatus

Check that the following samples and apparatus are all present.

Samples and reagents
• Microtube A containing sea urchin embryos – 1
• Microtube B containing sea urchin embryos – 1
• Microtube C containing sea urchin embryos – 1
• Wash bottle (distilled water) – 1

Apparatus
• Upright microscope – 1
• Micropipette (P20) – 1
• Pipette tips (for P20, yellow) – 1 box
• Pasteur pipette set – 1 set
• Glass slides – 1 box
• Cover slips – 1 box
• Cellophane tape – 1
• Vinyl tape – 1
• Scissors – 1
• Kent paper – 5 sheets

The Kimwipes, Kimtowels and wash bottle (distilled water) on the bench may be used freely. Use the three plastic beakers for waste: for paper and plastic, for glass, and for liquids. Make sure that you sort the waste.

Items used from those handed out
Take out your pencil, pencil sharpener, eraser and oil-based marker and put them on the bench.

Notes
• If the microscope light source stops working or the microscope lenses become dirty during the exam, report it promptly.
• Do not use the 100× lens.
• If you run out of glass slides or cover slips, raise your hand to signal.
• If you break glass, raise your hand to signal.
• Discard the slide preparations as they are into the plastic beaker for glass waste. There is no need to remove the cover slip from the glass slide.

Question 1.
Microtubes A, B and C contain eggs and embryos of the sea urchin Hari-sanshō-uni (ハリサンショウウニ). Take eggs or embryos out of each tube, make slide preparations, observe them and sketch them. When doing so, state clearly on the Kent paper from which tube the thing drawn in each sketch was taken. Furthermore, number the sketches in the order of the developmental process. Also, write the features of the sea urchin egg or embryo in the sketches you have drawn. Note that one of the microtubes A, B and C contains eggs or embryos of a different species, the sea urchin Bafun-uni (バフンウニ); sketch them, and write on the sketch which microtube contained the eggs or embryos of Bafun-uni. Write in the sketch the grounds on which you judged it to be a different species.
※ Draw two figures per sheet of Kent paper. If you do not have enough sheets because of redrawing etc., use the back of the Kent paper.
※ The sketched Kent paper will be collected with the answer sheets at the end of the answering time and will be assessed.
※ Stippling is not necessary.
※ Because of the nature of living material, some specimens that have developed poorly are included. As far as possible, choose specimens that you can judge to be in the normal course of development, and sketch them.

Method for making slide preparations (each step is only a general method, so understand the nature of the specimens and make adjustments as appropriate)
1) Rinse a glass slide lightly over the plastic beaker for liquid waste, using the water in the wash bottle. Wipe the water off the glass slide.
2) Holding the lid of the microtube closed, mix gently by inverting it two or three times by hand.
3) Fit a pipette tip to the 20 µL micropipette, insert it into the tube and draw up eggs or embryos together with the preservation solution. Judge the volume of liquid as appropriate.
4) Place it on the glass slide and put a cover slip over it to make a slide preparation.
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験２　発生生物学（制限時間　９０分）

はじめに

我々日本人にとって、ウニは磯遊びの時に簡単に触れることのできる動物として、また、寿司ネタなどの食材として、非常になじみの深い生き物です。一方、学問の世界において、ウニは細胞生物学や発生生物学のモデル生物として古くから世界中の研究者の間で利用されてきました。研究者が研究材料として主に利用するのは直径100 µm程の卵や胚で、顕微鏡下で観察し、その形や細胞の状態を実験ごと詳細に記載することで、様々な生命原理の発見につながってきました。ウニを含む海産無脊椎動物の中には、成体になる前の発生期に海中でプランクトン生活を送っているものが多数います。実際に海に行ってプランクトンネットを用いて採集することで、数えきれない種類のプランクトンを目にすることができますが、その中で様々なステージのウニの胚を目にすることができます。今回の実験試験では、“見る”学問であり、かつ“見せる”学問である生物学の基本ともいえる、顕微鏡による観察とスケッチを通じて、皆さん自身が目にした生物の特徴を、どのようにとらえ、表現すべきかについて考えていただきます。

サンプルと器具類

以下のサンプルと器具がそろっていることを確認しなさい。

サンプルと試薬
□ ウニの胚が入ったマイクロチューブA　１本
□ ウニの胚が入ったマイクロチューブB　１本
□ ウニの胚が入ったマイクロチューブC　１本
□ 洗ビン（蒸留水）　１本

器具
□ 正立顕微鏡　１台
□ マイクロピペット（P20）　１本
□ ピペットチップ（P20用、黄色）　１箱
□ パスツールピペットセット　１セット
□ スライドガラス　１箱
□ カバーガラス　１箱
□ セロハンテープ　１個
□ ビニールテープ　１個
□ ハサミ　１個
□ ケント紙　５枚

机の上においてあるキムワイプ、キムタオル、洗ビン（蒸留水）は自由に使えます。３つのプラスチックビーカーは廃棄物用に使用してください。紙・プラスチック用、ガラス用、液体用です。ゴミの分別は確実に行ってください。

配布物から利用するもの
鉛筆、鉛筆削り、消しゴム、油性マジックを出して、机の上においてください。

注意
・ 試験中に顕微鏡の光源がつかなくなったり、顕微鏡のレンズがよごれたりしたら速やかに申し出てください。
・ 100倍のレンズは使用しないでください。
・ スライドガラス、カバーガラスは足りなくなったら挙手をして合図してください。
・ ガラスを割った場合は挙手をして合図してください。
・ プレパラートはそのままガラスゴミ用のプラスチックビーカーに廃棄してください。カバーガラスをスライドガラスから外す必要はありません。

問題１．
A、B、Cのマイクロチューブの中に、ハリサンショウウニの卵や胚が入っています。それぞれのチューブから卵または胚を取り出し、プレパラートを作り観察、スケッチをしてください。その際、スケッチに描かれたものがどのチューブから取り出されたものであるかをケント紙に明記してください。さらに、発生過程の順に沿ってスケッチに数字で順番をつけてください。また、描いたスケッチ内にウニ卵または胚の特徴を書き込んでください。なお、A、B、Cのどれかひとつのマイクロチューブ内には別種であるバフンウニの卵または胚が入っているので、そのスケッチをして、バフンウニの卵または胚が入っていたマイクロチューブがどれであるかをスケッチ上に記してください。別種であると判断した根拠をスケッチに書き込んでください。
※ ケント紙１枚あたり２つの図を書いてください。書き直し等で枚数が足りない場合にはケント紙の裏面を使用してください。
※ スケッチしたケント紙は、解答時間終了後に解答用紙とともに回収され、評価対象となります。
※ 点描は必要ありません。
※ 生体試料の性質上、発生が悪い物も含まれます。可能な限り、正常な発生過程にあると判断できる試料を選択してスケッチを行ってください。

プレパラートの作製法（各工程はあくまで一般的な方法であるため、試料の性質を理解して適宜工夫をすること）
１）　スライドガラスを液体廃棄用プラスチックビーカー上で軽く洗う。洗浄瓶内の水を用いる。スライドガラス上の水を拭き取る。
２）　マイクロチューブの蓋を抑えたまま、手で軽く２、３回転倒混和する。
３）　20 µL用のマイクロピペットにピペットチップをつけて、チューブ内に差し込み卵または胚を保存液ごと吸い取る。液量は適宜判断すること。
４）　スライドガラス上にのせ、カバーガラスをかけてプレパラートとする。

Question 2.
In animals that reproduce sexually, in most cases normal development begins with fertilisation of an egg and a sperm one to one. On the other hand, the entry of several sperm into an egg is called polyspermy, and in this case normal development does not proceed. Explain the reason in about two lines. Also, state the number of the microtube in which a structure that prevents polyspermy could be observed in this experiment, and the name of that structure.
problems.problem_orig:
問題２．
有性生殖を行う動物においては、多くの場合、卵と精子が１対１で受精することによって正常な発生を開始する。一方、複数の精子が卵内に入ることは多精と呼ばれ、この場合は正常な発生が進行しない。その理由を２行程度で説明せよ。また、本実験において多精を防ぐ構造体が観察できたマイクロチューブの番号とその構造体の名前を記しなさい。

problems.title: Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam 3: Animal physiology (time limit 90 minutes)

Introduction

The nematode Caenorhabditis elegans (hereafter "C. elegans") is a very small organism whose adult body length is about 1 mm, but it is an excellent model organism that plays a major role in a wide range of biological research. In March last year, an early cancer diagnosis method using C. elegans, reported by researchers at Kyushu University, became a big topic in the mass media. Animals generally show behaviour in which they are attracted to, or avoid, particular chemical substances. This invention can be said to make clever use of the attraction of C. elegans to some chemical substance contained in the urine of cancer patients. In this practical exam, through observing the behaviour of C. elegans in its responsiveness to chemical substances, you will understand the scientific basis of the topic mentioned above and also think about the variability of the sensory responses of animals to chemical substances.

Samples and apparatus

Check that the following samples and apparatus are all present. The samples and reagents are labelled with the characters inside the quotation marks 「 」 in the description below. The samples and reagents are also arranged from left to right on the laboratory desk.

Samples and reagents
• 「①」 stock solution of the compound (100% 3-methyl-1-butanol, 10 µL) – 1 tube
• 「②」 100% ethanol (300 µL) – 1 tube
• 「③」 50 mm agar plates – 4 (including 2 spares)
• 「④」 50 mm agar plate on which C. elegans has been grown – 1
• 「⑤」 M9 buffer (5 mL) – 1 tube
• 「Balance 500 µL」 centrifuge balance 500 µL – 1 tube
• 「Balance 1mL」 centrifuge balance 1 mL – 1 tube
• Empty 1.5 mL microtubes in a plastic bag – 4 (including 2 spares)

Apparatus
• Micropipette (P1000) – 1
• Micropipette (P200) – 1
• Micropipette (P20) – 1
• Pipette tips (for P1000, white) – 1 box
• Pipette tips (for P20, yellow) – 1 box
• Microtube rack (blue) – 1
• Benchtop mini centrifuge – 1
• Stereomicroscope – 1
• Hand counter – 1
• Stopwatch – 1

The Kimwipes, Kimtowels and wash bottle (distilled water) on the bench may be used freely. Use the two plastic beakers for waste: one for solids such as pipette tips, the other for liquids.

Items used from those handed out
• Oil-based marker pen – 1
• Ruler – 1

Experimental procedure

The circled numbers inside the quotation marks 「 」 in the description below correspond to the numbers given under "Samples and reagents" on page 3.

Preliminary preparation
1. On the underside of all 4 (including the spares) new 50 mm agar plates (「③」), draw lines as in the figure on the right with the oil-based marker pen. Use the ruler if necessary.
- Draw line D so as to divide the plate into two halves.
- Draw circle C, about 10 mm in diameter, at the centre of the plate.
- Draw point A and point B at symmetrical positions on either side of line D, about 5 mm from the edge of the plate.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-5-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 線D = line D; 円C = circle C; 点A = point A; 点B = point B.

Precautions for the following experimental operations
When placing liquid on an agar plate with a micropipette, take care not to damage the agar deeply with the tip of the pipette tip.
If you have damaged the agar deeply, use a spare plate as necessary.

Experiment
2. Take one of the 50 mm agar plates with the lines drawn on it (「③」) and place 2 µL of the compound stock solution (「①」) on the agar at the position corresponding to point A. Next, place 2 µL of 100% ethanol (「②」) on the agar at the position corresponding to point B. This plate is used in step 16.
3. Dilute the compound (「①」) 100-fold with 100% ethanol (「②」). Specifically, take 198 µL of 「②」 and transfer it into an empty microtube, then take 2 µL of 「①」 and add it to the 198 µL of 100% ethanol. After adding, mix the liquid well by flicking the bottom of the microtube with a finger (tapping).
4. Take another 50 mm agar plate with the lines drawn on it (「③」) and place 2 µL of the diluted compound solution prepared in step 3 on the agar at the position corresponding to point A. Then place 2 µL of 100% ethanol (「②」) on the agar at the position corresponding to point B. This plate is used in step 16.
5. Put 1 mL of M9 buffer (「⑤」) onto the 50 mm agar plate with C. elegans (「④」).
6. By sucking up the M9 buffer put on the agar and blowing it onto the agar (pipetting), make the C. elegans float in the M9 buffer; collect 500 µL of the M9 buffer containing C. elegans and put it into a new microtube.
7. Centrifuge the microtube containing the C. elegans for 30 seconds in the mini centrifuge. At this time, balance the centrifuge using the 「centrifuge balance 500 µL」.
8. Remove 450 µL of the supernatant. At this time, take care not to suck up too many C. elegans.
9. Add 950 µL of fresh M9 buffer (「⑤」) to the microtube containing the C. elegans and invert the tube 5–10 times.
10. Again, using the mini centrifuge, centrifuge the microtube containing the C. elegans for 30 seconds. At this time, balance the centrifuge using the 「centrifuge balance 1 mL」.
11. Remove 950 µL of the supernatant. At this time, take care not to suck up too many C. elegans.
12. Add once more 950 µL of fresh M9 buffer (「⑤」) to the microtube containing the C. elegans and invert the tube 5–10 times.
13. A third time, using the mini centrifuge, centrifuge the microtube containing the C. elegans for 30 seconds. At this time, balance the centrifuge using the 「centrifuge balance 1 mL」.
14. Remove 950 µL of the supernatant. At this time, take care not to suck up too many C. elegans. This series of steps makes it possible to remove thoroughly the excess food and debris attached to the body wall. At this stage, about 50 µL of M9 buffer containing C. elegans should remain in the microtube.
15. Lightly flick the bottom of the microtube (tapping) to stir the C. elegans.
16. Onto the agar plates made in steps 2 and 4, at the position corresponding to circle C, drop 5 µL of the M9 buffer containing C. elegans from step 15.
17. Leave undisturbed for 20 minutes.
18. Under the stereomicroscope, count and record the number of individuals on the side where the compound was dropped and on the side where the ethanol was dropped, with line D of the plate as the boundary. At this time, you do not need to count the C. elegans remaining inside circle C. Also, C. elegans of various sizes are present, but count them without distinguishing differences in size or shape.

Question 1.
In general, a change in the motility of an organism in response to an external stimulus is called "taxis". This experiment focuses on the property of C. elegans of responding to a particular compound and approaching or moving away from that compound; with what kinds of stimuli, other than chemical substances such as compounds, may taxis be shown? Name one type of external stimulus and describe a specific example.
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験３　動物生理学（解答時間　９０分）

はじめに

線虫Caenorhabditis elegans（以下「シーエレガンス」）は、成虫の体長が1 mm程度の非常に小さな生き物ですが、幅広い生物学研究で大いに活躍している優れたモデル生物です。昨年３月、九州大学の研究者によって報告されたシーエレガンスを用いた早期がん診断法が、マスメディアで大きな話題となりました。動物は一般に、特定の化学物質に対して引き寄せられたり、あるいは避けたりする行動をとります。今回の発明は、がん患者の尿に含まれる何らかの化学物質に対するシーエレガンスの誘引性をうまく利用したものと言えます。今回の実験試験では、シーエレガンスの化学物質に対する応答性についての行動観察を通じて、上述の話題の科学的基盤を理解するとともに、動物の化学物質に対する感覚応答の可変性について考えます。

サンプルと器具類

以下のサンプルと器具がそろっていることを確認しなさい。サンプルと試薬は、以下の記述におけるカギ括弧「」内の文字でラベルされています。また、サンプルと試薬は実験デスクの左から右に並べてあります。

サンプルと試薬
□「①」化合物原液（100% 3-メチル-1-ブタノール、10 µL）１本
□「②」100% エタノール（300 µL）１本
□「③」50 mm寒天プレート４枚（予備２枚を含む）
□「④」シーエレガンスを飼育した50 mm寒天プレート１枚
□「⑤」M9緩衝液（5 mL）１本
□「バランス500 µL」遠心バランス500 µL １本
□「バランス1mL」遠心バランス1 mL １本
□ビニール袋に入った空の1.5 mLマイクロチューブ４本（予備２本を含む）

器具
□マイクロピペット（P1000）１本
□マイクロピペット（P200）１本
□マイクロピペット（P20）１本
□ピペットチップ（P1000用、白色）１箱
□ピペットチップ（P20用、黄色）１箱
□マイクロチューブ立て（青色）１個
□卓上小型遠心機　１台
□実体顕微鏡　１台
□手動式カウンタ　１個
□ストップウォッチ　１個

机の上においてあるキムワイプ、キムタオル、洗ビン（蒸留水）は自由に使えます。２つのプラスチックビーカーは廃棄物用に使ってください。1つはピペットチップなどの固体用、もうひとつは液体用です。

配布物から利用するもの
□油性マジックペン１本
□定規１本

実験手順

以下の記述におけるカギ括弧「」内の囲み数字は、３ページの「サンプルと試薬」に記載した番号に対応する。

前準備
1. ４枚（予備を含む）の新しい50 mm寒天プレート（「③」）すべての裏側に、右図のような線を油性マジックペンで描く。必要に応じて、定規を用いること。
- プレートを２分割するように線Dを描く。
- プレートの中心に直径約10 mmの円Cを描く。
- 線Dを挟んで対照の位置、そしてプレートの淵から約5 mm離れた位置に、点Aおよび点Bを描く。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-5-1-fig1.png

以下の実験操作における注意
マイクロピペットを用いて寒天プレートに液体を置く際、チップの先で寒天を深く傷つけないように注意を払うこと。
もし寒天を深く傷つけた場合、必要に応じて予備のプレートを使用すること。

実験
2. 線を描いた50 mm寒天プレート（「③」）１枚を取り、点Aの位置に対応する寒天上に、化合物原液（「①」）2 µLを置く。次に点Bの位置に対応する寒天上に、100% エタノール（「②」）2 µLを置く。このプレートは実験手順16で使用する。
3. 化合物（「①」）を100% エタノール（「②」）で100倍希釈する。具体的には、「②」を198 µL取って空のマイクロチューブに移し、そこに「①」を2 µL取って198 µL 100% エタノール中に添加する。添加後に、マイクロチューブの底を指で弾いて（タッピング）液をよく混和する。
4. 線を描いた50 mm寒天プレート（「③」）を新たに1枚取り、点Aの位置に対応する寒天上に、実験手順3で作製した希釈した化合物溶液2 µLを置く。次いで、点Bの位置に対応する寒天上に、100%エタノール（「②」）2 µLを置く。このプレートは実験手順16で使用する。
5. シーエレガンスがいる50 mm寒天プレート（「④」）の上に、M9緩衝液（「⑤」）1 mLを入れる。
6. 寒天に入れたM9緩衝液を吸い、寒天に吹き付ける作業（ピペッティング）によってシーエレガンスをM9緩衝液中に浮かせ、シーエレガンスを含むM9緩衝液500 µLを回収して、新しいマイクロチューブに入れる。
7. 小型遠心機でシーエレガンスの入ったマイクロチューブを30秒間遠心する。この際、「遠心バランス500 µL」を用いて遠心機の重心のバランスを取る。
8. 上清450 µLを抜く。この際、シーエレガンスをあまり吸わないように注意する。
9. シーエレンガスの入ったマイクロチューブに、新しいM9緩衝液（「⑤」）950 µLを加えて、チューブを5〜10回反転させる。
10. 再び、小型遠心機を用いて、シーエレガンスの入ったマイクロチューブを30秒間遠心する。この際、「遠心バランス1 mL」を用いて遠心機の重心バランスを取る。
11. 上清950 µLを抜く。この際、シーエレガンスをあまり吸わないように注意する。
12. シーエレンガスの入ったマイクロチューブに、もう一度新しいM9緩衝液（「⑤」）950 µLを加えて、チューブを5〜10回反転させる。

problems.title: Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam 4: Plant physiology (time limit 90 minutes)

Introduction

Plants live while interacting with various micro-organisms in the soil. As one example of the interactions between plants and micro-organisms, it is known that legumes and the soil bacteria rhizobia build a mutualistic symbiotic relationship called "root-nodule symbiosis". Rhizobia are bacteria that can carry out the nitrogen-fixation reaction, which converts nitrogen gas in the atmosphere into water-soluble ammonia. Legumes form symbiotic organs called root nodules on their roots and, by letting rhizobia live inside them, can use the ammonia made by the rhizobia through nitrogen fixation as a source of nitrogen nutrition. On the other hand, the plant provides the rhizobia with organic matter made by photosynthesis as the energy source for the survival of the rhizobia.

Lotus japonicus (ミヤコグサ) is a model legume with various advantages for carrying out experiments: the plant is small, the period required for one generation (the period from sowing seeds until the seeds of the next generation are obtained) is short, it can be grown in the laboratory, and so on. By treating normal wild-type Lotus japonicus with a chemical mutagen, the DNA is damaged at random and gene mutations are induced, and from the population of mutants produced, various mutants that cannot carry out root-nodule symbiosis normally have been isolated. By examining what kind of abnormality each mutant shows, and by examining the function of the gene responsible, understanding of the mechanism of root-nodule symbiosis is advancing.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-7-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 根粒 = root nodule; ミヤコグサの根 = root of Lotus japonicus; 根粒共生 = root-nodule symbiosis; 窒素栄養 = nitrogen nutrition; 有機物 = organic matter; 根粒菌 = rhizobia; ミヤコグサ（マメ科植物） = Lotus japonicus (legume).

The Kimwipes and Kimtowels on the bench may be used freely.
Use the three plastic beakers for waste: for solids such as pipette tips, for liquids, and for razor blades. Be sure to separate the waste properly.

Put the marker pen, ruler, magnifying glass, thread-cutting scissors and tweezers on the bench. However, you are free to use or not use the apparatus put on the bench.

Notes

Question 1.

problems.problem_orig:
実験試験４　植物生理学（制限時間　９０分）

はじめに

植物は土壌中の様々な微生物と相互に関わり合いながら生活しています。植物と微生物の相互作用の例の1つとして、マメ科植物と土壌細菌の根粒菌は“根粒共生”と呼ばれる相利共生関係を築いていることが知られています。根粒菌は、大気中の窒素ガスを水溶性のアンモニアへと変換する窒素固定反応を行うことができる細菌です。マメ科植物は、根に根粒と呼ばれる共生器官を形成し、その中に根粒菌をすまわせることにより、根粒菌が窒素固定して作ったアンモニアを窒素栄養源として利用することができます。その一方で、植物は光合成によって作られた有機物を根粒菌の生存のエネルギー源として根粒菌に提供します。

ミヤコグサ（Lotus japonicus）は、植物体のサイズが小さい、1世代に要する期間（種子をまき次の世代の種子がとれるまでの期間）が短い、実験室内での栽培が可能など、実験を行う上で様々な利点をもつマメ科のモデル植物です。正常な野生型のミヤコグサに化学変異原処理を行うことにより、DNAにランダムに傷をつけ、遺伝子の変異の誘発を引き起こし、作られた突然変異体の集団の中から、根粒共生を正常に行うことのできない様々な突然変異体が単離されています。それぞれの突然変異体がどのような異常を示すのかを調べ、また、その原因となる遺伝子の働きを調べることにより根粒共生の仕組みの理解が進んでいます。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-7-1-fig1.png

problems.problem:
Question 2.
Answer questions (1)–(3) below about the root nodules formed on the roots of wild type (+).

(1) Following the procedure below, make a preparation of a section of a root nodule, then observe it with the upright microscope and sketch the cross-sectional structure of the root nodule. For the sketch, use the 10× objective lens.

① Break a double-edged razor blade in half and separate it into two.
② Cut the copy paper to a size of about 4 cm × 2 cm and wet it with distilled water.
③ Sandwich the wetted copy paper between the two razor blades. At this time, shift the copy paper upwards by about 1 cm.
④ Holding the two razor blades and the copy paper with both hands so that they do not slip, bring the blades straight down towards the centre of the root nodule.
⑤ A section remains between the razor blades, so put it on a microscope slide and make a preparation.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-7-2-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 刃の部分は直接触らないように注意する = take care not to touch the edges directly; 1 cm 程度ずらす = shift by about 1 cm.

(2) Following the procedure below, make a preparation in which the rhizobia present in a root nodule are fixed and stained, then observe it with the upright microscope and sketch the form of the rhizobia. For the sketch, use the 100× objective lens (oil-immersion objective lens).

① Using tweezers, cut off one root nodule from a root of wild type (+) and crush it gently in a drop of water placed on a microscope slide. Remove the crushed root nodule from the microscope slide.
② Put the microscope slide on the slide stand. Using the gas lighter, gently heat the underside of the microscope slide with the flame to evaporate the water.
Caution: immediately after heating with the flame, the microscope slide and the slide stand may be hot, so take care when handling them.
③ Using a dropper, put 1 drop of bacterial staining solution A on the place where the water has evaporated, and wait about 1 minute.
④ Using the wash bottle (distilled water), wash off bacterial staining solution A.
⑤ Using a dropper, add decolourising solution until the blue colour of bacterial staining solution A no longer comes out.
⑥ Using the wash bottle (distilled water), wash off the decolourising solution.
⑦ Using a dropper, put 1 drop of bacterial staining solution B and wait about 1 minute.
⑧ Using the wash bottle (distilled water), wash off bacterial staining solution B.
⑨ Make a preparation.

How to use the oil-immersion objective lens

① Observe using the 10× to 40× objective lenses, and finally, when observing with the 40× objective lens, bring the object (the place where the bacteria are stained) into focus.
② Turn the revolver to make a space between the objective lens and the preparation.
③ Using the micropipette, take 3 µL of immersion oil from the microtube (containing immersion oil) and place it on the upper surface of the cover slip at the centre of the light path.
④ Change the objective lens to 100×. At this time, check that the space between the objective lens and the cover slip is filled with a layer of immersion oil.
⑤ Turn the fine-adjustment knob to focus.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2016-7-2-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 油浸対物レンズ = oil-immersion objective lens; 油浸液 = immersion oil; カバーガラス = cover slip; スライドガラス = microscope slide.

(3) Answer what kind of experiment should be designed to estimate efficiently the number of rhizobia present in one root nodule (you do not need to actually carry out the experiment).

(1)根粒の切片のプレパラートを下記の手順に従い作成後、正立顕微鏡で観察し、根粒の断面構造をスケッチしなさい。スケッチでは10倍の対物レンズを使いなさい。

In the traditional process of making sake, steamed rice on which kōji mould (麹菌) has been grown and water are put into an open vat, and the temperature is raised little by little from a low temperature of about 5 °C while the mixture is stirred slowly. The kōji mould dies as soon as the water is added, but the starch of the steamed rice is gradually broken down into sugars by the amylase that the kōji mould has secreted. Because the fermentation vat is deep and its contents are thick and mushy, the oxygen is soon used up even though the system is open. (5 points)

① Sake yeast: the only eukaryote; grows slowly. It carries out alcoholic fermentation, in which sugars are broken down to produce ethanol. It is sensitive to alkaline environments but very resistant to acidic environments. It can grow both in environments with oxygen and in anaerobic environments without oxygen.

② Bacillus subtilis (枯草菌): grows fast and forms heat-resistant spores. It is an aerobic bacterium that requires oxygen for growth. It is relatively resistant to alkaline environments but sensitive to acidic environments. It is highly sensitive to chemical substances with antibacterial properties, such as nitrite.

③ Lactic acid bacteria: carry out lactic acid fermentation, in which sugars are broken down to produce lactic acid. When oxygen is present they carry out hardly any lactic acid fermentation. They are sensitive to alcohol.

④ Bacteria of the genus Pseudomonas: aerobic bacteria that require oxygen for growth, but many of them have nitrate-reducing ability and use nitrate as an electron acceptor instead when the oxygen runs out. They prefer a pH near neutral.

Some plant organs show a bending response to particular stimuli. Such bending responses include tropisms, in which the direction of bending is determined by the direction of the stimulus, and nastic movements (nasties), in which the direction of bending is fixed regardless of the direction of the stimulus. Plant bending responses are classified into various types by combining the way the direction of bending is determined with the kind of stimulus that causes the bending.

Sundews (モウセンゴケ類) are a group of insectivorous plants that have glandular hairs covered with mucilage on the surface of their leaves. When a sundew leaf catches an insect in the mucilage, it bends so as to wrap around the insect and digests it inside. The bulleted list below is an outline of the results of experiments on the bending of this leaf carried out on one species of sundew.

Experimental results

• When a living fruit fly was attached to the upper side of a leaf, the leaf bent towards it within a short time.
• When an intact dead fruit fly was attached to the upper side of a leaf, the leaf eventually bent towards it, but it took a long time before the bending occurred.
• When a crushed dead fruit fly was attached to the upper side of a leaf, the leaf bent towards it within a short time.
• When a small stone about the same size as a fruit fly was attached to the upper side of a leaf, no bending occurred.
• When the upper side of a leaf was rubbed with a brush, no bending occurred.

From these results, what type of response is the bending of the sundew leaf thought to be? Choose from A–H the most appropriate answer. (5 points)

A. It is thought to be thigmotropism.

B. It is thought to be thigmonasty.

C. It is thought to be chemotropism.

D. It is thought to be chemonasty.

F. It is thought to be thigmotropism or chemotropism, but which of the two cannot be determined from these experimental results.

G. It is thought to be thigmonasty or chemonasty, but which of the two cannot be determined from these experimental results.

H. It is thought to be chemotropism or chemonasty, but which of the two cannot be determined from these experimental results.

In general, fertilisation is a biologically important event in which a sperm that has entered the egg fuses with the egg nucleus and the development of a new individual begins.

In sea urchin eggs, a sperm that has reached the egg surface enters the egg within 1 minute. The sperm that has entered the egg forms a sperm nucleus and moves through the egg cytoplasm, and 30 minutes after insemination (the addition of sperm) it fuses with the egg nucleus. After that, cell division (nuclear division) occurs about once an hour. The motile mechanisms of the actin filament system and of the microtubule system are involved in the process of fertilisation.

Cytochalasin B is an inhibitor that suppresses the motile mechanism of the actin filament system. Colcemid is an inhibitor that suppresses the motile mechanism of the microtubule system. problems.title: Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam I: Developmental biology (80 minutes)

Samples and apparatus
• Microtube A containing a sample – 1
• Microtube B containing a sample – 1
• Microtube C containing a sample – 1
• Microtube D containing a sample – 1
• Droppers – 4
• Slide glasses – 5
• Cover glasses – 1 box
• Tweezers – 1
• Vinyl tape – 1
• Scissors – 1
• Light microscope (biological microscope) – 1
• Laboratory gloves, size M – 1 pair

The two plastic beakers are used as waste bins for plastic and for glass. Paper waste goes into the paper-waste bag at the side of the bench. Sort the waste carefully.

Notes
• Preparations are discarded as they are into the plastic beaker for glass waste. There is no need to remove the cover glass from the slide glass.

Introduction

The development of an animal starts from a single cell, the fertilised egg, and in the process in which the number of cells then increases by cleavage and somatic cell division, the body is formed as genes that control development are expressed at the right time and in the right place. When a gene in the nucleus of a eukaryote is expressed, the base sequence of the DNA is copied into mRNA by transcription in the nucleus, and after being transported to the cytoplasm it is converted by translation into the amino-acid sequence of a protein.

When gene expression is analysed, a technique called hybridisation is used. First, a nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) with a base sequence complementary to the mRNA to be analysed is labelled with a radioactive isotope or a compound. This labelled nucleic acid is called a probe. After this probe is bound to the target mRNA through the complementarity of the base sequences, the position where the target mRNA is present can be examined by visualising the labelling compound by colour development or by light emission (Figure 1). Hybridisation carried out by electrophoresing RNA extracted from cells and transferring it to a membrane is called northern hybridisation, and detecting a target mRNA in fixed tissue is called in situ hybridisation.

Sea urchins and ascidians are used as model organisms in developmental biology, and genes that control development have also been analysed in them. Both of these animals are also important in analysing the course of evolution towards the vertebrates such as humans. The embryos of these animals are highly transparent, and in situ hybridisation can be carried out on fixed embryos as they are, so the time and site of expression of genes that control development can be analysed easily. In this practical exam, through in situ hybridisation of embryos and the observation and sketching of larvae, we consider the mechanisms of animal development and evolution.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2017-3-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 胚 = embryo; プローブ = probe; 発色 = colour development.

Figure 1 Principle of in situ hybridisation
To detect the mRNA present in the region of the embryo shown in blue, a probe with a base sequence complementary to this mRNA is bound to it. If the labelling compound attached to the probe is then visualised by colour development, the position where the target mRNA is present can be examined.

Question 1.
We want to examine the localisation of gene X mRNA in embryos of the sea urchin bafun-uni (バフンウニ) by in situ hybridisation. The sequence below shows part of the base sequence of gene X mRNA. Write in the answer box the base sequence of the RNA probe for detecting this mRNA. Write the base sequence with the 5′ end on the left and the 3′ end on the right.

5′-GAACGAUGCACUGAACCAUA-3′
problems.problem_orig:
実験試験Ⅰ　発生生物学（80分）

サンプルと器具
□サンプルが入ったマイクロチューブA　1本
□サンプルが入ったマイクロチューブB　1本
□サンプルが入ったマイクロチューブC　1本
□サンプルが入ったマイクロチューブD　1本
□スポイト　4本
□スライドガラス　5枚
□カバーガラス　1箱
□ピンセット　1本
□ビニールテープ　1個
□ハサミ　1個
□生物顕微鏡　1台
□実験用手袋M　1組

2つのプラスチックビーカーは，プラスチック用とガラス用のゴミ箱として使用する。紙ゴミは，机の側面の紙ゴミ用袋に入れる。ゴミの分別は確実に行うこと。

注意
・プレパラートは，そのままガラスゴミ用のプラスチックビーカーに廃棄する。その際，カバーガラスをスライドガラスから外す必要はない。

はじめに

動物の発生は受精卵という1個の細胞からスタートするが，その後の卵割および体細胞分裂により細胞数が増加する過程で，発生を制御する遺伝子が適切な時期に適切な場所で発現することにより体が形づくられる。真核生物の核内の遺伝子が発現するとき，DNAがもつ塩基配列は転写により核内でmRNAへと写し取られ，細胞質へ輸送された後に翻訳されてタンパク質のアミノ酸配列へと変換される。

遺伝子の発現を解析するとき，ハイブリダイゼーションという手法が用いられる。はじめに，解析の対象となるmRNAと相補的な塩基配列をもつ核酸（DNAやRNA）を放射性同位体や化合物で標識する。この標識された核酸をプローブとよぶ。このプローブを塩基配列の相補性を介して標的mRNAと結合させた後，標識化合物を発色もしくは発光により可視化すれば，目的のmRNAが存在する位置を調べることができる（図1）。細胞から抽出されたRNAを電気泳動し，これを膜に転写して行うのがノザンハイブリダイゼーション，固定された組織中にある標的mRNAを検出するのがin situハイブリダイゼーションとよばれる。

ウニやホヤは発生生物学のモデル生物として利用され，発生を制御する遺伝子の解析も行われてきた。また，どちらの動物も，ヒトなどの脊椎動物への進化の道筋を解析するうえでも重要な動物である。これらの動物の胚は透明度が高く，固定された胚をそのまま用いてin situハイブリダイゼーションを行うことができるため，発生を制御する遺伝子の発現時期・発現部位を容易に解析できる。今回の実験試験では，胚のin situハイブリダイゼーションや幼生の観察とスケッチを通じて，動物の発生および進化のしくみについて考える。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2017-3-1-fig1.png

図1　in situハイブリダイゼーションの原理
胚の青で示された領域に存在するmRNAを検出するために，このmRNAに相補的な塩基配列をもつプローブを結合させる。その後，プローブに付けられた標識化合物を発色により可視化すれば，目的のmRNAが存在する位置を調べることができる。

問1.
in situハイブリダイゼーションにより，バフンウニ胚における遺伝子X mRNAの局在を調べたい。下の配列は，遺伝子X mRNAの塩基配列の一部が示してある。このmRNAを検出するためのRNAプローブの塩基配列を，解答欄に記しなさい。塩基配列は，左を5’側，右を3’側として記すこと。

5’-GAACGAUGCACUGAACCAUA-3’

problems.title: Question 1
problems.problem:
Practical exam II: Molecular biology (85 minutes)

What you need for the experiment
In this experiment the apparatus and reagents shown below are used. If anything is missing, raise your hand.

• Micropipette – 1
• Micropipette tips – 1 box
• Tube racks – 2 kinds
• 4-tube strip – 1
• Primer mixture for amplifying *GA3ox* (labelled GA3ox) – 1
• Primer mixture for amplifying *UBQ* (labelled UBQ) – 1
• cDNA from dry seeds (labelled 乾燥, "dry") – 1
• cDNA from imbibed seeds (labelled 吸水, "imbibed") – 1
• Premix (labelled プレミックス, "premix") – 1
• Pure water (labelled 純水, "pure water") – 1

Notes
1. The reaction mixtures you prepare in Question 1 will be collected 40 minutes after the start of the exam. If they are not ready by this time, the subsequent reaction cannot be carried out. Prepare your reaction mixtures in time.
2. The reagents at hand will not be handed out again, so read the problem text carefully and carry out the experiment without mistakes.

Introduction
The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique for amplifying DNA specifically and rapidly, and it is effective even when the template DNA is present in very small amounts or is not pure. Kary Mullis, who developed PCR, received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1993. Real-time PCR is a method of measuring (monitoring) in real time the DNA amplified by PCR (the PCR product). In this experiment, the amounts of transcription of genes are compared by real-time PCR.

In a typical PCR, reaction steps under three different temperature conditions form one cycle, and the amplification of DNA proceeds by repeating this cycle. First, (1) by heating to 95 °C, the DNA strands forming the double strand are separated from each other (denaturation). Next, (2) the mixture is cooled to about 60 °C, and short single-stranded DNAs (primers) with sequences complementary to the regions at the two ends of the target sequence are bound to them (annealing). Finally, (3) at 72 °C the DNA synthesis reaction by DNA polymerase is brought about (extension). Through this series of reactions, a DNA strand is extended in the 5′ → 3′ direction starting from the primer DNA, and a double strand of the whole target sequence is completed. When the PCR proceeds ideally, the target DNA sequence can be amplified twofold in each cycle, so by repeating n PCR cycles the target DNA sequence can be amplified $2^{n}$-fold (2 to the power n).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2017-4-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): プライマー = primer; (1) 変性：加熱することでDNA鎖を分離する = (1) Denaturation: the DNA strands are separated by heating; (2) アニーリング：冷却によりプライマーを標的配列に結合させる = (2) Annealing: the primers are bound to the target sequence by cooling; (3) 伸長：DNAポリメラーゼによるDNA合成反応を引き起こす = (3) Extension: the DNA synthesis reaction by DNA polymerase is brought about.

Figure 1. Outline of PCR

In real-time PCR, the three reaction steps above are sometimes combined into two steps. First, (1) denaturation is carried out at 95 °C, and (2) annealing and extension are carried out at 60 °C. In real-time PCR, the amount of amplified DNA is measured by using a fluorescent substance. In this experiment, a method is used in which the amount of double-stranded DNA is measured by making use of the property that a fluorescent substance that has entered double-stranded DNA emits fluorescence when irradiated with excitation light. Because the intensity of the fluorescence increases in proportion to the amount of DNA, the amount of PCR product (amount of DNA) can be measured by measuring the intensity of the fluorescence.

In real-time PCR, if a graph is drawn with the number of PCR cycles on the horizontal axis and the amount of amplified PCR product (fluorescence intensity) on a logarithmic vertical axis, the amplification of DNA by PCR can be represented as in Figure 2. The amplification curves of samples with different template DNA concentrations are parallel (Figure 3). If one auxiliary line is drawn horizontally across the linear region of these amplification curves (A in Figure 3), the initial DNA concentrations can be estimated. The number of PCR cycles at the intersection of an amplification curve with the auxiliary line is called the Ct value (Figure 3). By examining the difference in the number of cycles (the difference in Ct values, ΔCt), differences in the initial concentration of DNA can be compared. If the Ct value for reaching the same amount of PCR product is larger by 1, the initial concentration is thought to be 1/2 as much, and if the Ct value is larger by 2, 1/4 as much.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2017-4-1-fig2.png

Figure 2. Amplification curve of real-time PCR with fluorescent labelling of DNA

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2017-4-1-fig3.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 蛍光強度（対数表示） = fluorescence intensity (logarithmic scale); サイクル数 = number of cycles; 補助線 = auxiliary line; Ct値 = Ct values.

Figure 3. The auxiliary line and Ct values

The methods of quantifying the amount of transcription by real-time PCR are absolute quantification and relative quantification. Relative quantification is a quantification method in which the amount of transcription of a target gene is compared between samples by normalising the amount of transcription of the target gene by the amount of transcription of a reference gene; there are a method that uses a calibration curve and the ΔΔCt method, which does not use a calibration curve. As the reference gene, a gene whose amount of transcription is the same in all cells, regardless of growth conditions, various treatments and so on, is used.

Experiment. Analysis of the amount of gene transcription by real-time PCR
Read the following problem text and answer each question. Also, carry out real-time PCR following the problem text.

Analysis of the amount of gene transcription by the ΔΔCt method is a method of comparing and quantifying the amount of transcription of a target gene between unknown samples from the difference between the Ct values of the target gene and the reference gene (the ΔCt value), and further from the difference between the ΔCt values (the ΔΔCt value). In this experiment, the amounts of transcription of the gibberellin 3-oxidase gene (hereafter *GA3ox*) in the dry seeds and the imbibed seeds of a certain plant are compared by the ΔΔCt method. The protein encoded by this gene catalyses part of the biosynthetic reactions of the plant hormone gibberellin. The ubiquitin gene (hereafter *UBQ*) is thought to have an amount of transcription product that does not change in any cell, regardless of growth conditions, various treatments and so on, and is therefore used as the reference gene.

Question 1.
Read the following text and write ① to ③ in the answer boxes. Also, prepare the reaction mixtures within 40 minutes. Using the two kinds of cDNA (complementary DNA) prepared from the dry seeds and from the imbibed seeds, the amounts of transcription of two genes, the target gene *GA3ox* and the reference gene *UBQ*, are examined. Therefore four reaction mixtures have to be prepared. The reaction solutions for real-time PCR are prepared by diluting the solutions provided as appropriate. Calculate the volumes of the solutions needed for the experiment on the basis of Table 1, and write ① to ③ in the answer boxes. The premix means a mixture containing DNA polymerase, nucleotides and so on. Also, [2×] premix and [10×] primer mixture mean solutions concentrated 2-fold and 10-fold, respectively.

Table 1. Preparation of the real-time PCR reaction mixture

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Required volume } (\mu\text{l}) & \text{Working concentration} \\ \hline \text{Pure water} & \text{①} & - \\ \hline [2\times]\ \text{premix} & \text{②} & [1\times] \\ \hline [10\times]\ \text{primer mixture } \langle\text{GA3ox or UBQ}\rangle & \text{③} & [1\times] \\ \hline \text{cDNA solution } \langle\text{乾燥 (dry) or 吸水 (imbibed)}\rangle & 2.0 & - \\ \hline \text{Total volume} & 20.0 & - \\ \hline \end{array}$$

⟨ ⟩ shows the label on the tube handed out.

Next, using the volumes you calculated, actually prepare the real-time PCR reaction mixtures in the 4-tube strip. Because real-time PCR measures the amount of fluorescence, the lids of the tubes must be handled cleanly. Put on rubber gloves before carrying out the experimental operations. Next, as shown by the red circle in Figure 4, write your name-tag number with an oil-based pen on the right end of the 4-tube strip. Write only your name-tag number with the oil-based pen, and write nothing on the lids or the sides. Number the tubes 1, 2, 3 and 4 from the left. Following Table 2, put the reaction mixture of Table 1 into tubes 1–4. Using the micropipette, measure out each solution in order from the top of Table 1 and put it into tubes 1–4.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2017-4-1-fig4.png

Figure 4. Writing the name-tag number on the PCR tubes (4-tube strip)

Table 2. Tubes and their contents

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Tube number} & \text{cDNA} & \text{Primer mixture} \\ \hline 1 & \text{Dry seeds} & \textit{GA3ox} \\ \hline 2 & \text{Dry seeds} & \textit{UBQ} \\ \hline 3 & \text{Imbibed seeds} & \textit{GA3ox} \\ \hline 4 & \text{Imbibed seeds} & \textit{UBQ} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

When all the solutions have been added to the 4-tube strip, finally mix the reaction solution thoroughly by slowly moving the push button up and down and repeatedly drawing up and expelling the liquid. When you have finished mixing, close the lids of the tubes firmly. Do not open the lids of the 4-tube strip once they have been closed. The tightness of the lids would decrease, and the reaction solution could all evaporate and be lost during the real-time PCR reaction. 40 minutes after the start of the exam, an assistant will collect the 4-tube strip and set it in the real-time PCR apparatus.
