The figure shows the light absorption spectra of oxygen-bound haemoglobin (solid line) and unbound haemoglobin (broken line).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-1-9-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 酸素結合型ヘモグロビン = oxygen-bound haemoglobin; 非結合型ヘモグロビン = unbound haemoglobin; 光の波長 nm = wavelength of light (nm).

The horizontal axis is the wavelength of light (nm), and the vertical axis is the absorbance per 1 mmol/L; between 470 nm and 660 nm it is magnified 10 times (central vertical-axis scale), and from 660 nm towards longer wavelengths it is magnified a further 10 times (right vertical-axis scale). Absorbance is defined as follows.

When light passes through a light-absorbing substance, the light is absorbed and its intensity decreases. Using the intensity $I_0$ of the irradiated light of a particular wavelength and the intensity $I$ of the transmitted light, the transmittance $T$ is defined by

$$T = \frac{I}{I_0}$$

In actual measurements, if the transmitted light becomes too weak it cannot be measured accurately, and $T$ needs to be at least about 0.01 (1%). The logarithm of the reciprocal of $T$ is the absorbance $A$:

$$A = \log_{10}\frac{I_0}{I} = -\log_{10}\frac{I}{I_0} = -\log_{10}T$$

For a particular substance, the following relationship holds (the Lambert–Beer law).

$$A = K \times c \times l$$

[where $K$: a constant for each substance and wavelength, $c$: concentration of the substance, $l$: optical path length (the length of the substance through which the light passes)]

Here, $K$ at a concentration of 1 mol/L and an optical path length of 1 cm is called the molar absorption coefficient and is denoted by ε. That is, the vertical axis of the graph shows the absorbance $A$ per 1 mmol/L of concentration and per 1 cm of optical path length. The numbers shown at the peaks of the spectra in the figure are the peak wavelengths.

Because oxygen-bound and unbound haemoglobin differ in absorbance depending on the wavelength, the proportion of the oxygen-bound form (oxygen saturation) can be measured with light of particular wavelengths. B. 433 nm

C. 542 nm

D. 556 nm

E. 576 nm

F. around 660 nm

G. around 900 nm

I. take the ratio of 542 nm and 556 nm

J. take the ratio of 556 nm and 576 nm

K. take the ratio of 660 nm and 900 nm

図は，ヘモグロビンの酸素結合型（実線）と非結合型（破線）の光吸収スペクトルである。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-1-9-fig1.png

横軸は光の波長（nm），縦軸は1 mmol/Lあたりの吸光度で，470 nmから660 nmの間は10倍に（中央縦軸目盛り），660 nmから長波長側はさらに10倍に（右側縦軸目盛り）拡大してある。なお，吸光度は以下のように定義される。

光を吸収する物質を透過すると光が吸収されて強度が小さくなる。特定の波長の照射した光の強度$I_0$と透過してきた光の強度$I$をもちいて，透過度$T$は

$$T = \frac{I}{I_0}$$

で定義される。実際の測定では透過光があまりに弱くなると正確に測定はできず，$T$は最低でも0.01（1%）程度は必要である。$T$の逆数の対数値をとったものが吸光度$A$で，

$$A = \log_{10}\frac{I_0}{I} = -\log_{10}\frac{I}{I_0} = -\log_{10}T$$

となる。特定の物質に対しては，以下のような関係をもつ（Lambert-Beerの法則）。

$$A = K \times c \times l$$

［ただし，$K$：物質，波長ごとの定数，$c$：物質の濃度，$l$：光路長（光が透過する物質の長さ）］

ここで，濃度1 mol/L，光路長1 cmのときの$K$をモル吸光係数といい，εであらわす。すなわち，グラフの縦軸は濃度1 mmol/Lあたり，光路長1 cmあたりの吸光度$A$を示している。なお，図中のスペクトルのピークに表示した数字は，ピーク波長である。

In the conversion of genetic information during translation, by which proteins are made, 3 nucleotides of mRNA (a codon) correspond to 1 amino acid. The table on the right shows this correspondence for nuclear genes of eukaryotes.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-1-20-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 遺伝暗号表 = genetic code table; 終止コドン = stop codon.

As shown in the table, all amino acids except methionine (Met) and tryptophan (Trp) have more than one codon. For example, glycine (Gly) corresponds to the 4 codons GGU, GGC, GGA and GGG. Because of this redundancy (degeneracy), even if the third base, C, of the codon GGC changes to A by mutation, the amino acid does not change. Such base substitutions that are not accompanied by a change of amino acid are called synonymous substitutions. On the other hand, if the first base of the same GGC is substituted, the amino acid changes to serine (Ser) for G→A, to arginine (Arg) for G→C and to cysteine (Cys) for G→U; whatever the substitution, the amino acid changes. Such base substitutions that are accompanied by a change of amino acid are called non-synonymous substitutions.

Now, the DNA sequences of a gene with a total length of 300 amino acids (codons), which has been conserved in various species, were examined in 3 species, X, Y and Z. Differences were observed in the DNA sequences corresponding to the 5th, 12th, 67th and 121st amino acids (codons). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-1-20-fig1.png

表にあるようにメチオニン（Met）とトリプトファン（Trp）を除くアミノ酸には複数のコドンが存在する。たとえば，グリシン（Gly）では，GGU，GGC，GGA，GGGの4個のコドンが対応する。その冗長性（縮退性）から突然変異でGGCのコドンの三番目の塩基CがAに変化してもアミノ酸は変わらない。このようなアミノ酸の変化を伴わない塩基置換は同義置換とよばれる。一方，同じGGCでも第一番目の塩基が置換した場合は，G→Aではセリン（Ser），G→Cではアルギニン（Arg），G→Uではシステイン（Cys）へとアミノ酸が変化し，どのような置換であってもアミノ酸は変化する。このようなアミノ酸の変化を伴う塩基置換は非同義置換とよばれる。

いま，さまざまな生物種で保存されてきた全長300個のアミノ酸（コドン）からなる遺伝子に対し，X，Y，Zの3種でDNA配列を調べた。すると5番目，12番目，67番目，121番目のアミノ酸（コドン）に対応するDNA配列に違いが観察された。これらの種の系統関係と各部位でのDNA配列は次のとおりである。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-1-20-fig2.png

この結果から種Xと種Yの共通祖先①から種Xと種Yへと進化する過程で生じた同義置換（アミノ酸の変化を伴わない塩基置換）の数を推定し，その値としてもっとも適切な組合せをA～Lから選べ。なおこれらの生物種は近縁であり，複数の置換が同じ塩基サイトに生じる可能性はないと仮定する。（6点）

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} & \text{A} & \text{B} & \text{C} & \text{D} & \text{E} & \text{F} & \text{G} & \text{H} & \text{I} & \text{J} & \text{K} & \text{L} \\ \hline \text{祖先種①から種X} & \text{0} & \text{1} & \text{2} & \text{3} & \text{0} & \text{1} & \text{2} & \text{3} & \text{0} & \text{1} & \text{2} & \text{3} \\ \text{祖先種①から種Y} & \text{0} & \text{0} & \text{0} & \text{0} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{2} & \text{2} & \text{2} & \text{2} \end{array}$$

problems.problem:
Pill bugs (ダンゴムシ) have the characteristic of "rolling the body up" when stimulated, whereas woodlice (ワラジムシ) usually do not roll the body up. The phylogenetic tree below is the result of a recent molecular phylogenetic analysis of terrestrial isopods.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-1-21-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English), from top to bottom: オカダンゴムシ類（丸くなる） = land pill bugs (roll up); ハヤシワラジムシ類（丸くならない） = forest woodlice (do not roll up); ワラジムシ類（丸くならない） = woodlice (do not roll up); コシビロダンゴムシ類（丸くなる） = broad-waisted pill bugs (roll up); ナガワラジムシ類（丸くならない） = long woodlice (do not roll up); ハマダンゴムシ類（丸くなる） = beach pill bugs (roll up).

The following passage describes the evolution of the trait "rolling the body up". Choose the appropriate combination of numbers that fill the blanks ( ) in the passage from A–L. (5 points)

In the evolution of the terrestrial isopods, if it is assumed that the common ancestor of this group did not roll its body up, there are ( ア ) ways in which the changes could have occurred that minimise the number of character changes, and the number of changes is then ( イ ). On the other hand, if it is assumed that the common ancestor rolled its body up, there are ( ウ ) ways in which the changes could have occurred that minimise the number of character changes, and the number of changes is then ( エ ).

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} & \text{A} & \text{B} & \text{C} & \text{D} & \text{E} & \text{F} & \text{G} & \text{H} & \text{I} & \text{J} & \text{K} & \text{L} \\ \hline \text{ア} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{2} & \text{2} & \text{2} & \text{2} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} \\ \text{イ} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} \\ \text{ウ} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} \\ \text{エ} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} \end{array}$$

ダンゴムシの仲間は刺激を受けると「体が丸くなる」という特徴があるが，ワラジムシの仲間はふつう体が丸くならない。下の系統樹は，最近の陸棲等脚類の分子系統解析の結果である。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-1-21-fig1.png

次の文章は「体が丸くなる」という形質の進化について述べたものである。文中の（ ）の中に入る数字として適切な組合せをA～Lから選べ。（5点）

陸棲等脚類の進化において，このグループの共通祖先は体が丸くならなかったと仮定すると，形質変化の回数が最小となる変化の起き方は（ ア ）とおりあり，その時の変化の回数は（ イ ）回である。いっぽう，共通祖先は体が丸くなっていたと仮定すると，形質変化の回数が最小となる変化の起き方は（ ウ ）とおりあり，その時の変化の回数は（ エ ）回になる。

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} & \text{A} & \text{B} & \text{C} & \text{D} & \text{E} & \text{F} & \text{G} & \text{H} & \text{I} & \text{J} & \text{K} & \text{L} \\ \hline \text{ア} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{2} & \text{2} & \text{2} & \text{2} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} \\ \text{イ} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} \\ \text{ウ} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{1} & \text{3} \\ \text{エ} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{1} & \text{3} & \text{3} & \text{3} \end{array}$$

problems.title: Experiment 1, Question 1-1
problems.problem:
Experiment 1 (実験1): "Measurement and comparison of the myrosinase activity in wasabi"

Specimens, reagents and apparatus (to be checked within 5 minutes of the start):

Specimens
• Wasabi (ワサビ) – 1 root (you may take it home)
• Plant I (wasabi) – 1 bag of flowers (you may take it home)
• Plant II – 1 bag of flowers (you may take it home)
• Plant III – 1 bag of flowers (you may take it home)
• Plant IV – 1 bag of flowers (you may take it home)
• Plant V – 1 bag of flowers (you may take it home)
• Plant VI – 1 bag of flowers (you may take it home)
• Plant VII – 1 bag of flowers (you may take it home)

Reagents
• 50 mM HEPES buffer, pH 7.0 (in a 50 mL tube) – 30 mL, 1 tube
• 2 mM sinigrin (in a 1.5 mL tube) – 1.4 mL, 1 tube
• Glucose test (in a 15 mL tube) – 6 mL, 1 tube
• 2 mM sodium ascorbate solution (in a 1.5 mL tube) – 0.5 mL, 1 tube
• 2 mM sodium acetate solution (in a 1.5 mL tube) – 0.5 mL, 1 tube
• 2 mM sodium phosphate solution (in a 1.5 mL tube) – 0.5 mL, 1 tube
• 3.2 mM glucose solution (in a 1.5 mL tube) – 0.5 mL, 1 tube
• Ion-exchanged water (in a 15 mL tube) – 10 mL, 1 tube

Apparatus
• Weighing scale – 1 (you may take it home)
• Grater – 1 (you may take it home)
• Spoon – 1 (you may take it home)
• Weighing dish – 1
• Magnifying glass (loupe) – 1 (you may take it home)
• Nitrile gloves (S, M, L) – 1 pair of each (choose the size that fits you)
• Syringe and plunger – 1 set
• Kimwipe – 1 sheet
• NAP-10 column – 1
• Empty 15 mL tubes – 5
• Rack for 15 mL tubes – 1
• 1 mL dropper – 1
• 3 mL dropper – 1
• 5 mL dropper – 1
• 200 µL micropipette – 1
• Micropipette tips – 1 box
• Empty 1.5 mL microtubes – 6
• Microtube rack – 1
• 96-well plate – 1
• Waste beaker – 1
• Wet tissues – 1 box
• Candidate-number sticker – 1
• 96-well plate seal – 1

Auxiliary items
• Paper towels – 1 set
• Oil-based marker pen – 1
• Rubbish bag – 1 (fixed to the table)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-3-1-fig1.png

Reference: NAP-10 column (参考: NAP-10 カラム).

You may write sample names etc. on the tubes with the oil-based marker pen if necessary. The use of computers, smartphones and calculators is prohibited. The weighing scale, grater, spoon and magnifying glass may be taken home after the examination.

Notes for working through the paper
• First read through the whole booklet and draw up an overall plan before starting work.
• No additional specimens, reagents or apparatus will be distributed.
• The 96-well plate after the reaction is kept as evidence: at the end of the experiment, apply the plate seal and the candidate-number sticker and keep the plate on your bench.
• Wear a lab coat, safety goggles and gloves during the examination. Some of the samples used in this experiment are not toxic but are irritant; take care that samples etc. do not come into direct contact with your eyes, mouth, skin and so on.

Units used in the questions
M: molar concentration (mole/L)
The SI prefixes are given below; refer to them as necessary.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Prefix} & \text{Symbol} & 10^{n} \\ \hline \text{milli} & \text{m} & 10^{-3} \\ \hline \text{micro} & \mu & 10^{-6} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Introduction
Wasabi is a plant rooted in our daily life, and its paste is used as an important spice in many dishes such as sushi and sashimi. The cultivation of true wasabi (本ワサビ) in particular is said to have begun in Shizuoka, and its history goes back to the Edo period.

Wasabi is classified in the Brassicaceae (アブラナ科), and the substance responsible for its pungency is isothiocyanate. In the plant body, isothiocyanate is stored in parenchyma cells as a glycoside (glucosinolate) linked to glucose by an S-glycosidic bond. One of the representative glucosinolates is called sinigrin, and it is the precursor of allyl isothiocyanate.

Many plants of the Brassicaceae use glucosinolates for their own defence responses. Brassicaceae plants have special cells called myrosin cells in the phloem, and inside them they store an enzyme called myrosinase, which hydrolyses thioglycosides. That is, normally the substrate, glucosinolate, and the enzyme that breaks it down, myrosinase, are spatially separated. However, when cells are damaged by feeding by insects and other animals, the two are mixed and isothiocyanate is produced; this forms a system by which the plant protects itself.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-3-1-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): シニグリン = sinigrin; ミロシナーゼ = myrosinase; グルコース = glucose; アリルイソチオシアネート = allyl isothiocyanate.

Figure 1. Reaction producing allyl isothiocyanate from sinigrin by myrosinase

Compared with other glycoside hydrolases, myrosinase has a special active centre, and the enzyme on its own has low activity. To show high activity it requires a coenzyme. The strength of the pungency therefore depends not only on the amounts of the substrate, glucosinolate, and of the enzyme (myrosinase), but also on the amount of substances that assist myrosinase activity.

In this experiment, a wasabi extract is fractionated with an NAP-10 column, and the myrosinase activity of each fraction is measured and compared. You will also investigate which chemical substance is required for myrosinase activity. Myrosinase produces isothiocyanate and glucose from its substrate, glucosinolate. The myrosinase activities are therefore compared by detecting the glucose produced, as a red-purple colour, with a glucose assay kit according to the reactions in Figure 2.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-3-1-fig3.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): α-D-グルコース = α-D-glucose; β-D-グルコース = β-D-glucose; ムタロターゼ = mutarotase; グルコースオキシダーゼ = glucose oxidase; グルコン酸 = gluconic acid; ペルオキシダーゼ = peroxidase; 4-アミノアンチピリン = 4-aminoantipyrine; フェノール = phenol; 赤色色素 = red dye; ラボアッセイ™ グルコース取扱説明書より改変 = modified from the LabAssay™ Glucose instruction manual.

Figure 2. Principle of glucose detection

Note that no additional reagents or apparatus will be distributed to candidates, so think carefully about the procedure and the amounts needed as you use them.

1. Preparation of a crude extract of the plant
To extract myrosinase, grate the wasabi with the grater. Large solid matter is removed by filtration so that it does not interfere with the subsequent column purification.

① Pack one Kimwipe into the syringe, push it down with the plunger and make a filter unit like the one in the figure below. After making it, pull the plunger out.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-3-1-fig4.png

Figure 3. Example of a syringe filter unit

② Wearing gloves, grate a little less than 1/4 of the wasabi root with the grater. Transfer the grated wasabi to the dish with the spoon and weigh it.
③ Transfer it to a 15 mL tube, add HEPES buffer (pH 7.0) at a ratio of 5 mL per 1 g of sample, close the lid and suspend. Make at least 5 mL of suspension.
④ Transfer the suspension into the syringe packed with the Kimwipe, insert the plunger that you removed and filter off the solid matter, collecting the "wasabi filtrate" in a new 15 mL tube. It does not matter if the liquid is cloudy.

2. Crude fractionation of the filtrate using the NAP-10 column
The NAP-10 column is a column that can fractionate samples on the principle of gel-filtration chromatography. For example, it can separate proteins from low-molecular-weight compounds.

① Remove the top and bottom caps and discard the storage solution into the beaker. Rest the column gently on a 15 mL tube, then put 3 mL of HEPES buffer into the top of the NAP-10 column. After the liquid has completely run out, put in 3 mL of HEPES buffer again. Put in 3 mL of buffer once more to equilibrate the inside of the column. Note that if the column is fitted tightly into the 15 mL tube, there is no outlet for air and the liquid will not elute.
② Load 1 mL of the filtrate. Fine precipitate in the filtrate may be loaded onto the column without any problem. Collect the liquid that comes out in the same tube as in ①.
③ Set the NAP-10 column on a new 15 mL tube, add 1 mL of buffer, and collect the eluted fraction A.
④ Set the NAP-10 column on a new 15 mL tube, add 2 mL of buffer, and collect the eluted fraction B.
* Precipitate forming in either fraction does not affect the activity measurement.

3. Measurement of myrosinase activity
For fractions A and B eluted from the NAP-10, carry out enzyme reactions with controls set up for the presence or absence of each coenzyme candidate and the presence or absence of the substrate. Pay attention to the combinations to be mixed.

<Preparation of the glucose standards>
① Mix the supplied 3.2 mM glucose solution and 50 mM HEPES buffer pH 7.0 as appropriate to make a series of glucose standard solutions of 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.6 and 3.2 mM in 1.5 mL microtubes.

<Glucosinolate degradation reaction of the purified fractions>
② Dispense 50 µL of fraction A, fraction B or buffer as a negative control into the 96-well plate.
③ Add 50 µL of each coenzyme-candidate solution or of ion-exchanged water to the wells.
④ Further add 100 µL of glucosinolate or of ion-exchanged water and leave at room temperature for 20 minutes to react. Write the start and end times of the reaction on the answer sheet.

<Glucose detection reaction>
⑤ Transfer 20 µL of the enzyme reaction mixture or of a glucose standard to another well, add 180 µL of the glucose test to it, and wait a further 10 minutes. Write the start and end times of the reaction on the answer sheet.
⑥ A red-purple colour reaction occurs according to the glucose concentration. After writing the positions of the glucose standards on the answer sheet, quantify the myrosinase reaction mixtures by comparing their colour intensity with that of the control reactions and of the glucose standards.
⑦ At the end of the experiment, seal the 96-well plate with the plate seal, then stick the candidate-number sticker where it does not get in the way of checking the colour results, and keep the plate on your bench.
* It has been confirmed that the colour is stable for at least 3 hours at room temperature and does not change during the examination.

Answer the following questions on the basis of the above experimental results.

Question 1-1 (問1-1)

For each condition, compare the degree of colour development with and without the substrate (glucosinolate) and with and without each candidate activity-assisting substance with the colour of the glucose standards, and choose the closest glucose concentration value.

From the four options below, choose the most appropriate description of the behaviour in the NAP-10 column of the myrosinase obtained from the wasabi extract.

problems.title: Experiment 2, Question 2-1
problems.problem:
Experiment 2 (実験2): "Observation of flower morphology"

Introduction
Today the phylogeny of organisms is inferred from DNA base sequences, but the morphological information that each organism has is still useful for classifying organisms. For the classification of angiosperms, morphological information on the flower, their reproductive organ, is important. In the structure of a flower, the pistil (雌しべ, 雌蕊) is at the centre, and outside it the stamens (雄しべ, 雄蕊), the petals and the sepals (がく, 萼) are arranged in this order (Figure 1); this order is conserved in almost all angiosperms. However, the numbers and shapes of the pistils, stamens, petals and sepals are diverse, and they are important for the phylogenetic classification of angiosperms. In addition, the flower with a superior ovary (子房上位花), in which the ovary is located above the points of attachment of the sepals, petals and stamens (Figure 1), the flower with an inferior ovary (子房下位花), in which the ovary is located below the points of attachment (Figure 2), and the intermediate perigynous flower (子房周位花) (Figure 3) are also important forms for the classification of angiosperms.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2023-3-8-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 雄しべ = stamen; 雌しべ = pistil; 花弁 = petal; がく = sepal; 子房 = ovary.

Figure 1 (left). Flower with a superior ovary. Figure 2 (centre). Flower with an inferior ovary. Figure 3 (right). Perigynous flower.

Observation procedure
Observe the flowers of the supplied plants I–VII, and examine the number of sepals, the number of petals, the number of stamens and the position of the ovary. The supplied plants I–VII are classified as in Table 1.

Table 1. The supplied plants and their classification

$$\begin{array}{ll} \hline \text{Plant I (wasabi)} & \text{Brassicaceae, Brassicales} \\ \text{Plant II} & \text{Cleomaceae, Brassicales} \\ \text{Plant III} & \text{Malvaceae, Malvales} \\ \text{Plant IV} & \text{Onagraceae, Myrtales} \\ \text{Plant V} & \text{Melastomataceae, Myrtales} \\ \text{Plant VI} & \text{Hydrangeaceae, Cornales} \\ \text{Plant VII} & \text{Ranunculaceae, Ranunculales} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Notes on the observation
• Two flowers of each of plants I–VII (but only one of plant V, because it is large) have been put in each bag, immersed in 70% ethanol.
• Observe the flowers without taking them out of the plastic bags.
• You may use the magnifying glass provided for the observation.
• Hold each bag by its edge so as not to crush the flowers inside it.
• Flowers that are difficult to observe have been stained red.

Experiment 1 (実験1): "Analysis of the localisation of a target protein by immunostaining"

Introduction

Immunostaining is a method that uses an antibody that specifically recognises the protein of interest (a primary antibody) to reveal the localisation of that protein. The distributed 1.5 ml tube marked A contains African clawed frog embryos about 2 days after fertilisation (hereafter "embryo A"). This "embryo A" is part-way through immunostaining with antibody A, a primary antibody that specifically recognises protein A. "Embryo N", in the 1.5 ml tube marked N, has been put through exactly the same procedure as embryo A, except that no primary antibody was added.

For "embryo A" and "embryo N", finish the immunostaining according to Procedure 1 below, and reveal the localisation of protein A in the African clawed frog embryo. You may use the same dropper throughout. Also, as no additional reagents or apparatus will be distributed to candidates, use them while thinking carefully about the procedure and the amounts needed.

Procedure 1
① Write your candidate number and "A" or "N" on the seal part of the two vials. Next, using a dropper, add about one third of the colour-development solution to each of the two vials.
② Using the dropper, draw up one embryo from the 1.5 mL tube containing embryo A and transfer it to the vial on which you wrote your candidate number and "A" in ①. The embryos are fragile, so handle them with great care. In the same way for embryo N, transfer one embryo to the vial on which you wrote your candidate number and "N". Check that each embryo is fully immersed in the staining solution in its vial.
③ After leaving them to stand for 1 minute, check the degree of staining by eye or under the stereomicroscope. Compare "A" and "N"; if a clear difference in the staining result can be seen, remove the colour-development solution from both vials with the dropper and transfer it to the waste-liquid container, and then add the water in the wide-mouthed bottle until the embryos are fully immersed. If no clear difference has arisen between the staining of "A" and "N", continue the staining and check the progress of the staining at intervals of about 30 seconds. When a clear difference between the staining of embryo A and embryo N is observed after the additional staining, remove the colour-development solution from both vials with the dropper and add the water mentioned above until the embryos are fully immersed.
*If no clear difference between the two is observed after 5 minutes, raise your hand and ask the invigilator for instructions.
④ Pour plenty of water into a distributed Petri dish, then transfer the embryos into it and observe them in detail with the stereomicroscope. You may label the Petri dishes with the oil-based pen as appropriate. Also, as there are two each of embryo A and embryo N in the 1.5 mL tubes, you may redo the staining as appropriate. If the colour-development solution runs out, raise your hand and inform the invigilator.

You may supplement the sketch with an explanation in sentences as appropriate, for example by identifying each tissue and organ as far as you can. problems.title: Experiment 3, Question 3–1
problems.problem:
Experiment 3 (実験3): "Dissection of the head appendages of an insect"

Introduction

Arthropods basically have a body plan in which several segments are joined in series, and each segment often bears a pair of projecting structures (appendages). The number and shape of these segments, and what form of appendage each segment bears, is one of the basic principles that produce the morphological diversity of arthropods.

The insect head is a structure in which several segments are fused. Therefore, several appendages are present on the insect head. Among the head appendages of insects, the one whose name is best known is (　A　). (　A　), present as a pair at the front of the head, are known as organs responsible for the senses, and generally bear many receptors for mechanical and chemical stimuli. (　B　), the maxilla and (　C　) are appendages involved in feeding in many insects. (　B　) is an appendage consisting of a single segment and is used mainly for chewing food. The maxilla is an appendage located on the caudal side of (　B　) and consists of several segments. In general, the maxilla has a structure in which a relatively well-sclerotised base (consisting of two segments, the cardo (軸節) and the stipes (蝶咬節)) bears a structure of several joined segments called the palp (髭), together with the galea (外葉) and the lacinia (内葉). (　C　) is an appendage located still further caudally than the maxilla. In general, (　B　) and the maxilla are paired structures, one on the left and one on the right, but in (　C　) the left and right structures are fused.

When an aqueous solution of double-stranded DNA is heated sufficiently, the hydrogen bonds between the two strands of the DNA are broken and the DNA separates into single strands. When the temperature is then lowered, complementary strands reassociate with each other to form double strands. The higher the concentration of complementary strands in the solution, the faster the reassociation proceeds. The rate of reassociation also depends on the salt concentration of the solution, but below all solutions are assumed to have the same salt concentration. It is also assumed that sonication fragments double-stranded DNA into double-stranded DNA pieces that are all 500 base pairs long.

The genome of a certain phage P is a double-stranded DNA of 50,000 base pairs that contains no repetitive sequences. This genome was fragmented by sonication, and an aqueous solution with a concentration of 50 mg/L was prepared. After this solution was heated so that all of the DNA separated into single strands, the temperature was lowered, and the proportion of the weight of DNA that remained single-stranded in the total weight of DNA in the solution was measured over time; the result was curve p in the figure. The time elapsed after the temperature was lowered is T, and the common logarithm of T is log T.

The genetic information of organisms is represented by the sequence of the four kinds of bases contained in DNA [adenine (A), cytosine (C), guanine (G) and thymine (T)]. One of the methods for determining a base sequence is the Sanger method.

In the Sanger method, a single strand of the DNA to be analysed is used as the template, and DNA fragments are synthesised in a reaction mixture containing one kind of primer that binds specifically to the template DNA, eight kinds of nucleotides (four kinds of deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates and four kinds of dideoxyribonucleoside triphosphates) and DNA polymerase. The dideoxyribonucleoside triphosphates are labelled with fluorescence of a different colour for each of the four bases (A: red, C: yellow, G: green, T: blue), and when one of them is incorporated into the growing new DNA strand, elongation of that strand stops. The synthesised single-stranded DNA is subjected to agarose gel electrophoresis with fluorescence detection, and the base sequence is read from the pattern of the bands obtained.

When an 8-base region of a certain single-stranded DNA was analysed by the Sanger method, the band pattern shown in the figure was obtained. ⊖ and ⊕ in the figure indicate the electrodes during electrophoresis.

The spike protein on the outside of the novel coronavirus (hereafter abbreviated as S protein) binds with its tip to the ACE-2 receptor on the surface of human cells, which triggers the entry of the virus into human cells. In “variants” in which part of the S protein has changed, binding to the ACE-2 receptor may become easier and infectivity may increase. Vaccines that induce antibodies which bind to the S protein to prevent entry have also been developed, but “variants” that bind less readily to the antibodies and cause immune evasion have also appeared. The novel coronavirus is an RNA virus that has RNA as its genetic information, and when it enters a human cell, the S protein and other proteins are synthesised in the cell on the basis of the information of the viral RNA. Designations such as “N501Y” and “E484K” are used to denote variants of the novel coronavirus. For example, “N501Y” indicates that the 501st amino acid of the S protein has changed from N to Y; N and Y are one-letter symbols for amino acids, N denoting asparagine and Y tyrosine.

The activities of our bodies are supported by the energy from the hydrolysis of ATP. The amount of ATP we produce and consume per day is far larger than the steady-state amount in the body: we carry out the reaction ADP + Pi → ATP (Pi is inorganic phosphate), that is, respiration, many times a day, and one molecule of ATP is made and used over and over again. In other words, it is recycled.

Let us therefore estimate roughly how many times an ATP molecule is recycled per day. Take the total amount of ATP in the body to be 50 g. For simplicity, assume that the calories consumed per day are 2500 kcal, that all of them are taken in as carbohydrate, and that 30 mol of ATP is produced from 1 mol of glucose.

The ATP produced from 2500 kcal worth of glucose is ( ア ) g. This is the total amount of ATP produced in one day. If the ATP in the body is 50 g, one molecule of ATP is calculated to be recycled about ( イ ) times a day. On the other hand, the energy obtained from the hydrolysis of ( ア ) g of ATP is considerably less than 2500 kcal. This is because the energy efficiency of respiration is not 100%; calculated with the standard free energy changes, the energy efficiency in this case is ( ウ )%. The energy that was not converted into ATP becomes heat. That heat is an amount that would raise the temperature of 60 kg of water by about ( エ ) °C.

problems.problem:
The courtship behaviour of fruit flies (ショウジョウバエ) consists of several behavioural elements. Among them, the pattern of wing sound (courtship song) that the male produces by vibrating his wings acts, via hearing, as a courtship signal to the female. Courtship song is species-specific and is thought to be one of the mechanisms by which females avoid mating with males of other species. To find out the ability of females to discriminate courtship songs, the following experiment was carried out using the common fruit fly (キイロショウジョウバエ).

Using sound-generation software, three different courtship songs were created artificially. The one identical to the courtship song of the common fruit fly was called courtship song I, one with some differences courtship song II, and one with large differences courtship song III. Flies were isolated one by one immediately after eclosion, and the wings of the males were removed. One female and one male with its wings removed were placed in the same space, and whether they mated was observed while one of the three different courtship songs was played from a speaker. As a control, whether they mated was also observed without sound. For each condition, the proportion that mated within 30 minutes of the start of observation was recorded. The table below shows the results.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c|c} \text{Courtship song played in the experiment} & \text{I} & \text{II} & \text{III} & \text{none} \\ \text{Proportion that mated} & 79\% & 78\% & 14\% & 25\% \end{array}$$

In the next experiment, females immediately after eclosion were divided into three groups. One group was played courtship song I for one week. Another group was played courtship song II for one week. The remaining group was kept without sound for one week. Using these females, an experiment similar to the previous one was carried out. The males used were males one week after eclosion with their wings removed. The table below shows the results.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c|c|c|c} \text{Courtship song played for one week} & \text{I} & \text{I} & \text{II} & \text{II} & \text{none} & \text{none} \\ \text{Courtship song played in the experiment} & \text{I} & \text{II} & \text{I} & \text{II} & \text{I} & \text{II} \\ \text{Proportion that mated} & 56\% & 22\% & 67\% & 60\% & 79\% & 78\% \end{array}$$

The following statements concern the ability of females to discriminate the courtship songs produced by males. Choose from A–L the combination of statements that can be inferred from the experimental results. (6 points)

⑥ When the ability to discriminate courtship songs rises, females come to mate actively with males that produce the courtship song of their own species.

⑦ When the ability to discriminate courtship songs rises, females come to reject males that produce the courtship song of other species.

The mark–recapture method is one of the methods for estimating the number of individuals in a population. The basic procedure of this method is as follows. $m$ individuals are captured at random from the population, marked and returned to the original population (first capture). After a certain period, $c$ individuals are captured at random from the population, and $r$ of them are found to be marked (second capture). The number of individuals in the population ($N$) is estimated from the relation $N : m = c : r$ as

$$N = \frac{mc}{r} \qquad (1)$$

Equation (1) is derived on the basis of several assumptions. The following passage concerns these assumptions. Choose from A–L the combination of statements that fill the blanks ( ). (6 points)

It is assumed that “in the second capture, the capture rate of marked individuals and the capture rate of unmarked individuals are equal”. If the capture rate of marked individuals is lower than that of unmarked individuals, the number of individuals estimated with equation (1) is expected to be ( ア ) than the actual number of individuals.

It is assumed that “the number of individuals neither increases nor decreases between the first capture and the second capture”. If during this period there is emigration from this population and the number of individuals decreases, the number of individuals estimated with equation (1) is expected to ( イ ). [The emigrating individuals are assumed to be chosen at random from this population.] Also, if during this period there is immigration into this population and the number of individuals increases, the number of individuals estimated with equation (1) is expected to ( ウ ).

個体群の個体数を推定する方法に標識再捕獲法がある。この方法の基本手順は次のとおりである。個体群から無作為（ランダム）に$m$個体を捕獲し，標識を付けて元の個体群に戻す（1回目の捕獲）。一定期間後，個体群から無作為に$c$個体を捕獲し，$r$個体に標識が付いていることを確認する（2回目の捕獲）。個体群の個体数（$N$）は，$N : m = c : r$の関係から，

$$N = \frac{mc}{r} \qquad \text{（1）}$$

problems.problem:
The common fruit fly (キイロショウジョウバエ) has one pair of sex chromosomes (XX in females, XY in males) and three pairs of autosomes. Assume that each of three loci P, Q and R has two alleles (P1 and P2, Q1 and Q2, R1 and R2). The phenotype of genotype P1/P1 is called type P1, the phenotype of genotype P2/P2 type P2, the phenotype of genotype Q1/Q1 type Q1, the phenotype of genotype Q2/Q2 type Q2, the phenotype of genotype R1/R1 type R1, and the phenotype of genotype R2/R2 type R2.

One female of phenotype P1 Q1 R1 was crossed with one male of phenotype P2 Q2 R2, and 30 females and 30 males were obtained as the offspring generation (F1 generation). When their phenotypes were examined, all 30 females were type P2 Q2 R2 and all 30 males were type P1 Q1 R1.

Next, the 30 females and 30 males of the F1 generation were crossed, and 1000 flies, females and males together, were obtained as the next generation (F2 generation). Their phenotypes were as shown in the table below.

$$\begin{array}{l|r} \text{type P1 Q1 R1} & \text{457 flies} \\ \text{type P1 Q1 R2} & \text{25 flies} \\ \text{type P1 Q2 R1} & \text{14 flies} \\ \text{type P1 Q2 R2} & \text{1 fly} \\ \text{type P2 Q1 R1} & \text{1 fly} \\ \text{type P2 Q1 R2} & \text{15 flies} \\ \text{type P2 Q2 R1} & \text{26 flies} \\ \text{type P2 Q2 R2} & \text{461 flies} \end{array}$$

Based on the above results, choose from A–L the most probable positions of loci P, Q and R. Recombination during meiosis is suppressed in males of the common fruit fly. Very few genes are located on the Y chromosome, and the possibility that loci P, Q and R are on the Y chromosome need not be considered. The effects of loci P, Q and R on survival and reproductive efficiency can be ignored. (7 points)

B. The three loci are on the X chromosome and are arranged in the order P, R, Q.

C. The three loci are on the X chromosome and are arranged in the order Q, P, R.

D. Loci P and Q are on the X chromosome, and locus R is on an autosome.

E. Loci P and R are on the X chromosome, and locus Q is on an autosome.

F. Loci Q and R are on the X chromosome, and locus P is on an autosome.

G. Locus P is on the X chromosome, and loci Q and R are on the same autosome.

H. Locus Q is on the X chromosome, and loci P and R are on the same autosome.

I. Locus R is on the X chromosome, and loci P and Q are on the same autosome.

J. The three loci are on the same autosome and are arranged in the order P, Q, R.

K. The three loci are on the same autosome and are arranged in the order P, R, Q.

L. The three loci are on the same autosome and are arranged in the order Q, P, R.

(8 points)

Alzheimer's disease is the largest cause of dementia in old age, and because the number of patients is increasing, the development of therapeutic drugs is awaited. In the brains of patients with Alzheimer's disease, characteristic deposits called senile plaques and neurofibrillary tangles are observed, and their main components are amyloid β peptide (Aβ) and tau protein, respectively. Because accumulation of the former is seen earlier than that of the latter, therapeutic drugs targeting the former are being developed all over the world.

Recently, "lecanemab", a monoclonal antibody against Aβ, was approved as a therapeutic drug for Alzheimer's disease, and in Japan it has come into clinical use as the first drug in line with a hypothesis of the cause of Alzheimer's disease. Lecanemab is prescribed to suppress the progression of mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease, and normally $_{\text{ア}}\underline{\text{10 mg/kg as lecanemab (genetical recombination)}}$ $\underline{\text{is administered intravenously by drip infusion,}}$ $\underline{\text{once every 2 weeks, over about 1 hour.}}$

(2) Antibody drugs are administered by injection or drip infusion because oral administration is difficult.

problems.problem:

The nematode C. elegans exists as hermaphrodites under ideal conditions. Self-fertilisation takes place inside the body of an adult hermaphrodite, larvae hatch from the eggs that are laid, and development proceeds. The nuclear phase of an individual is 2n and that of a gamete is n. The following experiment was carried out using this nematode C. elegans.

(1) One hermaphrodite (P) was transferred to an agar plate and allowed to produce the first generation ($\mathrm{F_1}$).

(2) So as not to confuse $\mathrm{F_1}$ with P, a sufficient number of larvae were chosen at random from the $\mathrm{F_1}$ produced, transferred to a new agar plate and maintained there, and the $\mathrm{F_1}$ was allowed to produce the second generation ($\mathrm{F_2}$).

(3) Thereafter, so as not to confuse successive generations ($\mathrm{F_{n-1}}$, $\mathrm{F_n}$) with each other, a sufficient number of larvae of $\mathrm{F_n}$ produced on the agar plate of $\mathrm{F_{n-1}}$ were chosen at random, transferred to a new agar plate and maintained there.

(4) The genotype of each individual of $\mathrm{F_n}$ present on the agar plate was determined.

Based on this, answer the following questions. When, for example, the environment deteriorates, males arise in C. elegans at a certain frequency, but in this problem no males arose at any step, and all the individuals that arose were hermaphrodites produced by self-fertilisation. A "sufficient number" of randomly sampled $\mathrm{F_n}$ means that the number was sufficient for "the frequencies shown by the randomly sampled Fn" to be regarded as identical to "the frequencies when the whole of Fn is taken as the population".

Question 1

In the nematode C. elegans, an allele a, a mutant form, exists for the wild-type gene A. In this experiment, when the genotype of P is Aa, find the proportion of AA individuals theoretically estimated when the whole of the nematodes of the 12th generation ($\mathrm{F_{12}}$) is taken as 1. Here, assume that the efficiencies with which gene A and gene a are passed on to the next generation in a hermaphrodite (efficiency of gamete formation, fertilisation efficiency, number of eggs laid, developmental efficiency, etc.) are completely equal to each other. Give the answer as an irreducible fraction*1, and write the integers for the numerator and the denominator in answer boxes $\fbox{6}$ and $\fbox{7}$, respectively.

The answer to Question 1 is $\dfrac{\fbox{6}}{\fbox{7}}$.

Question 2

In the nematode C. elegans, an allele b, a mutant form, exists for the wild-type gene B. Homozygotes for the mutant b (as opposed to the wild-type B) are embryonic lethal, and the laid eggs do not hatch. In this experiment, when the genotype of P is Bb, find the proportion of BB adults theoretically estimated when the whole of the adults of the 12th generation ($\mathrm{F_{12}}$) is taken as 1. Here, assume that the efficiencies with which gene B and gene b are passed on to the next generation in a hermaphrodite (efficiency of gamete formation, fertilisation efficiency, number of eggs laid, etc.) are completely equal to each other. Give the answer as an irreducible fraction, and write the integers for the numerator and the denominator in answer boxes $\fbox{8}$ and $\fbox{9}$, respectively.

The answer to Question 2 is $\dfrac{\fbox{8}}{\fbox{9}}$.

problems.problem_orig:
(11点)

線虫C. elegansは、理想的な環境では雌雄同体で存在する。雌雄同体の成虫の体内では自家受精が起こり、産み落とされた卵から幼虫が孵化し、発生が進む。個体の核相は2nであり、配偶子の核相はnである。この線虫C. elegansを用いて以下の実験を行った。

(1) 1匹の雌雄同体（P）を寒天培地に移し、第1世代（$\mathrm{F_1}$）を作らせた。

(2) $\mathrm{F_1}$とPを混同しないように、生じた$\mathrm{F_1}$から十分な数の幼虫を無作為に選んで新たな寒天培地に移して維持し、$\mathrm{F_1}$に第2世代（$\mathrm{F_2}$）を作らせた。

(3) 以下、世代同士（$\mathrm{F_{n-1}}$、$\mathrm{F_n}$）を混同しないように、$\mathrm{F_{n-1}}$の寒天培地で生じた$\mathrm{F_n}$の十分な数の幼虫を無作為に選んで新たな寒天培地に移して維持した。

(4) 寒天培地中に存在する$\mathrm{F_n}$の個々の遺伝子型を調べあげた。

これを踏まえて、以下の問いに答えなさい。なお、環境が悪化するなどした場合、線虫C. elegansには一定の頻度でオスが生じるが、本問ではすべての過程でオスは生じず、すべて自家受精による雌雄同体が生じた。また無作為に抽出した$\mathrm{F_n}$の『十分な数』というのは、『無作為に抽出したFnが示す出現頻度』が『Fn全体を母集団としたときの出現頻度』と同一と見なすのに十分であったことを意味する。

問1

線虫C. elegansにおいて、野生型の遺伝子Aに対して変異型のaという対立遺伝子が存在している。この実験でPの遺伝子型がAaであるとき、第12世代（$\mathrm{F_{12}}$）の線虫全体を1とした場合に理論的に見積もられるAAの個体の割合を求めなさい。ここで雌雄同体において遺伝子Aと遺伝子aとが次世代に引き継がれる効率（配偶子の形成効率、受精効率、産卵数、発生効率など）は互いに全く同等とする。解答は既約分数*1とし、分子と分母にあてはまる整数をそれぞれ解答欄 $\fbox{6}$ と $\fbox{7}$ に記入しなさい。

問1の答は $\dfrac{\fbox{6}}{\fbox{7}}$ である

問2

線虫C. elegansにおいて、野生型の遺伝子Bに対して変異型のbという対立遺伝子が存在している。野生型Bに対して変異型bのホモ接合体は胚性致死となり、産み落とされた卵の孵化が起こらない。この実験でPの遺伝子型がBbであるとき、第12世代（$\mathrm{F_{12}}$）の成虫全体を1とした場合に理論的に見積もられるBBの成虫の割合を求めなさい。ここで雌雄同体において遺伝子Bと遺伝子bが次世代に引き継がれる効率（配偶子の形成効率、受精効率、産卵数など）は互いに全く同等とする。解答は既約分数とし、分子と分母にあてはまる整数をそれぞれ解答欄 $\fbox{8}$ と $\fbox{9}$ に記入しなさい。

問2の答は $\dfrac{\fbox{8}}{\fbox{9}}$ である

*1 分子と分母が互いに素になるまで約分された分数のこと

シロイヌナズナのCLE遺伝子はペプチドホルモンをコードしている。植物感染性線虫のサツマイモネコブセンチュウが根に感染した後、CLE遺伝子の発現は根で上昇する。CLEペプチドは地上部に移動し、CLV1受容体に受容される。CLV1受容体が活性化すると、糖輸送体の遺伝子発現が誘導され、葉から根への糖の輸送が促進される。このようなCLE-CLV1が関わる全身性シグナルにより、線虫感染が促進される。

problems.problem:
(7 points)

The virus strain S-2L, which infects Synechococcus, a kind of cyanobacterium, is known to have 2-aminoadenine (Z) instead of adenine (A) in its DNA, and it has four kinds of bases: Z, C, G and T. In the DNA double-helix structure formed with these bases, the combination of Z and T takes the place of A and T. Whereas the bond between A and T consists of two hydrogen bonds, Z and T have three hydrogen bonds and can therefore bind more strongly (Figure 7-1). In addition, DNA in which A has been replaced by Z is no longer cut by restriction enzymes that recognise sequences containing A (an infection-defence mechanism of Synechococcus), but as genetic information A and Z are equivalent. Bearing the above in mind, answer the following questions.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2024-2-7-fig1.png

Figure 7-1. DNA bases. The dotted lines show hydrogen bonds and the wavy lines show the sites of bonding to the sugar. Left: A and T; right: Z and T

Question 1

A virus strain W was created in which the Z in the genome sequence of strain S-2L was replaced by A. When strain S-2L and strain W were each used to infect Synechococcus, strain S-2L was able to infect it and multiply, but strain W was unable to multiply even though it infected it. From statements (1)–(5) below, choose all those that are appropriate as possible causes of this, and mark the numbers of all the chosen options in the answer box. If you judge that all the statements are correct, mark only (9); if you judge that there is no correct statement, mark only (0). Answer box: $\fbox{18}$

(2) Because the genomic DNA of strain W was not cut by the restriction enzymes of Synechococcus

Question 2

At high temperatures, the hydrogen bonds between the bases of double-stranded DNA break and it becomes two single-stranded DNAs. This is called denaturation of DNA, and the temperature at which half of the DNA in an aqueous solution is denatured is called the melting temperature (Tm) of that DNA. Tm differs depending on the nucleotide sequence of the DNA, and Tm is higher when the proportion of CG base pairs, which have three hydrogen bonds, is high. If the value of Tm is calculated as 4 °C per CG base pair and 2 °C per AT base pair, the Tm of the DNA with the sequence

$$\begin{array}{l} 5'\text{-AGTATGATCCTCGAG-}3' \\ 3'\text{-TCATACTAGGAGCTC-}5' \end{array}$$

is 44 °C.

If all the A in this DNA are replaced by Z, the value of Tm changes because there are three hydrogen bonds between Z and T. Calculate what the Tm of this DNA would then be in °C, and write the integer that fits ( A ) below in the answer box. Calculate the value of Tm as 4 °C per ZT base pair. Answer box: $\fbox{19}$

The answer to Question 2 is ( A ) °C.

Find the value to one decimal place, and write the number that fits ( B ) below in the answer box. Assume that in strain S-2L all the A in the genome has been replaced by Z. Answer box: $\fbox{20}$

The answer to Question 3 is ( B ) %.

(6 points)

The way a snail moves forward as if crawling is called crawling (這行, shakō). When a crawling snail was placed on a transparent glass plate and observed from the underside, several stripes such as those in Figure 8-1(a) were observed. When one of these stripes (X) was viewed from directly beside it, it was found to be as shown in Figure 8-1(b) (here, the region between stripes is called Y). The gap between the foot and the glass plate is filled with the snail's secretion (mucus), and this mucus is made viscous by glycoproteins called mucins. This mucus has the following properties.

• When left at rest, or when the applied force is at or below a threshold, this mucus behaves like a solid with elasticity.
• When this mucus is stirred or a sudden force is applied to it, and the applied force exceeds a certain threshold, it behaves like a liquid with viscosity.
• When the force applied to this mucus falls below the threshold, the mucus that was showing the properties of a viscous liquid quickly regains its properties as an elastic solid.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2024-2-8-fig1.png

Figure 8-1. (a) A crawling snail placed on a glass plate, as observed from below. (b) The foot of a crawling snail observed from the side

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 進行方向 = direction of travel; 殻 = shell; 隙間 = gap; 腹足 = foot; ガラス板 = glass plate.

With these in mind, the mechanism by which a snail crawls can be explained by thinking as follows. In Figure 8-1(a), when the muscles of part X of the foot contract with respect to the snail's direction of travel, contraction stripes appear on the foot. As these stripes form, a depression such as that in Figure 8-1(b) arises in the gap between the foot and the contact surface, and within this depression a sudden force exceeding the threshold is applied to the mucus filling the gap, so that the mucus is stirred. As a result, when X and Y of the foot of a snail crawling as in Figure 8-1 are compared, the frictional force of ( あ ) is stronger, and ( あ ) serves as the foothold as the snail moves forward. For this reason, while the snail is crawling forward, the stripes including X appear to move along the foot ( い ).

The basic structure of the cell membrane is a lipid bilayer in which the hydrophilic heads of the phospholipid molecules, which carry negative or positive charges, are arranged on the (ア), and the carbon chains of the fatty acids (the hydrophobic parts) on the (イ). Because of this structure, compared with gas molecules such as $\mathrm{O_2}$ and $\mathrm{CO_2}$, (ウ) such as sugars and urea, and molecules carrying negative or positive charges, pass through the cell membrane with difficulty. Conversely, (エ) can enter the cell membrane freely, and so readily permeate from outside the cell into the cell. To get general drugs or artificially synthesised chemicals actively taken up into cells, their solubility in aqueous solution is also important, but the ease with which they permeate into cells varies with differences in the hydrophobicity or hydrophilicity of the drug or chemical.

Here, the discussion has in mind an experiment that measures the amount of water moving across the cell membrane and, at the same time, examines the effect of drugs on the channels involved in that movement. To examine the movement of water into and out of cells accurately, it is convenient to use spherical cells such as eggs. On the basis of the three assumptions below, Figure 9-1 (solid lines) shows the results of simulations predicting how the diameter of a spherical cell of radius 80 µm changes after it is immersed in a solution more concentrated than the intracellular osmotic pressure (hypertonic solution) or in a less concentrated solution (hypotonic solution).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2024-2-9-fig1.png

problems.problem:
(8 points)

Just after germination, plants extend their roots in the direction of gravity and their above-ground parts in the direction opposite to gravity. The plant hormone auxin is involved in these phenomena, called gravitropism. Some time after germination, plant roots no longer show gravitropism. When the distribution of roots is observed in a Japanese forest, the roots are densely distributed down to a depth of 30 cm from the ground surface (photograph). In this forest, volcanic ash had accumulated to a depth of several metres. It can also be observed that the roots extend horizontally. The layer in which the roots are distributed contains much soil organic matter, and the soil at greater depths contains hardly any soil organic matter.

Question 1

Concerning the mechanism of the phenomenon in which, when a root just after germination is placed horizontally, the root bends in the direction of gravity as it grows, choose the one most appropriate option from (1)–(4) below, and mark the number of the chosen option in the answer box. Answer box: $\fbox{34}$

(1) Because the lower side, where the auxin concentration is low, contracts, the root bends in the direction of gravity.

(2) Because the lower side, where the auxin concentration is high, contracts, the root bends in the direction of gravity.

(3) Because the upper side, where the auxin concentration is low, elongates, the root bends in the direction of gravity.

(4) Because the upper side, where the auxin concentration is high, elongates, the root bends in the direction of gravity.

Question 2

There are several hypotheses that explain the root distribution seen in Japanese forests from the viewpoint of adaptation. From options (1)–(4) below, choose all those thought not to apply to the Japanese environment, and mark the numbers of all the chosen options in the answer box. If you judge that all the statements are correct, mark (9); if you judge that there is no appropriate statement, mark only (0). Answer box: $\fbox{35}$

(1) Because there is much water near the ground surface, roots evolved to be distributed near the ground surface.

(2) Because there are many inorganic nutrients such as nitrogen near the ground surface, roots evolved to be distributed near the ground surface.

(3) As in paddy fields, there is little oxygen in the lower layers of forest soil, so roots evolved to be distributed near the ground surface.

(4) Because the layer below the one in which the roots are distributed is bedrock, roots can be distributed only near the ground surface.

Question 3

From options (1)–(4) below, choose two that are thought to be appropriate as benefits that we humans gain from plant roots being densely distributed, and mark the numbers of the chosen options in the answer box. Answer box: $\fbox{36}$

(1) They suppress the decomposition of soil organic matter by the respiration of soil microorganisms, and prevent a rise in the atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration.

(2) Because they absorb inorganic nitrogen and similar nutrients efficiently, eutrophication of rivers, lakes and marshes is suppressed.

(3) They can stop landslides that occur at depths below the layer in which the roots are distributed.

(4) Because they prevent fine soil particles with water-holding capacity from being lost by erosion, a sudden outflow of precipitation into rivers is suppressed.

problems.problem_orig:
(8点)

発芽直後の植物は重力の方向に根を伸ばし、重力と反対方向に地上部を伸ばしていく。これらの重力屈性と呼ばれる現象にはオーキシンという植物ホルモンが関係している。植物の根は発芽後しばらく経つと重力屈性を示さなくなる。日本の森林で根の分布を観察すると、根は地表から30cmまでの深さに密に分布している（写真）。この森林の場合、数mの深さまで火山灰が堆積していた。また、根は水平方向に伸長していることも観察できる。根の分布する層には土壌有機物が多く含まれており、それより深い場所の土壌には土壌有機物がほとんど含まれていない。

問1

発芽直後の根を水平に置くと根が重力の方向に曲がって伸長する現象の仕組みついて最も適当なものを以下の選択肢(1)-(4)からひとつ選び、選んだ選択肢の番号を解答欄にマークしなさい。解答欄は $\fbox{34}$

(1) オーキシン濃度の低い下側が収縮するため、根は重力方向に曲がる。

(2) オーキシン濃度の高い下側が収縮するため、根は重力方向に曲がる。

(3) オーキシン濃度の低い上側が伸長するため、根は重力方向に曲がる。

(4) オーキシン濃度の高い上側が伸長するため、根は重力方向に曲がる。

問2

日本の森林で見られる根の分布を適応の視点から説明するいくつかの説がある。日本の環境には当てはまらないと考えられるものを以下の選択肢(1)-(4)からすべて選び、選んだ選択肢の番号をすべて解答欄にマークしなさい。なお、すべての記述が正しいと判断した場合は(9)を、適切な記述が無いと判断した場合は(0)だけをマークしなさい。解答欄は $\fbox{35}$

(1) 地表面近くに水が多いため、根は地表面近くに分布するように進化した。

(2) 地表面近くに窒素などの無機栄養が多いため、根は地表面近くに分布するように進化した。

(3) 水田と同様、森林土壌の下層には酸素が少ないため、根は地表面近くに分布するように進化した。

(4) 根が分布する層の下は岩盤となるため、根は地表面近くにしか分布できない。

問3

植物の根が密に分布していることで私達人間が得ている恩恵について適当と思われるものを以下の選択肢(1)-(4)からふたつ選び、選んだ選択肢の番号を解答欄にマークしなさい。解答欄は $\fbox{36}$

(1) 土壌有機物が土壌微生物の呼吸によって分解されるのを抑制し、大気中二酸化炭素濃度の上昇を防ぐ。

(2) 無機窒素などを効率的に吸収するため、河川や湖沼の富栄養化が抑えられる。

(3) 根の分布する層よりも深い場所で起きる地滑りを止めることができる。

(4) 保水力のある細かい土壌粒子が浸食で失われることを防いでいるため、降水が河川に一気に流出するのを抑えられる。

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}N_1}{\mathrm{d}t} = r_1N_1\left(1-\frac{N_1+a_2N_2}{K_1}\right) \qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}N_2}{\mathrm{d}t} = r_2N_2\left(1-\frac{N_2+a_1N_1}{K_2}\right)$$

$$N_1 = K_{(\text{あ})} - a_{(\text{い})}N_2 \qquad N_2 = K_{(\text{う})} - a_{(\text{え})}N_1$$

(2) (あ) 1 (い) 2 (う) 2 (え) 1

(3) (あ) 2 (い) 1 (う) 1 (え) 2

(4) (あ) 2 (い) 2 (う) 1 (え) 1

Question 3

Of Figure 12-1 (1)–(4), choose the one showing coefficient conditions under which species 1 and species 2 can coexist regardless of the initial values of their population sizes, and mark the number of the chosen option in the answer box. Answer box: $\fbox{39}$

Question 4

With reference to this mathematical model, choose all the correct sentences describing two species that are in a competitive relationship over resources, and mark the numbers of all the chosen options in the answer box. 図12-1(1)-(4)のうち、種1と種2がそれらの個体数の初期値に関わらず、共存できる係数条件を示しているものを選び、選んだ選択肢の番号を解答欄にマークしなさい。解答欄は $\fbox{39}$

問4

今回の数理モデルを参考にして，資源を巡って競争関係にある2種について記述した文章として正しいものをすべて選び、選んだ選択肢の番号をすべて解答欄にマークしなさい。なお、すべての記述が正しいと判断した場合は(9)だけをマークし、正しい記述が無いと判断した場合は(0)だけをマークしなさい。解答欄は $\fbox{40}$

(1) 今回想定した環境下で競争関係にある2種が共存する係数条件は$a_1a_2 < 1$である

(2) 競争の優劣は生息環境の影響を受けない

(3) 自然環境下では競争で劣位となる種が存続することはできない

(4) 2種の地理的分布が隣接するとき，資源競争がその側所的分布の原因とは限らない

Problem 1 (問題1)

Specimens, reagents and apparatus (checked before the start of the examination):

Specimens

• Petri dish containing fixed and decolourised plant specimens (Petri dish 2)
  ➢ Handle it carefully so as not to spill the liquid inside.

  ➢ Handle it carefully so as not to spill the liquid inside.

Read the passage below and answer the questions.

Arabidopsis (シロイヌナズナ) is a dicotyledonous plant whose sporophyte has the nuclear phase 2n, and it reproduces by self-pollination. A seedling germinated from a seed with the wild-type genotype consists of three kinds of organs, two cotyledons, one hypocotyl and one radicle, and at the tips of the body there are the shoot apical meristem and the root apical meristem. Shoot organs such as leaves and stems are produced by division of the cells of the shoot apical meristem.

Petri dish 1 contains a mixture of two kinds of Arabidopsis seedlings: seedlings with a normal shape (hereafter, normal type) and seedlings with cup-shaped cotyledons (hereafter, cup type). In the normal type the two cotyledons have expanded, and the formation of foliage leaves has also begun. In the cup type, because of a mutation in a gene involved in morphogenesis, the two cotyledons are fused at their margins.

Question 1 (問1)

The part between the cotyledons of the normal type (hereafter, the shoot apex) will be observed under the microscope. For this, prepare a specimen by the following method. As long as there are some in the Petri dish, you may use as many normal-type seedlings as you need until a good specimen is obtained.

1. Peel the seal off Petri dish 1 and open the lid. The seal is not needed afterwards, so roll it up and put it somewhere out of the way.
2. Referring to Figure 1, make a specimen stand for observing the plants. Choose a place on Petri dish 1 where no plants are growing, and from there cut out two pieces of agar about 1 cm square, using the tips of the forceps. It does not matter if their shape is somewhat spoiled. Place them on a glass slide, keeping the surface of the agar pieces facing upwards. Hereafter this is called glass slide 1. Pierce the centre of each agar piece vertically with the tips of the closed forceps to make a small hole about 2–3 mm deep.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2024-3-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 寒天片 = agar piece; スライドグラス1 = glass slide 1; X: 穴を開ける位置 = X: position where the hole is made.

Figure 1

3. Observe Petri dish 1 with the magnifying glass, choose one normal-type individual that is average in both size and shape, and pick it up by gripping the junction of the hypocotyl and the root with forceps. The root part is not needed, so cut it off using the other forceps and return it to an empty place on Petri dish 1. Insert the plant, hypocotyl downwards, into the hole of one of the agar pieces on glass slide 1. Adjust its orientation so that the plant faces as straight upwards as possible.
4. Close the lid to prevent the plants on Petri dish 1 from drying out.
5. Set the objective lens of the microscope to the 4× position and place glass slide 1 on the microscope stage. After adjusting the position of the stage so that the specimen is directly below the objective lens, look into the microscope and focus on the specimen. Then move the stage to bring the centre of the shoot apex to the middle of the field of view.

After carrying out the above operations, sketch the specimen with the 4× objective lens. The sketch need only show the outlines of all the organs visible in the field of view. Many branched trichomes (トゲ) are observed on the surface of the foliage leaves; add only one trichome per foliage leaf to the sketch and omit the other trichomes.

Problem 1 (問題1), continued

Question 2 (問2)

Next, prepare a specimen of the cup type by the following operations and observe it under the microscope.

1. Return glass slide 1 to the bench.
2. Observe Plate 1 with the magnifying glass and choose a cup-type individual of average size whose mouth is wide open. If you cannot find an individual with an open mouth, gently pinch the sides of the cotyledons of an individual with a closed mouth with the forceps to widen the mouth. Pick up the chosen individual by gripping the junction of the root and the hypocotyl with forceps, and remove the root with the other forceps.
3. Insert it, hypocotyl downwards, into the hole of the other agar piece on glass slide 1.
4. Set the objective lens of the microscope to the 4× position and place glass slide 1 on the microscope stage. After adjusting the position of the stage so that the specimen is directly below the objective lens, look into the microscope and focus on the uppermost part of the specimen. Then move the stage to bring the centre of the cup to the middle of the field of view.
5. Take your eyes away from the eyepiece of the microscope for a moment and, while checking the specimen with the naked eye, switch the objective lens to 10×. Look into the microscope again and focus on the part corresponding to the "bottom" of the cup.

After carrying out the above operations, sketch the specimen with the 10× objective lens. In doing so, make the shapes of the individual cells at the "bottom" of the cup clearly recognisable. About 10 cells should be sketched; the remaining cells may be omitted.

Problem 1 (問題1), continued

Question 3 (問3)

The seeds sown in Petri dish 1 are part of a seed stock obtained by self-pollination of one Arabidopsis individual (hereafter, stock S). In parts (ア) and (イ) below, the genotype of the parent individual of stock S is estimated.

(ア) Figure 2 is a photograph of seedlings germinated from seeds chosen at random from the same stock S; by image processing, only the green parts of the plants have been extracted. For every individual in this figure, determine whether it is normal type or cup type, and find the number of individuals of each. Also find the proportion of cup-type individuals in the total number of individuals as a percentage (%). Round the percentage to the second decimal place and write it to one decimal place.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2024-3-3-fig1.png

Figure 2

(イ) The cup-type phenotype involves loss-of-function mutations at two loci located on different chromosomes. If the wild-type alleles are written A and B, and the loss-of-function alleles a and b, respectively, it is known that only individuals with the genotype aabb show the cup-type shape and that all others show normal morphology. One normal individual was chosen from the seedlings germinated from stock S and grown, and when 100 seeds of the next generation obtained by self-pollination were sown, all the seedlings were normal type. Next, one individual was chosen from these 100 individuals and crossed with another individual already known to have the genotype AAbb, and F1 seeds were obtained. When this F1 was sown and grown, and the F2 seeds obtained by self-pollination were sown, cup-type seedlings appeared. From these results, estimate the genotype of the parent plant of stock S and answer with a combination of four letters. Also calculate the expected number of cup-type individuals when 250 F2 seeds are germinated. Round the value to the second decimal place and give it to one decimal place.

Problem 1 (問題1), continued

Question 4 (問4)

To investigate the functions of genes A and B in detail, the expression of gene C, which is expressed specifically in the shoot apical meristem, will be compared between wild-type individuals and cup-type individuals. Figure 3 is a schematic diagram of the structure of gene C and of the structure of the recombinant gene C′ made to investigate the expression of C.

Also, x and y are each the same DNA sequence. Both schematic diagrams are aligned so that transcription proceeds from left to right, and they are drawn to the same scale as the 500 base-pair line at the lower right. Enzyme D catalyses a chemical reaction that converts a colourless substrate X into a blue pigment X′. Of the following options ①–⑤ concerning C and C′, choose all that are appropriate.

① The sequence to which RNA polymerase first binds during transcription lies slightly to the right of x.
② In the mRNA precursor transcribed from C, there are more exons than introns.
③ Transcription of C begins at the left end of the leftmost coding sequence and terminates at the right end of the rightmost coding sequence.
④ The polypeptide chain translated from C is shorter than the polypeptide chain translated from C′.
⑤ Because codons differ in part between E. coli, a prokaryote, and plants, which are eukaryotes, enzyme D made when C′ is introduced into Arabidopsis differs in part in its amino acid sequence from enzyme D made by E. coli.

Question 5 (問5)

When wild-type Arabidopsis transformed with the recombinant gene C′ was left to react for 12 hours while immersed in a solution containing substrate X, only the cells of the shoot apical meristem were stained blue. In a separate experiment, the sites where C and C′ are transcribed were examined, and they coincided with the sites where staining occurs in the C′ transformants. From options ①–⑤ below, choose all that are appropriate as inferences from these experimental results. Assume that substrate X permeates uniformly into every cell of Arabidopsis, and that the mRNA produced from C′ is translated with the same efficiency in every cell of Arabidopsis. Also assume that C′ has been inserted at a site in the Arabidopsis genome where no gene is present, and that it does not affect the function of any gene, including A, B and C.

① The enhancer needed for the gene to be transcribed specifically in the shoot apical meristem is not contained in region y.
② The enhancer needed for the gene to be transcribed specifically in the shoot apical meristem is contained in both regions x and y.
③ X′ produced from X stays inside the cells, and its diffusion to the surrounding cells can be neglected.
④ Because D is an enzyme of E. coli, it has no activity inside Arabidopsis cells.
⑤ Wild-type Arabidopsis cells contain no enzyme with the same activity as D.

Problem 1 (問題1), continued

Question 6 (問6)

Petri dish 2 contains plant specimens of wild-type individuals into which the recombinant gene C′ has been introduced (genotype AABB) and of cup-type individuals into which C′ has likewise been introduced (genotype aabb), each of which was left to react for 12 hours in a solution containing substrate X. To make the stained sites easier to observe, the chlorophyll has been removed from the specimens after the end of the reaction. Place these plants on glass slides by the following procedure to prepare specimens for microscopic observation.

1. Put on gloves to prevent the clearing solution from getting on your hands.
2. Place one new glass slide in an empty space on the bench. Hereafter this is called glass slide 2. Choose two wild-type seedlings from Petri dish 2, arrange both in the centre of glass slide 2 with forceps, and adjust their orientation. Arrange them so that they will not stick out when a cover glass is placed on them in a later operation. Also take care not to touch the shoot apex, which is to be observed, directly. Remove excess liquid with the corner of a paper wipe.
3. Using the dropper used in the preliminary trial (the one marked with oil-based marker), drop clearing solution onto the specimens. Draw up clearing solution to the 50 µL position (Figure 4, arrow) and put it on the centre of glass slide 2.
