4. Place a cover glass. In doing so, take great care that the cover glass and the clearing solution do not stick out from glass slide 2.
5. Next, place another glass slide in an empty space on the bench. Hereafter this is called glass slide 3. Choose two cup-type seedlings from Petri dish 2 and carry out operations 1–4.
6. For the two observation slides prepared, check that no liquid is attached to the bottom or the sides. If any is attached, wipe it off carefully with a paper wipe.
7. Remove the gloves.

Observe the prepared specimens with the microscope and answer parts (ア)–(ウ) below.

(ア) For each of the normal type and the cup type, state whether or not there is staining. If there is staining, explain where that site is in terms of its position relative to the other organs.
(イ) From the above results and the observations in Question 1-1 and Question 1-2 (問1-1, 問1-2), state what abnormality you can conclude has arisen in the shoot apical meristem of the cup-type individuals.
(ウ) Consider what interrelationships there are between genes A, B and C, and state them concisely.

Problem 2 (問題2)

[Introduction]

In ectothermic vertebrates such as fish and reptiles, body colour changes according to the surrounding environment, the state of tension of the individual, and so on. This is due to the action of cells containing pigment (chromatophores) present in the body surface. Chromatophores are broadly classified by the colour of their pigment. For example, the scales of the medaka (メダカ) contain melanophores, which have melanin granules and appear black; xanthophores, which have carotenoid granules and appear yellow; and leucophores, which have guanine granules and appear white by reflecting light. These chromatophores are thought to be formed by differentiation from the same cells that give rise to chromatophores (stem cells).

When a scale is removed from a medaka, immersed in a physiological salt solution and observed with a microscope using transmitted illumination, melanophores with their pigment granules in a dispersed state and xanthophores around them can be seen. Although they cannot be observed directly, the nerve terminals of chromatophore nerves are densely distributed around the chromatophores. Also, with changes in environmental conditions, melanophores and xanthophores change to a state in which the pigment granules are gathered at the centre of the chromatophore. This response is an aggregation response of the pigment granules, and it is known that the outline of the chromatophore does not change. On the other hand, when medaka scales are observed using epi-illumination, leucophores with their pigment granules gathered at the centre of the chromatophore can be seen. Also, with changes in environmental conditions, leucophores change to a state in which the pigment granules are dispersed.

Notes on the experiment (実験上の注意)
* Mixing of the experimental solutions may prevent correct results from being obtained, so use the three unmarked droppers separately as appropriate.
* Normally, transmitted illumination is used to observe melanophores and xanthophores, and epi-illumination is used to observe leucophores. However, depending on the room lighting, it may be possible to observe melanophores, xanthophores and leucophores without particularly distinguishing between these illumination methods. Carry out the experiment with whichever illumination method makes observation easier in the circumstances.

Question 1 (問1)

For scale A and scale B taken from wild-type medaka, observe the melanophores and leucophores under transmitted illumination and under epi-illumination, and sketch them. Indicate melanophores with arrowheads and leucophores with arrows, and sketch about five of each kind of chromatophore seen in the same field of view in the microscopic observation. For the method of observing the scales, read [Experimental method 1-1] shown below carefully and carry it out.

[Experimental method 1-1] (【実験方法 1-1】)
① Transfer one scale in the 4-well Petri dish, together with its water, to a 2-well hollow slide using a dropper (or transfer it to the 2-well hollow slide with forceps), place that hollow slide on the stage of the upright microscope, and observe the scale under transmitted illumination; melanophores and xanthophores can be observed.
② Switch off the transmitted illumination and observe the scale by epi-illumination using the LED light; leucophores can be observed. Note that most leucophores lie one above the other with melanophores, so when the scale is observed from the melanophore side, the leucophores may not be observable. When the leucophores cannot be observed, turn the scale over and check the leucophores.
③ Write the necessary items in the designated spaces on the answer sheet.

Problem 2 (問題2), continued

Question 2 (問2)

To clarify the actions of the autonomic nervous system on melanophores and leucophores, the actions of noradrenaline and acetylcholine, neurotransmitters of the autonomic nervous system, will be examined. Read [Experimental method 1-2] shown below carefully and carry out the experiment, and write down the changes in the melanophores and leucophores of scale A and scale B 5 minutes after administering noradrenaline and acetylcholine. Furthermore, consider whether the autonomic nervous system that regulates the granule movement of the melanophores and of the leucophores is the sympathetic or the parasympathetic nervous system, for each, and write it down.

[Experimental method 1-2] (【実験方法 1-2】)
① Dilute the prepared neurotransmitters, the noradrenaline solution and the acetylcholine solution, 10-fold with physiological saline (0.5 ml → 5 ml). For the dilution, use a dropper and a 15 ml tube.
② Put the diluted noradrenaline solution into one well of the 4-well Petri dish, and the diluted acetylcholine solution into the neighbouring well. Fill each well with diluted solution to about 1/3 of its depth.
③ With forceps, transfer one scale each into the diluted noradrenaline solution and the diluted acetylcholine solution in the 4-well Petri dish. After leaving them to stand for 5 minutes or more, transfer each scale together with the liquid to a 2-well hollow slide using a dropper, and judge the aggregated or dispersed state of the chromatophores with the upright microscope.
④ Write the necessary items in the designated spaces on the answer sheet.

Problem 2 (問題2), continued

Question 3 (問3)

The mental state of vertebrates is controlled mainly by the balance of the autonomic nervous system. Judging from the granule movements of the melanophores and leucophores of scale A and scale B, what balance of the autonomic nervous system and what body colour is the wild-type medaka from which scale B was taken inferred to have? Based on the experimental results, answer with a number from the options below. Also, if this medaka were placed in a dark place, what balance of the autonomic nervous system and what body colour would it be inferred to have? Answer with a number from the options below.

① The parasympathetic nerves work dominantly over the sympathetic nerves, and the body colour becomes black.
② The parasympathetic nerves work dominantly over the sympathetic nerves, and the body colour becomes white.
③ The sympathetic nerves work dominantly over the parasympathetic nerves, and the body colour becomes black.
④ The sympathetic nerves work dominantly over the parasympathetic nerves, and the body colour becomes white.

Problem 2 (問題2), continued

Question 4 (問4)

Medaka have an XX–XY type of sex determination: sex is determined by a sex-determining gene located on the Y chromosome, and XX individuals differentiate into females and XY individuals into males. Apart from the sex-determining gene on the Y chromosome, the same genes are present on both the X chromosome and the Y chromosome. Meanwhile, many strains of medaka exist; strain W is a strain that has a recessive loss-of-function mutation in gene w, a gene related to chromatophores located on the sex chromosomes, and this mutation has been confirmed on either one of the X chromosome and the Y chromosome, or on both.

First, observe the chromatophores of scale C from an XX individual and scale D from an XY individual of strain W according to [Experimental method 1-1]; next, read [Experimental method 1-2] shown below and carry out the experiment, and write down the differences between the chromatophores of scale C and scale D.

Next, choose from the options below on which chromosome the mutation lies in this strain.

① X chromosome
② Y chromosome
③ Both the X chromosome and the Y chromosome

Also, consider what kind of role gene w is inferred to play with respect to chromatophores.

[Experimental method 1-1] (【実験方法 1-1】)
① Transfer one scale in the 4-well Petri dish, together with its water, to a 2-well hollow slide using a dropper (or transfer it to the 2-well hollow slide with forceps), place that hollow slide on the stage of the upright microscope, and observe the scale under transmitted illumination; melanophores and xanthophores can be observed.
② Switch off the transmitted illumination and observe the scale by epi-illumination using the LED light; leucophores can be observed. Note that most leucophores lie one above the other with melanophores, so when the scale is observed from the melanophore side, the leucophores may not be observable. When the leucophores cannot be observed, turn the scale over and check the leucophores.
③ Write the necessary items in the designated spaces on the answer sheet.

[Experimental method 1-2] (【実験方法 1-2】)
① Dilute the prepared neurotransmitters, the noradrenaline solution and the acetylcholine solution, 10-fold with physiological saline (0.5 ml → 5 ml). For the dilution, use a dropper and a 15 ml tube.
② Put the diluted noradrenaline solution into one well of the 4-well Petri dish, and the diluted acetylcholine solution into the neighbouring well. Fill each well with diluted solution to about 1/3 of its depth.
③ With forceps, transfer one scale each into the diluted noradrenaline solution and the diluted acetylcholine solution in the 4-well Petri dish. After leaving them to stand for 5 minutes or more, transfer each scale together with the liquid to a 2-well hollow slide using a dropper, and judge the aggregated or dispersed state of the chromatophores with the upright microscope.

problems.problem:
Succinate dehydrogenase is an enzyme involved in the citric acid cycle; it catalyses the dehydrogenation of succinate to fumarate. In this reaction the coenzyme FAD acts as the hydrogen acceptor. This enzyme is also known to be competitively inhibited by malonate, whose chemical structure is similar to that of succinate.

Fresh chicken liver was ground in a mortar and strained through gauze, and the filtrate was suspended in a buffer; this was used as the succinate dehydrogenase solution. In addition, part of this enzyme solution was heated in a water bath at 90 °C for 10 minutes; this was used as the heat-treated enzyme solution. Four Thunberg tubes 1, 2, 3 and 4 were prepared, and reaction solutions of the compositions below were added to the main chamber and the side chamber of each (table below). Methylene blue is a redox indicator: its oxidised form is blue, but its reduced form is colourless. In this experiment, oxidised (blue) methylene blue was added to the reaction solution.

We take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide by respiration. This is because nutrients are metabolised in the body. The volume ratio of the amount of carbon dioxide released to the amount of oxygen taken into the body (volume of carbon dioxide released ÷ volume of oxygen taken up) is called the respiratory quotient. From this value we can get a rough idea of what kinds of nutrients are being consumed in the body. For example, when only glucose is being metabolised, the reaction equation is as follows.

$$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O}$$

Since the volume of a gas at constant temperature and pressure is nearly proportional to the number of moles, the respiratory quotient of glucose is 6/6 = 1.

The following statements concern the respiratory quotients of various nutrients. Which of them are appropriate? Choose the combination of appropriate statements from A–J. Assume that the nutrients are completely metabolised and excreted. (6 points)

① The respiratory quotient of disaccharides is 1, as for monosaccharides.

② The respiratory quotient of cholesterol ($\mathrm{C_{27}H_{46}O}$) is approximately 0.6.

③ Saturated fatty acids have a smaller respiratory quotient than unsaturated fatty acids.

④ The respiratory quotient of ethanol ($\mathrm{C_2H_6O}$) is higher than 1.

⑤ To determine the respiratory quotient of proteins, the volume of the nitrogen they contain must also be measured, because it is excreted as nitrogen dioxide.

B. ①③

C. ①④

D. ①⑤

E. ②③

G. ②⑤

私達は呼吸によって酸素を吸収し，二酸化炭素を排出している。これは体内で栄養素が代謝されるためである。体内に吸収される酸素量に対する排出される二酸化炭素量の体積比（排出される二酸化炭素の体積÷吸収される酸素の体積）は呼吸商とよばれている。この値によって，体内でどのような栄養素が消費されているかの概要を知ることができる。たとえばグルコース（ブドウ糖）だけを代謝している場合，反応式は以下のようになる。

$$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O}$$

気体の定温定圧下での体積はモル数にほぼ比例することから，グルコースの呼吸商は6/6＝1となる。

次の記述はさまざまな栄養素の呼吸商について述べたものである。このうち，適切なものはどれか。適切な記述の組合せをA～Jから選べ。ただし栄養素は完全に代謝され排出されるものとする。（6点）

The subject consciously breathed in several different patterns and rhythms, from shallow breathing to deep breathing, and the ventilation due to breathing and the amount of carbon dioxide in the expired air were measured. This measurement shows the characteristics of the ventilation system, centred on the lungs.

Measurement 2. The subject breathed air to which carbon dioxide had been artificially added in the inspired air (the label x % CO₂ in the figure is the concentration of carbon dioxide added to the inspired air), and the ventilation and the amount of carbon dioxide in the expired air were measured. In this case the depth and rate of breathing were not changed consciously; the subject breathed naturally and unconsciously. This measurement shows the response of the system controlling the amount of breathing to the amount of carbon dioxide in the blood.

The figure summarises the results of the measurements in one graph: measurements at rest are shown in blue and the results of measurements during exercise in red; the results of measurement 1 are shown by open symbols and solid lines, and the results of measurement 2 by filled symbols and dotted lines. Note that in measurement 1 the amount of carbon dioxide in the expired air was measured while the amount of breathing (and therefore the ventilation) was varied, but, in order to display it together with the results of measurement 2, ventilation is plotted on the vertical axis.

problems.problem:
Much research has been done on the mechanisms that control body size in holometabolous insects. The larvae feed and increase their body weight, stop feeding partway through the final larval instar, and then pupate. Because body weight basically does not increase during the pupal stage, how the cessation of feeding of the final instar larva is controlled is important as the mechanism that determines adult body weight.

In the final instar larvae of a certain insect, the growth rate (taken as the increase in body weight per unit time) differs according to the concentration of nutrients in the food. Eating concentrated food gives a high growth rate, and the more dilute the food, the lower the growth rate. In this insect, hormone X has the function of inhibiting the cessation of feeding, and production of X stops when the body weight of the final instar larva reaches a certain value Y. From that point, X in the body fluid is metabolised at a constant rate, and when it has disappeared after a certain time (T), cessation of feeding occurs immediately (Figure 1). If the endocrine gland that produces X is removed before the body weight of the final instar larva reaches Y, cessation of feeding occurs when the same fixed time T as above has elapsed after the removal, regardless of the concentration of the food or the body weight at the time of removal (Figure 2).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-1-7-fig1.png

Figure 1. Relationship between larval growth, cessation of feeding and the concentration of hormone X

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-1-7-fig2.png

Figure 2. Experiment in which the endocrine gland that produces X is removed

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 体重 = body weight; 摂食停止 = cessation of feeding; 体液中のXの濃度 = concentration of X in the body fluid; 終齢幼虫になってからの時間 = time since becoming a final instar larva; 切除 = removal; 濃い餌 = concentrated food; 薄い餌 = dilute food.

For this insect, an experiment was carried out in which final instar larvae were reared under various nutritional conditions and the relationship between the timing of the cessation of feeding and the body weight at that time was examined. Many individuals, reared under the same nutritional conditions until they became final instar larvae, were divided into 4 groups immediately after becoming final instar larvae, and from then until the cessation of feeding they were given food of different concentrations. In decreasing order of the concentration of the food given, the 4 groups were named richest nutrition, moderately rich nutrition, moderately poor nutrition and poorest nutrition. For every individual, the time t from becoming a final instar larva until the cessation of feeding and the body weight m at the cessation of feeding were measured. Which graph is the most appropriate plot of the mean values of t and m calculated for each group? Choose from A–H in Figure 3. (5 points)

ある昆虫の終齢幼虫では，餌に含まれる栄養分の濃度によって成長率（単位時間あたりの体重の増分とする）が異なる。濃い餌を食べると成長率は大きく，薄い餌ほど成長率は小さくなる。この昆虫ではホルモンXは摂食停止を抑制するはたらきをもっており，終齢幼虫の体重が一定の値YになるとXの産生が止まる。その時点から体液中のXが一定のスピードで代謝され，一定時間（T）後に消失すると，ただちに摂食停止が起こる（図1）。終齢幼虫の体重がYに達する前に，Xを産生する内分泌腺を切除すると，餌の濃度や切除時の体重によらず，切除してから上記と同じ一定時間Tが経過した時点で摂食停止が起こる（図2）。

problems.problem:
Natural selection increases the frequency of alleles with higher fitness. Suppose that, at a locus where only allele $A_1$ is present, an allele $A_2$ with higher fitness arises by mutation. Then, depending on whether $A_2$ is dominant, recessive or semi-dominant to $A_1$, the relative fitnesses of the homozygotes and the heterozygote differ as in the following table. Here s is a value called the selection coefficient; in general it indicates by how much the relative fitness of the other genotypes is lower than that of the genotype with the highest fitness. Semi-dominance (半顕性, also called 半優性) is the state in which neither allele is dominant or recessive and the effects of the two alleles are equal.

$$\begin{array}{l|ccc} & \text{Relative fitness} & & \\ A_2 \text{ relative to } A_1 & A_1 \text{ homozygote} & \text{Heterozygote} & A_2 \text{ homozygote} \\ \hline \text{Dominant} & 1 - s & 1 & 1 \\ \text{Semi-dominant} & 1 - s & 1 - s/2 & 1 \\ \text{Recessive} & 1 - s & 1 - s & 1 \end{array}$$

In a large population, in which chance fluctuations of gene frequencies are small, the rate at which allele $A_2$ replaces allele $A_1$ differs according to whether $A_2$ is dominant, recessive or semi-dominant to $A_1$. The rate also differs according to whether or not random mating takes place in the population.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-1-16-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 図1, 図2, 図3, 図4 = Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 4.

The figures above show the change in allele frequency for random mating, as in some plants that show self-incompatibility, namely for the three cases

(X) $A_2$ is dominant to $A_1$ under random mating

(Y) $A_2$ is semi-dominant to $A_1$ under random mating

(Z) $A_2$ is recessive to $A_1$ under random mating

and for the case

(W) in which 10% of pollinations are by the plant's own pollen and 90% by pollen from other individuals (selfing rate 10%), that is, a plant that does not show self-incompatibility and undergoes partial selfing, in which $A_2$ is recessive to $A_1$

(vertical axis: frequency of allele $A_2$; horizontal axis: number of generations). Here the selection coefficient s is 0.1 in every case, and the initial frequency of allele $A_2$ is 0.04.

自然選択は適応度の高い対立遺伝子（アレル）の頻度を高める。対立遺伝子$A_1$のみが存在している遺伝子座に，より適応度の高い対立遺伝子$A_2$が突然変異で生じたとする。このとき，$A_2$が$A_1$に対し顕性（優性），潜性（劣性），あるいは半顕性（半優性）かにより，ホモ接合体やヘテロ接合体の相対適応度は次の表のように異なる。ここでsは選択係数とよばれる値で，一般にもっとも高い適応度の遺伝子型に対して他の遺伝子型の相対的な適応度がどの程度が低くなるかを示した値である。また半顕性は半優性ともよばれ，顕性でも潜性でもなく２つの対立遺伝子の効果が同等な状態のことである。

$$\begin{array}{l|ccc} & \text{相対適応度} & & \\ A_2 \text{が} A_1 \text{に対して} & A_1 \text{のホモ接合体} & \text{ヘテロ接合体} & A_2 \text{のホモ接合体} \\ \hline \text{顕性（優性）} & 1 - s & 1 & 1 \\ \text{半顕性（半優性）} & 1 - s & 1 - s/2 & 1 \\ \text{潜性（劣性）} & 1 - s & 1 - s & 1 \end{array}$$

偶然による遺伝子頻度の変動が少ない個体数の多い集団においては，対立遺伝子$A_2$が対立遺伝子$A_1$に置き換わる速度は$A_2$が$A_1$に対し顕性（優性），潜性（劣性），あるいは半顕性（半優性）かということによって異なる。また，集団内で任意交配が行われるか否かによっても速度は異なる。

(9 points)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-2-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): ノイラミニダーゼ (NA) = neuraminidase (NA); ヘマグルチニン (HA) = haemagglutinin (HA); エンベロープ = envelope; ゲノムRNA = genomic RNA.

Figure 1. Structure of the influenza virus. © 2016 DBCLS TogoTV / CC-BY-4.0

In Japan, seasonal influenza spreads every winter. The main symptoms of influenza are fever of 38 °C or higher, joint and muscle pain, general fatigue, headache, runny or blocked nose, sneezing, cough and sore throat; when there are symptoms such as a high fever suggesting influenza, (ア) rapid tests are carried out, for example at fever outpatient clinics.

The causative virus, the influenza virus, is mainly classified into types A, B and C, of which types A and B cause major epidemics. As shown in Figure 1, these types are covered by an envelope made of a lipid bilayer, and on its surface they have the proteins haemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA). HA binds to a sugar called sialic acid on the surface of the host cell and enables the virus to enter the cell, while NA has the function of cutting off sialic acid when the virus leaves an infected cell. (イ) According to differences in HA and NA, type A viruses are further divided into several subtypes.

The main treatment for influenza is to take anti-influenza virus drugs; taken within 48 hours of the onset of symptoms, they are effective in improving the symptoms and preventing the disease from becoming severe. The main drugs include (ウ) oseltamivir, taken orally, and zanamivir, taken by inhalation; these inhibit NA, thereby blocking the release of the virus from cells and suppressing the multiplication of the virus (its spread in the body).

Question 1

With regard to the underlined part (ア), a "rapid diagnostic kit" such as that in Figure 2 is used to diagnose influenza virus infection. Just by dropping a nasal swab fluid or similar sample from the person tested onto the sample well and letting it react for 3–5 minutes, the proteins of type A and type B viruses can each be detected, so that the type can be determined with a single kit. However, if the test is carried out within 12 hours of the onset of symptoms, a false negative may result. As the principle of detection of the rapid diagnostic kit and the reason why false negatives occur, choose only the one most appropriate combination from options (1)–(9) and mark the corresponding number in the answer box. Answer box: 1

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-2-1-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 判定部 = result window; 滴下部 = sample well; 3滴 = 3 drops.

Figure 2. Rapid diagnostic kit for diagnosing influenza virus infection

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Option} & \text{Principle of detection of the kit} & \text{Reason why a false negative is likely when tested within 12 hours of onset} \\ \hline (1) & \text{PCR}^{*1} & \text{Because it is a period when the virus mutates actively} \\ (2) & \text{PCR} & \text{Because the amount of virus may not be sufficient less than 12 hours after onset} \\ (3) & \text{PCR} & \text{Because the body temperature is below 37 °C and the symptoms are stable} \\ (4) & \text{Antigen–antibody reaction} & \text{Because it is a period when the virus mutates actively} \\ (5) & \text{Antigen–antibody reaction} & \text{Because the amount of virus may not be sufficient less than 12 hours after onset} \\ (6) & \text{Antigen–antibody reaction} & \text{Because the body temperature is below 37 °C and the symptoms are stable} \\ (7) & \text{Electrophoresis} & \text{Because it is a period when the virus mutates actively} \\ (8) & \text{Electrophoresis} & \text{Because the amount of virus may not be sufficient less than 12 hours after onset} \\ (9) & \text{Electrophoresis} & \text{Because the body temperature is below 37 °C and the symptoms are stable} \end{array}$$

*1 PCR: polymerase chain reaction

Question 2

With regard to the underlined part (イ), type A influenza viruses are classified according to the kinds of HA and NA, taking their initial letters and numbers, as in "H1N1". In 2013, two new kinds each of HA and NA were identified from bats, so that the number of subtypes of type A viruses became theoretically 198. As the numbers of kinds of HA and NA assumed before this 2013 report, choose only the one most appropriate combination from options (1)–(8) and mark the corresponding number in the answer box. Answer box: 2

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} & (1) & (2) & (3) & (4) & (5) & (6) & (7) & (8) \\ \hline \text{HA} & 18 & 19 & 16 & 18 & 16 & 18 & 11 & 12 \\ \text{NA} & 11 & 11 & 12 & 12 & 9 & 9 & 18 & 18 \end{array}$$

Question 3

With regard to the underlined part (ウ), NA is in general an enzyme that cleaves sialic acids from glycoproteins, and oseltamivir is a compound that inhibits its enzyme activity.

For an enzyme, with reaction rate $v$ and substrate concentration [S], the basic equation of enzyme kinetics is expressed as

$$v = \frac{V_{\mathrm{max}}[\mathrm{S}]}{K_{\mathrm{m}} + [\mathrm{S}]} \quad \cdots \quad \text{(エ)}$$

$V_{\mathrm{max}}$ in the equation is the maximum reaction rate. $K_{\mathrm{m}}$ is called the Michaelis constant and corresponds to the substrate concentration at which the rate is $\frac{1}{2}V_{\mathrm{max}}$.

When the relationship between the reaction rate of an enzyme and the substrate concentration is determined experimentally by measuring the enzyme activity at various substrate concentrations, and the results are plotted with the substrate concentration on the horizontal axis and the enzyme activity on the vertical axis, the plot takes the shape of curve (オ) in Figure 3. When an inhibitor such as oseltamivir is added to such an experimental system, the plot changes from curve (オ) to curve (カ).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-2-1-fig3.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 反応初速度 $v$ = initial reaction rate $v$; 基質濃度 [S] = substrate concentration [S]; 曲線 (オ) = curve (オ); 曲線 (カ) = curve (カ).

Figure 3. Relationship between substrate concentration and reaction rate. Modified from the Wikimedia Commons file "Michaelis-Menten saturation curve of an enzyme reaction LARGE.svg".

Further, taking the reciprocals of both sides of equation (エ),

$$\frac{1}{v} = \frac{K_{\mathrm{m}}}{V_{\mathrm{max}}}\,\frac{1}{[\mathrm{S}]} + \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{max}}} \quad \cdots \quad \text{(キ)}$$

the plot of $\frac{1}{v}$ against $\frac{1}{[\mathrm{S}]}$ is a straight line (Figure 4, line (ク)); this is called a Lineweaver–Burk plot, or double-reciprocal plot.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-2-1-fig4.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 直線 (ク) = line (ク); 直線 (ケ) = line (ケ); 勾配 = slope.

Figure 4. Lineweaver–Burk plot. Line (ク) is the result in the absence of oseltamivir, and line (ケ) the result in the presence of oseltamivir.

From an interpretation based on enzyme kinetics, choose all the correct statements (1)–(4) about NA and oseltamivir, and mark the numbers of all the chosen options in the answer box. If you judge that all the statements are correct, mark (9); if you judge that there is no appropriate statement, mark only (0). Answer box: 3

(1) Oseltamivir binds to sialic acid and changes the initial reaction rate $v$ of NA.

(2) As the concentration of oseltamivir increases, the slope $\frac{K_{\mathrm{m}}}{V_{\mathrm{max}}}$ of the dotted line in the Lineweaver–Burk plot of Figure 4 becomes larger.

(3) When the concentration of oseltamivir is constant, until $\frac{1}{2}V_{\mathrm{max}}$ is reached the reaction rate does not change even if the substrate concentration is increased.

(4) The maximum rate $V_{\mathrm{max}}$ when the concentration [S] of substrate S is increased sufficiently is the same whether or not oseltamivir is present.

図1. インフルエンザウイルスの構造．©2016 DBCLS TogoTV / CC-BY-4.0

日本では冬になると季節性のインフルエンザが流行する。インフルエンザの主な症状は、38 ℃以上の発熱、関節痛・筋肉痛、全身の倦怠感、頭痛、鼻水・鼻づまり、くしゃみ、咳、喉の痛みなどであり、インフルエンザが疑われる高熱などの症状がある場合には発熱外来などで(ア)迅速検査が行われる。

原因ウイルスであるインフルエンザウイルスは、主にA、B、C型に分類され、そのうち大きな流行の原因となるのはA型とB型である。これらの型は、図1のように脂質二重層のエンベロープで覆われ、その表面にヘマグルチニン（HA）とノイラミニダーゼ（NA）というタンパク質をもつ。HAは宿主細胞の表面にあるシアル酸という糖に結合してウイルスが細胞内に侵入できるようにはたらき、一方のNAはウイルスが感染細胞から細胞外へ出る際に、シアル酸を切り離す機能を担っている。(イ)HAとNAの違いにより、A型ウイルスはさらに複数の亜型に分けられる。

インフルエンザの主な治療法は、抗インフルエンザウイルス薬を服用することであり、発症後48時間以内に服用すると、症状の改善や重症化を防ぐ効果がある。主な治療薬として、(ウ)内服薬のオセルタミビルや吸入薬のザナミビルがあり、これらはNAを阻害することにより細胞からのウイルス放出を阻害しウイルスの増殖（体内での拡散）を抑える作用をあらわす。

問1

下線部(ア)に関して、インフルエンザウイルス感染の診断のために図2のような「迅速診断キット」が用いられる。検体者の鼻腔ぬぐい液などを滴下部に滴下して3-5分反応させるだけで、A型とB型の各々のウイルスのタンパク質を検出してひとつのキットで型別判定が可能である。しかし、発症から12時間以内に検査した場合、偽陰性になることがある。迅速診断キットの検出の原理および偽陰性が出現する理由として、最も適切な組合せを選択肢(1)-(9)からひとつだけ選び、該当する番号を解答欄にマークしなさい。解答欄は 1

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-2-1-fig2.png

図2. インフルエンザウイルス感染の診断を行うための迅速診断キット

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{選択肢} & \text{キットの検出の原理} & \text{発症から12時間以内で検査した場合に偽陰性となりやすい理由} \\ \hline (1) & \text{PCR}^{*1} & \text{ウイルスの変異が盛んな時期だから} \\ (2) & \text{PCR} & \text{発症後12時間未満ではウイルス量が十分でないことがあるから} \\ (3) & \text{PCR} & \text{体温が37 ℃未満で症状が安定しているから} \\ (4) & \text{抗原抗体反応} & \text{ウイルスの変異が盛んな時期だから} \\ (5) & \text{抗原抗体反応} & \text{発症後12時間未満ではウイルス量が十分でないことがあるから} \\ (6) & \text{抗原抗体反応} & \text{体温が37 ℃未満で症状が安定しているから} \\ (7) & \text{電気泳動} & \text{ウイルスの変異が盛んな時期だから} \\ (8) & \text{電気泳動} & \text{発症後12時間未満ではウイルス量が十分でないことがあるから} \\ (9) & \text{電気泳動} & \text{体温が37 ℃未満で症状が安定しているから} \end{array}$$

*1 PCR: ポリメラーゼ連鎖反応

問2

下線部(イ)に関して、A型のインフルエンザウイルスはHAとNAの種類により、それぞれの頭文字と番号をとって「H1N1」というように分類される。2013年にコウモリから新たにHAとNAが2種類ずつ確認されたことにより、A型ウイルスの亜型は理論上198種類となった。2013年のこの報告よりも前に想定されていたHAとNAの種類として、最も適切な組合せを選択肢(1)-(8)からひとつだけ選び、該当する番号を解答欄にマークしなさい。解答欄は 2

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} & (1) & (2) & (3) & (4) & (5) & (6) & (7) & (8) \\ \hline \text{HA} & 18 & 19 & 16 & 18 & 16 & 18 & 11 & 12 \\ \text{NA} & 11 & 11 & 12 & 12 & 9 & 9 & 18 & 18 \end{array}$$

問3

下線部(ウ)に関して、NAは一般にシアル酸類を糖タンパク質から切断する酵素であり、オセルタミビルはその酵素活性を阻害する化合物である。

酵素は、その反応速度を$v$、基質濃度を[S]とした場合、酵素反応速度論の基本式として、

$$v = \frac{V_{\mathrm{max}}[\mathrm{S}]}{K_{\mathrm{m}} + [\mathrm{S}]} \quad \cdots \quad \text{(エ)}$$

で表される。式中の$V_{\mathrm{max}}$は最大反応速度を示す。$K_{\mathrm{m}}$はミカエリス定数とよばれ、$V_{\mathrm{max}}$の$\frac{1}{2}$となる基質濃度に相当する。

酵素の反応速度と基質濃度の関係は、実験的にさまざまな基質濃度で酵素活性を測定し、横軸に基質濃度、縦軸に酵素活性をとってプロットした場合、図3の曲線(オ)の形となる。また、このような実験系にオセルタミビルのような阻害剤を添加した場合、曲線(オ)から曲線(カ)のように変化する。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-2-1-fig3.png

図3. 基質濃度と反応速度の関係. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Michaelis-Menten_saturation_curve_of_an_enzyme_reaction_LARGE.svg を改変

また、式(エ)の両辺の逆数をとって、

$$\frac{1}{v} = \frac{K_{\mathrm{m}}}{V_{\mathrm{max}}}\,\frac{1}{[\mathrm{S}]} + \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{max}}} \quad \cdots \quad \text{(キ)}$$

としたとき、$\frac{1}{[\mathrm{S}]}$に対する$\frac{1}{v}$のプロットが直線となり（図4直線(ク)）、ラインウィーバー・バーク プロット、または二重逆数プロットとよばれる。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-2-1-fig4.png

図4. ラインウィーバー・バーク プロット．直線(ク)はオセルタミビル非存在下であり、直線(ケ)はオセルタミビル存在下の結果である．

酵素反応速度論的な解釈から、NAとオセルタミビルに関する記述(1)-(4)について、正しいものをすべて選び、選んだ選択肢の番号をすべて解答欄にマークしなさい。なお、すべての記述が正しいと判断した場合は(9)を、適切な記述が無いと判断した場合は(0)だけをマークしなさい。解答欄は 3

(1) オセルタミビルは、シアル酸と結合してNAの反応初速度$v$を変化させる。

(2) オセルタミビルの濃度が高くなると、図4のラインウィーバー・バーク プロットの点線の傾き$\frac{K_{\mathrm{m}}}{V_{\mathrm{max}}}$は大きくなる。

(3) オセルタミビルの濃度が一定の場合、$\frac{1}{2}V_{\mathrm{max}}$に到達するまでの間では、反応速度は基質濃度を高くしても変化しない。

(4) 基質Sの濃度[S]を十分に増加させたときの最大速度$V_{\mathrm{max}}$は、オセルタミビルの有無にかかわらず等しくなる。

problems.problem:
(8 points)

Land plants are a group of organisms that evolved from green algae in the broad sense, and their closest lineage is the charophyte algae. The common ancestor of land plants is thought to have moved onto land about 470 million years ago, and then, (ア) by acquiring morphological features adapted to the environment on land, they diversified into various groups as shown in the phylogenetic tree (Figure 7). Looking at life cycles, the charophyte algae have a life cycle in which the zygote formed by the fusion of gametes undergoes meiosis without undergoing mitotic division. Land plants, on the other hand, have a life cycle in which the fertilised egg undergoes mitotic divisions and (イ) the sporophyte and the gametophyte, both multicellular generations, alternate.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-2-4-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): シャジクモ藻類 = charophyte algae; ツノゴケ類 = hornworts; 蘚類 = mosses; 苔類 = liverworts; ヒカゲノカズラ植物 = lycophytes; シダ植物 = ferns; 裸子植物 = gymnosperms; 基部被子植物 = basal angiosperms; 単子葉植物 = monocots; 真正双子葉植物 = eudicots.

Figure 7. Phylogenetic relationships of the main groups of land plants. A phylogenetic tree simplified with reference to Figure 1 of Harris et al. (2020), taking the latest findings into account.

Question 1

Of the following statements (1)–(5) about the underlined part (ア), choose all the correct descriptions of shared derived characters of land plants, and mark the numbers of all the chosen options in the answer box. If you judge that all the options apply, mark only (9); if you judge that none applies, mark only (0). Answer box: 30

(1) They came to have vascular bundles that carry water, nutrients and so on through the plant body.

(2) They came to have roots that absorb water and inorganic salts from the soil.

(3) They came to have leaves that carry out photosynthesis.

(4) A cuticle layer that prevents excessive loss of water from the plant body came to cover the epidermis.

(5) They came to have stomata that exchange gases, water and so on between the plant and the outside air.

Question 2

With regard to the underlined part (イ), in the course of the diversification of land plants, an evolutionary change took place in which the generation that is central to the life of the plant was switched. Of ①–⑦ shown in the phylogenetic tree (Figure 7), choose the one correct place where this evolutionary change took place, and mark the chosen number in the answer box. Answer box: 31

Question 3

Choose all the correct statements (1)–(5) relating to the phylogenetic tree (Figure 7), and mark the numbers of all the chosen options in the answer box. If you judge that all the options apply, mark only (9); if you judge that none applies, mark only (0). Answer box: 32

(1) Plants that reproduce by spores are a paraphyletic group.

(2) Plants that are fertilised by flagellated sperm are a polyphyletic group.

(3) Microphylls are a shared derived character of lycophytes and ferns.

(4) Flowers and fruits are shared derived characters of plants that reproduce by seeds.

(5) Monocots evolved from plants with two cotyledons (dicots).

(8点)

陸上植物は、広義の緑藻から進化した生物群で、最も近い系統群はシャジクモ藻類である。陸上植物の共通祖先は、約4.7億年前に陸上へ進出したと考えられているが、(ア)陸上での環境に適応した形態的な特徴を獲得することで、その後、系統樹（図7）に示すように、さまざまな群に多様化した。生活環をみると、シャジクモ藻類では配偶子が融合した接合子は、体細胞分裂は行わずに減数分裂を行う生活環を持っている。一方、陸上植物では、受精卵が体細胞分裂を行い、(イ)多細胞性の世代である胞子体と配偶体が交互に現れる生活環を持っている。

(3) 光合成を行う葉をもつようになった。

(1) 胞子で繁殖する植物は、側系統群である。

(3) 小葉は、ヒカゲノカズラ植物とシダ植物の共有派生形質である。

(10点)

ほとんどの植物は光合成を行うことで成長する。光合成電子伝達の基本的な仕組みはどの植物でも同じであり、最終的にカルビン回路で$\mathrm{CO_2}$を固定する点も共通するが、カルビン回路に$\mathrm{CO_2}$を供給する経路には複数の様式が知られており、多くの乾生植物が行うベンケイソウ型有機酸代謝(Crassulacean Acid Metabolism: CAM)は、そのひとつである。

問1

プラストキノンは光合成電子伝達系で働く電子運搬体である。植物の葉緑体には、ひとつの光化学系IIあたり10～20個のプラストキノン分子が存在し，それらの総体をプラストキノンプールとよぶ。光照射により光合成電子伝達を駆動した際に、プラストキノンプールが通常よりも強く酸化した状態を引き起こすと考えられる処理や条件を、以下の選択肢(1)-(8)からすべて選び、選んだ選択肢の番号をすべて解答欄にマークしなさい。すべての記述が正しいと判断した場合は(9)を、適切な記述が無いと判断した場合は(0)だけをマークしなさい。解答欄は 46

(1) 薬剤により、光化学系I内部における電子伝達を阻害する。

(2) 薬剤により、光化学系IIの酸素発生複合体を破壊する。

(3) 薬剤により、シトクローム$b_6f$複合体の働きを阻害する。

(6 points)

All cells have biological membranes. Biological membranes are composed of membrane proteins and membrane lipids, and they function in the compartmentalisation of cells and organelles and also as sites of exchange of information between the inside and the outside. They are also the sites of the electron transport of photosynthesis and respiration. The membrane lipids are mainly phospholipids and glycolipids.

Figure 12 shows an image of a typical biological membrane.

Question 1

By separating the inside and the outside of cells and organelles, biological membranes contribute to the maintenance of their homeostasis. For this reason, biological membranes are selectively permeable to substances. Of the following options, which substances or other items easily pass through the lipid bilayer of a biological membrane made of membrane lipids? Choose all the appropriate ones from options (1)–(5), and mark the numbers of all the chosen options in the answer box. If you judge that all the statements are correct, mark (9); if you judge that there is no appropriate statement, mark only (0). Answer box: 52

(1) Oxygen molecules and carbon dioxide molecules

(2) Water molecules

(3) Electrons

(4) Lipid-soluble substances

(5) Ions

Question 2

The thylakoid membrane, in which the electron transport reactions of photosynthesis take place, consists mainly of glycolipids, and contains less phospholipid than other biological membranes. This is thought to be because phosphorus is not very abundant in the growth environment, so that its use is kept as low as possible. To test this hypothesis, a certain cyanobacterium was cultured under phosphorus-deficient conditions and the effect on the membrane lipids was examined; it was found that phospholipids decreased and that, among the glycolipids, digalactosyldiacylglycerol (DGDG) and sulfoquinovosyldiacylglycerol (SQDG) increased.

To test whether DGDG and SQDG are required for the electron transport reactions of the thylakoid membrane under phosphorus deficiency, an experiment was planned comparing the differences in the electron transport reactions between two strains. Choose two of the following options (1)–(7) that are considered not appropriate as the combination of strains used in this experiment. The mutant strains are deletion mutants, and under optimal culture conditions no difference is seen between the wild-type strain and the mutant strains. Answer box: 53

(2) DGDG synthase gene mutant expressing a phospholipid synthase gene, and wild type

(3) DGDG synthase gene mutant, and wild type expressing a phospholipid synthase gene

(4) SQDG synthase gene mutant and wild type

(5) SQDG synthase gene and DGDG synthase gene double mutant, and wild type

(6) SQDG synthase gene and DGDG synthase gene double mutant, and DGDG synthase gene mutant

(7) SQDG synthase gene and DGDG synthase gene double mutant, and SQDG synthase gene mutant

Food processing in mammals takes place in four stages: ingestion, digestion, absorption and elimination. When food enters the oral cavity, (　あ　) contained in saliva breaks down starch and glycogen. The food is then pushed along by peristalsis and taken into the stomach. In the stomach, two main components of gastric juice help to liquefy the food. The first component is (　い　), which aids digestion by denaturing proteins and killing bacteria, and the other is (　う　), a protein-digesting enzyme. Because the concentration of (　い　) is high, gastric juice is a strong acid of about pH 2, and most bacteria are killed here. The food, whose digestion has progressed in the stomach, is then carried to the small intestine. The approximately 25 cm of the small intestine on the stomach side is called the duodenum, where the chyme from the stomach is mixed with the digestive juices of (ア) the pancreas, liver, gall bladder and small intestine. Carbohydrates are broken down into monosaccharides by digestion and absorbed into the blood, so that the blood glucose level rises. This is why blood glucose becomes high after a meal. Because a blood glucose level that stays high has harmful effects on the body, the blood glucose level is lowered by the action of hormones, and (イ) homeostasis of the blood glucose level is maintained.

Question 1

哺乳類の食物の処理は、摂取・消化・吸収・排泄の4段階で行われる。口腔に食物が入ると唾液に含まれる（　あ　）がデンプンやグリコーゲンを分解する。その後、食物は蠕動によって押し出されて胃へと取り込まれる。胃では胃液を構成する主要なふたつの成分が胃での食物の液状化を助ける。ひとつ目の成分がタンパク質の変性や殺菌によって消化を助ける（　い　）であり、もうひとつがタンパク質分解酵素である（　う　）である。（　い　）の濃度が高いため、胃液はpH約2の強酸であり、大半の細菌はここで死滅する。胃で消化が進んだ食物はその後、小腸へと運ばれる。小腸の胃側領域の25 cm程は十二指腸と呼ばれ、胃からの糜汁が、(ア)膵臓、肝臓、胆嚢、小腸の消化液と混合される。炭水化物は消化によって単糖類に分解され、血中に吸収されることで血糖値が上昇する。よって、食事後には血糖が高くなるのである。血糖値が高いままでは体に悪影響を及ぼすためホルモンの働きによって血糖値が減少し、(イ)血糖値の恒常性が保たれている。

(1) 脂質の吸収と消化を担う胆汁酸塩は、肝臓から分泌されて胆嚢で蓄積、濃縮されたものである。

(2) 胆嚢は消化酵素を産生して十二指腸に直接分泌し、タンパク質の分解を担っている。

In vertebrates such as humans, the liver and muscles are the main sites of energy storage. In the cells of these tissues, excess energy from food is stored in the form of glycogen, a polymer of many glucose units. When the glycogen stores of the liver and muscles reach their upper limit, the further excess energy is stored as fat in adipocytes.

Animals living in the wild are likely not to be able to eat regularly as humans do. When placed in such a fasting state, animals survive by mobilising the energy sources in their bodies. To elucidate this survival strategy, a fasting experiment was carried out using African clawed frogs (Xenopus) (アフリカツメガエル). The frogs were divided into a 3-week experimental group, a 3-month experimental group and a 7-month experimental group, and in each experimental group a control group that was fed during the period and a fasting group that was fasted during the period were prepared. At the end of the experimental period, the frogs of each experimental group were dissected, the blood glucose concentration, the amount of liver glycogen, the amount of muscle glycogen, the weight of adipose tissue and the weight of muscle tissue were measured, and the data were expressed as values relative to the respective control group (the fed group). The results are shown in Table 4. For the amounts of liver glycogen and muscle glycogen, a relative value of about 0.1 (with the control group taken as 1) is considered to indicate an almost depleted state. problems.problem:
(10 points)

Buckwheat (ソバ) is a traditional food in Japan, and in recent years it has also become increasingly popular worldwide as a health food. Buckwheat belongs to the family Polygonaceae and has long-styled flowers, in which the pistil is longer than the stamens, and short-styled flowers, in which the pistil is shorter than the stamens. The flower type is genetically determined for each individual (plant), and fertilisation is not possible without exchange of pollen between flowers of the two types. A buckwheat flower is a one-day flower that is open for just one whole day, but an individual plant produces flowers one after another over about 2 weeks as it grows.

In many crops the western honeybee is known as the main pollinator (pollen vector), but buckwheat is known to be visited by a wide variety of insects. To examine how much various insects contribute to the seed set of buckwheat, bagging experiments excluding flower-visiting insects were carried out in the field.

Experiment ①: To examine the contribution to seed set of insects of different body sizes, two kinds of bag were prepared: bags of fine mesh (0.5 mm), which let no insects at all through, and bags of coarse mesh (5 mm), which keep out only large insects; the bags were placed over inflorescences (groups of flowers) of buckwheat in a buckwheat field. Bagging was done early in the morning just after the flowers opened, the bags were removed the next morning, and later the inflorescences were brought back to the laboratory and all the flowers were examined for whether they had set seed.

Experiment ②: To examine the contribution to seed set of the insects that visit during the day and at night respectively, inflorescences to be bagged only during the day and inflorescences to be bagged only at night were chosen. For each of day and night, the two kinds of bag with different meshes, as in Experiment ①, were placed over the respective inflorescences, and later the flowers were examined for seed set.

Experiment ③: As the control plot for the above experiments, inflorescences left in their natural state without any treatment were chosen, and later the flowers were examined for seed set.

Figure 15 shows the results for the seed-set rate (the proportion of all the flowers that set seed) in the various bagging treatment plots (or the untreated plot) described above.

(10点)

ソバは日本の伝統食であり、近年世界的にも健康食として人気が高まっている。ソバはタデ科に属し、雌しべが雄しべより長い長花柱花と、雌しべが雄しべより短い短花柱花がある。花のタイプは個体（株）ごとに遺伝的に決まっていて、両タイプの花間での花粉のやり取りがないと受精できない。ソバの花は丸1日だけ開花する一日花であるが、個体は成長しながら約2週間にわたり次々と花をつける。

多くの作物ではセイヨウミツバチが主な送粉者（花粉媒介者）として知られているが、ソバには多様な昆虫が訪れることがわかっている。さまざまな昆虫がソバの結実にどの程度貢献しているかを調べるために、野外で訪花昆虫を排除する袋掛け実験を行った。

実験① 体サイズが異なる昆虫による結実への貢献を調べるため、昆虫を全く通さない細メッシュ（0.5 mm）の袋と、大型昆虫のみを通さない粗メッシュ（5 mm）の袋の2種類を用意し、ソバ畑のソバの花序（花の集まり）に対して袋掛けを行った。袋掛けは開花直後の早朝に行い、翌朝に袋を回収し、後日花序を実験室に持ち帰り、すべての花の結実の有無を調べた。

実験② 昼と夜のそれぞれに訪れる昆虫の結実への貢献を調べるために、昼のみ袋掛けする花序と、夜のみ袋掛けする花序を選んだ。また、昼と夜それぞれについて、実験①と同様にメッシュが異なる2種類の袋をそれぞれの花序に袋掛けし、後日結実の有無を調べた。

実験③ 上記実験の対象区として、何も処理をしない自然状態のままの花序を選び、後日結実の有無を調べた。

problems.problem:
(8 points)

In behavioural ecology, which studies animal behaviour, behaviour is analysed on the assumption that it is a product of adaptive evolution by natural selection. As a result of adaptive evolution, an individual is expected to behave so as to choose, from the options available to it and on the basis of the information available at that time, the one that maximises its fitness as an individual. On the basis of this expectation, let us consider the size of the flocks that arise from a chain of foraging behaviour in a certain bird.

Every morning these birds fly one individual at a time from the roost to a grassland feeding ground; each independently chooses its foraging method once and then forages at the feeding ground until evening. The first individual begins foraging alone, but from the second individual onwards there is a choice between foraging alone and joining the individuals already at the feeding ground to forage as a member of the flock. Each individual has information on which option yields more food, and this information is summarised in Table 5. Table 5 shows, according to the number of individuals in the foraging flock, the total energy of food (unit: kJ) that the flock as a whole can obtain on that day. From the expectation stated above, each individual is thought to choose, on the basis of this information, the option that gives it the greater fitness. There are no individual differences in the characteristics of this bird, and the fitness of an individual is determined only by foraging at the feeding ground considered here.

(8点)

動物の行動を研究する行動生態学においては、行動が自然選択による適応進化の産物であると考えて分析を行う。適応進化の結果として、個体はその時点で利用可能な情報に基づいて、取りうる選択肢の中から個体としての適応度を最大化するものを選ぶように行動することが予想される。この予想に基づいて、とある鳥の採餌行動の連鎖によって生じる群れの大きさについて考えよう。

この鳥は、毎朝ねぐらから餌場の草原に1個体ずつ飛来し、それぞれが独立に1回、採餌方法を選んで、そのまま夕方まで餌場で採餌する。1番目の個体は単独で採餌を始めるが、2番目以降の個体には、単独で採餌するか、先に餌場にいる個体に合流して群れの一員として採餌するかの選択肢が生じる。各個体は、どちらの選択肢がより多くの餌を得られるかの情報を持っており、その情報をまとめたものが表5である。表5では、採餌群れに参加する個体数に応じて、群れ全体としてその日に獲得できる餌の総エネルギー量（単位：kJ）を示した。上に述べた予想から、個体はこの情報に基づいて、自分の適応度が大きくなる方の選択肢を選ぶと考えられる。なお、この鳥の性質に個体差はなく、個体の適応度は、ここで考えている餌場での採餌のみによって決まるとする。

2番目の個体は、単独採餌なら（　あ　）kJを、1個体目に合流して採餌するなら（　い　）kJを、個体あたりで獲得できるため、（　A　）ことを選択すると考えられる。同様に考えていくと、4番目の個体は（　B　）ことを、6番目の個体は（　C　）ことを、それぞれ選択すると考えられる。最終的に、その日の餌場には、最大でサイズ（　う　）の群れが形成される。

表5からは、群れ全体として最大の採餌効率を示す群れサイズは、個体として最大の採餌効率が得られる群れサイズと比べて（　D　）ことが読み取れる。また、この鳥の例においては、多数の個体による最適な行動選択の連鎖の結果、実現する群れサイズは、個体として最大の適応度が得られる最適群れサイズに比べて常に（　E　）ことが結論される。

Problem 1. Read the following passage and answer Questions 1 to 4.

Materials and safety (shared by the whole booklet)

When carrying out the experiments, always wear gloves and safety glasses. The developing tank is made of glass and may be slightly chipped, so handle it carefully to avoid injury.

Samples
• Seven 1.5 mL tubes containing solutions (labelled 1-1 to 1-5, 2-1 and 2-2 on the lid)

Apparatus
• Safety glasses
• Rack for 1.5 mL tubes
• Micropipette (Gilson P-20), 1
• Micropipette tips, several
• Cup for used tips
• Developing tank containing developing solvent (with yellow tape attached)
• Thin-layer plate
• Ultraviolet light source
• Cardboard box for shielding
• Ruler
• Paper towels

Reagents
• 1N HCl (1.5 mL tube with "HCl" written on the lid)
• 1N NaOH (1.5 mL tube with "NaOH" written on the lid)

Samples
• 1.5 mL tubes 1-1, 1-2, 1-3, 1-4, 1-5
• 1.5 mL tubes 2-1, 2-2

Do you know about fluorescent proteins? Fluorescent proteins are proteins that absorb ultraviolet or visible light and emit light of a different wavelength (fluorescence). Fluorescent proteins are not only used by jellyfish and corals themselves; because introducing them into cells has made it possible to observe a wide variety of life phenomena while keeping the cells alive, they have been used in many experiments in the life sciences. In recognition of this achievement, the 2008 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to three people, Osamu Shimomura, Martin Chalfie and Roger Y. Tsien, "for the discovery and development of the green fluorescent protein (Green Fluorescent Protein, GFP)".

How do these fluorescent proteins absorb light? A protein has a structure in which many amino acids are linked in a chain. The 20 kinds of amino acids that make up proteins each differ in the structure of their side chain. Aromatic amino acids such as tryptophan and tyrosine can absorb ultraviolet light but cannot absorb visible light. Therefore, proteins that absorb visible light and emit fluorescence (fluorescent proteins) have a chromophore for absorbing visible light. The chromophores of fluorescent proteins fall broadly into two kinds: in one, a specific pigment binds to the protein and functions as the chromophore, whereas in the other, the chromophore is formed by autocatalytic activity from several amino acid residues of the protein itself. Both of these two kinds are also known among green fluorescent proteins, which absorb blue light (or ultraviolet light) and emit green fluorescence; the proteins corresponding to the former bind a pigment called flavin.

The samples used in Problem 1 are as follows.

1.5 mL tube 1-1: flavin A
1.5 mL tube 1-2: flavin B
1.5 mL tube 1-3: flavin C
1.5 mL tube 1-4: fluorescent protein A
1.5 mL tube 1-5: fluorescent protein B

Question 1: Place 1.5 mL tubes 1-4 and 1-5 in the cardboard box, irradiate them with ultraviolet light and confirm that each of them emits fluorescence. In this case, state which is higher: the total energy of the light absorbed by each substance or the total energy of the light being emitted as fluorescence. Then discuss what has become of the difference between these energies.

In this process, the components in the sample repeatedly adsorb to and desorb from the silica gel coated on the thin-layer plate and the solvent. Therefore, highly polar substances, which adsorb readily to silica gel, move more slowly. Also, proteins are denatured in organic solvents and do not dissolve, so they cannot be developed.

Question 3: A substance that absorbs light has a constant, ε (the molar absorption coefficient), characteristic of that substance for the absorption of light. Riboflavin can absorb light in the region from ultraviolet to blue light, and its molar absorption coefficient at 445 nm is 12,500. When the absorbance (ABS) at 445 nm of riboflavin diluted to a certain concentration was measured, it was 0.5. According to the Beer–Lambert law, the following equation holds between the absorbance, the molar absorption coefficient, the molar concentration of the light-absorbing substance and the optical path length. From this equation and the information above, calculate the molar concentration of the riboflavin whose absorbance was measured. Question 4: Read the following passage and answer (A) and (B).

The well-known fluorescent substance green fluorescent protein, GFP, was discovered in the crystal jelly (オワンクラゲ). GFP has a chromophore formed by the bonding of specific amino acids in the protein. In addition, the crystal jelly expresses aequorin, a luminescent substance (a substance that emits light even without being illuminated). Aequorin reacts with calcium ions and emits blue light.

(A) When the crystal jelly is swimming, in the cells that have both aequorin and GFP no blue light emission is observed; only green light emission is observed. State a hypothesis for why this phenomenon occurs.

(B) Both aequorin and GFP were expressed in cultured nerve cells, with the same localisation as in the cells of the crystal jelly. When various treatments are applied to these nerve cells, what do you expect to happen to the luminescence or fluorescence? On the answer sheet, put ○ where you expect luminescence or fluorescence to be observed.
Here, assume that luminescence is observed in the dark without illuminating with anything, and fluorescence is observed in the dark while illuminating with UV light.
The treatments of the nerve cells are as follows.
(1) Nothing is done.
(2) An electrical stimulus is given to the cell body, producing an action potential.
(3) The Na$^{+}$ concentration of the extracellular fluid is raised and the same stimulus as in (2) is given.
(4) The Ca$^{2+}$ concentration of the extracellular fluid is lowered and the same stimulus as in (2) is given.

Problem 2. Read the following passage and answer Questions 1 to 4.

(Materials as listed at the start of the booklet: 1.5 mL tubes 2-1 and 2-2; 1N HCl and 1N NaOH in 1.5 mL tubes; micropipette (Gilson P-20) and tips; ultraviolet light source; cardboard box for shielding. Always wear gloves and safety glasses.)

The sequence of a gene on DNA specifies the primary amino acid sequence of the protein corresponding to that gene. A protein synthesised from DNA via transcription and translation takes a variety of structures in its initial state, but it is thought that it finally converges to a single stable structure. This folding of a protein into its correct shape is called folding. It is also known that, for some proteins, proteins called chaperones assist folding.

Question 1: Using the samples in 1.5 mL tubes 2-1 and 2-2, carry out Experiment 2 below and answer questions (A) and (B).

The 1.5 mL tubes contain only the following substances.
1.5 mL tube 2-1: GFP
1.5 mL tube 2-2: Red Fluorescent Protein (RFP)
GFP and RFP: fluorescent proteins that form their chromophore from the protein alone

Experiment 2
(1) Inside the cardboard box, irradiate 1.5 mL tubes 2-1 and 2-2 with ultraviolet light and confirm that they emit fluorescence.
(2) Treatment 1: Using the micropipette, add 5 µl of 1 N HCl solution to 1.5 mL tubes 2-1 and 2-2 and mix well by tapping. Observe their appearance at that time. Then, inside the cardboard box, irradiate each tube with ultraviolet light and observe their appearance at that time.
(3) Treatment 2: Next, using the micropipette, add 5 µl of 1 N NaOH solution to each tube and mix well by tapping. Observe their appearance at that time. Then, inside the cardboard box, irradiate each tube with ultraviolet light and observe their appearance at that time.

(A) Record the results of your observations after each treatment.

(B) What is the difference between the proteins in 1.5 mL tubes 2-1 and 2-2? Discuss on the basis of your results.

Question 4: DnaK, a chaperone of Escherichia coli, together with DnaJ and GrpE, can convert denatured proteins into proteins with the correct folded structure through a cycle like that in the figure below. This was found from studies in which experiments were carried out by adding factors such as DnaK, DnaJ and GrpE to denatured proteins in test tubes. In such experiments, luciferase is often used as the denatured protein. Luciferase is an enzyme that catalyses the reaction in which the luminescent substance luciferin is oxidised and light is emitted. This enzyme loses its enzyme activity when it is denatured, for example by heat. Even if it is left at room temperature its enzyme activity does not return, but when suitable amounts of denatured luciferase, DnaK, DnaJ, GrpE and ATP are added to a test tube and left at room temperature, it regains its enzyme activity, and light emission is observed when luciferin is added.
There are Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, which used denatured luciferase. The result of each experiment revealed a part of this chaperone cycle. Explain which part of the cycle each experiment revealed. Note that other possibilities cannot be ruled out by these experiments alone, but you may ignore that.

The protein cycle by the chaperones of Escherichia coli

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2025-3-8-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 正しい構造のタンパク質 = protein with the correct structure; 変性タンパク質 = denatured protein; 無機リン酸 = inorganic phosphate.

A denatured protein first binds to DnaJ. This DnaJ–denatured protein complex binds to DnaK with ATP bound (hereafter ATP-DnaK) and hands the denatured protein over to DnaK. After that, the ATP is hydrolysed and the ATP bound to DnaK changes into ADP. At that time the binding between DnaK and DnaJ is released. After that, through the action of GrpE, the ADP bound to DnaK comes off and is replaced by ATP. At that time the denatured protein is also released and folds into the correct structure.

Lysozyme is an enzyme that degrades the polysaccharides of bacterial cell walls; aspartic acid and glutamic acid in its active site take part in the reaction. Figure 1 is a schematic diagram showing how lysozyme cleaves the bond between sugars. Figure 2 shows the relationship between the extent to which the side-chain carboxy groups of aspartic acid and glutamic acid are ionised depending on pH, and the activity of lysozyme. Lysozyme cleaves the bond between sugars by the following mechanism. First, the side chain of an ionised amino acid binds to the carbon enclosed by the dashed circle in Figure 1. From the ionisation tendencies of aspartic acid and glutamic acid in Figure 2, this amino acid is expected to be ( ア ). Next, the oxygen linking the sugars binds a hydrogen ion supplied by ( イ ) and becomes a hydroxy group, whereby the bond between the sugars is first cleaved. At the pH at which lysozyme is active, the side chain of ( ウ ) also readily loses its hydrogen ion. However, because the active site is in a hydrophobic environment, the side chain of ( ウ ) tends to retain its hydrogen ion. As a result, its apparent acid strength becomes weaker, as for amino acid X in Figure 2, and it can supply a hydrogen ion even at the pH at which the enzyme is active. After that, the bond between the side chain of ( ア ) and the sugar is cleaved by the addition of water, and the degradation reaction is complete. As shown in Figure 2, the activity of lysozyme decreases as the pH becomes higher. This is because the side chain of ( エ ), which supplies the hydrogen ion in the active site, becomes less able to retain its hydrogen ion.

The information in DNA is transcribed into RNA, and proteins are made on ribosomes on the basis of the information in the mRNA made from that RNA (in eukaryotes, after splicing). On the ribosome, part of the tRNA that brings an amino acid (the anticodon) pairs with the information in the mRNA (the codon), so that the information in the base sequence of the mRNA is converted into an amino-acid sequence.

Figure 1 below shows a part of a certain double-stranded DNA, the mRNA made from that part, the bases of each of the tRNAs that pair with that mRNA on the ribosome, and the correspondence with the amino acids carried by the tRNAs; only some of the bases are shown. problems.problem:
Nitrogen is one of the major nutrients for plants. Plants absorb nitrogen through their roots, mainly in the form of nitrate ions, and use it. However, nitrate ions are distributed unevenly in the soil. To clarify how plants efficiently absorb nitrate ions in such an environment, the following Experiment 1 was carried out using the model plant Arabidopsis (シロイヌナズナ) as material.

[Experiment 1]

The roots of wild-type plants were split into left and right halves as in Figure 1, and the left-hand roots were placed in contact with a nitrogen-sufficient medium containing a high concentration of nitrate ions. For the right-hand roots, on the other hand, two conditions were set: in contact with nitrogen-sufficient medium (condition 1), or in contact with nitrogen-deficient medium containing no nitrate ions at all (condition 2). After the plants had been grown for a fixed period under each condition, the expression level of the NRT2.1 gene, which encodes a transporter involved in nitrate-ion uptake, was measured in each of the left and right roots; the results were as shown in Figure 2.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2026-1-6-fig1.png

Figure 1. Method of growing plants with the roots split in two

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2026-1-6-fig2.png

Figure 2. NRT2.1 expression under each condition

Figure labels (Japanese → English), Figures 1 and 2: 培地入りシャーレ = Petri dish containing medium; 根 = root; 仕切り = partition; 窒素充足 = nitrogen-sufficient; 窒素欠乏 = nitrogen-deficient; 条件1, 条件2 = condition 1, condition 2; 相対発現量 = relative expression level; 左 = left; 右 = right.

Later research revealed that X, a kind of peptide signalling molecule, is specifically expressed in roots only when they are in contact with nitrogen-deficient medium. Furthermore, a receptor Y that specifically receives X was also identified. To examine the roles of X and Y in the absorption of nitrate ions distributed unevenly in the soil, the following Experiment 2 was carried out.

[Experiment 2]

The roots of wild-type plants or of plants lacking the function of Y (Y loss-of-function mutants), grown for a fixed period, were split into left and right halves as in Figure 1 and placed under the same conditions as in Experiment 1. In addition, by grafting, the shoot of a Y loss-of-function mutant was joined to the roots of a wild-type plant, and the shoot of a wild-type plant was joined to the roots of a Y loss-of-function mutant. After the plants had been grown for a fixed period under each condition, the expression level of the NRT2.1 gene was measured in each of the left and right roots; the results were as shown in Figures 3 and 4.

窒素は植物にとって主要な栄養素の一つである。植物は，窒素を主に硝酸イオンの形で根から吸収して利用している。しかし，土壌中において硝酸イオンは不均一に分布している。そこで植物がこのような環境下で硝酸イオンをどのように効率的に吸収しているかを明らかにするため，モデル植物であるシロイヌナズナを材料に使って，以下の実験1を行った。

［実験1］

野生型植物の根を図1のように左右に二分し，左側の根は硝酸イオンを高濃度に含む窒素充足培地に接するようにした。一方，右側の根は窒素充足培地に接する条件（条件1），もしくは硝酸イオンを全く含まない窒素欠乏培地に接する条件（条件2）の2条件を設定した。各条件下で植物を一定期間育てた後，左右それぞれの根において，硝酸イオンの取り込みに関わるトランスポーターをコードするNRT2.1遺伝子の発現量を測定したところ，図2のようになった。

［実験2］

一定期間育てた野生型もしくはYの機能を欠失した植物（Y機能欠損変異体）の根を図1のように左右に二分し，実験1と同様の条件においた。その上で接ぎ木により，野生型植物の根にY機能欠損変異体の地上部を，Y機能欠損変異体の根に野生型植物の地上部をそれぞれ接着した。植物を各条件下で一定期間育てた後，左右それぞれの根においてNRT2.1遺伝子の発現量を測定したところ，図3および図4のようになった。

Among aquatic invertebrates, with regard to osmoregulation in the body, there are species that, like vertebrates, keep the osmotic pressure of their body fluid constant, and species that do not keep the osmotic pressure of their body fluid strictly constant relative to the external environment, so that the body fluid changes following the outside. In the latter case, an osmotic difference arises between the cell interior and the body fluid, which greatly affects cell function; therefore, inside the cells the osmotic pressure of the cell is often regulated by using free amino acids in addition to inorganic ions.

Table 1 below shows, for two euryhaline arthropods able to live even in environments where the salinity changes greatly — the lined shore crab (イワガニ; marine) and the whiteleg shrimp (バナメイエビ; brackish water) — the concentrations (mmol/L) of inorganic ions and free amino acids in the body fluid and in muscle extracts when they were kept in their natural environments of 100% seawater and 71% seawater respectively, and 5 days after they were transferred to environments of different salinity.

水棲無脊椎動物の体内の浸透圧調節は，脊椎動物と同様に体液の浸透圧を一定に保つ種と，体液の浸透圧を体外環境に対して厳密に一定に保たずに，体液が外界に追従して変化する種がある。後者の場合，細胞内と体液の浸透圧差が生じて細胞機能に大きな影響を与えるため，細胞内では無機イオンに加えて遊離アミノ酸を利用することによって，細胞の浸透圧を調節している場合が多い。

次の表1は，塩分濃度が大きく変化する環境でも生息できる（広塩性）節足動物であるイワガニ（海生）とバナメイエビ（汽水生）について，それぞれ生存環境である100％海水及び71％海水で維持した場合と，違う塩分濃度環境に移して5日後の，体液及び筋肉の抽出液の無機イオン及び遊離アミノ酸濃度(mmol/L)を示す。

problems.problem:
On high mountains the oxygen concentration is low, so breathing becomes laboured, but eventually one becomes accustomed and can breathe normally. As a response to the low oxygen concentration at this time, changes in the oxygen-binding properties of haemoglobin take place. The figure below shows oxygen dissociation curves of human haemoglobin; the black line shows the state on low-lying land, and the red line and the blue line show two stages of change that occur on moving to a high-altitude location.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2026-1-10-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 酸素飽和度 % = oxygen saturation %; 酸素分圧 (mmHg) = partial pressure of oxygen (mmHg).

On low-lying land, the partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood is 100 mmHg*1, and in venous blood it becomes 40 mmHg. Therefore the blood transports*2 25% of the haemoglobin-bound oxygen (converted to an amount of oxygen, this is about 5.2 mL of O₂ per 100 mL of blood). At high altitude the atmospheric pressure is lower, so the partial pressure of oxygen also falls, and at around 2500 m above sea level the partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood is about 60 mmHg. Oxygen sensors in the body, beginning with the carotid bodies, detect this, and first the breathing rate increases. The excretion of CO₂ then increases and the pH of the blood rises, so the dissociation curve shifts to the ( ア ). With this change, if the partial pressure of oxygen in venous blood does not change, the amount of oxygen transported becomes about ( イ ) % of the haemoglobin-bound oxygen*2. After a few days, in response to the change in blood pH, the concentration of 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG) rises, and the dissociation curve shifts to the ( ウ ) of the curve on low-lying land. The amount of oxygen transported then becomes about ( エ ) % of the haemoglobin-bound oxygen*2.

*1: mmHg, also called millimetres of mercury, is a unit used to express pressures in the body, such as blood pressure; 1 mmHg = 1.3332 hPa.

*2: The amount of oxygen transported is to be expressed as a percentage of the maximum amount of oxygen bound to haemoglobin, that is, by the value on the vertical axis of the graph.

Which words or numbers fill the blanks ア–エ in the text? Choose the most appropriate combination from A–H below. (6 points)

高い山では酸素濃度が低くなるため息が苦しくなるが，やがて慣れて普通に呼吸ができるようになる。このときの低酸素濃度に対する応答として，ヘモグロビンの酸素結合特性の変化が起こっている。次の図はヒトのヘモグロビンの酸素解離曲線で，黒線が平地での状態，赤線，青線は標高の高い土地に移動した際に起こる2段階の変化を示している。

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2026-1-10-fig1.png

平地においては，動脈血の酸素分圧は100 mmHg*1であり，静脈血では40 mmHgになる。したがって血液はヘモグロビン結合酸素量の25％を運搬する*2（酸素量に換算すると，血液100 mLあたりO₂ 5.2 mL程度となる）。高地では大気圧が低くなるために酸素の分圧も下がり，海抜2500 mあたりでは動脈血酸素分圧は60 mmHg程度となる。頸動脈小体をはじめとする体内の酸素センサーがこれを感知して，まず呼吸の頻度が上がる。するとCO₂の排出量が増加して血液のpHが上昇するため，解離曲線は $\fbox{ ア }$ に移動する。この変化によって，静脈血の酸素分圧が変わらなければ酸素の運搬量はヘモグロビン結合酸素量*2の $\fbox{ イ }$ ％程度となる。数日経つと，血液のpH変化に反応して2,3-ジホスホグリセリン酸（2,3-DPG）の濃度が上昇し，解離曲線は平地でのものよりも $\fbox{ ウ }$ に移動する。こうなると，酸素の運搬量はヘモグロビン結合酸素量*2の $\fbox{ エ }$ ％程度となる。

*1：mmHgは水銀柱mmとも呼ばれ，血圧など体内での圧力を示すのに使われる単位であり，1 mmHg ＝ 1.3332 hPaである。

*2：運搬される酸素量は，ヘモグロビン結合最大酸素量に対する％値，すなわちグラフ縦軸の数値で表すこととする。

文中の空欄ア～エにはどのような語・数字が入るか。その組み合わせとして最も適当なものを，次のA～Hから選べ。（6点）

$$\begin{array}{c|cccccccc} & \text{A} & \text{B} & \text{C} & \text{D} & \text{E} & \text{F} & \text{G} & \text{H} \\ \hline \text{ア} & \text{右} & \text{右} & \text{右} & \text{右} & \text{左} & \text{左} & \text{左} & \text{左} \\ \text{イ} & 43 & 25 & 8 & 16 & 43 & 25 & 8 & 16 \\ \text{ウ} & \text{左} & \text{左} & \text{左} & \text{左} & \text{右} & \text{右} & \text{右} & \text{右} \\ \text{エ} & 16 & 8 & 25 & 43 & 16 & 8 & 25 & 43 \end{array}$$

problems.problem:
Muscle contraction is brought about through the hydrolysis of ATP. Because the ATP present in muscle is only a small amount, to perform exercise it is necessary to produce ATP using creatine phosphate, glycogen, fatty acids and so on. These substances are also present in muscle, but any shortfall is supplied through the blood.

Glycogen stored in the liver and elsewhere is broken down into glucose, enters the blood and is carried to the muscles. Under oxygen-deficient conditions, glucose that has entered the muscle is converted into lactic acid, producing ATP. When sufficient oxygen is present, glucose that has entered the muscle is completely broken down, producing ATP. Neutral fat stored in fat cells and elsewhere is broken down into glycerol and fatty acids; the glycerol enters the blood and, at times of energy shortage, is converted into glucose in the liver. The fatty acids bind to albumin and are carried to the muscles via the blood. Note that the binding of fatty acids to albumin is sensitive to changes in pH: when the pH shifts towards the acidic side, the binding strength between fatty acids and albumin decreases. When sufficient oxygen is present, fatty acids that have entered the muscle are completely broken down, producing ATP.

To find out the effects of exercise intensity and duration on the concentrations of glucose and fatty acids, the following experiment was carried out. Athletes of a university cycling club were asked to pedal a cycling machine (fitness bike). Three exercise intensities were used, 25%, 65% and 85% of maximal oxygen uptake, and the duration was 120 minutes at the 25% and 65% intensities and 30 minutes at the 85% intensity. Blood was sampled three times in total (twice at the 85% intensity) — immediately before the start of exercise, and 30 minutes and 120 minutes after the start of exercise — and the concentrations of glucose, fatty acids and glycerol in the plasma were measured. In addition, the plasma lactic acid concentration was measured twice, immediately before the start of exercise and 30 minutes after the start of exercise. The table below shows the results.

筋肉の収縮はATPの加水分解を介して行われる。運動を行うには，筋肉中に存在するATPは少量であるため，クレアチンリン酸，グリコーゲン，脂肪酸などを利用してATPを産生する必要がある。これらの物質は筋肉中にも存在するが，不足分は血液を通じて供給される。

肝臓などに蓄えられているグリコーゲンはグルコースに分解され，血液に入り，筋肉に運ばれる。酸素不足の状態では，筋肉に入ったグルコースは乳酸に変換され，ATPを産生する。酸素が十分に存在する状態では，筋肉に入ったグルコースは完全に分解され，ATPを産生する。脂肪細胞などに蓄えられている中性脂肪はグリセロールと脂肪酸に分解されるが，グリセロールは血液に入り，エネルギー不足時には肝臓でグルコースに変換される。脂肪酸はアルブミンと結合し，血液を介して筋肉に運ばれる。なお，脂肪酸とアルブミンの結合はpHの変化に敏感であり，酸性に傾くと脂肪酸とアルブミンの結合力は低下する。酸素が十分に存在する状態では，筋肉に入った脂肪酸は完全に分解され，ATPを産生する。

運動の強度と継続時間がグルコースと脂肪酸の濃度に与える影響を知るために，次のような実験を行った。ある大学の自転車競技部の選手にサイクリングマシーン（フィットネスバイク）を漕いでもらった。運動強度は最大酸素摂取量の25％，65％，85％の3種類とし，継続時間は25％と65％の強度では120分，85％の強度では30分とした。運動開始直前，運動開始から30分後と120分後の計3回（85％の強度では2回）採血し，血しょう中のグルコース，脂肪酸，グリセロールの濃度を測定した。また，血しょう中の乳酸濃度は，運動開始直前と運動開始後30分の2回測定した。下表はこの結果である。

Problem 1 (第1問)

Specimens, reagents and apparatus (checked before the start of the examination):

Documents
• Handout (4 pages) – 1 booklet

Specimens
• Petri dish containing 3 Welsh onion roots treated with pure water (marked 「水」 ("water") on the bottom) – 1
• Petri dish containing 3 Welsh onion roots treated with caffeine (marked "Cf" on the bottom) – 1
※ The Welsh onion roots are supplied immersed in a preservation solution.

Reagents and apparatus
• Forceps – 2
• Stand for glass slides and cover glasses – 1
• Glass slides (inserted in the stand) – 3 (of which 1 is a spare)
• Cover glasses (inserted in the stand) – 9 or more (of which 3 or more are spares)
• Micropipette (with tips) – 1
• Oil-based marker pen – 1
• Kimwipes (paper for wiping) – 2
• Light microscope – 1
• Scientific calculator – 1

Near the root tip of a plant, there are broadly a division zone, where cell division is active, and an elongation zone, where cells elongate rapidly; the root grows as the cells produced by division elongate. Caffeine, well known as a component of coffee, is known to inhibit root elongation. Therefore, to investigate the effect of caffeine on roots, Welsh onion (ネギ) roots were treated with an aqueous caffeine solution or with pure water for 24 hours and then stained with aceto-orcein. Observe the root tips of the Welsh onion by the following procedure and answer the questions below (Questions 1–4).

Note that the right eyepiece contains an eyepiece micrometer, but no stage micrometer is provided. Measure the size of the specimens using the relationship between the eyepiece micrometer and the stage micrometer for each objective lens shown in Figure 1 (an enlarged version of Figure 1 is given in the handout).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2026-3-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): 対物ミクロメーター（全長1 mm） = stage micrometer (total length 1 mm); 接眼ミクロメーター（接眼レンズにセットされた等間隔の目盛） = eyepiece micrometer (equally spaced scale set in the eyepiece); 4倍の対物レンズでの視野 = field of view with the 4× objective lens; 10倍の対物レンズでの視野 = field of view with the 10× objective lens; 40倍の対物レンズでの視野 = field of view with the 40× objective lens.

Figure 1. (a) Schematic diagram of the stage micrometer. It is 1 mm long in total, is graduated at 0.01 mm intervals, and is placed on the stage for observation. (b) Schematic diagram of the eyepiece micrometer. It is fitted in the eyepiece, and the length represented by one division changes with the magnification of the objective lens. (c)–(e) Schematic diagrams of the field of view when the stage micrometer is observed with (c) the 4× objective lens, (d) the 10× objective lens and (e) the 40× objective lens.

1. Place a glass slide on the plate part attached to the stand for glass slides and cover glasses.
2. The plate has three slits (gaps). Directly above each slit, drop 50 µL of the preservation solution from the Petri dish with the micropipette (Figure 2a).
3. With the forceps, place one water-treated root on each of the three drops and cover with a cover glass (Figure 2b). When taking the roots out with the forceps, take care not to grip the root-tip part (the darkly stained part).
4. Write 「水」 ("water") at the edge of the glass slide with the oil-based marker pen.
5. Carry out the same procedure with the caffeine-treated roots, and write "Cf" on the glass slide.
6. Observe the three roots of each treatment with the light microscope. Of these, use the one whose root tip is undamaged and whose staining is the clearest and easiest to observe for the subsequent observations.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/jbo-2026-3-1-fig2.png

Figure labels (Japanese → English): スライド・カバーガラススタンドの下に突き出た板の部分 = the part of the plate projecting below the stand for glass slides and cover glasses; 液滴 = drop; スライドガラス = glass slide; カバーガラス = cover glass; ネギの根 = Welsh onion root; 広がった液滴 = spread drop.

Figure 2. (a) Drop 50 µL of the preservation solution onto the glass slide at the intervals indicated in the figure. (b) Place a root on each drop, and cover it from above with a cover glass.

Question 1 (問1)

Sketch the outline of the root over a range of about 1.5 mm from the root tip (you need not draw cells or nuclei), and describe what differences there are between the water-treated root and the caffeine-treated root.
